tornadoes.name: Purcell
tornadoes.label: Purcell
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed near 180th Street and Ladd Road southwest of Purcell and moved northeast. One home about 3 miles southwest of Purcell had the roof removed. The tornado moved through Purcell causing roof damage to a few homes and damaging utility poles and trees. Moving out of the northeast side of Purcell, the tornado crossed the Canadian River into Cleveland County. One outbuilding was significantly damaged north of Lexington.

tornadoes.name: Lake Thunderbird Tornado
tornadoes.label: Lake Thunderbird Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado likely developed over Lake Thunderbird and moved northeast producing tree damage southwest of 156th Avenue Northeast and Tecumseh Road.

tornadoes.name: Tornado near Shawnee Lakes
tornadoes.label: Tornado near Shawnee Lakes
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed just west of the Cleveland-Pottawatomie County line where trees and a flag pole were damaged. The tornado moved northeast into Pottawatomie County damaging an outbuilding and trees. Roofs were damaged to at least two additional houses between the Shawnee Lakes.

tornadoes.name: Shawnee Tornado
tornadoes.label: Shawnee Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed just north of Shawnee Regional Airport and moved northeast damaging a couple of homes southwest of 45th Street and Kickapoo Street. The tornado then crossed Interstate 40 and damaged the roof of a hotel and damaging a business as it approached Harrison Street.

tornadoes.label: Near Wynona, OK
tornadoes.notes: A tornado damaged the roofs of several homes, destroyed a large outbuilding, and blew down trees.

tornadoes.label: Near Kokomo, MS
tornadoes.notes: An EF1 tornado touched down just southwest of Fordsville Road east of Tylertown, MS. The worst damage damage was seen just northeast of the touchdown point with light damage to a roof and an area of tree damage with multiple uprooted trees. Light tree damage was noted along the path until it crossed into Marion County where the roof of a restaurant was damaged on Highway 98.

tornadoes.name: Madison/Leake Tornado
tornadoes.label: Madison/Leake Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This weak tornado touched down near Highway 43 and Matlock Road in eastern Madison county and tracked 4.6 miles and dissipated at Red Dog Road in western Leake county. Tree damage, from a handful of uprooted trees, were the main damage at the very beginning of the path. The remaining damage was mostly small/large limbs down along Red Dog Road and the Natchez Trace. One large limb downed a power line. Max winds were 85 mph (EF0) and total path length was 4.6 miles.

tornadoes.name: Marion County Tornado
tornadoes.label: Marion County Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A EF-1 tornado struck western Marion County near Kokomo. The tornado caused some tree damage near the intersection of Welch Lane and Branton Bay Road. The tornado tracked northeast closely following Branton Bay Road up to Highway 98. The tornado did cause some roof damage to Popwell's Family Restaurant on Hwy 98. The tornado ended as it crossed Old Hwy 24. Max winds estimated at 90 MPH.

tornadoes.name: North Laurel Tornado
tornadoes.label: North Laurel Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This weak tornado began along Bush Dairy Rd and was observed by security cameras at least two businesses, damaging a sign and producing tree limb damage as it crossed Audubon Dr. The roof of an adult care facility was partially removed. The tornado crossed MS Highway 15, then caused shingle damage to several apartment buildings along Barberry Dr before lifting.

tornadoes.name: Coushatta, LA
tornadoes.label: Coushatta, LA
tornadoes.notes: Around midnight on January 10th, 2026 a supercell thunderstorm was moving toward the town of Coushatta. Rotation then quickly developed near HWY 480, several miles south of Coushatta, moving east. A tornado briefly touched down on HWY 71 near the Rolling Hills Trailer Park. Fortunately, no structural damage was found, however, multiple large branches were snapped off of nearby softwood trees and several hardwood trees were found uprooted and with large branches snapped right along the highway. As the tornado crossed HWY 71, it moved into a field where additional softwood trees were found uprooted and snapped. The tornado likely then lifted as it moved farther into the field/heavily wooded rural area. Some wind damage was then found in the Grand Bayou Resort campground area, with a few large branches off of nearby trees blown down.

tornadoes.name: Wanilla Tornado
tornadoes.label: Wanilla Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A tornado briefly touched down in the Wanilla community in northern Lawrence County. The tornado caused very minor tree damage along Smith Ferry Road and Old Highway 27. The tornado dissipated just beyond Old Highway 27 near the Pearl River.

tornadoes.name: Stringer Tornado
tornadoes.label: Stringer Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This weak, brief tornado touched down along Jasper Co Road 7. A barn had tin pealed off the roof and a tree was snapped along with other large limbs broken. The path was brief but focused. Max winds were 70 mph.

tornadoes.name: Carson Tornado
tornadoes.label: Carson Tornado
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado touched down in the Carson community in Jefferson Davis County. The tornado started just south of Carson on King Lane and tracked northeast crossing Highway 42 on the east side of Carson. There was significant tree and vegetation damage along Old Highway 42 and Alex Daley Road. Numerous trees were uprooted and snapped along Alex Daley Road. A chicken farm was hit just off of Alex Daley Road and sustained substantial damage. Most of the homes in this area had very little structural damage. The tornado continued northeast crossing Haw Pond Road and Highway 35 causing more tree damage. The tornado then continued to Santee Baptist Church Road where it damaged another chicken farm and continued to cause more tree damage. The tornado ended just beyond Santee Baptist Church Road in a wooded area.

tornadoes.name: Goodwater Tornado
tornadoes.label: Goodwater Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began near the intersection of US Highway 11 and MS Highway 528, initially mainly producing damage to tree limbs as it tracked across southeast Jasper County. Along CR 642, the roof of a mobile home was damaged and trees were uprooted. The tornado strengthened after crossing into Clarke County, producing a concentrated path of snapped trees as it crossed CR 250 west of the Goodwater community. Multiple utility poles were snapped and additional tree damage occurred along CR 280. Along the northern end of CR 291, the roof was removed from a barn and from a house before the tornado lifted.

tornadoes.name: Mars Hill Tornado
tornadoes.label: Mars Hill Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The National Weather Service in Birmingham surveyed damage in northern Cleburne County and confirmed an EF-0 tornado with winds up to 80 mph. The tornado began in a heavily forested area between County Road (CR) 549 and CR 205, where several pine trees were uprooted or limbs were snapped. The track moved northeast across a large area of inaccessible land and emerged at CR 296 and CR 49, where several more small pine trees were snapped or uprooted. More tree damage was noted at the intersection of CR 40 and CR 65, with very minor damage to a couple homes. The tornado then followed along CR 65, with additional tree damage along both sides of the road. Tree damage became slightly heavier as the tornado approached the Mars Hill community. The tornado struck four chicken houses and peeled the roofing off the southern end of three, scattering debris to the east and northeast. A home sustained minor roof damage, and a detached garage was damaged by a falling tree. Just downstream, a shed was destroyed in the yard of another residence. A tornado debris signature then became apparent on radar. The damage became more sparse as the path continued, with tree damage, mostly to pines, continuing across CR 123 and CR 253. The damage path appeared to end just past CR 253, before reaching the Georgia state line.

tornadoes.label: Near Roopville, GA
tornadoes.notes:
A brief tornado touched down just south of Lowell in southern Carroll County, late Saturday morning. The tornado was embedded within a line of showers and isolated thunderstorms (also referred to as a Quasi-Linear Convective System). Damage was first seen at a residence near Lake Circle and Staples Dairy Road. A 2-story home had a good portion of its roof cover pulled up along with the southwest-facing wall/siding severely damaged. The structure remained intact. Adjacent to the home, a barn was nearly destroyed with several 6' x 6' poles ripped out of the ground (secured in the ground by concrete). Based on this damage, it is estimated the tornado reached near its peak intensity of 90-95 mph (EF-1). It was in this area, a CC drop/TDS on FFC radar occurred. Debris from the barn was thrown more than 300 yards away.

The tornado continued to track east damaging another barn and uprooting several trees as it moved across Liberty Church Road. Another older barn at a residence just east of Liberty Church Road sustained significant damage, with most of its (sheet-metal) roof ripped off and walls destroyed. Additional trees were seen snapped or uprooted at this location and about 1/4 mile downstream in a wooded area (seen also by drone footage). Beyond this final point, no notable damage was seen

tornadoes.name: Rolling Acres Tornado
tornadoes.label: Rolling Acres Tornado
tornadoes.notes: NWS meteorologists assessed storm damage along the Lowndes County and Montgomery County line, in the community of Rolling Acres, and determined it was the result of a tornado. The tornado began on the west side of Cruise Road, just north of Bibb Road, where a few snapped and uprooted trees were observed. The tornado then continued eastward to County Road 26 and Hargrove Lane, producing similar timber damage along the way. The tornado then struck a manufactured home (MH) as well as two site-built homes along Treat Road. The first site-built home sustained damage to an attached carport and associated roofing on the south side of the structure. The MH had its sheet metal roof completely removed, though the roof truss structure remained intact. Insulation from its roof was noted to have been blown southeastward while the metal roofing material was blown northward. Next door, the tornado removed from a site-built home a large section of its roof structure on the west side of the structure. A splattering of insulation was noted on the east side of the residence. This damage pattern suggest a cyclonic wind field (i.e., a tornado). Several trees were uprooted or snapped in the vicinity of the structures. The tornado then produced additional timber damage, fairly minor in nature, east to near the shoulder of Interstate 65. 99% of this tornado's path was characterized by EF-0 damage, though a maximum rating of EF-1 is assigned due to the level of damage to the site-built home, making the worst of damage very, very short-lived.

tornadoes.name: Walton County Tornado
tornadoes.label: Walton County Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A tornado touched down in Walton County just west of Kings Lake Road and traveled east through a neighborhood along and just north of Paradise Island Drive. The tornado then presumably crossed the northern portion of Kings Lake causing more tree damage to the east of the lake. Along most of the path, EF-0 damage was observed. However, near the beginning of the patch two large trees were uprooted and rated EF-1. Near the end of the path, the tornado caused significant removal of the roofing material of a single family home. The porch was also badly damaged. Winds here were estimated at 95 mph, the highest found in this survey. The tornado then lifted quickly as there was no damage east of U.S 331 which is a swampy inaccessible area.

tornadoes.name: Geneva County Tornado
tornadoes.label: Geneva County Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A tornado touched down in a western Geneva neighborhood causing mainly EF-1 damage between Campbell and Magnolia Avenues. EF-2 damage occurred downtown on Commerce St. where roofing material was peeled off three adjacent low-rise buildings. After crossing a swampy area, a significant number of snapped trees were observed on either side of the SR 52 bridge over the Choctawhatchee River. The tornado continued east causing sporadic damage on McDougald St. in Eunola, Spring Creek Road, and East CR 4 before lifting near Spring Creek itself. Both EF-2 areas had maximum winds of 115 mph.

tornadoes.name: Northeast Houston County
tornadoes.label: Northeast Houston County
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began west of Center Church Road where it snapped large hardwood tree branches and removed several shingles off of a manufactured home. It continued to push east-southeast to Bill Yance Road where it snapped a few softwood tree trunks. It then crossed highway 52 where it continued to snap large softwood tree branches and slightly bent a street sign just off of highway 52. As it continued to move eastward to across county road 95, it continued to snap softwood tree limbs. Thereafter, the tornado pushed east southeast to across River Road where it partially collapsed a tin RV car port and snapped a few software tree trunks, before lifting just before the Georgia state line. Damage was consistent with an EF1 tornado with winds of approximately 88mph.

tornadoes.label: Near Madrid, AL
tornadoes.notes: A tornado briefly developed along Decatur Road in southwestern Houston County. The tornado lifted the roof off of a manufactured home before dissipating shortly thereafter without causing any additional known damage. An associated Tornadic Debris Signature (TDS) was noted on the Eglin AFB (KEVX) Radar data. The damage was consistent with an EF0 tornado with winds of approximately 85 mph.

tornadoes.name: Plum Grove Tornado Segment 1
tornadoes.label: Plum Grove Tornado Segment 1
tornadoes.notes:
Preliminary damage path of the first tornado segment of the Plum Grove Tornado. Tornado appears to initially touched down within a wooded area between CR 3708 and CR 3709, then turned eastward along CR 3709 for a short distance before lifting up shortly before River Ln. Through the use of a drone, did not see any damage in the deeply wooded area along the East Fork of the San Jacinto River. So, will end the first tornado just before the River Ln and CR 3709 intersection.

Majority of the damage seen was broken trunks and branches of pine trees and fences down. Power lines were also reported blown down, but the power line poles remained upright.

tornadoes.name: Plum Grove Tornado Segment 2
tornadoes.label: Plum Grove Tornado Segment 2
tornadoes.notes:
The second tornado segment starts along FM 1010 and Wooden Ln with an uprooted tree and broken wood signage. Drone footage showed no signs of damage within the wooded area between the first and second segments.

The most significant damage occurred at a metal structure off of FM 1010 with preliminary estimated peak winds of 85 mph. The tornado entered a largely empty field between FM 1010 and CR 3405, but still saw some tree damage. The tornado then entered the Bella Vista subdivision, causing tree damage, fence damage, and metal structure damage between CR 3405 and CR 3404.

No further damage was seen beyond the intersection of CR 3404 and CR 3410.

tornadoes.name: Moss Lake
tornadoes.label: Moss Lake
tornadoes.notes: The tornado started just east of 108 and just south of the Vincent Settlement elemetary school crossed over Oak Lake Drive just north of Moss Lake where mostly tree damage and minor siding damage was observed. The tornado crossed the ship channel and went across the north portion of Gray Plantation and crossed over Big Lake Road, where trees and an overturned shed was observed. The tornado ended just east of Elliot road where significant shingle damage was observed. Before the Rear flank downdraft winds overwhelmed the tornadic circulation. The observed damage to the south and east was from the rear flank down draft with winds estimated in the 60 to 80 MPH range.

tornadoes.name: NE Shelby County Tornado
tornadoes.label: NE Shelby County Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
This brief EF-1 tornado began along County Road 3156, where a few trees were downed, and then it traveled southeast to cross Highway 7 where it intersected with County Road 3153. Most of the damage here was also to trees with a consolidated area of snapped softwood trees giving the tornado its estimated maximum windspeed rating of 95 mph. The tornado then continued to the southeast and was judged to have ended just after crossing County Road 3215. One outbuilding was destroyed at this location, but otherwise the survey team could verify only minor damage done to a few buildings here and earlier when the tornado crossed Highway 7. Localized snapping of tree trunks was also quite evident around a pond just to the west of County Road 3215. Fortunately, there were no human injuries or fatalities associated with this brief and short-lived tornado.

Many thanks to TDEM and Emergency Management Officials the Shelby County for their assistance locating the damage.

tornadoes.name: Westport Tornado
tornadoes.label: Westport Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Tornado touched down near Bunion Marcle Rd then continued eastward across Freedom Rd, completely destroying 4 outbuildings.

tornadoes.name: Kateland, LA
tornadoes.label: Kateland, LA
tornadoes.notes: Shortly before 9PM CST on February 14th, 2026, a line of severe thunderstorms was moving east towards Grant Parish. Around 8:44 pm CST rotation along the line developed rapidly just east of the Red River and West of Louisiana State Highway 8, around Thompson Road. A tornado quickly touched down, initially damaging a large hardwood tree where multiple branches were downed before then damaging a barn where a significant portion of the metal roofing was torn off and blown downstream towards the highway. Additional debris from the roof and some large branches were then found just east of Louisiana State Highway 8 before the tornado lifted and the line of severe thunderstorms continued eastward.

tornadoes.name: Union Hill
tornadoes.label: Union Hill
tornadoes.notes: Pine Tree damage and uprooted. Large branches 1-3 inches in diameter broken off. Tree damage to a residence.

tornadoes.name: Highway 14 Tornado
tornadoes.label: Highway 14 Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Tornado touched down west of Hwy 14 on Pinewood Drive where minor damage was observed to mobile homes. It continued southeast across HWY 14, damaging several large live oak trees near Walden drive. A home sustained roof damage when the tornado ripped the awning from the home on Wilson Drive. Several homes and outbuildings received minor damage as the tornado exited the neighborhood to the southeast.

tornadoes.label: Near Oberlin, LA
tornadoes.notes: Extensive pine tree damage.

tornadoes.name: Mayo Ridge Tornado
tornadoes.label: Mayo Ridge Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Tornado touched down somewhere in the woods west of Veterans Memorial HWY then continued northeast to HWY 167 where it dissipated. Several pine trees were snapped at their trunks, a few outbuildings were destroyed or had their roof peeled, and a canopy was thrown a distance off.

tornadoes.name: Crooked Creek Tornado
tornadoes.label: Crooked Creek Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Tornado started in the wooded areas southeast of the Crooked Creek Reservoir where an area of trees were snapped. To the east, a private drive sustained varying degrees of damage to roughly six outbuildings including a pool house which lost part of its roof. Damage was noted to the east where the tornado crossed Crooked Creek Pkwy, where further tree damage was noted.

tornadoes.name: Cheneyville Tornado
tornadoes.label: Cheneyville Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Tornado touched down east of Hwy 71 and continued northeastward towards Bayou Rd. Damage to a few outbuildings occurred, with one sustaining significant damage. Additional damage to trees and one mobile home had its roof peeled off.

tornadoes.name: NW Bunkie Tornado
tornadoes.label: NW Bunkie Tornado
tornadoes.notes: There is a concentrated area of damage east of HWY 71 where a tornado touched down. It progressed northeastward across the highway, where it caused additional minor damage to fences and trees before dissipating in an open field.

tornadoes.name: Hancock Rd Tornado
tornadoes.label: Hancock Rd Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado touched down near the intersection of Hancock Rd and Leger Rd where it caused damage to an outbuilding and a canopy.

tornadoes.name: Lyons Point Gully Tornado
tornadoes.label: Lyons Point Gully Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A short lived tornado touched down near the intersection of Madison road and Ebenezer road where tree damage was observed. The tornado continued northeast where it snapped trees and destroyed an outbuilding at Ruby Lane. The tornado lifted just east of Ebenezer road.

tornadoes.name: Port Barre Tornado
tornadoes.label: Port Barre Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado started due southeast of Port Barre along LA 741 where it lifted the sheet metal roofing from a home. Several outbuildings were destroyed or heavily damaged. Trees showed damage as well. Tornado winds flipped a pontoon boat and horse trailer. The tornado continued northeast across a field and lifted within a grove of trees south of LA 190.

tornadoes.name: Centreville
tornadoes.label: Centreville
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado touched down along Ancil Cox Road on the southwest side of Centreville near Griffin Lane. A few trees were downed here, with at least one of them taking down a powerline. The tornado tracked northeast, generally paralleling Ancil Cox Road until reaching the intersection with Old Highway 33. The most significant damage occurred near this intersection, where approximately a dozen trees were uprooted or snapped which supports the 90 mph wind rating. Beyond this point, the tornado continued northeastward producing sporadic tree and limb damage along its path. The final accessible point of the tornado’s track was near Centerville Academy. Minor damage was observed on campus, including a downed light pole, partial roof uplift on a metal building, and a baseball pitching backstop that was thrown approximately 250 feet into a chain-link fence. The tornado continued northeast beyond Lower Centreville Rd where additional minor tree damage was identified. The tornado evidently lifted over inaccessible areas to the survey team prior to reaching Hwy 48.

tornadoes.name: Slaughter
tornadoes.label: Slaughter
tornadoes.notes: The damage path of an EF-0 tornado was identified in extreme southwestern East Feliciana Parish, near Lindsay, LA. This tornado caused predominantly minor tree damage including evident displacement and damage of trees consistent with maximum estimated winds near 80 mph. The tornado tracked from King's View Circle through Highway 964 and Thompson Rd before evidently dissipating over open rural fields near the parish line. This damage path was closely located with a strong area of rotation on KHDC radar imagery.

tornadoes.name: Enterprise, MS Tornado
tornadoes.label: Enterprise, MS Tornado
tornadoes.notes: An NWS storm survey with additional support from a local storm report has confirmed an EF-1 tornado occurred west of Liberty, MS in Amite County. This tornado began near Berwick Cassels and Smylie Rd where minor tree damage was identified. Additional patches of increasingly more notable tree damage as wide as 175 yards occurred as the tornado tracked northeast along Smylie Rd. The tornado reached peak intensity with maximum sustained winds near 100 mph as it approached Enterprise Rd and Lower Liberty Gloster Rd where it snapped tree trunks and uprooted numerous trees. A manufactured observed minor roof damage. More tree damage from this tornado was identified where it crossed MS Hwy 24, moving northeast. A local storm report identified additional notable tree damage with a few uprooted/snapped medium to large pine trees near Rattlesnake Ln. This tornado evidently lifted near the Amite River just before reaching Old 24 Compromise Rd.

tornadoes.name: Peoria, MS
tornadoes.label: Peoria, MS
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado with peak winds of 100 mph tracked north of Peoria, MS in Amite County. The tornado began near Patterson Rd where minor tree damage was identified. This minor tree damage continued northeast becoming gradually more severe as the tornado approached Peoria Rd. Dozens of trees were snapped and uprooted near and northeast of Peoria Rd as the tornado reached its peak intensity and a width of 200 yards. The tornado tracked northeast, crossing Highway 24 and East Fork Rd. Numerous trees were snapped and uprooted along this portion of the path. Additional minor tree damage was identified beyond East Fork Rd and Pray Rd on high resolution satellite imagery as the tornado evidently weakened. Patches of tree damage continued through Bass, Barron, Brown, and Thompson roads. Another brief swath of heavier tree damage occurred north of Thompson Rd as the tornado briefly reached a second peak at EF-1 intensity. The tornado weakened again and is estimated to have lifted after crossing Tangipahoa Rd and Hwy 570 where tree damage became too sparse to be considered a coherent track.

tornadoes.name: Pike/Lincoln
tornadoes.label: Pike/Lincoln
tornadoes.notes: An EF-0 tornado with maximum sustained winds estimated near 80 mph touched down near US Hwy 98 in far northeast Amite County, MS causing minor tree damage and removing a few metal panels from an outbuilding. The tornado continued northeast into Pike County where additional minor tree damage was found on Kenna Rd. This tornado continued northeast into Lincoln County, MS where it strengthened into a large, strong EF-1 tornado with maximum sustained winds near 110 mph southwest of Norfield, MS in NWS Jackson's area.

tornadoes.name: Norfield Tornado
tornadoes.label: Norfield Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began near the Pike Lincoln County line and tracked northeastward across southern Lincoln County, snapping and uprooted numerous trees along its path. The broad damage footprint with embedded areas of more concentrated damage suggests this path consisted of multiple vortices originating from the same parent mesocyclone. Tree damage was most prolific west of I-55 along Jack Lane, Summit Drive, Beachnut Trail, Wallace Drive, Montgomery Road, Dry Creek Trail, and Homesville Road. A house on Jack Lane sustained shingle damage, and outbuildings were damaged on Montgomery Road, Beachnut Trail, and Big Creek Drive. A mobile home was also damage along Beachnut. The tornado crossed I-55 about two miles south of the Bogue Chitto exit, then weakened and lifted as it moved through the Norfield community. This tornado may have began farther southwest, and additional surveys are planned to determine the correct starting point.

tornadoes.name: Hillaryville
tornadoes.label: Hillaryville
tornadoes.notes: An NWS storm survey team determined that an EF-1 tornado with peak winds of 90 mph embedded in a line of storms touched down along Highway 1 in far western Ascension Parish just after midnight on February 15th. Here, the tornado mainly snapped large branches and small tree trunks. The tornado continued eastward causing minor tree damage as it crossed Hwy 405 and the Mississippi River. More damage to large branches and tree tops was observed along River Rd north of Darrow. The tornado continued to move east-southeast over inaccessible areas until it reached Ruffin Martinez Rd and Highway 22. More large branches were snapped here as it continued moving to the east-southeast towards Walter Hill Rd. The tornado then crossed the Mississippi River a 2nd time and remained over either open fields or a refinery. The tornado reached peak intensity as it approached Highway 70 where it snapped a few tree trunks. The tornado then continued over the marsh east of Highway 70 where it likely lifted near the Ascension/St. James Parish line. This track remains preliminary and additional changes could occur after further review of high-resolution satellite imagery in the coming weeks.

tornadoes.name: Enterprise Tornado
tornadoes.label: Enterprise Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began near Mount Olive Road and tracked northeastward across Shell Oil Lane and MS Highway 583 before lifting near Highway 583 and Bethel Road. Along the tornado path, the roof of an outbuilding was damage on Shell Oil Lane and a house on Highway 583 sustained roof damage. Several trees were snapped and uprooted.

tornadoes.name: Donaldsonville
tornadoes.label: Donaldsonville
tornadoes.notes: An NWS Storm Survey team determined that an EF-1 tornado with peak winds of 105 mph embedded in a line of storms touched down just north of the Ascension/Assumption Parish line shortly after midnight on February 15th. This tornado started by snapping large branches and uprooting a tree on Te Nom Landry Rd and Highway 308 south. It continued moving east-northeast over open fields until reaching the intersection of Highway 3089 and Highway 70. Here, the tornado strengthened to EF-1 intensity where a power pole and tree trunk were snapped. This tornado maintained intensity as it continued moving to the east-northeast where it snapped a series of powerlines off of Baxter Rd on the south side of the CF Industries complex. The tornado then started to intensify to peak intensity as it crossed into St. James Parish while moving through mainly open fields before it hit a series of powerlines in an open field, snapping 4 lines. It maintained strength as it crossed another open field along Badger Rd before snapping another series of powerlines along Highway 18. The tornado appeared to weaken as it continued to move east-northeast across the Mississippi River. When the tornado reached Highway 3125, it partially snapped/bent another powerline. The tornado then moved into the marsh north of Highway 3025 before reaching Highway 61 where it uprooted another tree. The last damage point for this tornado is along I-10 where it snapped more large branches. This track remains preliminary and additional changes could occur after further review of high-resolution satellite imagery in the coming weeks.

tornadoes.name: Lincoln/Lawrence Tornado.
tornadoes.label: Lincoln/Lawrence Tornado.
tornadoes.notes: This EF-1 tornado began just south of Union Road Southeast, where it broke some large branches. The tornado continued northeast and crossed Harmon Drive Southeast where it snapped a couple of trees. The tornado also snapped a few trees and caused roof damage to a home along Pleasant Grove Drive. The tornado crossed Highway 84 uprooting a few more trees, before crossing into Lawrence County. The tornado crossed Foster Road where it caused damage to the roof of an outbuilding and ended just east of Foster Road. Max Winds 100 mph. Max width 250 yards.

tornadoes.name: Monticello Tornado
tornadoes.label: Monticello Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This EF-1 tornado began just north of Bethel Road with some minor roof damage to a home. The tornado continued northeast crossing John Payton lane, where it uprooted some trees and caused damage to a manufactured home. The tornado was at its strongest at this point. The tornado crossed Highway 587 snapping a few trees along the way. The tornado crossed the Pearl River and ended near Highway 184 East, where it snapped some large branches. Max wind 105 mph. Max width 400 yards.

tornadoes.name: Arm Tornado
tornadoes.label: Arm Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This weak tornado tracked from along Arm Road northeastward across Saint Stephens Road before lifting. Relatively minor tree damage occurred along the path with trees uprooted and several tree limbs broken.

tornadoes.name: Progress Tornado
tornadoes.label: Progress Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began along Progress Road, damaging a mobile home and uprooting trees and breaking tree limbs. It continued northeast across Taylor Lucas Road and Dykes Road, where additional tree damage occurred. Finally, it crossed Burkett Road, Pleasant Hill Road, and McNeese Griffith Road producing additional minor tree damage and downing a utility wire before lifting.

tornadoes.name: Prentiss Tornado
tornadoes.label: Prentiss Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began on the west side of Prentiss near Progress Road, uprooting and damaging trees as it tracked across MS Highway 184. As it moved across US Highway 84 on the northwest side of Prentiss, it removed much of the roof of a house on Ryjiah Lane. The tornado continued northeastward across MS Highway 42, Two Mile Road, and Skating Rink Road producing additional tree damage and damaging the roof of an outbuilding. Finally, it damaged old poultry houses along MS Highway 13 just before lifting.

tornadoes.name: Folsom
tornadoes.label: Folsom
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado touched down along August Ln, just west of Polo Rd, where it damaged trees and a roof of a residence. It moved east along Polo Rd with sporadic tree damage. The heaviest tree damage occurred along Spirit of the Forest Ln and River Trace Rd where more than a dozen very large trees were uprooted or snapped. Periodic tree and large limb damage occurred along the remainder of the path until the tornado lifted in the Merrywood Estates subdivision. Path length was 9.3 miles. Max width was 75 yards. Estimated maximum winds around 95 mph.

tornadoes.name: Thibodaux
tornadoes.label: Thibodaux
tornadoes.notes: An NWS storm survey team confirmed an EF-0 with peak winds of 85 mph touched down on the southern side of Thibodaux at 12:45am on February 15th. An trailer RV was partially flipped off of Talbot Ave as the tornado moved to the east-southeast. The tornado then reach peak strength as it impacted Tabernacle Pentecostal Church. Here, the tornado lifted a significant portion of the roof of the church, displacing it to the east. The wood framing of the roofing had evidence of rotting, so the lower bound for that damage was used in this case. The tornado slightly weakened as it moved east-southeast where minimal damage was found until it reached Percy Brown Rd where multiple large branches were snapped along it. The tornado remained very weak as it continued to the east-southeast where the next notable damage came on Crossing North St where a backyard awning was uplifted. As the tornado moved to the east-northeast, vegetation damage was noted on high-resolution imagery north of Rousseau where the tornado appeared to have lifted though additional analysis will be needed to determine the end point over inaccessible areas. This track remains preliminary and additional changes could occur after further review of high-resolution satellite imagery in the coming weeks.

tornadoes.name: Bogue Chitto
tornadoes.label: Bogue Chitto
tornadoes.notes: An NWS ground survey confirmed an EF-0 tornado with maximum sustained winds estimated near 85 mph tracked across parts of southwest and central Washington Parish, south of Franklinton, LA. This tornado began near Sam Smith Rd where it snapped a rotted large hardwood tree. Additional tree debris and minor damage to skirting of a manufactured home was noted nearby. The tornado continued east-northeast where more abundant tree damage was identified including snaps of smaller tree trunks and branches along Daniels Rd, west of LA Hwy 25. This was where the tornado appeared to be at its strongest and widest, spanning about 75 yards wide. The tornado continued across the Bogue Chitto River, and additional minor tree damage was found by the survey team along LA Hwy 16, Tullos Rd, and Gene Williams Rd. Near Lee Rd and Thigpen Rd was where the last area of more concentrated minor tree damage was noted and this was the estimated end point of this tornado damage path. No additional damage was identified on Moore Rd nor LA Hwy 439, however, minor sporadic tree damage did continue farther east, north of Bogalusa, LA.

tornadoes.name: North Prentiss Tornado
tornadoes.label: North Prentiss Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began along Odom Bass Road north of Prentiss and tracked northeastward along Mount Zion Road, crossing Whitesand Church Road before lifting southwest of the Clem community. The tornado produced relatively minor tree damage along its path.

tornadoes.name: Salem Tornado
tornadoes.label: Salem Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This very brief tornado damaged three chicken houses along Gaylons Drive. It also uprooted trees and caused other minor tree damage. The tornado lifted before reaching Salem School Road.

tornadoes.name: Northeast Covington Tornado
tornadoes.label: Northeast Covington Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This very brief tornado resulted in minor tree damage south of Taylorsville as it tracked across Charlie Red Drive and Ben Stroud Road.

tornadoes.name: Pearl River
tornadoes.label: Pearl River
tornadoes.notes: The track of an EF-0 tornado was identified via high resolution satellite imagery in association with a quick spin-up circulation within a line of storms. This tornado evidently damaged and/or displaced trees along mainly inaccessible areas near South Valley Rd and Kennedy Creek in Pearl River County, MS. The damage path peaked at approximately 70 yards wide and apparently ended after crossing Sun Valley Acres Rd, prior to reaching John Amacker Rd.

tornadoes.name: Wheeler Tornado
tornadoes.label: Wheeler Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Storm chaser video confirmation from two chasers of the tornado touching down about 1 mile southeast of Wheeler. The tornado caused minor damage to trees as it travelled northeast across Highway 33 before dissipating just east of N 500th St.

tornadoes.name: Yale Tornado
tornadoes.label: Yale Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A short-lived tornado occurred in a field 3 miles southwest of Yale. Evidence was seen along side of the road where the tornado went through the field.

tornadoes.name: Hardinville-Flat Rock Tornado
tornadoes.label: Hardinville-Flat Rock Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down about 3 miles southeast of Hardinville where it damaged several trees near the intersection of E 350th Ave and N 825th St. The tornado traveled northeast doing tree damage until it reached N 1000th St. The it intensified to EF-1 intensity as it severely damaged two homes, one mobile home was thrown off its foundation and wrapped around a tree injuring an elderly woman who was taken to the hospital with serious injuries. The tornado progressed northeast crossing several tree lines and also damaging additional homes and farm buildings along 1125th St and along E 465th Ave. The remainder of the damage was minor to a few trees before it dissipated about 2.5 miles north-northeast of Flat Rock.

tornadoes.name: SullivanTornado2026
tornadoes.label: SullivanTornado2026
tornadoes.notes: The tornado initially touched down west of the Wabash River in Crawford County, Illinois, before lifting and then crossing the river into southwestern Sullivan County near State Road 58. The tornado appeared to frequently come in contact with the ground at a few locations east of State Road 58 but never remained in contact with the ground for a long distance, but it demonstrated damage that reflects high-end EF0 or around 80 mph. The tornado maintained EF-0 intensity as it moved east-northeast through agricultural land, snapping a mix of large hardwood and softwood trees before lifting from Sullivan County. Damage was observed just northwest of Carlisle, where several small outbuildings sustained major damage. In this location, wind speeds were estimated at 80 mph, consistent with EF-0 intensity. The tornado continued across US-41 just south of Paxton, where an additional outbuilding was completely destroyed along with a neighboring home that had several large trees knocked over and snapped. This is where the strongest damage was found where wind speeds were estimated to be upwards of 85 mph. The storm survey estimates that the width of the tree damage spanned around 300 yards in an adjacent field. The circulation began to weaken and lift with just some minor tree damage to the northeast before lifting completely into the Greene County line. The National Weather Service would like to thank Sullivan County Emergency Management and local first responders for their assistance during this survey.

tornadoes.name: MonroeCoTor
tornadoes.label: MonroeCoTor
tornadoes.notes:
The tornado first developed around 6:56PM EST in wooded areas west of the Monroe County Airport before rapidly intensifying as it moved into a small neighborhood just west of the airport. This area experienced extensive tree damage along with multiple points of structural damage to homes, with the most intense damage estimated at 120 mph.

As the tornado progressed eastward, it caused damage to an airplane hangar at the airport. While passing over the airfield, the KBMG ASOS recorded a wind gust of 70 mph. The tornado then continued east of the airport, damaging numerous homes before striking a newly constructed neighborhood, where additional high-end EF1 to low-end EF2 damage was observed. Additional EF1 damage was observed to the northeast at an apartment complex.

The tornado dissipated around 7:06PM EST near the business district west of I-69, after producing damage to a bank overhang and causing roofing damage to several warehouse structures.

tornadoes.name: Bible Grove Tornado
tornadoes.label: Bible Grove Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Much of the damage was concentrated at a farmstead along the Clay/Effingham county line east of 1800th St. Metal from the top of a silo was blown off, and a barn was damaged with roof pieces blown northeast for about a half mile. Tracks through corn stubble in fields was found until reaching E. 200th Ave. west of county road 2200.

tornadoes.name: Edgewood Tornado
tornadoes.label: Edgewood Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down just south of the Clay and Effingham county line, near the Edgewood Rd. curve. Damage was limited to tree branches.

tornadoes.name: Trussville Tornado
tornadoes.label: Trussville Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service surveyed damage in Trussville and determined that a high-end EF-0 tornado occurred. Damage began along the north end of Mary Taylor Rd, where a construction trailer was flipped. A portion of the Metro Mini Storage had doors blown in and metal roofing lifted/peeled back. Next to this, approximately 13-14 trees in close proximity were uprooted, including 12 cedar trees in a tight row. Winds were estimated at about 80 mph here. The tornado crossed Highway 11, where minor roof damage was done to a car wash and Velma’s restaurant. As the tornado moved southeastward along Mary Taylor Rd, large doors were partially blown in and roofing was removed from a warehouse, and a fence was damaged at a dog daycare center. The tornado crossed a railroad and struck Daniel Iron, with a section of a warehouse having large doors blown in and large pieces of metal roofing removed. A few flatbed semi trailers were moved in the lot as well.

The tornado then ascended a small ridge and moved through a subdivision, causing mainly shingle and fence damage at numerous homes, along with a few trees and limbs being downed. At least one home was observed to have had a garage door damaged. Of particular note was the discovery of a large chunk of steel roofing from the Daniel Iron warehouse that landed on a home before sliding off and coming to rest on the side of another home. This caused considerable roof damage to the first home, resulting in water damage from rain. After this, minor tree and shingle damage continued across Hidden Brook Dr, Amber Trace, Yvonne St, and Alabama Dr, with the most notable damage being a few uprooted trees in close proximity along Yvonne St. The last area of discernable damage, very minor in nature, was observed near a lake in a curve along Queenstown Rd. Wind speeds at the peak were estimated at 85 mph at Daniel Iron. The NWS would like to thank Jefferson County EMA for their assistance during this survey.

tornadoes.name: Iantha
tornadoes.label: Iantha
tornadoes.notes: An EF0 with winds up to 80 mph and a width of 50 yards wide initially overturned portions of irrigation pivots approximately 1 mile northeast of Iantha, MO. The tornado destroyed an outbuilding along Northwest 30th Lane and turned easterly. Roofing components from the outbuilding were spread easterly over a mile away and some rafters embedding in fields up to 200 yards away. Several power poles were broken as well. South of the path, two sets of pivots had sections blown down northward, along with estimated 70 mph winds that downed tree limbs and damaged another outbuilding.

tornadoes.name: W of Orienta and Cleo Springs
tornadoes.label: W of Orienta and Cleo Springs

tornadoes.name: SW of Helena to NW of Nash
tornadoes.label: SW of Helena to NW of Nash

tornadoes.name: Sumner 1
tornadoes.label: Sumner 1
tornadoes.notes: Damage occurred to the top of a tank battery, overturned a pumpjack, snapped a few power poles and cedar trees along with damage to multiple outbuildings

tornadoes.name: Sumner 2
tornadoes.label: Sumner 2
tornadoes.notes: Occluded tornado with damage to a couple of outbuildings, and it moved several round hay bales. A couple small headstones in the cemetery were knocked over.

tornadoes.name: Edwardsburg_MI
tornadoes.label: Edwardsburg_MI
tornadoes.notes: A disorganized circulation touched down northwest of the intersection of Runkle St and Conrad Rd, destroying an attached garage and damaging the front of a home. One fatality, a 12 year old boy, was confirmed at the home. The tornado continued northeast, causing damage to mainly trees with some minor roof damage as it moved across Yankee St, east of Dailey Rd. The tornado then widen and intensified with the peak damage occurring along Harris St, between Hess Rd and M-62 where numerous trees were snapped or uprooted. Some damage to pole barns and homes (mainly roofs) was noted. The tornado crossed M-62 and continued northeast, crossing portions of Oil City Rd and Monette St to Curtis, Day and Chain Lakes before lifting just east of the intersection of South and Walnut Rd.

tornadoes.name: ThreeRivers
tornadoes.label: ThreeRivers
tornadoes.notes: Another tornado from the same supercell that produced the Edwardsburg tornado touched down west of Arthur L Jones Rd, north of M60. The tornado quickly intensified and produced EF-2 damage with estimated wind speeds of 120-130 mph. Here, the tornado hit a Menards, removing the roof on the southwest and northwest portions of the building, along with an exterior wall collapse. One section of an nearby Uhaul facility was also completely destroyed. The tornado continued through the heart of Three Rivers, producing EF-1 and isolated pockets of EF-2 damage to residences and businesses (including the hospital). The tornado crossed the St. Joseph River, producing extensive damage to a lumber yard before uprooting many trees in a local cemetery. The tornado produced another pocket of EF-2 damage to a double-wide mobile home and a brand new school transportation facility. Multiple school trailers were tossed either across the street or inside the transportation facility itself which had its roof removed. As the tornado became cut off from the main supercell, it began to jog more eastward. It produced more damage north of Centreville, including a large barn and additional trees snapped.

tornadoes.name: Union Lake/City, MI
tornadoes.label: Union Lake/City, MI
tornadoes.notes: The most intense and deadly tornado of the cyclic tornadic supercell touched down in northwest Branch county, northwest of Union Lake between Blossom Rd and Mendon Rd. This tornado was well photographed from multiple angles, and it quickly turned into a multi-vortex wedge. After destroying a pole barn and damaging a residence, the tornado deposited a 500 gallon propane tank in a field. Drone footage also showed ground scouring in the same field. The tornado continued northeast and caused the most widespread and intense damage along Prairie Rose Ln. Every residence along this stretch was either heavily damaged or completely destroyed. Tragically, three individuals lost their lives here when their manufactured homes were lofted and tossed. One of these trailers was well anchored and tossed approximately 100 yards, badly twisting the frame. Numerous vehicles were also tossed in this area. The maximum peak intensity of 160 mph was estimated to be at the corner of Tuttle Rd and Prairie Rose Ln. This 2 story block home was completely destroyed. Construction quality and older building codes of all homes in this area contributed to their failure and precluded the survey team from being able to rate higher than an EF-3. The tornado continued off to the northeast into Union City producing EF-1 to EF2 damage along the way before dissipating at the Branch/Calhoun county line. Special thanks to the various subject matter experts on the Quick Response Team that helped NWS Northern Indiana determine this tornado's intensity.

tornadoes.label: Near Tekonsha, MI
tornadoes.notes: EF-0 tornado with peak winds around 85 mph began just west of the intersection of P Drive South and 18 1/2 Mile Road. The damage path ended near N Drive South between 20 Mile Road and 21 1/2 Mile Road. Several trees were uprooted along the path, and some unhealthy trunk snaps. There was minor damage to some structures, including a roof off a chicken coop, and an exposed farm outbuilding with some walls collapsed and metal roof material scattered downfield. The end point had an uprooted tree or two, but also numerous trees that had limbs recently torn off presumably not associated with the tornado, as the only torn limbs were those hanging over the road right-of-way.

tornadoes.label: Near Bristow, OK
tornadoes.notes: The tornado developed approximately 4 miles northwest of Bristow, west of South 401st West Avenue and north of West 221st Street South. Moving northeast, it crossed South 401st West Avenue, where it destroyed a single-wide mobile home and an outbuilding. As the tornado continued northeast across State Highway 16, it uprooted trees and snapped large limbs. At the intersection of State Highway 48 and West 181st Street South, the tornado impacted an industrial site, collapsing overhead doors and removing roof sections from two metal buildings. The tornado maintained a northeast track, breaking additional tree branches along South 337th West Avenue, before dissipating north of State Highway 66.

tornadoes.label: Near Turley, OK
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed near N Gilcrease Museum Road, north of W Newton Street. It moved northeast damaging a number of homes, damaging the roof of an apartment complex, uprooting trees, and snapping numerous large tree limbs in neighborhoods west of N Tisdale Parkway. It crossed into Tulsa County near W Apache Street. The tornado damaged many homes and snapped numerous large tree limbs between the county line and the Gilcrease Expressway. It continued to move northeast damaging many homes north of the Gilcrease Expressway, and intensified as it approached E 36th Street N. An office building was severely damaged and the Tulsa Technology Center was severely damaged as the tornado approached N Peoria Avenue. Numerous trees were snapped and uprooted in that area. The tornado moved north-northeast across E 46th Street N and dissipated north of E 61st Street N. Many homes were damaged, a few trees were uprooted, numerous large tree limbs were snapped, and mobile homes were damaged in that portion of the path. This tornado produced a tornadic debris signature from the KINX WSR-88D.

tornadoes.label: Near Welty, OK
tornadoes.notes: Chaser video and a debris signature from KINX WSR-88D indicated this tornado began west of highway 48 about 6 miles north-northwest of Castle. The tornado crossed highway 48 where it damaged the roof of two mobile homes and downed small branches along E980 road before dissipating.

tornadoes.label: Near Owasso, OK
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed just west of N Yale Avenue and north of E 76th Street N. It uprooted a tree as it crossed N Yale Avenue and moved northeast across a neighborhood on E 82nd Street N. Several homes were damaged, light poles were blown down, and large tree limbs were snapped. The tornado blew down power poles and snapped large tree limbs as it crossed E 86th Street N. Outbuildings were damaged and large tree limbs were snapped by the tornado as it crossed N Hudson Avenue, and then crossed N Sheridan Avenue, where it dissipated.

tornadoes.label: Near Limestone, OK
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed over heavily wooded, inaccessible (by road) terrain, east of N 161st East Avenue, where the KINX WSR-88D detected a tornadic debris signature. The tornado moved east-northeast across the Caney River, and then destroyed a home and damaged several others south of the river. A large recreational vehicle was rolled and severely damaged. Numerous trees were snapped and outbuildings were damaged. The tornado then moved through another area of inaccessible terrain and crossed the Caney River again, and then crossed the S 4090 Road. Large tree limbs and power poles were snapped as it crossed the E 430 Road, and the tornado dissipated north of the E 430 Road.

tornadoes.label: Near Beggs, OK
tornadoes.notes: The tornado began on the west side of Beggs, directly impacting the Beggs Public Schools campus. The High School and Middle School roof sustained significant damage, and the bus barn was also suffered heavy damage to the roof and overhead doors. As it moved northeast, it crossed 15th Street, uprooting and snapping trees. After crossing Happy Camp Road, it destroyed outbuildings and began a brief jog northward, paralleling North 180 Rd. This strongest and widest phase of the tornado occurred as it moved east along Grimes Road. One single-wide manufactured home was completely destroyed and several other single-family residences were heavily damaged with the loss of roofs and windows. Two fatalities and two injuries occurred at one homestead where a double-wide manufactured home was completely destroyed and several automobiles were moved and tossed 20–30 yards. A nearby barn was destroyed and heavy limb loss occurred on large trees. The tornado then continued northeast crossing State Highway 75, where it threw a metal shipping container across the lanes and uprooted trees. The tornado dissipated after crossing North 205 Road about three miles south of the Tulsa County line.

tornadoes.label: Near Broken Arrow, OK
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed just south of the Muskogee Turnpike, east of S 225th East Avenue. It moved northeast across a neighborhood west of S 241st East Avenue, and then into the southern portion of Forest Ridge. The tornado uprooted a few trees, damaged the roofs of several homes, snapped large tree limbs, and blew down large sections of privacy fences.

tornadoes.label: Near Coweta, OK
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed over open country north of E 91st Street S and west of S 257th East Avenue. It moved northeast across a neighborhood west of S 257th East Avenue, where the roofs of numerous homes were damaged and windows were broken. The tornado damaged the roofs of more homes east of S 257th East Avenue, along E 85th Street S, E 86th Street S, and Joy Avenue. Several outbuildings were also damaged in this area, several trees were snapped or uprooted, and numerous large tree limbs were snapped. The tornado dissipated just west of S 273rd East Avenue. Based on KINX WSR-88D radar data, this tornado rotated anticyclonically.

tornadoes.label: Near Inola, OK
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed over the southern portion of Inola, and moved northeast across the east side of town. One home had a portion of the roof blown off, and a number of other homes received minor damage. Many large limbs were snapped from trees. The tornado then moved northeast across the E 595 Road, where the roof of a home was damaged and trees were blown down. It uprooted trees as it moved across the E 590 Road, crossed Highway 412, and blew a portion of the roof from a home on the E 580 Road. The tornado moved into Mayes County near the E 580 Road, where large tree limbs were snapped and several power poles were blown down. It moved across open country until it dissipated near the W 570 Road and S 427 Road. The tornado produced a tornadic debris signature from the KINX WSR-88D.

tornadoes.name: Shawnee_Mar6
tornadoes.label: Shawnee_Mar6
tornadoes.notes: Shortly after 1130 PM CST on Friday 3/6/2026, an EF-0 tornado developed within a line of severe thunderstorms in northern Johnson County Kansas. The tornado started in northern Shawnee, KS moving east into portions of Merriam, KS and along and near the I-35 Corridor into Southern Wyandotte County Kansas before crossing the State Line into Kansas City, Missouri shortly after 11:40 PM CDT. The tornado ended shortly before Westport near Southwest Traficway around 11:45 PM CDT. The majority of damage was to trees with peak wind speed estimated around 75 MPH.

tornadoes.name: Prospect, TX
tornadoes.label: Prospect, TX
tornadoes.notes: Around 3:09am on March 7, 2026 a severe thunderstorm produced a tornado near the community of Prospect, Texas. The tornado initially touched down just west of HWY 59 where multiple snapped trunks of hardwood trees were noted. As the tornado quickly continued east, it heavily damaged several structures. A residential home west of the highway was damaged by a fallen tree. Next to the home, a barn was completely destroyed, with only the wooden frame remaining. Debris from the barn along with the barn’s contents were strewn across the front yard and into the highway median and onto the northbound side of the highway. Just to the east of HWY 59, another residential home experienced significant damage after being moved feet away from its foundation. Several large hardwood trees were also uprooted and fell on top of a nearby shed. Just north of this home, another home experienced tornado damage. In the backyard of this home, a small shed was completely destroyed, with contents strewn across the yard, along with damage to vehicles. In this yard, a camper was tossed and rolled into another nearby shed, where several occupants were thrown about and injured. The tornado continued east/northeast, snapping and uprooting numerous trees before moving into additional residential areas on East Prospect Rd. Here, damage to several roofs were noted, and additional sheds and barns experienced significant damage, along with major hardwood tree snaps and downed powerlines. Thereafter, the tornado weakened as it moved northeast away from East Prospect Rd and crossed Scotts Bayou. Some tree damage was then found along Hall Road before the tornado then lifted as it moved as East CC Rd and toward the town of Lodi around 3:14am.

tornadoes.name: Willisville, AR
tornadoes.label: Willisville, AR
tornadoes.notes: During the morning hours on Saturday, March 7, 2026 a severe thunderstorm produced a tornado with peak winds of 125 mph just west of Willisville, Arkansas. This same storm had a history of producing tornadoes across eastern Texas. The first sign of damage from the tornado was seen just south of the intersection of Highway 32 and County Road 9 near a large open field. The tornado brought down multiple large trees before heading northwest through the large open field. On the far northeast corner of the field is where tree damage picked up again, before tracking across Highway 32 just to the west of County Road 17. The more significant damage was found near County Road 122, County Road 17, and County Road 1702 where numerous structures sustained damage. A single wide residence was lifted off the rooted foundation and tossed around 100 feet before landing and being completely destroyed. There was one occupant in the residence who thankfully walked away from the incident with minor injuries. It was at this location that the tornado was rated an EF-2 with max winds of 125 mph. The tornado then went through another grove of trees before crossing County Road 17 just north of County Road 1702 where it destroyed a small garage/storage unit. Damage from this unit was scattered all throughout an open field all the way to County Road 124. It also brought down a number of very large trees as it crossed the road. As the tornado crossed over County Road 124, it appears to have started to lift, as damage was more sporadic in an wide open field. The adjacent tree line at the end of the field along the path of the tornado had a few trees down, but there was no evidence that the tornado remained on the ground from this point. A special thanks goes out to to the Nevada County Office of Emergency Management for helping us locate the damage and to Josh Klober who helped us gain additional points from locations unreachable.

tornadoes.name: Symsonia
tornadoes.label: Symsonia
tornadoes.notes: A very narrow tornado/gustnado on the leading edge of a gust front embdded in a broader circulation produced amage along Elva Loop Road northeast of Symsonia. A couple of metal outbuildings sustained roof and other structural damage. Debris was carried semi-convergently downstream. A doorbell camera captured a vortex with dirt/mud being lofted passing through the area.

tornadoes.name: Jones Sparkman Rd
tornadoes.label: Jones Sparkman Rd
tornadoes.notes: A very brief tornado began producing minor limb and tree damage before crossing Jones Sparkman Rd west of Murray where it significantly damaged a fairly wide swath of vinyl fence. Wooden stakes holding the fence were pulled from the ground and a gate was thrown upstream from the storm path. A tree was uprooted convergently into the storm path near the fence location. A large goat shed was tossed just downstream of the fence location. The tornado path appeared to end about 8/10ths of a mile from its origin where it removed shingles from a home. A small/brief TDS was apparent on radar at the time of the event.

tornadoes.name: Groundhog Road Tornado
tornadoes.label: Groundhog Road Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service surveyed damage in western Jefferson County and determined that an EF-0 tornado occurred, embedded within a larger area of straight-line wind damage. The tornado began south of Lock 17 Rd near Betty Hill Rd, where several softwood trees were uprooted, knocking down power lines. An area of weak rotation was noted on radar associated with this damage and the feature continued to the section of Groundhog Rd in the area of Woods Creek. Here, extensive softwood tree damage was observed, with numerous trees uprooted and smaller trees snapped. Much of the treefall was found to be laying easterly to east-northeasterly, with overall storm motion to the southeast. Minor softwood tree damage associated with the same radar feature was observed along Mud Creek Rd north of the Groundhog Rd intersection, with a couple uprooted trees and several limbs down.

In addition, sporadic wind damage as a result of a surge of straight-line winds was observed elsewhere along Lock 17 Rd and Groundhog Rd from near the Providence community to just south of the Groundhog Rd and Mud Creek Rd intersection in the Mud Creek community. The most extensive area of non-tornadic damage was observed to be along Mud Creek Rd south of Groundhog Rd, where several trees were uprooted, minor roof damage occurred to two homes and a small outbuilding, and power poles were broken with lines in the road, causing a portion of the roadway to be closed much of the day following the storm. Very minor, sporadic tree damage was observed in the Adger and North Johns areas, mainly limbs down.

tornadoes.name: Pontiac
tornadoes.label: Pontiac
tornadoes.notes: Based on video evidence, a brief tornado occurred just north of Pontiac. Surveillance video shared by a property owner showed a clear circulation with multiple sub-vortices on a quarry lake just west of 1600 East Road, north of old US-66. The tornado was observed in storm chaser videos crossing old US-66 just south of North Creek. Damage along the path of the tornado included the removal of a roof to a boat house and damage to a dock, garage, and fence. The maximum width of the tornado was estimated from the aforementioned surveillance and storm chaser videos.

tornadoes.name: Kankakee - Roselawn
tornadoes.label: Kankakee - Roselawn
tornadoes.notes:
This tornado began just north of W 3000S Road southwest of Kankakee, IL, about one mile east of State Route 115. The tornado intensified while traveling east-northeastward into the far southern section of the city of Kankakee in the vicinity of Route 45, where concentrated higher end EF-1 tree damage and structural damage was observed. The tornado intensified further while moving across E 2500S Road, destroying a two-story home and several metal farm buildings, consistent with EF-3 caliber wind speeds. Concentrated extreme tree damage was noted, with numerous large hardwood trees snapped, stubbed, or uprooted despite lacking leaves, likely due to extensive debris lofting in the area.

After crossing I-57 and the Kankakee River, the tornado rapidly increased in size, producing a swath of significant damage in and near northern portions of Aroma Park. In this area, multiple homes were heavily damaged to an estimated EF-2 intensity, and one fatality also occurred. The tornado’s peak width occurred here and was estimated to be approximately 1550 yards. Ground survey and aerial imagery suggests that the tornado further intensified as it tracked east-southeast before crossing the Kankakee River again. Within a narrow 150-200 yard wide section along S. Sandbar Road to the northeast of Aroma Park, three homes were completely destroyed, consistent with EF-3 caliber winds, and multiple others were heavily damaged and rendered uninhabitable. A heavy pickup truck parked in front of the garage of one of the destroyed homes was moved over 100 feet into a ditch next to the driveway, possibly being spun around the remnants of a small tree before reaching the ditch. In addition, on the other side of Sandbar Road, a crossover type SUV appeared to have been rolled onto the adjacent property and deposited onto a pile of debris just north of a heavily damaged residence. Along the swath of the most intense structural damage, concentrated extreme tree damage was noted, with numerous large hardwood trees snapped, stubbed, or uprooted despite lacking leaves, likely owing to extensive flying debris. Along Sandbar Road and through the Kankakee Elks Golf Course, the tornado’s width was estimated at near 1500 yards. The tornado then continued generally east to east-northeast towards the Indiana state line, downing numerous additional trees, causing occasional structural damage, and flipping irrigation pivots as it moved just north of the communities of Wichert and Hopkins Park.

While crossing into Newton County between W 800 N Road and W 900 N Road near N 650 W Road, the tornado destroyed multiple outbuildings and significantly damaged multiple homes. On N 600 W Road, multiple homes were completely destroyed with debris blown clear of their foundations, consistent with EF-3 caliber winds. Two fatalities occurred at one of these homes. Nearby forested areas had almost all trees snapped or uprooted with some trees remaining standing with only stubs of a few large branches remaining, likely due to extensive lifted debris. Multiple homes were damaged, and a farm outbuilding was destroyed along N 500 W Road and along and near N 400 W Road.

As the tornado crossed US-41 into the south side of Lake Village, it widened to approximately 1100 yards while damaging the roof and canopy of a gas station and a nearby retail building. Further north along N 300 W Road, multiple blocks of homes had significant roof damage and almost all trees were uprooted or snapped. The tornado continued eastward into a wooded area near the Lugene Links Golf Course, where a continuous corridor of trees was entirely uprooted. As the tornado neared W 950 N Road and N 150 W Road, a few homes were damaged, and a farm outbuilding was completely destroyed. The tornado continued to produce damage to trees and outbuildings as it traveled northeastward through mainly rural portions of northern Newton County and northern portions of Roselawn.

The tornado crossed into far northwestern Jasper County between W 1100 N Road and W 1200 N Road. Along N 1200 W Road just east of I-65, a continuous corridor of trees was entirely uprooted, a few outbuildings were damaged, and the roof was removed from a house. In the community of Forest City, a continuous corridor of trees was uprooted, and a few residences had shingles removed. The tornado diminished in intensity as it moved northeast toward N 1100 W Road, and then dissipated just south of the intersection of N 1100 W Road and W 1300 N Road.

tornadoes.name: Sun River Terrace 1
tornadoes.label: Sun River Terrace 1
tornadoes.notes: High-resolution satellite imagery, storm chaser video, and radar data all depicted a generally southward-moving satellite tornado. Storm chaser video looking southeast from IL-17 captured the development of the tornado, which initially moved southwestward for about 30 seconds before becoming obscured by rain. Clear swirl marks (including several loops) were evident in a field north of S. Sandbar Road in Gray Sky satellite imagery near the start of the tornado. As the tornado continued southward, it uprooted a grove of trees in the vicinity of S. Sandbar Road, consistent with wind speeds near 90 mph. Sporadic tree damage was noted in high-resolution satellite imagery south of the Kankakee River, just to the east of a subdivision on Bittersweet Drive, before the tornado dissipated.

tornadoes.name: West Jersey Tornado
tornadoes.label: West Jersey Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado developed about 4 miles west of West Jersey where it toppled a shipping container and caused tree damage. It intensified as it reached 100 E Rd and snapped more trees, damaged homes and outbuildings and tossed the debris to the east. The tornado dissipated shortly after it crossed State Route 78 where it damaged a home roof, broke windows and caused extensive siding damage.

tornadoes.name: Toulon-Wyoming Tornado
tornadoes.label: Toulon-Wyoming Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Spotters reported a tornado touchdown north of Toulon and again north of Wyoming. NWS damage survey crews located tree damage north of Wyoming that correlated with that track.

tornadoes.name: Wheatfield
tornadoes.label: Wheatfield
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began in Jasper County about 2 miles south of Stoutsburg along CR W 1000 N, where there was damage noted to a solar panel field and power poles. The tornado moved east-northeast, causing damage to a farmstead on CR N 200 W. The most significant damage from this tornado was noted just south of Wheatfield on the 0-100 block of CR W 1100 N and on the 1100 block of State Route 49, where numerous homes sustained considerable damage and numerous trees and power poles were downed. The tornado continued to damage solar panel fields, trees, power poles, and farmsteads as it moved toward the Starke County line, passing through the unincorporated community of Tefft. The tornado dissipated before reaching Starke County on the 500 block of CR E 1350 N.

tornadoes.name: Lacon-Varna Tornado
tornadoes.label: Lacon-Varna Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Video evidence from an Illinois River barge operator confirmed the starting point of a tornado 3.5 miles NW of Lacon. The tornado crossed the IL river and continued eastward where it damaged numerous trees north of Lake Wildwood. Photo evidence from a spotter showed the tornado still occurring 2 miles south of Magnolia before it dissipated just east of Highway 89.

tornadoes.name: Starke, IN Tornado #1
tornadoes.label: Starke, IN Tornado #1
tornadoes.notes: Based on radar, an NWS Survey and reports from numerous spotter and emergency management officials, one final tornado has been confirmed with a cyclic supercell that originated in eastern Illinois. The tornado quickly developed about 3 miles northeast of the end of the Wheatfield, IN tornado, starting southwest of the intersection of US 421 and CR W 400 S where 2 large pole barns suffered extensive damage, as well as 3 empty grain bins. The debris was carried up to a half mile downstream. Videos and eyewitness reports indicate a large cone shaped funnel continued northeast causing damage to trees, some center pivot irrigation systems and a few other barns and homes, eventually crossing State Road 39 near CR W 150 S. It then continued over mainly over unplanted fields before causing some additional damage at SR 8 and CR N 250 E. It lifted just southeast of the Starke county airport. The tornado has a few areas which suggested some multi vortex funnels caused damage in the larger swath. After careful analysis, along with storm chaser video footage and high resolution satellite data, it was determined that a second weaker tornado touched down south of Jackson for a brief period of time. The max estimated width has also been revised to 1200 yards.

tornadoes.name: Starke, IN Tornado #2
tornadoes.label: Starke, IN Tornado #2
tornadoes.notes: Video obtained from storm chasers claiming to be on the south-southeast side of the parent mesocyclone clearly show two distinct tornadoes occurring at the same time. One larger storm, with a smaller 2nd circulation off to the southwest. Based on the unusual damage path that the NWS damage assessment uncovered, this aligns with the idea that a small, short-lived circulation formed on the southern periphery of the large wedge tornado, producing brief EF-0 damage before dissipating.

tornadoes.name: SW Donnellson
tornadoes.label: SW Donnellson
tornadoes.notes: An EF1 tornado with peak winds of 95 to 100 mph begun its 1.5 mile long path by downing some tree branches. The tornado increased in strength causing damage to the door of a farm outbuilding along with damage to additional farm out buildings. The tornado continued east along 230th street, causing sporadic tree damage for around 1 mile. The tornado then strengthened even more near 230th street and 160th avenue, where it destroyed two farm outbuildings and snapped numerous tree trunks. This is where the tornado was the strongest. Shortly after crossing 160th street, the tornado weakened and eventually dissipated.

tornadoes.name: Wilson Lake Park
tornadoes.label: Wilson Lake Park
tornadoes.notes: An EF1 tornado with max winds near 90 mph begun its 2.1 mile long path with damage to tree branches. The tornado then caused damage to some fascia on a house. It then crossed into Wilson Lake park where additional trees were downed. Some trees were uprooted with a couple of trees had their trunks snapped. Tree damage became more sporadic as the tornado continued east leading to minor tree damage through the remainder of its path.

tornadoes.name: Wever Area Tornado
tornadoes.label: Wever Area Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Large section of shingles tore off a roof and the soffit blew in on multiple sides of a house. About 10-15 snapped trees, with most snapped halfway up. There were also 5-8 trees that were uprooted. In addition, a power pole was snapped. Damage largely confined to along and just west of 330th Avenue.

tornadoes.name: Havana-Topeka Tornado
tornadoes.label: Havana-Topeka Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down on the far east edge of Havana near Laurel Hill Cemetery, and moved northeast to near Topeka. A number of tree trunks were snapped along the path, and several power poles were snapped along county road 2130. The worst damage was about a mile west-northwest of Topeka, where a horse barn was partially destroyed, killing one horse.

tornadoes.name: Forest City Tornado
tornadoes.label: Forest City Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A number of irrigation pivots were overturned along the path, and several trees had branches damaged. The tornado moved northeast toward Green Valley where it snapped off 8 power poles before dissipating a short time later.

tornadoes.name: E of Golden, OK
tornadoes.label: E of Golden, OK
tornadoes.notes: Around 12:00am CDT on March 11, a line of severe thunderstorms moved into McCurtain County, Oklahoma. Beginning around 12:30am CDT, the line of thunderstorms began to rotate, one of which quickly produced a tornado that began on Old Golden Highway, resulting in snapped trees and the loss of shingles to a local residence. The tornado then continued east, reaching Thomas Road near the intersection of Old Golden Highway where more trees were snapped and uprooted and a barn/shed experienced damage to the roof. The tornado then began to pick up in intensity as it moved across Oak Hill Road where numerous trees were snapped and uprooted. As the tornado then continued northeast towards Rhoden Road, it caused significant damage to a family residence, resulting in the collapse of most exterior walls and an injury to the occupant who had to be airlifted to the hospital. Trees were then uprooted and fell on this residence, causing additional damage. Next door to this home, significant damage was found to other structures as well as additional tree damage. Right before reaching Rhoden Road, another residence was damaged, where areas of the roof were uplifted, multiple trees were snapped and uprooted, and the neighboring barn experienced significant roof damage. The tornado then moved north/northeast of the road, pushing a small outbuilding off of its foundation and snapping and uprooting more trees. The tornado lifted as it crossed Highway 3, ending around 12:37am CDT.

tornadoes.name: S of Gillham, AR
tornadoes.label: S of Gillham, AR
tornadoes.notes: Shortly after 1am CDT on March 11, 2026, a line of strong thunderstorms moved into Sevier County, Arkansas. The line of thunderstorms produced a brief tornado around 1:12am CDT east of Highway 71. As the tornado touched down east of the highway, it damaged several large barns before then snapping several hardwood trees in a downstream field. The tornado then crossed Kind Rd where multiple trees were snapped and uprooted. As the tornado moved east of Kind Rd, it damaged several more trees before quickly lifting around 1:14am CDT.

tornadoes.label: Near Grafton, IL
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado was confirmed both with radar data and detailed photographs of damage. This tornado cause significant roof damage to a local restaurant, along with other miscallaneous to a local hotel and residence.

tornadoes.label: Near Moro, IL
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado moved through the communities of Moro and Midway, IL early in the morning of March 11, 2026. This tornado produced wind damage indicative of maximum wind speeds of approximately 110 miles per hour. Damage to trees, homes, and grain bins was observed. One injury was also reported.

tornadoes.label: Near Williamson, IL
tornadoes.timing_issue: start and end time are identical

tornadoes.name: Yale Tornado
tornadoes.label: Yale Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A tornado touched down about 2 miles northwest of Yale where it did some tree damage, then progressed to the northeast where it destroyed a barn near the intersection of 2100E and 2000N. The tornado dissipated shortly after.

tornadoes.name: Vera Cruz, IN
tornadoes.label: Vera Cruz, IN
tornadoes.notes: A weak circulation touched down in an open field southwest of the intersection of CR S 600 E and E 350 S.
