Mud splatter occurred to the front of the home at this location, and a wood plank was thrown backward into the roof above the living room. Several wood pieces were impaled into the ground at the property.

The tornado continued north northeast, causing damage in a forested area that opened up into Horn Cemetery. It then caused structural damage along Constantine Rd. Downstream wooded areas showed evidence that the occluding tornado still caused damage before lifting southwest of Slaughter Rd. At that point the rear flank downdraft surged ahead and caused damage along a swath just east of this track.

tornadoes.name: HardinMeadeTor
tornadoes.label: HardinMeadeTor
tornadoes.notes:
Per high resolution satellite imagery of damage in a heavily forested area, a new tornado track began just near the intersection of Hardinsburg Rd and Fields Rd. This track briefly crossed Saint John Rd, but missed any structures there before entering another forested area. The first structural damage along this path was along Tyson Ln near Brizendine Ln where a barn hit the threshold of visible damage. Another open air barn along Brizendine Ln had its roof thrown into a wooded area west of the barn. A little farther downstream towards New Salem Church Rd there was additional structural damage.

This tornado crossed into Meade County near Rineyville Rd. A bigger tree fell onto a house in the Country Ct area. The tornado took a leftward turn, heading north mimicking a turn in the tight mesovortex seen on radar imagery. It caused damage at the Meade County Bank near the intersection of Flaherty Rd and Joe Prather Hwy. Damage was observed to trees and some houses along Camelot Drive and Rabbit Run Road. The tornado continued across fields and did extensive damage to a farm beside Fort Avenue. Multiple farm buildings were significantly damaged with roofs lofted across Rabbit Run Rd east of Fort Avenue, where the damage appeared to end.

It should be noted that an advanced spotter on base at Fort Knox reported seeing broad rotation as the storm passed his location, but with no contact with the ground. He sheltered in his basement as the storm passed and heard debris hitting his house. After heading out he saw large limbs in his yard from a tree across the street. Then he observed with a handheld anemometer a 76 mph wind gust behind the first wave, likely with a rear flank downdraft surge. As of this writing, no damage has been noted connecting this third tornado or the downdraft surge in the narrative below with this damage at Fort Knox. We may yet have further updates here.

tornadoes.name: Lexington/Bonnertown EF1
tornadoes.label: Lexington/Bonnertown EF1
tornadoes.notes:
A storm survey team determined that a tornado touched down in an open field west of Earnest Street and south of Highway 4 in Lexington. As it approached Earnest Street, it caused an open outdoor structure propped up on cinder blocks to slide to the north as well as snapped 4x4s and uprooted trees. The tornado tracked northeast toward Lexington City Hall and caused minor roof damage to five structures. Continuing northeast, the tornado uprooted numerous trees along Highway 64 before crossing highway 59. Along the way, multiple trees were snapped, homes had siding damage, several small open structures collapsed, and a garage door was blown in. It continued snapping and uprooting trees as it approached the state line.

The tornado crossed the Tennessee/Alabama state line and moved northeast, continuing for 10 more miles in Tennessee. In Bonnertown, many residences were impacted, with several homes damaged. A few manufactured homes were moved off their piers, and a couple mobile homes were lofted or slid, remaining in tact. Other structural damage included missing awnings, removed shingles, carports thrown, and trees falling onto the structures. Several farm outbuildings were damaged. Numerous trees were snapped or uprooted.

Beyond Bonnertown, the tornado continued east along Appleton Road, downing trees and destroying a chicken farm. As the tornado crossed into Giles County, damage was mostly trees downed or uprooted, and branches snapped. A few structures were impacted in Giles County south to southwest of Minor Hill due to trees falling. A few metal farm outbuildings were also collapsed. The tornado ended quickly south-southeast of Minor Hill.

tornadoes.name: Clinton County Tornado
tornadoes.label: Clinton County Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service conducted a storm survey on Wednesday, March 18th for the storms that occurred early Monday morning, March 16th. A tornado was determined to have occurred in Clinton County with max winds of 100 MPH (EF1).

Storm damage was first observed along Wright Parish Road southwest of Albany near Wolf River Dock Road. A line of cedar trees had extensive damage, with several treetops and branches pointing to the north, east, and opposite of the northeast storm motion to the southwest. Some branches showed signs of being ripped and twisted from the trees as well, which was indicative of rotation from a tornado.

The tornado continued uphill to a nearby residence with several outbuildings. One barn was completely moved from the foundation with roof damage lofted into nearby fields. The damage direction was mainly to the east, pointing toward the tornadic circulation that was moving to the northeast. Another section of barn damage was pointing to the north, indicating the right side of the circulation nearby. A drone flight confirmed this information. A nearby residence had awning damage that was moved to the northeast, with the most notable damage being a couple of wood plank impalements that were driven into the ground facing the opposite direction of the storm motion to the southwest. The max wind speed near this damage along Rice Road and Wolf River Dock Road was 100 mph.

The tornado continued to the northeast and damage to trees and outbuildings occurred along Hay Road, Huntersville Road, and Robert Page Road. Several trees were snapped and a barn was leveled, and the convergent signature of the tree damage to the north and east directions were noted. The tornado continued northeast along Robert Page Road where a residence had roof and siding damage that was lofted to the northeast away from the property. The debris went up to US Highway 127, and no other damage was observable past this point.

The National Weather Service would like to thank Clinton County Emergency Management for their assistance on the storm survey, as well as the helpful homeowners who allowed access to their properties.

tornadoes.name: West King
tornadoes.label: West King
tornadoes.notes: High resolution satellite imagery revealed an EF1 tornado began along Waynesboro Shubuta Road tracking east-southeast for roughly 2 miles. The tornado primarily damaged forest reaching a peak width of 200 yards just east of Waynesboro Shubuta Road. A couple older outbuildings appeared to have been damaged to destroyed via high resolution satellite imagery. The tornado lifted shortly after crossing Yellow Creek Church Drive.

tornadoes.label: Near Stonecrest, GA
tornadoes.notes: An EF0 spun up in southeast Dekalb County within a line of storms moving through the region at 6:10 AM EDT on March 16, 2026. The tornado first touched down near the Snapfinger community in a wooded region west of Tarragon Dr. The tornado uprooted a tree onto a home along Tarragon drive trapping a teenager in the 2nd floor bedroom. As the tornado continued east, leaf debris and limbs were observed until the tornado crossed hwy 155 and hwy 212 where a couple trees were snapped near the intersection of 212 and Framingham Dr. The tornado then crossed into the Valley Oaks neighborhood where numerous trees were uprooted or snapped, including 2 onto homes in the neighborhood along Gracehill Road and Oak Run Dr. Both homeowners were home when the trees crashed in including 1 narrowly missing them while in the bed. The tornado continued east snapping trees along Valley Oaks Road and along Salem road near the intersection of Panola Road. A tree was downed along Miles E Fowler PKwy and roof damage was observed to a home on Salem Springs Pl. A small tree was snapped on Walnut Ct before the tornado lifted as it crossed Salem road near the intersection of Hunters Pace Dr. Damage along the entirety of the path of this tornado was intermittent suggesting that the tornado was consistently regenerating along the path.
tornadoes.timing_issue: duration over 3 hours

tornadoes.label: Near Sunset, GA
tornadoes.notes: Tornado damage was first observed on Hendricks Church road where a few small pine trees were snapped. Damage continued across Hurricane Creek where approximately 20-30 trees were knocked down or uprooted in private farmland. The path continues with some minor outbuilding damage before reaching Ellerbeetown Rd where some additional tree damage was noted. The track continues eastward towards the intersection of McCard Rd and 74 where additional tree damage was observed as well as some minor structural damage to a home. After crossing Womble Creek, the tornado uprooted trees along Thurston School Rd before continuing east where it caused some minor tree and outhouse damage near the intersection of Butts Rd and Pickard Rd. From there, the path ends and the tornado appears to have lifted. This damage was in line with the estimated maximum wind speed of 78 mph and an EF0 rating.

tornadoes.name: 20260316_madison1
tornadoes.label: 20260316_madison1
tornadoes.notes: A brief, weak tornado touched down just south of Mars Hill along Interstate 26. It traveled for about half a mile, snapping several branches and uprooting a few trees before lifting.

tornadoes.name: 20260316_madison2
tornadoes.label: 20260316_madison2
tornadoes.notes: An EF-0 tornado with peak estimated winds around 80 mph touched down several miles east of Mars Hill, uprooting and snapping numerous trees. A path of damage was evident for a little over 2 miles along Paint Fork Road before disappearing into the higher terrain approaching Chestnut Mountain. A few additional trees were downed as part of inflow into the storm.

tornadoes.label: Near Yatesville, GA
tornadoes.notes: A weak velocity couplet was detected on radar northwest of the intersection of Grays Chapel Rd and Grady Pennyman Rd at 7:20 AM. The storm tracked to the east, with a tornado debris signature (TDS) appearing at 7:24 AM over Grays Chapel Rd. Two trees were uprooted along the road, and four trees were snapped at their tops. By 7:26 AM, the velocity couplet had weakened and was located over Israel Creek east of Grays Chapel Rd, although the TDS persisted due to lofted debris.

tornadoes.label: Near Macon-Bibb County, GA
tornadoes.notes: A weak velocity couplet was detected on radar just east of Forsyth Rd /Vineville Ave, north of Payne around 7:58 AM. The storm tracked to the east-northeast and caused damage neighborhoods along Pierce Avenue and in the vicinity of Northwoods Academy between 8:00 AM and 8:03 AM. Uprooted trees and minor damage to siding, carports and gutters suggested a high-end EF-0 tornado with peak wind speeds of 85 mph. Notable damage included several trees on homes and damage to vehicles and an overturned U-Haul truck. Leaf debris and limbs were noted along the tornado track, but at some points damage was limited to snapped tree tops, suggesting the tornado may have briefly lifted several times along the path. The weak velocity couplet was no longer detected on radar once the storm reached the Ocmulgee River just east of I-75 at 8:05 AM, although a tornado debris signature (TDS) remained apparent due to lofted debris.

tornadoes.name: 20260316_charlotte
tornadoes.label: 20260316_charlotte
tornadoes.notes: An EF-0 tornado touched down along N Graham St near the intersection of Moretz Ave where several small trees were snapped. The tornado moved northeast into a residential area where additional large limbs were snapped. The tornado reached peak intensity of 85 mph as it crossed Atando Ave where sheet metal was peeled back off a large industrial building. Another warehouse sustained more significant roof damage with a large section of roofing removed. Several large pine trees were snapped behind the warehouse. The tornado weakened and eventually dissipated as it moved into another residential area along Drury Dr where a few small limbs were downed.

tornadoes.name: New Windsor
tornadoes.label: New Windsor
tornadoes.notes:
...NWS Damage Survey for 03/16/26 New Windsor, MD Tornado...

.New Windsor, MD Tornado...

Rating: EF-0 Estimated Peak Wind: 80 mph Path Length /statute/: 1.68 miles Path Width /maximum/: 150 yards Fatalities: 0 Injuries: 0

Start Date: 03/16/2026 Start Time: 12:02 PM EDT Start Location: 2 SSE Linwood / Carroll County / MD Start Lat/Lon: 39.53609 / -77.12975

End Date: 03/11/2026 End Time: 12:05 PM EDT End Location: 2 ESE Linwood / Carroll County / MD End Lat/Lon: 39.55740 / -77.11459

Survey Summary:

A line embedded supercell developed and tracked over north-central Maryland during the late morning into early afternoon hours on Monday, March 16, 2026. This storm was part of a much larger system that brought multiple rounds of severe weather to much of the eastern United States.

Rotation was evident within the storm around 2000 to 3000 feet above ground on the KLWX WSR-88D radar, prompting a Tornado Warning as the storm moved from Frederick into Carroll County. The FAA TDWR TBWI showed this rotation quickly strengthen and lower to below 2000 feet just to the southeast of the mid-level mesocyclone being sampled by the KLWX WSR-88D. The tightened lower-level rotation persisted on TBWI for 1 to 2 minutes after the mid-level rotation on KLWX had notably weakened.

It was beneath the tightening low-level rotation at around 12:02 PM EDT that the first evidence of tornadic damage was found. Several trees in a weakened state just southeast of the intersection of Hawks Hill Road and Beth Way snapped near the trunk, and fell toward the east, west, and north. The parent storm motion was northeast. The trees that fell were only around 100 feet apart at most, with an undisturbed landscape around it indicating an initially very narrow vortex perhaps no larger than about 25 to 50 yards in width.

The tornado then crossed through open fields, lifting the south end of a long irrigation system and rolling it about 100 feet toward the north just east of Winters Church Road.

After this, the circulation continued northeastward crossing several more fields and groves of trees, as well as Little Pipe Creek. The next visible and accessible damage was noted as the tornado approached and crossed MD-75 Green Valley Road near the intersection with MD-84 Union Bridge Road. Here, a couple dozen trees fell in opposing directions (southeast, northeast, east, northwest, and north). One large tree toppled onto power lines taking down a power pole and briefly trapping a motorist between the downed wires, pole, and downed trees. Several large pine trees at the intersection had their tops sheared off, falling toward the north, northeast, and east. Two trees on a hill just east of Mill Dale Lane fell toward the north-northwest, likely just outside the circulation but in its inflow as it passed across MD-84 Union Bridge Road. Meanwhile, an outbuilding just to the southwest of MD-75 Green Valley Road suffered a near total roof collapse, with the west-northwest facing walls partially collapsed inward. Similar to the trees off Mill Dale Lane, this outbuilding may have been just outside the tornadic circulation, with the damage a result of inflow winds into the vortex as it passed. It is at this point where the tornado reached its largest and strongest, with an estimated path width of 150 yards and peak winds of 80 mph. Despite the extent of the damage, only about one-third of the trees in its path at this point sustained visible damage, with no other visible damage to other outbuildings or the farmhouse at the nearby farm.

A video taken from the Carroll County Emergency Operations Center showed a swiftly rotating lowering, likely the tornado in progress as it approached and crossed the intersection of MD-75 Green Valley Road and MD-84 Union Bridge Road, just northwest of their facility. Although trees in the foreground obstructed the view and could not confirm ground contact, the video was directly coincident with radar and the observed (convergent) damage.

A few trees had their tops snapped off just northeast of MD-84 Union Bridge Road, but no visible damage was noted beyond this point. It is possible, based on the rotation signature on TBWI, that the tornado could have persisted for up to another mile over open fields, but the path length in this survey can only confidently conclude a path up to this point, approximately 1.68 miles in length.

The National Weather Service Baltimore/Washington Weather Forecast Office thanks Carroll County Office of Emergency Management for their assistance. Additionally, thanks to the trained spotters, media, and public that sent in reports of damage.

tornadoes.name: La Fontaine, IN
tornadoes.label: La Fontaine, IN
tornadoes.notes: A weak, very narrow circulation developed along E 1100 S, east of S 600 E and moved quickly towards a home where the southwest portion of the roof was removed and thrown to the northeast. A small building was tipped and rolled towards the north and extensive leftover corn stubble and corn combs were noted in the yard and also carried to the north, landing on the east facing side of the home.

tornadoes.name: Banquo, IN
tornadoes.label: Banquo, IN
tornadoes.notes: A survey of damage indicated a brief tornado was confirmed within a swath of wind damage south of Banquo. The circulation touched down just east of S 100 W35 and N of E 700 N in far southwestern Huntington county. It moved quickly southeast, causing extensive damage to a converted animal barn as well as a grain elevator on the property. Some tree damage was noted and a few projectiles were observed in 2 different roofs. The tornado cause tree damage to a residence as it crossed into Grant county. Additional tree damage was located on E 650 N, east of Indiana 9. Debris from the pole barn was found all the way through the track.

tornadoes.name: GileadTor
tornadoes.label: GileadTor
tornadoes.notes:
The tornado began northeast of Mount Gilead along US 42 near Home Road, causing extensive tree damage including multiple snapped and uprooted trees. The tornado continued southeast crossing Township Road 103, causing sporadic tree damage. The tornado then crossed OH 95 near Township Road 110, destroying a 60ft by 100ft outbuilding. Debris from this outbuilding was thrown 100-200 yards to the south southeast by the tornado before the tornado ended.

Scattered tree and some structural damage associated with straight line winds were found both north and south of the tornado track, consisted with straight line winds up to 75 mph.

tornadoes.name: 032726-Kenton
tornadoes.label: 032726-Kenton
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service has confirmed a tornado near the city of Kenton in Hardin County, Ohio. The peak wind estimates were near 90 mph, resulting in a lower end EF1 classification. Some damage points were caused by winds estimated to be closer to 80 mph or higher end EF0. This tornado occurred during the evening hours on Thursday, Mar 26, 2026.

There was a cluster of storms approaching northern and western Hardin County, in which an outflow boundary began causing power line damage near 8pm. As the cluster of storms continued moving east southeast through the county, wind damage occurred near Alger which was more conducive to straight line winds.

When the final storm of the larger complex of storms pushed toward Kenton, it produced a brief tornado at the Hardin County Fairgrounds just south of County Road 140, with minor roof damage first observed. Several wooden power poles were damaged and even snapped completely in half. One hardwood tree was also completely snapped on the northern side of the fairgrounds. One building experienced a major loss of metal roofing panels and another building had its concrete block siding blown out, causing a partial collapse of the roof. There was also uplift of an open-ended barn structure, in which large support poles were lifted and shifted slightly from the ground. The final damage occurred on the eastern side of the fairgrounds with additional power poles snapped and minor roof damage to additional buildings.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Hardin County Emergency Management Agency for their assistance with this damage survey.

tornadoes.name: KnoxTor
tornadoes.label: KnoxTor
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado began just west of Granny Creek road southwest of Fredricktown. The tornado ripped off part of a metal roof of a barn and carried it southeast, with debris scattered across a field on the east side of the road.

tornadoes.name: Wayne County Tornado
tornadoes.label: Wayne County Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
A brief tornado touched down just west of Honeytown Road in Wooster and moved east across three residential properties before lifting east of Honeytown Road. The tornado caused EF0 damage with estimated maximum wind speeds of 85 mph. Damage along the path included several uprooted and snapped trees, with some large branches impaled into the ground, indicating strong localized winds. A car awning was lifted and pushed across a home, knocking down a TV antenna and causing a chimney to collapse onto the roof. Additional impacts included a blown-down fence, as well as roof damage and damage to an external propane tank at another residence.

No injuries or fatalities were reported with this event.
tornadoes.timing_issue: start and end time are identical

tornadoes.name: Hicksville
tornadoes.label: Hicksville
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado, embedded within a large swath of damaging straight line winds associated with a bookend vortex, touched down southeast of Hicksville, Ohio. The brief tornado caused some minor tree damage in wooded area before destroying a large pole barn on Clemmer Rd. The tornado moved through open fields, before removing much of the roof off a new construction single family home. Surrounding damage throughout southern Defiance County was determined to be from straight line winds of 60-80 mph.

tornadoes.name: Richmond
tornadoes.label: Richmond
tornadoes.notes: This tornado snapped/uprooted trees, bent power poles, and damaged several outbuildings along its path. The roofs on 1 machine shed and 3 hog confinement buildings were destroyed as the tornado moved through.

tornadoes.name: Downey
tornadoes.label: Downey
tornadoes.notes: This tornado lofted a corn crib, snapped trees, bent an auger, and partially destroyed a roof on a farm outbuilding.

tornadoes.name: Preston
tornadoes.label: Preston
tornadoes.notes: An NWS Storm Damage Survey Team confirmed an EF1 tornado with peak winds of 105 mph and maximum estimated width of 250 yards. Damage included over ten snapped power poles, over ten outbuildings and sheds destroyed, numerous homes with shingle damage, and many trees with large sections snapped.

tornadoes.name: Galesburg Tornado
tornadoes.label: Galesburg Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down about 4 miles southwest of Galesburg where it damaged a few trees before heading northeast toward Galesburg. The tornado did primarily tree damage as it crossed Galesburg and went into East Galesburg. The tornado dissipated just east of East Galesburg.

tornadoes.name: Savanna
tornadoes.label: Savanna
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado developed northeast of Savanna with maximum winds near 90 mph. The tornado caused tree damage in a convergent path and also tossed and damaged a small shed.

tornadoes.name: Sterling
tornadoes.label: Sterling
tornadoes.notes: A tornado passed through northern portions of Sterling, with estimated maximum wind speeds around 90 mph. Along the path, damage was done to trees (including snapped) and two garages in the path saw complete loss of their roofs. Minor damage was noted to two church roofs. There was also a 3000 lb rooftop HVAC unit rolled over, consistent with maximum winds of at least 90 mph.

tornadoes.name: Palmyra-Woosung
tornadoes.label: Palmyra-Woosung
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado began in far eastern Whiteside County just north of Fulfs Road and just west of the Whiteside-Lee county line, where satellite imagery showed the beginning of a narrow southwest-northeast path of disturbed soil through farm fields. Drone footage taken along Mound Hill Road in Lee County revealed swirl marks in the field to the west that aligned with the path that was evident in the satellite imagery, confirming that the tornado remained on the ground continuously as it tracked into Lee County. The tornado crossed Mound Hill Road, downing a number of power poles and impacting a property on the east side of the road. The tornado reached its peak intensity here, destroying multiple outbuildings and snapping several trees at this property. The tornado left additional swirl marks in a field to the northeast of the property before causing damage to trees, a residence, and a metal outbuilding along and just south of Lenox Road. As the tornado reached Timber Creek Road, it caused damage to a barn, at least one power pole, and several trees. On the north side of the road, the tornado pushed an old barn off of its foundation into a grain leg, causing the grain leg to collapse. A concrete silo was also toppled at the same location. The tornado then continued northeastward, causing tree and roof damage at a property along Peek Home Road, then damaging an outbuilding, a house, and more trees at a property at Penrose Road and Swarts Road. The tornado produced its last instance of damage at the Hey Tree Service facility along U.S. Route 52/State Route 26 southeast of Woosung before dissipating prior to reaching the Ogle County line. Straight-line wind damage was also observed to the south and east of the tornado's track.

tornadoes.name: Yates City Tornado
tornadoes.label: Yates City Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado developed near Douglas or about 3.5 miles west of Yates City along State Rt 8, where it damaged an outbuilding. It progressed to the northeast causing some damage to an outbuilding and numerous large trees along Knox Hwy 18 just south of 750 N. The tornado also damaged a couple of homes roofing and siding in that area before moving northeast across Knox Rd 2300 E where it did more tree damage before dissipating.

tornadoes.name: Laura Tornado
tornadoes.label: Laura Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down about 2 miles southeast of Williamsfield just west of the Knox County line, where it destroyed an outbuilding. It crossed into Peoria County and strengthened to 110 mph winds as it snapped off 7 large power poles along State Route 78 near the intersection with Hwy 150. The tornado progressed eastward producing tree damage near N Brimfield Rd and N Maher Rd before dissipating.

tornadoes.name: Elba Center Tornado
tornadoes.label: Elba Center Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down about 2 miles east of Elba Center where it did some tree damage just south of Knox Road 900 N. It progressed across I-74 near E Knox Rd where it damaged an outbuilding and some trees. It caused additional tree damage along N Elmore Rd and W Swab Run Rd before dissipating near N McClellan Rd. Debris was thrown to the east of there as the tornado dissipated.

tornadoes.name: Pine Creek Township
tornadoes.label: Pine Creek Township
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado with a path length of less than one mile occurred along Ridge Road between Grand Detour and Oregon in southern Ogle County. The tornado caused damage to a few buildings and trees between Penn Corner Road and Henry Road. One house had approximately two-thirds of its roof removed by the tornado. This was the most significant damage that was caused by the tornado, allowing it to be assigned a high-end EF-1 rating.

tornadoes.name: ParkeCoTor
tornadoes.label: ParkeCoTor
tornadoes.notes: A bookend vortex moving near Cecil Harden produced a brief tornado that crossed East Mallard Drive. Drone imagery showed clear signs of convergence within tree damage in a grove of trees between Meadows Lane and Mallard Drive with 30-40 trees either uprooted or snapped along the short path. Structure damage was limited to minor siding damage outside of damage caused by falling trees. Additional damage was found several miles both upstream and downstream of the tornado but was determined to be just localized areas of enhanced straight-line winds.

tornadoes.name: Holcomb
tornadoes.label: Holcomb
tornadoes.notes: An EF-0 tornado began one mile west-southwest of the community of Holcomb near Church Road, where it damaged trees and peeled part of a sheet metal roof off of a barn. The tornado tracked east-northeastward across open fields before impacting Holcomb. In Holcomb, numerous trees were uprooted, snapped, or lost branches and limbs; a church had its roof and windows damaged; a few houses suffered minor roofing and fascia damage; and a barn was destroyed. A grain leg also collapsed, blocking the railroad tracks on the east side of the community. The tornado then continued east-northeastward for a little over one mile longer, impacting a property along State Route 251 between Big Mound Road and Holcomb Road before dissipating. Sporadic straight-line wind damage continued for several miles to the northeast of the tornado's end point.

tornadoes.name: OKC-OCCC
tornadoes.label: OKC-OCCC
tornadoes.notes: A tornado likely began near Portland Avenue and Interstate 44, on the eastern grounds of Will Rogers International Airport. Moving to the southeast, the tornado damaged an exterior wall and windows of a building on the campus of Oklahoma City Community College. Generally sporadic damage occurred at several residences between May Avenue and Pennsylvania Avenue, including damage to roofs, sheds and fences. Several trees and large tree limbs were blown down along the path as well. The tornado likely dissipated just east of Pennsylvania Avenue. The event time is estimated from radar.

tornadoes.name: West of Tinker AFB
tornadoes.label: West of Tinker AFB
tornadoes.notes: This tornado was embedded within a larger area of wind damage and produced areas of tree damage from just southeast of SE 44th St and Bryant Road to along SE 47th Street east of Sooner Road, or just west of Tinker AFB.

tornadoes.name: Dale 1
tornadoes.label: Dale 1
tornadoes.notes: The first of two tornadoes began west of Dale and north of I-40, near S3340 Road. This tornado produced sporadic damage between I-40 and Westech Road, just south of Dale. Damage to trees and a few power lines was noted as the tornado curved to the northeast. A tree was uprooted just south of Garretts Lake Road and US Highway 177 north of Shawnee. The tornado dissipated a short time later. The event time is estimated from radar.

tornadoes.name: Dale 2
tornadoes.label: Dale 2
tornadoes.notes: A few minutes after the Dale tornado dissipated, a separate circulation was noted on radar, which tightened and moved to the south and southeast. This tornado likely began northwest of the Leo Road and Wolverine Road intersection. While moving to the southeast, sporadic EF0 damage to trees was noted on Leo Avenue, north of Garretts Lake Road. EF1 damage was assessed to a gas station awning along Oklahoma State Highway 18 and Westech Road. The event time is estimated from radar.

tornadoes.name: NW of Little
tornadoes.label: NW of Little
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began near the NS 3510 County Road and EW 1140 County Road intersection. The tornado produced tree and power line damage as it moved north and east. EF1 tree damage was noted along EW 1130 Road, just south of Interstate 40, where large tree limbs were broken off. The tornado then crossed Interstate 40 just east of the Seminole Rest Area, before dissipating near E 1120 County Road and S 354 County Road. The event time is estimated from radar.

tornadoes.name: E of Lindale, TX
tornadoes.label: E of Lindale, TX
tornadoes.notes:
A mini-supercell developed and produced a short-lived, small, but intense EF1 east and northeast of Lindale, TX. The tornado began in a field just south of FM 16 W downing some small tree limbs and snapping the trunk of a pecan tree. At this same location, significant roof damage, consisting of shingle and roof decking loss, occurred to a single-family residence, resulting in a rating of EF1. The tornado downed a few more tree limbs before crossing FM 16 W. A couple of homes in the Woodcrest subdivision sustained minor shingle damage. Home security cameras in this subdivision recorded the tornado's passage.

The tornado continued northeast and crossed Legion Hills Road. In this location, a second single-family home sustained significant roof damage corresponding to a rating of EF1. A large oak tree was also uprooted on this property. The tornado continued northeast sporadically downing large tree limbs. A few more tree limbs were downed before the tornado lifted near the intersection of FM 2710 and County Road 4107.

This tornado was initially confirmed via multiple videos posted to social media by members of the public. Many thanks go to the Texas Department of Emergency Management and the Smith County Office of Emergency Management for their assistance locating damage.

tornadoes.name: Defiance
tornadoes.label: Defiance
tornadoes.notes: A NWS damage assessment determined that an EF-1 rain-wrapped tornado was embedded in a line of severe thunderstorms that went through Defiance during the afternoon of April 4th. Beginning on the southwest side of town, the tornado produced some minor shingle/tree damage. At least one home was likely destroyed due to a fallen tree. Sporadic, significant tree damage was observed through Riverside Cemetery. The tornado then nearly paralleled S Clinton St as it moved from southwest to northeast. The most impressive damage was done near Davidson and S. Clinton St where several trunks were snapped, a branch lodged into a roof, and several wooden transmission lines were snapped. The circulation continued into downtown Defiance, uprooting/snapping trees, and producing minor to moderate roof damage to numerous businesses including a large church, bank, and USPS building, among others. Notable tree damage was done at the Old Fort before the tornado crossed the river confluence. Video footage from residence confirms a circulation made it across the river. Widespread additional tree and roof damage was then noted in the neighborhoods just north of the Maumee River and west of Carpenter Rd. Finally, several trunks were snapped or uprooted in the Eagle Rock Golf Course before the circulation appears to have dissipated.

tornadoes.name: Van Buren Twp
tornadoes.label: Van Buren Twp
tornadoes.notes: The tornado started just south of Martz Rd between Rawsonville and Hoeft Rd. It first flipped a hayride trailer and continued northeast toward Hull Rd. EF-1 damage occurred along Hull Rd with the greatest concentration of EF-1 damage along and just south of Hull Rd between Elwell Rd and Bak Rd. This damage included multiple trees uprooted and snapped, telephone poles snapped, and a large barn wall blown out. The tornado continued northeast crossing Sumpter Rd producing EF-0 damage with scattered large tree limbs and power lines downed. The tornado lifted right before reaching Savage Rd.

tornadoes.name: Folsom, LA Tornado
tornadoes.label: Folsom, LA Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The track of a short-lived EF-0 tornado was confirmed via a combination of ground survey, aerial imagery, and the existence of a tornado debris signature on KHDC radar data. The tornado is estimated to have touched down between Charlie Lee Rd and Lee Settlement Rd in rural northwest St. Tammany Parish, west of Folsom, LA. Minor damage to tree tops was visible on aerial imagery which was collocated with a tornado debris signature on KHDC. A tree was partially snapped near the base south of Lee Settlement Rd pointed northwest with additional tree debris noted near the road. The tornado debris signature continued to the northeast beyond Lee Settlement Rd, but no additional tree damage was identified. Therefore, this is where the end point of the tornado is estimated to be.

tornadoes.name: PSN Tornado
tornadoes.label: PSN Tornado
tornadoes.timing_issue: start and end time are identical

tornadoes.name: Cache/Rich County Tornado
tornadoes.label: Cache/Rich County Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado is estimated to have touched down at 2:25PM MT approximately 1 mile south of the Sink Rd./HWY 89 intersection in far northwestern Rich county. The tornado promptly produced EF-1 damage snapping a few softwood trees. The tornado continued tracking north along the terrain into Cache county, increasing in width and producing a notably wider swath of softwood tree damage consistent with an EF-1 rating. The tornado then took a slight turn to the northeast and slightly weakened, producing a few more instances of EF-1 damage to softwood trees before dissipating in far southern Cache county at around 2:27PM. The maximum width of this tornado was 100 yards with a path length of 0.44 miles. Special thanks to the Cache and Rich county emergency managers for the assistance getting to the damage location, and another special thanks to our local spotters for reporting the damage.

tornadoes.name: NW of Gillman, WI
tornadoes.label: NW of Gillman, WI
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down approximately 3 miles northwest of Gilman Wisconsin and traveled northeast through mainly rural area. Minor damage occurred to outbuildings and trees on the broken 3.5 mile path.

tornadoes.name: Truman MN 2
tornadoes.label: Truman MN 2
tornadoes.notes: Ground contact most of the way, but not always, as there were two or three occasions when ground circulation was not evident for one or two minutes. But video showed it to be entirely from the same parent circulation, hence one tornado.

tornadoes.name: West of Elmore MN
tornadoes.label: West of Elmore MN
tornadoes.notes: Tornado track based mostly on chaser video. It struck one farm, taking tin off a shed and blowing in garage doors. Trees were also broken.

tornadoes.name: 20260413_webb
tornadoes.label: 20260413_webb
tornadoes.notes: Path estimated based on first hand account, video, and radar data. Tornado caused damage to several trees and buildings on one property near the start of the track, but mainly travelled through open fields.

tornadoes.name: Freeborn Township MN
tornadoes.label: Freeborn Township MN
tornadoes.notes: Tornado track and timing based on drone and ground survey and multiple chaser videos. Three outbuildings destroyed. Another shed had much of its roof removed. Several dozen trees were broken or snapped. A house had two portions of the roof damaged, along with some missing shingles.

tornadoes.name: Hillsdale
tornadoes.label: Hillsdale
tornadoes.notes: Shortly before 8:20 PM CDT on Monday April 13th, 2026, a supercell thunderstorm, that had previously resulted in an EF-2 tornado in Ottawa, KS, strengthened and developed a second tornado just east of Hillsdale Lake in northern Miami County, Kansas. Initial damage was confined to the campground and park headquarters. The torando strengthend to an EF-1 as it followed W 255th St and crossed Harmony Rd. The Tornado continued east toward the town of Hillsdale, KS. After crossing Hospital Rd, the tornado strengthend to EF-2 with a peak wind estimated to be 115 mph as it impacted a single family home, before doing significant damage to several storage facilities just west of Old KC Rd. The tornado began to weaken as it crossed rural areas, before ending just short of US Hwy 169 north of 255th St.

tornadoes.name: Beaver Dam
tornadoes.label: Beaver Dam
tornadoes.notes: Brief tornado started south of Beaver Dam and went through a garage near Shaw Hill Rd, west of the Shaw Marsh Wildlife Area. Other wind damage was noted on the southern side of the tornado path, attributed to straight line winds.

tornadoes.name: Rockdale
tornadoes.label: Rockdale
tornadoes.notes: Tornado appears to have started west of I-39 along Church Rd where it tracked to the north side before hitting a farmstead along Highway 73. Two metal barn structures were completely destroyed with sheet metal from these buildings found in the trees in the far farm hill. A cement silo was also lifted up and had 3 large chunks of the cap broken off of it. The tornado appears to have gone southeast toward County Road A before ending near Woodside School Rd. Extensive straight line/rear flank downdraft damage occurred about a mile or two to the south of the tornado with one farm shed destroyed along Hwy 73 south of Thronson Rd. Sheet metal from this building appeared to be tumbled into the nearby field to the east.

tornadoes.name: Masonville
tornadoes.label: Masonville
tornadoes.notes: EF1 tornado with peak winds of 100-105 mph began east-southeast of Winthrop and tracked into Delaware County to just east-southeast of Masonville. A barn was completely destroyed at the beginning of its 4.3 mile long path. Additional damage to outbuildings and numerous trees was observed. The tornado also crossed U.S. Highway 20 just south of Masonville. The tornado did roll over a semi trailer.

tornadoes.name: N of Union Center, WI
tornadoes.label: N of Union Center, WI
tornadoes.notes: The tornado begin 2 miles NNE of Hillsboro, continuing northeast for about 7 miles. The worst damage, rated lower EF3 with winds to 140 mph, was to a home on Raese Road NW of Union Center. A large downburst interacted with the tornado downstream of this point as the tornado tracked north and northeast of Union Center with the width of the downburst nearly 1/2 of a mile in spots. After the tornado crossed the Baraboo River, the downburst began undercutting the tornado and eventually caused the circulation to dissipate near Ackerman Road. There was one brief spin-up from the parent mesocyclone about a mile downstream of this point which has been included in the path of the main tornado.

tornadoes.name: Sussex
tornadoes.label: Sussex
tornadoes.notes: Tornado appeared to develop in the Lisbon Oaks subdivision, causing mainly tree damage before intensifying closer to Highway 164. Tornado was at it's most intense near Indian Grass Lane where it caused damage at multiple businesses. The strongest damage was to a insurance car shop port that had a well anchored roof that was completely blown off and found approximately 3-4 blocks to the east near Highway 164. Damage then occurred to a church near Wildwood Way and multiple homes along Conservancy Court. Tornado appeared to end near Waukesha Ave along Linda Dr.

tornadoes.name: Endeavor
tornadoes.label: Endeavor
tornadoes.notes: Tornado started near Grouse Rd east of Briggsville and then tracked to the northeast. The worst damage was to an onion farm south of County Road O. The tornado then crossed I-39 and dissipated near County Rd CX. Storm chaser video and photos confirm the tornado.

tornadoes.name: Dubuque
tornadoes.label: Dubuque
tornadoes.notes: An EF1 tornado began just northwest of the Dubuque Regional Airport. Max winds of 100 to 105 mph was observed. The tornado caused damage to trees, snapping and uprooting trees along its path. A newly constructed home had roof damage on three sides of the roof.

tornadoes.name: Pearl City
tornadoes.label: Pearl City
tornadoes.notes: A tornado formed briefly in the occlusion of an RFD northwest of Pearl City. It heavily damaged and destroyed several farm outbuildings, lifted a large farm wagon into an outbuilding, damaging the roof and side. The tornado also snapped several tree trunks and tree damage. Power poles were also snapped as the tornado crossed Illinois Highway 73 before lifting shortly thereafter. The tornado caused EF-1 damage with maximum estimated winds of 105 mph.

tornadoes.name: East Troy
tornadoes.label: East Troy
tornadoes.notes: Tornado started NW of County Rd ES, west of I-43 south of East Troy where it heavily damaged two barns. Corn stubble was noted to be deposited from the corn field to the west all along a path through a cemetery up to I-43. Some tree damage was noted at the Alpine Valley Golf Course. The tornado then moved along County Road D and caused additional damage to some barns and outbuildings along with trees. Tornado ended somewhere south of County Rd D and northwest of Valley View Rd.

tornadoes.name: Waterford
tornadoes.label: Waterford
tornadoes.notes: Tornado developed NW of Honey Creek Rd and then hit a barn along the road, shifting it off of the foundation. The tornado then continued southeast toward Waterford, removing sheet metal from a shed along Buena Park Rd. The tornado then continued through the north side and downtown Waterford where most of the damage was to trees and houses from the trees falling on them. A few trees were noted to have been lofted and dropped into the Fox River. The tornado then continued through the east side of Waterford before ending near Highway 36.

tornadoes.name: Kansasville
tornadoes.label: Kansasville
tornadoes.notes: Sporadic damage path along Plank Rd with mainly tree damage. Some barn/outbuilding damage to roof sheet metal panels in 2 spots.

tornadoes.name: Somers
tornadoes.label: Somers
tornadoes.notes: Tornado began NW of Somers east of the interstate. It went through the north and east side of the city, through the fire department and near Somers Elementary School.

tornadoes.label: Near Carson, MI
tornadoes.notes: A tornado produced a continuous path of damage from east of Fenwick in Montcalm County to Perrinton in Gratiot County. Trees were snapped and uprooted along the path. Over a dozen barns and outbuildings were heavily damaged or destroyed. About 10 houses had roof damage. Start and end times are based on radar data. The tornado damage was embedded in a larger area of downburst wind damage that was over half a mile wide.

tornadoes.label: Near Oakhurst, OK
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed south of W 81st Street S and just west of S 39th West Avenue. The tornado moved east-northeast damaging the roofs of several homes, some severely, destroying outbuildings, snapping or uprooting numerous trees, and snapping power poles before it crossed into Tulsa County near W 81st Street S. In Tulsa County, the tornado damaged several more homes, uprooted numerous trees, snapped the trunks of some trees, and blew down power lines until it dissipated near Highway 75, north of W 78th Street S. The tornado produced a tornadic debris signature from the KINX WSR-88D.

tornadoes.label: Near Otsego, MI
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began near Schermerhorn Lake in Allegan County and was on the ground for around 6.5 miles. The tornado crossed over the intersection of M-40 and 108th avenue before lifting south of 108th Avenue near 24th street. Mostly tree damage occurred along this path. A couple of homes had minor shingle and siding damage and several homes were impacted by falling tree debris. Pockets of thunderstorm wind damage were found south of the tornado path.

tornadoes.label: Near Hickory Corners, MI
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down on the north side of the Kalamazoo River along 106th avenue north of Otsego. It crossed into Barry County near Silver Lake and Lake Doster traveling East before lifting near Hickory Corners. Widespread tree damage occurred along the tornado path. Several large barns were heavily damaged and multiple homes and businesses lost roofing material or were damaged by fallen trees. Debris from one business landed on US-131 forcing it to be closed for a period of time following the tornado. Pockets of thunderstorm wind damage occurred just south of the tornado path. Both Otsego and Plainwell had significant tree and property damage as a result of thunderstorm winds south of the tornado path. Thunderstorm damage was also found east of Hickory Corners after the tornado dissipated.

tornadoes.label: Near St. Charles, MI
tornadoes.timing_issue: duration over 3 hours

tornadoes.label: Near Muskogee, OK
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed just east of Highway 69, northeast of Summit, where trees were uprooted, homes were damaged, and power poles were snapped. The tornado moved northeast across Highway 64, damaging numerous homes, snapping and uprooting trees, and snapping power poles. It then crossed Highway 351 and turned easterly along Hancock Street before crossing the Arkansas River and dissipating east of Highway 10. A few trees were uprooted and numerous large tree limbs were snapped in the path east of Highway 351.

tornadoes.label: Near Park Hill, OK
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed west of the S 490 Road and south of the W 830 Road. It moved northeast toward Park Hill, crossed Highway 82 and Murrel Road. The tornado uprooted numerous trees, damaged outbuildings, snapped numerous large tree limbs, and blew down power poles. A few trees were uprooted as it moved across Willis Road, then crossed the Illinois River and dissipated after producing more tree damage on the E 785 Road.

tornadoes.label: Near Westville, OK
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed south of Highway 51, southeast of Eldon, where numerous large tree limbs were snapped. It moved northeast into Adair County and across rugged terrain. Trees were uprooted as it moved across the 4630 Roads southwest of Christie, and the roof of a manufactured home was damaged. The tornado uprooted numerous trees and snapped numerous large tree limbs along Highway 62, with more trees uprooted along Cemetery Road and Highway 59, and along the 4750 Road before moving into Washington County, AR. It moved northeast across Highway 59 near Cincinnati, where numerous large tree limbs were snapped. Numerous large tree limbs were also snapped as it crossed Rennic Road and Ham Road before dissipating.

tornadoes.label: Near Piney, OK
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed just west of Piney Road, south of the 782 Road, where trees were uprooted. The tornado moved northeast uprooting trees along Piney Road and the 4765 Road, before crossing into Washington County, AR. The tornado crossed the Baron Fork River, and damaged outbuildings, uprooted trees, and snapped numerous large tree limbs along Salem Springs Road. Trees were uprooted or snapped along Highway 59 and Sugar Hill Road, before the tornado dissipated southwest of Lincoln.

tornadoes.name: Coldwater, MI
tornadoes.label: Coldwater, MI
tornadoes.notes: A survey of damage south of Coldwater Michigan indicates that a circulation may have attempted to touch down on Sanford Rd, north of Fenn Road where a barn suffered damage with debris thrown to the east, impacting portions of a solar farm with some damage to panels. A few tree tops showed some minor damage from Sanford Rd to near Interstate 69 where it appears the circulation touched down at a business on the southeast side of the Interstate, causing damage to a pole barn on the property. It continued southeast causing tree damage until reaching the area of Dubendorf and Quimby Road where a garage lost its roof, trees were blown down and vinyl fencing around a pool was blown down. The tornado then impacted a pole barn on South Wood Rd, throwing the debris well east into the field before lifting. Maximum wind speeds were estimated in the 85 to 90 mph range.

tornadoes.name: Clinton 01
tornadoes.label: Clinton 01
tornadoes.notes: A supercell thunderstorm developed through 5:30 PM Wednesday evening into southwestern Henry County. At 6:03 PM, this storm resulted in a tornado beginning south of Clinton, MO near the Lake. As it continued northeast into the southeast side of the city. The tornado strengthend to EF-1 with a peak wind speed of 98 MPH as it crossed E. Calvird Rd. The tornado weakend to EF0 before ending near E. Clinton St. and S. 8th St. This was the first of two tornadoes associated with this storm.

tornadoes.name: Clinton 02
tornadoes.label: Clinton 02
tornadoes.notes: This is the second tornado that resulted from a supercell thunderstorm that developed in Henry county and impacted Clinton, MO. The NWS Survey team found a gap in damage and security video from Henry County Emergency Management confirmed a second tornado developed from the same parent mesocyclone. This second tornado began near E. Lincoln St around 6:09 PM and continued northeast to N. 6th St, following along the Katy Trail and into the northeast side of the city, crossing Hwy 7 just west of the intersection of hwy 52.

tornadoes.name: Elkhorn
tornadoes.label: Elkhorn
tornadoes.notes: Tornado began west of Quinney Rd and tracked to the southeast, hitting 4 barns as it tracked across farmland west of Elkhorn.

tornadoes.name: S of Oslo, MN
tornadoes.label: S of Oslo, MN
tornadoes.notes: This EF0 tornado began near the Dodge and Mower County line before entering rural Dodge County. The tornado caused minor damage to a grain silo and downed several trees. The track continued northeast and weakened/roped out. This tornado was captured in video from MNDOT cameras south of Rochester. Additional adjustments to the track are likely once high resolution satellite imagery is reviewed.

tornadoes.name: SE of Oslo, MN
tornadoes.label: SE of Oslo, MN
tornadoes.notes: This EF0 tornado affected mainly rural areas southeast of Oslo MN and was on the ground concurrently with another tornado to the west for several minutes. Mainly farm outbuildings and trees sustained light damage along the path of the tornado.

tornadoes.name: Marion, MN
tornadoes.label: Marion, MN
tornadoes.notes: The tornado formed on the northeast of Stewartville and traveled about 10 miles north-northeast, damaging numerous homes and farms. Some of the worst damage was seen near Marion Road, just northeast of Highway 52, where multiple homes were severely damaged with roof removal and partially collapsed exterior walls.

tornadoes.name: NW of Elgin, MN
tornadoes.label: NW of Elgin, MN
tornadoes.notes: The tornado began in a northeast neighborhood of Rochester and traveled northeast into more rural areas. The first portion of the tornado was weak and intermittent with EF0 damage. North of 65th St, the tornado path became more continuous and intensified to produce approximately 100 mph winds with tree and farm outbuilding damage.

tornadoes.name: NW of Saratoga, IA
tornadoes.label: NW of Saratoga, IA
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed northwest of Saratoga and tracked northeast, damaging one outbuilding during its existence. The tornado was witnessed and photographed by multiple individuals. The tornado rolled a truck, with the driver suffering minor injuries.

tornadoes.name: Galena Territory Tornado
tornadoes.label: Galena Territory Tornado
tornadoes.notes: EF1 tornado with max winds speed of 90-95 mph begun just east of the Galena Territories causing damage to the awning of house. The tornado then caused sporadic tree damage along it's 3.7 mile long path. Of interesting note, the tornado mainly caused damage in the valley areas where stretching of the vortex likely increased wind speeds.

tornadoes.name: S of Plainview, MN
tornadoes.label: S of Plainview, MN
tornadoes.notes: The EF2 tornado affected mainly rural areas northeast of Rochester MN beginning about 5 miles east-northeast of Viola in northeast Olmsted county. The tornado tracked northeast damaging trees and outbuildings. One farm house lost a roof and garage roof portions. The tornado ended in Wabasha county a few miles southeast of Plainview MN.

tornadoes.name: E of Cream, WI
tornadoes.label: E of Cream, WI
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed several miles southwest of Cream and reached its peak intensity quickly as it descended a ridge to the west of State Road 88, where low-end EF3 damage was observed to one house. The tornado tracked onward to the northeast and damaged mostly trees and a few residences along the remainder of its path as a high end EF1.

tornadoes.name: Lena Tornado
tornadoes.label: Lena Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A high-end EF2, possible multi-vortex, tornado with estimated peak winds around 130 mph started along Highway 20, southwest of Lena IL, and tracked through Lena before lifting just southwest of Orangeville. The tornado caused significant damage to trees along its path, including uprooting and snapping trees. When the tornado begun it immediately caused EF1 damage to trees, gaining strength to an EF2 tornado snapping many power poles southwest of Lena. The tornado turned to the right, into town causing a lot of roof damage and tree damage. A lot of houses had shingle and siding damage. The most significant damage occurred on Grove Street, where three houses lost their entire roof structure. Two of the homes experienced partial exterior wall collapses. Damage in this area is consistent with 130 MPH winds. In Lena, the damage footprint in Lena is approximately 1250 yards wide. As the tornado moved to the northeast, damage to farm structures was noted. Even towards the end of the path, the tornado was causing EF1 damage to trees.

tornadoes.name: Olivet Tornado
tornadoes.label: Olivet Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Estimated start and end points based off radar and end of debris field

tornadoes.name: N of Blair, WI
tornadoes.label: N of Blair, WI
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed west-northwest of Blair and tracked east, affecting mainly rural areas. The track was a few miles north of Blair with mainly tree damage noted. The tornado path became more intermittent at the end and ceased to the west of the Trempealeau/Jackson county line just north of State Road 95.

tornadoes.name: E of Osseo, WI
tornadoes.label: E of Osseo, WI
tornadoes.notes: The EF1 tornado formed near Interstate 94 where County Road B nearly intersects about 3 miles southeast of Osseo, WI. The tornado affected rural areas causing tree damage, sometimes extensive acreage, before ending near the intersection of Highway 10 and Moe Rd.

tornadoes.name: Glandon Tornado
tornadoes.label: Glandon Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A tornado developed about 3 miles northwest of Glandon, at the end of Pine Haven Road near County Road J, about 4:44 pm in Marathon County. The tornado produced significant damage to a barn by collapsing the entire top floor of half the barn, pushed a silo off its foundation, and damaged a metal outbuilding by tearing off most of the roof and some exterior walls. The tornado moved north-northeast, crossing the Lincoln County line around 4:46 pm. The tornado then crossed County Road X and Highway 64, downing trees and producing significant damage to garages and outbuildings by tearing off most of the roof of a garage. The tornado dissipated 5 miles south of Doering at the end of Elm Ridge Road in Lincoln County around 4:55 pm.

tornadoes.name: Ringle
tornadoes.label: Ringle
tornadoes.notes: A tornado developed about 3 miles west-southwest of Ringle, east of Kronenwetter near Martin and Creek Road, at about 4:46 pm. The tornado moved northeast, crossing highway 29 and downing hundreds of trees. It then moved through neighborhoods along and near River Road from Shady Lane to north of Clubhouse Road. In this area, dozens of homes suffered significant roof damage, with failures of attached garages common. At least three homes in this area had complete removal of their roofs with failure of all external walls and several interior walls, consistent with EF-3 damage. Hundreds more trees were downed in this area, with many snapped near the base. Multiple sheds and outbuildings were destroyed. The tornado continued northeast, closely following the Eau Claire River, and dissipated between Gold Dust Road and County Road Z, 5 miles southwest of Hogarty, at about 5:03 pm. There have been no reported injuries or fatalities.

tornadoes.name: S of Hatfield, WI
tornadoes.label: S of Hatfield, WI
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed southwest of Hatfield along the Black River and churned eastward, causing extensive damage to trees as it roughly paralleled Old Highway 54. Despite the extensive tree damage, damage to buildings along the path was limited. The tornado was embedded within a larger downburst that caused equal, if not greater, damage than the tornado itself. The downburst undercut the tornado after only a few minutes in existence.

tornadoes.name: Harrison
tornadoes.label: Harrison
tornadoes.notes: A high-end EF-1 tornado began near Stephens Road between Harrison Road and Meridian Road southeast of Harrison, initially causing damage to trees and a few sheds and outbuildings. Video footage from storm chasers documented the tornado becoming fully condensed and growing in size and intensity as it tracked east-northeastward across Favor Road and impacted two farmsteads, causing significant damage to a few outbuildings and snapping and uprooting multiple trees. Additional storm chaser footage showed the tornado intensifying again as it tracked northeastward across Gummow Road and then reaching peak intensity as it impacted a property along Freeport Road. At this property, the majority of an older two-story house's roof was removed, several trees were snapped, and an old barn was destroyed. The footage then captured the tornado making a sharp turn to the southeast and crossing Freeport Road once again before roping out and eventually dissipating in open fields near Owen Center Road.

tornadoes.name: North of Washington Tornado
tornadoes.label: North of Washington Tornado
tornadoes.notes: An EF1 tornado with estimated max winds of 100-105 mph begun roughly 3 miles east-northeast of West Chester, IA. Along its 5.3 mile path, it snapped several power poles and tree trunks, along with ripping sheet metal roofs off of farm outbuildings. A semi truck was also tipped over near the intersection of State Highway 1 and 92, which can be associated with a localized wind surge south of the tornado.

tornadoes.name: Belton
tornadoes.label: Belton
tornadoes.notes: UPDATED: An intense line of thunderstorms moving across Miami County Kansas into Cass County Missouri through 5 PM on Friday April 17, 2026 produced an embedded circualation which resulted in an EF 1 Tornado. This tornado began on the south side of Belton, MO around 5:19 PM CDT and continued northeast resulting in structure and tree damage through a neighborhood and across the Belton Cemetery before moving more east-northeast. Past the cemetery, the tornado weakend briefly to an EF 0, before increasing in intensity back to an EF 1 as it entered another neighborhood south of Highway 58 and S. Mullen Rd. Sporadic EF 0 damage was found east of S. Mullen Rd. Toward I-49/US 71, the tornado weakend and sporadic EF 0 damage was found crossing Hwy 58 and through neighborhoods southwest and just east of Johnston Lake. The tornado ended around 5:29 PM CDT. Thank you to Belton Emergency Management and Fire Department for assisting in the Survey.

tornadoes.name: La Prairie
tornadoes.label: La Prairie
tornadoes.notes: Brief tornado that caused damage near Maple Ln southeast of Janesville. Storm chaser video confirmed a brief tornado in this area. Damage further west and east of this point is from rear flank downdraft.

tornadoes.name: Emerald Grove
tornadoes.label: Emerald Grove
tornadoes.notes: Brief tornado went through Emerald Grove, destroying a barn and causing damage to an antique store. Significant tree damage along the path as well with debris lofted well to the ENE from the structures.

tornadoes.name: Richmond
tornadoes.label: Richmond
tornadoes.notes: Multivortex tornado documented southwest of Richmond. Originally thought it may go up toward Richmond, but think that that damage was downburst wind related. Multiple sheds with sheet metal damage along County Highway M before entering Walworth County.

tornadoes.name: Delavan 1
tornadoes.label: Delavan 1
tornadoes.notes: The tornado appeared to start north of School Section Rd and west of Old 89 Rd with mainly tree damage going to the east-northeast. The tornado then tracked along near State Road 11 going east toward Delavan. About 4 farmsteads had damage to them, including one empty silo that was blown down from about halfway up. The tornado then continued east-southeast along Hwy 11 and ended near Redwood Ct on the west side of Delavan where it caused some tree damage.

tornadoes.name: Viola Tornado
tornadoes.label: Viola Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A brief EF0 tornado passed through Viola, IL, with maximum winds around 85 mph. Much of the damage noted along the short path was done to trees, uprooting and snapping some, with tree tops also sheared off others. Some structural damage was noted in town, where half of a house roof was uplifted with insulation scattered along the tornado path. Damage was also done to the north side of a business's brick facade.

tornadoes.name: Delavan 2
tornadoes.label: Delavan 2
tornadoes.notes: Tornado appeared to begin along Turtle Creek west of Klug Rd and south of County Road M. The tornado destroyed an open facing barn shed along Klug Rd. It then tracked to the northeast and caused damage to 3 barns, a garage and a house along County Road P. It then continued to the northeast and crossed Dam Rd before ending near Turtle Creek again.

tornadoes.name: Ponca City
tornadoes.label: Ponca City
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed near Ranch Road just north of U.S. Highway 60 west of Ponca City. It moved east causing sporadic tree and power pole damage across the south side of Ponca City before crossing the Arkansas River into Osage County. Further information about the damage in Osage County will be available from the NWS Office in Tulsa.

tornadoes.name: Denver Tornado
tornadoes.label: Denver Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A high-end EF1 tornado developed southwest of Denver IL and tracked through town. Through the path of the tornado, there were dozens of utility poles damaged. When factoring in the rear flank downdraft (RFD), over 50 poles were broken or bent. Many trees were snapped, some in Denver with high concentration. Some structural damage was also seen, largely to facades, windows, and roofs in Denver.

tornadoes.name: Roscoe
tornadoes.label: Roscoe
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado began near the intersection of Freeport Road and Bates Road southeast of Harrison, initially downing several tree branches at and near a small cemetery. The tornado produced additional tree damage as it tracked eastward along Roscoe Road before entering the west side of Roscoe and reaching its peak intensity as it tracked through the Hawks Point, Crystal Hills, and Oxford Commons subdivisions. There, multiple homes had portions of their roofs torn off or damaged and had sections of siding and fascia peeled off. A few homes also had their garage doors blown in, leading to parts of their garage walls getting blown out. Numerous trees were also uprooted or damaged in these subdivisions. The tornado then continued eastward, knocking down several power poles along Gleasman Road and damaging a nearby farm outbuilding before crossing the Rock River. East of the Rock River, the tornado continued to cause extensive tree damage. Multiple additional houses sustained roof and fascia damage from the tornado as well. The tornado appeared to dissipate just as it reached the Winnebago-Boone county line. Extensive straight-line wind damage was also observed in close proximity to the tornadic circulation, particularly along its southern flank.

tornadoes.label: Near McCord, OK
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed west of Ponca City. It moved east into Osage County and across McCord, where numerous trees were uprooted, power poles were blown down, and homes and businesses were damaged. The tornado continued to move east, roughly paralleling the Arkansas River, and briefly back into Kay County, south of McFadden Cove. It uprooted and snapped numerous trees and damaged homes southeast of McFadden Cove after moving back into Osage County. The tornado moved east-northeast across Kaw Dam Road, Osage Cove Road, and Burbank Landing Road before dissipating over open terrain.

tornadoes.name: Northern Henry County Tornado
tornadoes.label: Northern Henry County Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A short lived EF1 tornado with estimated max winds around 100 impacted a farmstead in far northern Henry County Illinois, with max width around 50 yards. Damage was largely noted to a couple of farm outbuildings and some minor tree damage.

tornadoes.name: Kaw Lake
tornadoes.label: Kaw Lake
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed just northwest of Hideaway Marina just west of the Kaw Lake dam. The tornado moved across the marina causing damage to the boat shelters at the marina.

tornadoes.label: Near Kaw, OK
tornadoes.notes: This tornado crossed into Osage County from Kay County, after damaging boat docks at the marina. In Osage County, a few trees were uprooted south of Kaw Dam Road.

tornadoes.name: Colmar Tornado
tornadoes.label: Colmar Tornado
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado starting in Hancock County tracked east-southeast before turning east through western McDonough County. It tracked just north of Colmar. Along the path was concentrated tree snapping, many at the base, and some uprooted. Structural damage was noted at several outbuildings, including one destroyed. Several power poles were snapped or heavily leaning on the nearby railroad track.

tornadoes.name: Knox-Stark County Tornado
tornadoes.label: Knox-Stark County Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
The tornado began approximately three miles east of Victoria, starting its path in a field just north of Knox Road 2250 N where it initially damaged large tree limbs. Tracking northeastward, it crossed Knox Road 2350 E, causing damage to a few power poles.

Upon crossing into Stark County, the tornado damaged a two-story residential home, resulting in shingle and siding loss. Additionally, a large outbuilding along County Road 100 E sustained substantial damage, including the loss of some metal roof panels. Approximately one half mile further northeast, along County Road 150 E, another two story residence experienced shingle damage to its roof.

The storm continued to produce occasional tree damage after crossing north of County Road 600 N, affecting areas along County Roads 700 N and 750 N.

The tornado then entered Toulon, first causing damage to an outbuilding, a carport, and electrical poles along Turner Avenue. Later, along E Jefferson St, it uprooted multiple large trees and damaged two separate single resident homes with shingle and vinyl siding loss.

Its track concluded in an empty field just east of Toulon, near Downend Rd.

tornadoes.name: Warsaw
tornadoes.label: Warsaw
tornadoes.notes: An NWS survey concluded an EF1 tornado touched down southwest of Warsaw, crossing the lake, and tracking just east of Highway 65. The tornado flipped several mobile homes resting on blocks, damaged signs and roofing associated with stores along Highway 65, and created a pattern of tree damage including many uprooted or snapped, surveyed through in-person and Sentinel-2 satellite surveys.

tornadoes.name: Honey Lake
tornadoes.label: Honey Lake
tornadoes.notes: The tornado began along Spring Prairie Road and moved to the southeast. This tornado had an intermittent path with a few trees uprooted, some shingles peeled from the south side of a roof, another roof peeled back on the southeast corner, and siding damage to a garage. The track continued to the southeast with several limbs snapped from the tops of trees, ending near Old County Highway DD north of Highway 11.

tornadoes.name: Warsaw South
tornadoes.label: Warsaw South
tornadoes.notes: An NWS survey concluded an EF0 tornado caused damage to a building on 83 and Highway MM southeast of Warsaw. This tornado is also reported to have damaged trees in the area which was confirmed via Sentinel-2 satellite data analysis.
tornadoes.timing_issue: start and end time are identical

tornadoes.name: Whitakerville
tornadoes.label: Whitakerville
tornadoes.notes: A combination of NWS ground surveys and reanalysis of satellite data concluded that an EF-1 tornado with estimated maximum winds of 100 mph occurred east of Whitakerville, which was south of other previously identified tornadoes in the Warsaw area. Satellite data revealed that the tornado began within a forested area between Highway 83 and Highway 65, creating a 150-yard wide scar of uprooted trees. Eyewitness accounts then reported rotation crossing Highway 65 where tree damage became more light and intermittent east of Highway MM. The tornado then damaged roofing of an add-on building of the Warsaw High School where video showed lofting and rotation of the roofing material. After producing damage over 1.6 miles in approximately 2 minutes, the tornado then dissipated around Kindle road where it uprooted trees within a narrow corridor.

tornadoes.name: Industry-Bernadotte Tornado
tornadoes.label: Industry-Bernadotte Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado began about 3.5 miles northeast of Industry where it did some tree damage followed by snapping of 7 power poles along N 600th Rd. It progressed east between N 600th Rd and N 500th Rd as it produced tree and significant outbuilding damage. The tornado then turned northeast where it did significant tree damage, producing wind speeds around 115 mph. It then crossed into Fulton County along Waters Rd and did roof damage to a home along with more extensive tree damage, snapping off large trees, and destroying a machine shed. It also destroyed a newer grain bin as it moved to the northeast. As it continued to the northeast it likely merged with a newer tornado that came from the south.

tornadoes.name: NW Waterford
tornadoes.label: NW Waterford
tornadoes.notes: Tornado started in a mainly open field to west of Highway 83. A few branches were downed. Along the intermittent path, multiple trees were downed in different directions. A port-a-potty was displaced and pushed over. The tornado continued to northeast into in accessible field. No damage noted along Marsh Rd.

tornadoes.name: Table Grove-Bryant Tornado
tornadoes.label: Table Grove-Bryant Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down 2 miles east of Table Grove along Rifle Range Rd with a peak intensity of 130 mph when it laid down a swath of tree damage 500 yards wide, snapping off trees up to 2 to 3 feet in diameter just north of Rifle Range Rd. The tornado curved northeast through mostly forested area, where additional tree damage occurred along with some outbuilding damage. The tornado progressed to the east passing north of Bernadotte and Depler Springs before dissipating just north of Bryant. Along its path, the tornado mainly produced tree damage including uprooting and snapping off trunks. A couple of outbuildings lost their roofing material north of Depler Springs.

tornadoes.name: NW Gravois Mills
tornadoes.label: NW Gravois Mills
tornadoes.notes: Debris from a barn and outbuildings thrown mainly east with some north near the beginning of the tornadoes track. Numerous trees were also uprooted and damaged along with many large limbs downed along McCasland Road.

tornadoes.name: North Gravois Mills
tornadoes.label: North Gravois Mills
tornadoes.notes: A combination of ground NWS surveys and Sentinel-2 satellite data concluded an EF1 tornado occurred 2 miles north of Gravois Mills. Several trees were uprooted in a cyclonic pattern and multiple other trees and limbs were damaged along the tornado's path. A window on a home was broken and two outbuildings suffered damage damaged as well.

tornadoes.name: Bath-San Jose Tornado
tornadoes.label: Bath-San Jose Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This long track tornado spanned nearly the entire width of Mason County. It touched down in extreme eastern Schuyler County near Bluff City, crossed the Illinois River west of Bath and ended just across the Logan County line in San Jose. Several trees were snapped, and a metal outbuilding blown down, between Bluff City and the Illinois River. In Bath, a few walls collapsed. Along the path, a number of irrigation pivots were overturned, and trees were snapped. Grain bins were destroyed along Peterville Rd east of state highway 97, along with near the intersection of 1300N and 2600E. Some of the greatest damage was in San Jose, where several huge trees were snapped.

tornadoes.name: Muskego Lake
tornadoes.label: Muskego Lake
tornadoes.notes: The tornado began over a farm field where a few small limbs were downed. The tornado continued to the northeast, snapping a few trees and downing several large limbs. Further to the northeast, the view was not accessible with the tornado ending southwest of Big Muskego Lake, south of the Big Muskego Lake Wildlife area.

tornadoes.name: TMKE South
tornadoes.label: TMKE South
tornadoes.notes: Tornado started near Raynor Ave and tracked to the northeast while crossing 5 Mile and 6 Mile Rd before ending near 7 Mile Rd. Most damage was minor but some sheet metal was lofted from a barn. Tornado tracked just to the east of the Milwaukee Airport Terminal Doppler radar.

tornadoes.name: TMKE North
tornadoes.label: TMKE North
tornadoes.notes: Tornado started near 6 Mile Rd west of Raynor Ave and tracked to the northeast, ending in southern Milwaukee county. Possible that this tornado merged with the other one directly to the south.

tornadoes.label: Near Barnett, MO
tornadoes.notes: An NWS survey team found damage associated with a tornado that tracked north of Barnett, MO. Damage included tree debris blown to the east and north, and metal rods sheltering hay bales bent. These results are preliminary, and an additional extension of the path to the northeast and southwest may be warranted with further analysis.

tornadoes.label: Near Hartsburg, MO
tornadoes.notes: Proposed track by GIS Mutual Aid.

tornadoes.name: Forest City-Manito Tornado
tornadoes.label: Forest City-Manito Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
The tornado's path began approximately one mile north of Forest City ,along County Road 2800 E, where it first caused substantial tree damage. It then tracked northeastward through Union, crossing E Manito Rd and damaging a small outbuilding. Continuing its movement, the tornado entered the south side of Manito, resulting in snapped and uprooted trees and downed power lines.

After crossing north of Hickory Grove road, the storm peeled the roof off a small outbuilding, lofting the debris eastward. The tornado then crossed into Tazewell County, just southeast of Parkland, where more tree damage and a tipped irrigation system were documented.

The tornado proceeded to cross the Mackinaw River and caused extensive tree damage as it moved toward South Pekin, lifting slightly past the interchange of Townline Road and Towerline Road.

tornadoes.name: Mendota
tornadoes.label: Mendota
tornadoes.notes: The tornado appeared to start just south of County Road 2200 N in Bureau County, where a barn structure sustained roofing damage. The tornado then moved northeastward into LaSalle County, producing damage to trees and farm outbuildings. Several wooden power poles were damaged just southeast of Mendota before a semi truck was blown over on I-39 as the tornado continued northeastward. The tornado then passed near Meriden, causing additional damage to trees and farm outbuildings before dissipating in an open field northwest of Earlville.

tornadoes.name: Powerton-Pekin Tornado
tornadoes.label: Powerton-Pekin Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down just southwest of Powerton Lake, and moved along the south side of the lake, before curving northeast.
