North of the prison, it began to track more eastward south of Koch St. before dissipating over Arlan Lake. A number of tree trunks were snapped along the west-east portion of the track, and an industrial building near the railroad tracks sustained some roof damage.

tornadoes.name: Middletown Tornado
tornadoes.label: Middletown Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado formed roughly 2.5 miles northeast of Greenview and continued almost due east along N Middletown Road. It produced tree damage along its path, including some snapped trees. The tornado took a slight turn to the southeast and crossed into Logan County, producing minor tree damage in Middletown before dissipating.

tornadoes.name: Marquette Heights Tornado
tornadoes.label: Marquette Heights Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down along Lincoln Blvd on the southwest side of Marquette Heights where it did tree damage and minor home siding damage. It moved east and crossed through McNaughton Park and eventually dissipated along Cole Hollow Rd. While it was on the ground it caused mainly tree damage.

tornadoes.name: South Pekin Tornado
tornadoes.label: South Pekin Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado tracked east along Red Shale Hill Rd., before turning northeast at Egg Ranch Rd. Most of the damage was toward the end of the track, in a wooded subdivision along Forest Hill Dr. Here, several tree trunks were snapped.

tornadoes.name: Delevan Tornado
tornadoes.label: Delevan Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado touched down about 3 miles south of Delavan and moved northeast. It ripped off part of the roof of a pig barn, blowing it into the field across the street, and blew in the doors to a barn. In another spot it destroyed and large machine building, blowing the debris to the north-northeast into the field. The tornado stayed in the fields as it moved northeast and dissipated before reaching I-155.

tornadoes.label: Near Fulton, MO
tornadoes.notes: Proposed track by GIS Mutual Aid.

tornadoes.name: Boynton Tornado
tornadoes.label: Boynton Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado touched down near Boynton, IL and moved northeast. Along the way it destroyed a machine building on a farm stead and snapped the trunk of an evergreen. Debris from the machine building was blown to the north, northeast, and one 2x4 was driven into the house to the northwest of the machine building. The tornado continued northeast and snapped more trees, ripped off part of the roof of a pig barn. The tornado dissipated after being on the ground for only 4 minutes.

tornadoes.name: Morton-Deer Creek Tornado
tornadoes.label: Morton-Deer Creek Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down on the northwest side of Morton just north of the interchange of I-155 and I-74, where it damaged the roofs of a few warehouse buildings. As it reached the intersection of W Jackson St and Detroit Ave it snapped off a power pole and did some damage to business roofs. It progressed east across Morton just south of I-74 producing some minor tree damage along the way before dissipating southeast of Deer Creek. Photo evidence confirmed it was on the ground just southwest of Deer Creek.

tornadoes.name: 2 SW Washburn Tornado
tornadoes.label: 2 SW Washburn Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down about 2 miles southwest of Washburn in a field just north of County Road 2100. The tornado destroyed a well built Morton Outbuilding, snapping the 6x6 wood support beams. The building was tossed to the east into a nearby building, and then for about a 1/2 mile to the northeast into the field. The next building also sustained significant roof damage. The tornado is estimated to have dissipated about one-quarter mile to the northeast of the farm stead in an empty field.

tornadoes.name: Mackinaw Tornado
tornadoes.label: Mackinaw Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down near Lake Windermere where it caused tree damage and some minor siding damage at various locations around the Lake. It progressed to Mackinaw and Heritage Lake where it produced more tree damage. It eventually moved into northwestern McLean County where it snapped of 3 large power poles along N 150 East Road. It dissipated shortly after that.

tornadoes.name: Stanford Tornado
tornadoes.label: Stanford Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado touched down 3 miles south of Minier and moved northeast destroying a farm outbuildings and blowing to west east into the field. It damaged a farm building and then moved northeast and entered the far west side of Stanford. In the northwest side of town it did lots of tree damage and then moved northeast toward Bloomington, IL. The tornado damaged more trees and then dissipated 2 miles west of I-55/I-74 on Rte 9.

tornadoes.name: SE Tazewell County Tornado
tornadoes.label: SE Tazewell County Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado briefly touched down and did minor tree damage and blew a portion of the roof of a machine building. It was on the ground for 1 mile.

tornadoes.name: Lilly Tornado
tornadoes.label: Lilly Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down along Runyon Rd about a half mile west of the Tazewell-McLean County line. It cause extensive damage to that area, snapping off 7 large power poles and causing damage to several outbuildings. One large grain bin was tossed several hundred yards to the east. The tornado progressed into McLean County where it caused primarily tree damage before dissipating just north of Woodruff.

tornadoes.name: Downs-Ellsworth Tornado
tornadoes.label: Downs-Ellsworth Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down about 2.5 miles southeast of Funks Grove where it produced some tree damage along E 400 North Rd. It progressed northeast crossing Hwy 51 just south of Randolph, causing damage to numerous trees along the way. As it headed toward Downs, it caused EF-1 damage to a home several large trees, with estimated wind speeds of 100 mph. As the tornado moved northeast toward Ellsworth, it caused more tree damage and some home damage, with wind speeds up to 100 mph. The remainder of the tornado path were through countryside areas, with tree damage the primary impacts. The tornado dissipated about 1.5 miles from the McLean County line along E 1700 North Rd.

tornadoes.name: Normal-Towanda Tornado
tornadoes.label: Normal-Towanda Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado touched down on Old Peoria Rd 1 miles west of Rivian Parkway on the far west side of Bloomington, IL and did just tree damage. It then moved northeast and damaged several metal buildings. As it moved northeast across Normal, IL, it did significant tree damage, especially between Main Street and North Linden Street. It continued to do tree damage as it moved northeast. As it left town, it flipped over a semi on I-55. It then entered Towanda, doing minor damage and ended just northeast of town.

tornadoes.name: Bloomington Tornado
tornadoes.label: Bloomington Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed just south of Fox Creek Rd. between I-55 and Veterans Parkway, with a few greenhouses damaged along the track. It traveled near Veterans Parkway and into Highland Park Golf Course where it did tree damage. It continued northeast and did extensive tree damage in Evergreen Memorial Cemetery. It continued northeast through the southeast corner of the Bloomington Country Club Golf Course, where it produced more tree damage. As it moved northeast it broke two power poles on Empire St and then traveled across Veterans Parkway into a housing area. It did significant tree damage as it moved northeast and then broke two more power poles on GE Road. It continued northeast, doing more tree damage as it headed out of Bloomington moving northeast. It snapped off trees about 1.5 miles northeast of Bloomington along E 1750 North Rd, as well as along E 1900 North Rd where it also did significant damage to an outbuilding near the intersection with N 2300 East Rd. As it continued northeast, it did soffit damage to a home, snapped branches, and damaged an outbuilding along E 2100 North Rd. As it passed to the southeast of Pleasant Hill, it damaged the roofs and doors of two outbuildings along E 2250 North Rd then dissipated after it snapped a power pole and a tree about 2 miles northeast of Pleasant Hill along N 2900 East Rd.

tornadoes.name: Chestnut Tornado
tornadoes.label: Chestnut Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado touched down in an open field and moved east-northeast. The only damaged was to a power pole along Hwy 54 at the intersection of 2000 Ave.

tornadoes.name: Rowell Tornado
tornadoes.label: Rowell Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado touched down near the intersection of 1500 North Rd and 550 East Rd, where it damaged two farm out buildings and damaged a tree. As it moved east, it damaged a power pole and snapped the top of a tree off, throwing it 300 yds to the east. The tornado continued to the east, crossing Hwy 51 and then ending on Weldon Springs Rd where it damaged another farm out building and the top of a tree.

tornadoes.name: Lexington Tornado
tornadoes.label: Lexington Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A tornado moved across the northwest portions of town, mainly snapping tree branches and power poles. One house received some minor roof damage.

tornadoes.name: McLean-Livingston Tornado
tornadoes.label: McLean-Livingston Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado began in rural northeast McLean County about 4 miles northwest of Colfax, damaging trees and power poles and power lines. The tornado crossed into rural Livingston County, damaging more trees and a machine shed.

tornadoes.name: Saybrook Tornado
tornadoes.label: Saybrook Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A tornado tracked ENE across western and northern portions of Saybrook. A narrow, one block damage path consisted of several downed trees and multiple broken large tree limbs. The narrow path and few available damage indicators resulted in inconclusive evidence of a track extending farther to the WSW or ENE into Gibson City.

tornadoes.name: Gibson City
tornadoes.label: Gibson City
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down on the west side of Gibson City, producing significant roofing damage to several buildings along 8th Street. The tornado continued ENE for several miles, producing primarily tree damage before lifting approximately 3 miles ENE of Gibson City.

tornadoes.label: Near New Haven, MO
tornadoes.notes: A Tornado Debris Signature off of the KLSX radar appeared at 0231z and tracked along this path, dissipating around 0240z. Ground survey was unable to find damage directly associated with tornado, but NWS GIS Mutual Aid analysis of high resolution satellite imagery was able to find damage consistent with an EF-0 tornado.

tornadoes.name: Lodge Park Tornado
tornadoes.label: Lodge Park Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado set down west of the farmstead and collapsed an empty, 90 ft concrete grain silo. It also blow out the east side doors of a machine building and two north wall panels. The tornado likely continued to the east northeast, ending 2 miles away.

tornadoes.name: Loda-Buckley
tornadoes.label: Loda-Buckley
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down west of Loda with initial damage consisting of the collapse of two empty grain bins. The tornado continued ENE to just south of Buckley, downing and uprooting trees and blowing over semi-trucks on Interstate 57. Near the end of the damage track, the roof of a large outbuilding was removed, while nearby trees were snapped near the base and deposited in various directions.

tornadoes.name: Bondville Tornado
tornadoes.label: Bondville Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down just south of Rte 10 and damaged a power pole and quickly moved east-northeast. It did minor tree damage before dissipating.
tornadoes.timing_issue: start and end time are identical

tornadoes.name: Woodland
tornadoes.label: Woodland
tornadoes.notes: This tornado caused damage to trees and outbuildings east and northeast of Woodland.

tornadoes.name: Darrow
tornadoes.label: Darrow
tornadoes.notes: The tornado appeared to touch down in an open field southwest of the intersection of E 1200 North Road and N 2450 East Road and impacted a farm, leading to damage to several structures. The tornado then continued northeastward, causing damage to trees and farm outbuildings. The peak intensity of the tornado occurred near the end of the path along the Iroquois and Newton county border, where over a dozen new wooden power poles were snapped at their base. The tornado then appeared to lift just northeast of US-24 in southwestern Newton County.

tornadoes.name: Momence
tornadoes.label: Momence
tornadoes.notes: This brief tornado track started near Farr Creek in the small community of Eldridge within unincorporated Momence. Along the path, a combination of scattered tree damage and outbuilding roof damage was noted. As the tornado tracked north of the center of Momence, multiple power poles were downed along IL-1, with additional tree damage noted near 5500N. The tornado appears to have dissipated just northeast of Trimm Creek.

tornadoes.name: Kentland
tornadoes.label: Kentland
tornadoes.notes: A narrow EF-1 tornado touched down near the intersection of W 1700 S and S 350 W roads, where several large tree branches were downed. The tornado then crossed US Highway 41 at peak intensity, downing a billboard, uplifting a large portion of the roof of a restaurant, and pushing over a semi truck. A farm outbuilding was damaged nearby, as well. Debris was thrown nearly 2 miles downstream in an open field just north of US Highway 24. A narrow path evident in satellite imagery in open fields to the northeast of this debris suggested that the tornado likely continued to the northeast for approximately two more miles without impacting any trees or structures before dissipating.

tornadoes.name: Lowell
tornadoes.label: Lowell
tornadoes.notes: The tornado began just west of the Illinois-Indiana border with the first instances of uprooted softwood trees, downed large branches from hardwood trees, and minor structural damage noted near Stateline Rd on either side of the border. As the tornado quickly tracked northeast, it caused additional tree damage on at least one property near US-41. Along the path toward and through Lowell, the tornado blew out sections of a gas station canopy along IN-2 and then a garage wall at a residence just northwest of downtown Lowell. This was in addition to causing further tree and minor structural damage in a defined narrow path. The tornado continued through southern and southeastern sections of Lake Dalecarlia, causing primarily tree damage and minor structural damage due to fallen trees. Based on the ground survey, the tornado likely dissipated prior to reaching IN-55. Finally, just south of the tornado track through portions of Lowell, the survey team documented a fairly narrow corridor of straight-line wind damage.

tornadoes.name: Tilton Tornado
tornadoes.label: Tilton Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado did only tree damage as it quickly moved west to east.
tornadoes.timing_issue: start and end time are identical

tornadoes.name: German Township, IN
tornadoes.label: German Township, IN
tornadoes.notes: A survey of damage near the Indiana/Michigan state line confirmed as disorganized tornado touched down on Adams Rd, between Mayflower and Portage Rd then quickly tracked across Portage Rd into 2 subdivisions on the east side of Portage Rd. Pockets of tree damage occurred with the majority of any structure damage caused by falling trees. The tornado lifted east of Alpine Ridge Ct. Maximum winds were estimated at 80 mph.

tornadoes.label: Near Little Sioux, IA
tornadoes.notes: A tornado developed approximately 1.5 miles north-northwest of Little Sioux at 1:46 PM. The tornado began just southeast of the intersection of 120th Street and Dayton Avenue, flipping a center pivot. It continued northeast, damaging farm outbuildings, trees, and power poles near 120th Street and Early Avenue. Just over 1 mile northeast of this intersection, another center pivot was flipped over. The tornado then turned slightly more eastward and tore the fabric roofing off part of a hoop barn near Gage Lane and Easton Trail, where it came to an end.

tornadoes.label: Near Farragut, IA
tornadoes.notes: Several videos and photographs from multiple angles indicated that a weak tornado developed and moved to the east northeast along this approximate path. While the near-surface dust cloud was wider, the core circulation was quite narrow and weak. The only damage along the track was minor tree damage as it crossed mostly open fields.

tornadoes.label: Near Alma, KS
tornadoes.notes: Intermittent tornado damage noted on survey.

tornadoes.label: Near Eskridge, KS
tornadoes.notes: Radar confirmed debris from tornado, likely from trees in the river valley.

tornadoes.label: Near College Springs, IA
tornadoes.notes: Two spotter reports confirmed a funnel with rotating dust at ground level with minor tree damage at one location. The track was mainly over open fields.

tornadoes.name: Braman
tornadoes.label: Braman
tornadoes.notes: The Braman tornado began near the Grant / Kay County line, near the intersection of W Earth Road and N 140th Street. This tornado moved to the east and eventually northeast, spawning at least two satellite tornadoes. The tornado crossed I-35 near W Fork Road. At least EF1 damage was noted with numerous utility lines being damaged or destroyed. Research radar data from Doppler on Wheels gave additional detail to the tornado path.

tornadoes.name: Braman Satellite 1
tornadoes.label: Braman Satellite 1
tornadoes.notes: Satellite tornado observed on video. Path is somewhat estimated.
tornadoes.timing_issue: start and end time are identical

tornadoes.label: Near Admire, KS
tornadoes.notes: Confirmed with video evidence.

tornadoes.name: Braman Satellite 2
tornadoes.label: Braman Satellite 2
tornadoes.notes: EF-unknown. Satellite tornado observed on video and mobile research radar. Path is based largely on mobile radar data.

tornadoes.name: Stanberry
tornadoes.label: Stanberry
tornadoes.notes: Shortly before 8 PM CDT, a strong line of thunderstorms moved through Gentry County. A circulation embedded within the line resulted in a tornado developing around 7:58 PM on the northwest side of Stanberry. This tornado continued east-northeast through the north side of Stanberry, strengthening to a high end EF 1 tornado, as it crossed US 136, damaging several homes before continuing northeast. The tornado ended shortly after moving across the intersection of US 136 and State Highway F. Thanks to Gentry County Sheriff's office for providing assistance with the damage survey.

tornadoes.name: Enid
tornadoes.label: Enid
tornadoes.notes:
This long track tornado began to the south and west of Vance AFB at 811 CDT. The storm moved to the northeast, producing EF4 damage in a neighborhood just east of US81 as well as near S 30th Street and E Rupe Road. Finally, the storm moved to the east and northeast, dissipating just to the west of Enid Woodring Regional Airport.

Although some minor adjustments to the tornado path may occur as investigation of aerial damage imagery continues, this will likely be a near-final assessment.

tornadoes.name: Clay County KCMO - Nashua
tornadoes.label: Clay County KCMO - Nashua
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began just east of U.S. Highway 169 in Nashua, producing sporadic tree damage near Main Street to Oak Trafficway. The tornado strengthened as it moved east to Charlotte Street, producing extensive tree damage between 113th Street and 115th Street as it began moving northeast through Tracy Avenue and Virginia Avenue. A few trees fell onto and damaged vehicles and homes. The tornado contracted as it moved northeast toward Cunningham Drive and Woodland Avenue, dissipating shortly after damaging several trees at a residence just north of Cookingham Drive.
tornadoes.timing_issue: duration over 3 hours

tornadoes.name: Kearney
tornadoes.label: Kearney
tornadoes.notes: Just after 9 PM CDT Thursday April 23, 2026, within a severe line of thunderstorms, an embedded circulation resulted in a brief EF 0 Tornado beginning on the south side of Kearney, MO just north of 19th street and Regency Dr. This tornado continued east-northeast across HWY 33 and resulted in EF 0 damage to trees and homes before ending near east 14th street and Stonecrest Dr. Thanks to Kearney Fire and Clay County Emergency Management for assisting with the survey.

tornadoes.name: Southern Clinton County MO
tornadoes.label: Southern Clinton County MO
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed near 200th Street on the Clay County side of the Clinton/Clay county border. It produced minor tree damage along 200th Street before moving northeast toward 204th Street. Several trees were visibly snapped near their tops on the north side of the tree grove near Owl Creek. The tornado then damaged several trees and power poles along 204th Street. Metal debris was strewn onto trees and property at a residence along the road. The tornado then tracked north of the road, damaging several more trees before dissipating west of Fightmaster Road. Notably, there was minor/sporadic tree and limb damage to the southeast of the tornado track, but as all of this damage was northeast-facing, this appears to be straight-line wind damage.

tornadoes.name: Joplin Tornado
tornadoes.label: Joplin Tornado
tornadoes.notes: An NWS survey concluded an EF1 tornado with peak winds of 95mph damaged an outdoor maintenance storage building at the golf course at the W 2nd Street and S Schifferdecker Ave in Joplin. The torando then tracked to the northeast downing numerous trees in a cyclonic manner. Minor roof damage occurred to a few homes, and several other homes were damaged by trees falling on them.

tornadoes.label: Near Kiowa, OK
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed north of Harper Valley Road and west of Poe Lane. It moved east-southeast across Harper Valley Road, where trees were uprooted and large tree limbs were snapped. The tornado then moved southeast across Kiowa, where numerous trees were uprooted or snapped, homes were damaged, outbuildings were destroyed, and power poles were snapped. It then dissipated just southeast of Kiowa.

tornadoes.label: Near Deport, TX
tornadoes.notes: The County EM reported a path of damage near FM 1497 and CR 15600 in the southeast part of the county. Tree damage was observed in a twisted manner and along a convergent path, a shipping container was moved, and a boat dock was displaced out of a pond to the south along the track.

tornadoes.name: Greens Creek Tornado
tornadoes.label: Greens Creek Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began near the eastern end of Mapp Turner Rd and tracked across Lily Rose Rd, downing large tree limbs. It crossed MS Hwy 13 near the intersection with Greens Creek Rd, uprooting trees and damage siding at a home along Clay Lee Johnson Dr. The tornado then made a leftward turn as it occluded, downing additional large tree limbs as it lifted near the intersection of Greens Creek Rd and Jot-Em Down Rd.

tornadoes.name: Bill Strong Tornado
tornadoes.label: Bill Strong Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This brief weak tornado started near the intersection of Betigheimer Rd and Canada Cross Rd and tracked east-southeast along Bill Strong Rd, dissipating near Old Port Gibson Rd. Many trees were damaged with limbs or tops broken out and some uprooted. The tornado crossed Middle Rd just north of Bill Strong Rd and essentially paralleled Bill Strong Rd. More trees were damaged along with a portion of a roof taken off a barn, a metal carport thrown and some minor roof damage to a home.

tornadoes.name: Gatesville Tornado
tornadoes.label: Gatesville Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This brief tornado began west of Terry Gatesville Rd, downing multiple trees and large tree limbs along its path before lifting beyond the eastern end of Byrd Dr north of the Gatesville community. One tree fell on a house and another fell on a shed.

tornadoes.name: Clear Branch Tornado
tornadoes.label: Clear Branch Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began near E Tucker Rd and Quicks Cv in the Clear Branch community and tracked southeast across Clear Branch Rd, ending near the intersection of Poplar Springs Rd and Cousins Dr. Along the path, several trees were uprooted and several large tree limbs were downed, with some falling on utility lines.

tornadoes.name: Braxton Tornado
tornadoes.label: Braxton Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began along Holly Grove Cir and tracked eastward across Harrisville Braxton Rd before lifting. Along the path, multiple trees were uprooted and large tree limbs downed.

tornadoes.name: Pinola Tornado
tornadoes.label: Pinola Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed near the Strong River and crossed MS Hwy 43 before lifting. Multiple trees were uprooted along the path.

tornadoes.name: Boggan Ridge Tornado
tornadoes.label: Boggan Ridge Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began east of MS Hwy 13 in the Boggan Ridge area, tracking east southeastward across Main St, D and C Farm Dr, Macedonia, Rd, and Lee Boggan Rd before ending around Rials Creek Rd. Along the path, several trees were snapped or uprooted.

tornadoes.name: Magee Tornado
tornadoes.label: Magee Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed over downtown Magee just north of the Magee General Hospital and tracked southeastward crossing from 1st St to 5th St between 4th Ave and 12th Ave. It then crossed MS Hwy 28 and Beulah Rd before lifting near Tugwell Rd. Along the path, several large tree limbs were downed, power lines were downed, and shingle damage occurred.

tornadoes.name: Stringer Tornado
tornadoes.label: Stringer Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado occurred north of Stringer along County Road 17. This tornado caused some damage to a small outbuilding removing the roof and compromising the structure. The more notable damage was done to several uprooted and snapped trees. This was enough to get this storm rated a low end EF-1 with winds of 90 MPH. Path width estimated to be 75 yards.

tornadoes.name: Paulding Tornado
tornadoes.label: Paulding Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This weak tornado tracked along CR 16 west of Paulding, uprooting trees and snapping large tree limbs along its path.

tornadoes.label: Near Gulfport, MS
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado with peak winds of 95 mph touched down just north of the intersection of Ohio Ave. and Polk St. in Gulfport. The tornado quickly tracked to the south causing sporadic tree damage that consisted primarily of large tree limbs being blown off of trees as tracked southward between Wisconsin Ave. and West Railroad Ave. The tornado continued south-southeast across US Hwy 49 with no visible damage observed to commercial businesses in this area. Large branches and snapped trees were observed between 34th St. and 28th St. At the intersection of 28th St. and 22nd Ave. two metal buildings had their garage doors blown out as the tornado continued south-southeast. At the intersection of Pass Road and 22nd Ave. a large hardwood tree was completely uprooted. The tornado then crossed Pass Road and produced additional tree damage in the form of large branches and a few snapped trees. The snapped trees were either dead and diseased, so the windspeed was lowered to 90 mph to account for this. As the tornado crossed the railroad track, minor damage to a home in the form of a few removed shingles was observed on 3rd St. The tornado then moved offshore near the intersection of Beach Blvd. and Pratt Ave.

tornadoes.name: Gulfport Tornado #2
tornadoes.label: Gulfport Tornado #2
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado with peak winds of 90 mph touched down at 30th Street and Brookwood Ave. where large branches were down on several trees. Similar damage occurred as the tornado tracked to the southeast across Pass Road and 28th Street. The tornado continued to the southeast and reached peak intensity of 90 mph near the intersection of 5th Avenue and 25th Street where a few trees were snapped. One hardwood tree was hollow inside and the other snap was very high. Numerous large branches were also removed from several trees near this intersection. The tornado then continued to the southeast crossing Gulf Avenue near 24th Street producing sporadic tree damage. The tornado then crossed the railroad just west of Hewes St. where additional large branches were removed from several trees all the way to Beach Blvd. Numerous trees were observed to have lost large branches between Roberts Ave. and Centennial Plaza on Beach Blvd.
tornadoes.timing_issue: duration over 3 hours

tornadoes.label: Near Jacksboro, TX
tornadoes.notes: A tornado formed west of US Highway 148 and its intersection with Puddin Valley Road, in northern Jack County. This tornado tracked southeastward through open country, producing scattered tree damage and light structural damage to one residence. The tornado dissipated shortly after crossing Post Oak Road. The damage was consistent with high-end EF-0 windspeeds of 75-80 mph.

tornadoes.label: Near Jacksboro, TX
tornadoes.notes: A second tornado formed in northern Jack County in association with the intense supercell which tracked across the county into Wise and Parker counties. This second tornado formed west of Post Oak Road, just north of its intersection with Campsey Road. The tornado moved southeast in open terrain producing substantial tree damage as it paralleled Campsey Road. Most of these trees exhibited damage consistent with high-end EF-0 winds on the order of 70-80 mph. However, a number of trees exhibited more significant snapping and twisting along this part of the track, commensurate with low end EF-1 wind speeds of approximately 90 mph. The tornado continued southeast for approximately 4-5 more miles producing additional high end EF-0 and low end EF-1 damage to trees, a couple of oil storage tanks, and a few homes and outbuildings. The tornado crossed State Highway 59 west of Cundiff and dissipated shortly thereafter.

tornadoes.label: Near Runaway Bay, TX
tornadoes.notes: A team from the National Weather Service Forecast Office in Fort Worth conducted a damage survey in Runaway Bay, Texas following a severe thunderstorm event which impacted Wise County the evening of April 25th, 2026. The survey team determined that an EF-2 tornado occurred on the southwest side of Runaway Bay with peak winds estimated to be 130 mph. This tornado formed just south of Highway 380 near Port O Call Drive and Pinto Court where a narrow swath of EF-0 tree damage was observed. The tornado then continued towards the west, uprooting some trees and snapping large branches as it approached Cimmarron Trail. By this time, the tornado was nearly a quarter of a mile wide, causing substantial tree damage and minor roof damage before moving into a residential area between Cimmarron Trail and Jasper Creek Road. Most homes in this neighborhood sustained high-end EF-0 and EF-1 damage with heavily damaged manufactured homes, broken windows, failed garage doors, uprooted trees, and substantial roof damage to single family homes. Within the broader area of EF-0/EF-1 damage, small vortices embedded in the tornado produced narrow corridors of EF-2 damage. The first instance was a two-floor residence on the northeast corner of the Cactus Canyon Drive and Brookview Drive intersection. Here, the home lost a substantial amount of roofing along with some exterior walls on the second floor. Two single-wide manufactured homes in the vicinity of this house were completely destroyed with debris displaced away from their original location. A second home in the northeast side of the neighborhood on Cactus Canyon Drive lost nearly all of its roofing. Wind estimates of this damage ranged from 120-125 mph. The tornado was also at its maximum width at this time, around a third of a mile wide. The most intense damage was observed with a double-wide manufactured home near the intersection of Overland Trail and Cumberland Trail. The metal frame was found 100 yards downwind of the original home site, with additional debris several hundred yards to the west. Severe tree damage was also noted just on the west side of Jasper Creek Road. This damage was consistent with a high-end EF-2 intensity tornado containing estimated wind speeds of up to 130 mph. A fatality occurred in this destroyed residence. The tornado continued into a forested area dissipating approximately 600 yards west of Jasper Creek Road, completing its 1.4 mile long path.

tornadoes.name: Springtown, TX Tornado
tornadoes.label: Springtown, TX Tornado
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado occurred in Parker County starting west-northwest of Springtown, and tracking nearly 10 miles southeast. The width of the tornado damage is listed as 2/3rd of a mile, but the distinction between the tornado track and nearby RFD winds of 80-90 mph is tough to determine. Damage along the path of the tornado was majority large tree limbs damaged and damage to lightweight/metal buildings and roofs. Two homes sustained more significant damage to the second story of each home. These two homes were the justification for the 105 mph max winds.

tornadoes.name: MiamiCo_0426
tornadoes.label: MiamiCo_0426
tornadoes.notes: At 4:20 PM CDT on Sunday April 26, 2026, an EF 1 tornado developed within a severe line of thunderstorms in northwest Miami County Kansas. This tornado began near the intersection of Pleasant Valley Rd and W 247th Rd. This tornado ended near Indianapolis Rd around 4:25 PM CDT.

tornadoes.name: LinnCo_0426
tornadoes.label: LinnCo_0426
tornadoes.notes: Shortly after 4:30 PM CDT on Sunday April 26th, an embedded circulation within a severe line of thunderstorms resulted in an EF 0 Tornado. This tornado started at 4:38 PM CDT southwest of Goodrich, KS and continued northeast ending at 4:45 PM CDT. Damage was primarily to trees and some outbuildings.

tornadoes.label: Near Foraker, OK
tornadoes.notes: Approximate path of tornado witnessed by numerous storm chasers that remained over mainly open country. Power poles were snapped by the tornado on Foraker Road, south of Foraker. Otherwise no known damage occurred from this tornado.

tornadoes.name: Buffalo
tornadoes.label: Buffalo
tornadoes.notes: A tornado produced an intermittent damage path to the east northeast of Buffalo, MO, Reports of a funnel cloud near the ground were received from the Springfield Street area southeast of Buffalo, with the first damage viewed north of Quarry Road in a wooded area. The tornado did the majority of its damage as it crossed Ozark Trail. One mobile home suffered broken glass on the south and north sides of the structure and another on the east side of the structure. Additional damage was noted to several outbuildings. Additional large limbs were noted on Steelman Road and west of Engle Road via Sentinel-2 satellite data analysis.

tornadoes.name: Sherwin
tornadoes.label: Sherwin
tornadoes.notes: Several trees uprooted or snapped. Railcars were overturned. Grain bins were significantly damaged. Outbuilding were destroyed. Several power poles were snapped and broken. Additional modifications to the path are possible after satellite data review.

tornadoes.name: South of Tonganoxie
tornadoes.label: South of Tonganoxie
tornadoes.notes: Early Monday April 27, 2026, a supercell thunderstorm moving across southern Leavenworth County Kansas resulted in a brief, EF 1 tornado at 3:31 AM CDT. The tornado began just west of US 24, south of Tonganoxie, between Honey Creek Road and north of Hemphill Road. EF 1 damage to an outbuilding and trees were surveyed just west of US 24. The tornado continued across open country east of US 24 before causing EF-0 damage to an outbuilding and power poles near the intersection of Hemphill Road and 214th St. Special thanks to Leavenworth County Emergency Management for the survey assistance.
tornadoes.timing_issue: duration over 3 hours

tornadoes.name: JoCo_0427
tornadoes.label: JoCo_0427
tornadoes.notes: A brief EF 0 Tornado occured just northeast of Spring Hill, KS in southeast Johnson County KS at 5:38 AM CDT on Monday April 27, 2026. This tornado was only on the ground for about 1 minute. It began along W 207th St near the intersection with S Ridgeview Road. Damage was primarily to trees.

tornadoes.name: JoCo_0426
tornadoes.label: JoCo_0426
tornadoes.notes: The same storm that resulted in a short lived EF 0 Tornado just northeast of Spring Hill, resulted in a second tornado, this one an EF 1 Tornado just along the Johnson County KS and Miami County Kansas line. This was also a short lived tornado, with EF 1 damage to a manufactured home north of W 215th Street.

tornadoes.name: Slater-Gilliam-Glasgow
tornadoes.label: Slater-Gilliam-Glasgow
tornadoes.notes:
A tornado developed near Bluebird Trail southwest of Slater at 652 am on April 27, producing sporadic tree damage as it moved northeastward to near Route O west of Slater. The tornado strengthened as it progressed through Slater, producing widespread tree damage, with several residential properties and vehicles damaged from fallen trees or limbs. A set of grain bins was heavily damaged north of Industrial Boulevard, and several houses to the north of the grain bins suffered minor roof and shingle damage. The tornado then progressed northeastward near Route 240 to the town of Gilliam. Severe tree and power pole damage was observed near and just to the east of Gilliam. One property in Gilliam was heavily damaged from a large, uprooted tree that fell onto vehicles and the home. Dozens of power poles were downed or snapped along Route 240 east of Gilliam, with the snapped poles confirming EF-2 damage. Just to the south of Route 240, hog barns and outbuildings near the damaged power poles were heavily damaged or destroyed. A newly constructed barn just to the north of Route 240 east of Gilliam was severely damaged, with walls caved in on multiple sides. Debris from the barn was lofted over 200 yards to the northeast. Irrigation pivots near the barn were overturned as well. As the tornado approached the Missouri River west of Glasgow, a long series of power poles was snapped or downed. The tornado then moved into the north side of Glasgow, producing significant tree, power line, and shingle damage. The tornado weakened as it moved northeast of Glasgow, producing primarily tree damage for the rest of its path as it moved east-northeast to south of Armstrong and eventually Route A south-southeast of Higbee. A couple of properties between Glasgow and Higbee were damaged from fallen trees. The last visible signs of damage were east of Route A and north of County Road 136 in far northeast Howard County, where several trees were snapped at their tops west of Moniteau Creek. Maximum winds of the tornado were approximately 115 mph (EF2) with a path length of nearly 36.5 miles and an approximate maximum width of 350 yards.

NWS Kansas City would like to thank Brad Hinz, emergency manager for Saline County, for his help surveying much of the damage path.

tornadoes.name: CharitonRandolph
tornadoes.label: CharitonRandolph
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado touched down around 7:11 am on April 27 just south of Rascal Flats Road in Chariton County. The tornado produced multiple significant scars to tree groves along Switzer Mill Road, with hundreds of tree tops chopped in this corridor. Damage to power poles and outbuildings was also observed, including the complete collapse of at least two outbuildings. The tornado then crossed Route 129, damaging two residences and a couple of outbuildings as well as several more tree groves south of Hickory Road. The tornado continued east-southeastward to just north and east of Roanoke in Randolph County, damaging numerous trees along County Road 2405 as well as at least five power poles. The tornado then gradually moved eastward across County Road 2410, downing or uprooting several trees. Eventually, the tornado moved generally east-northeast from just north of Yates to between Moberly and Renick, producing substantial tree damage. On County Road 2480, a structure was damaged in which the roof of a single family residence was lofted and removed from the building. Trees surrounding the structure also fell in multiple different directions. The tornado lifted near County Road 2735 southeast of Moberly. Notably, substantial straight-line wind damage was observed to the north and south of the tornado track for most of its path, including in far northwest Howard County, in Roanoke, Yates, and Higbee in Randolph County, and both in Moberly and between Moberly and Renick near and east of U.S. Highway 63. The National Weather Service in Kansas City would like to thank the NWS in Saint Louis, David Gaines and his staff at Randolph County Emergency Management, and Blake Rasmussen and Chariton County Emergency Management for all of their help before and during the multiple surveys of this tornado track.

tornadoes.name: Renick
tornadoes.label: Renick
tornadoes.notes: An EF-0 tornado developed between Higbee and Renick around 7:29 am on April 27. The tornado produced mostly tree damage as it tracked northeastward toward Renick. However, one outbuilding suffered roof damage possibly from a fallen tree. The most severe damage occurred in Renick, with numerous trees down along Business Route 63 between the railroad tracks and U.S. Highway 63. A grove of trees was severely damaged just to the north of the highway, with several other trees downed in this stretch. Minor property damage was also observed at several residences, mostly from fallen trees. The tornado tracked eastward along Route NN east of Renick, chopping tree groves in several spots before gradually weakening as it approached the Monroe County line.
tornadoes.timing_issue: duration over 3 hours

tornadoes.name: MiddleGrove
tornadoes.label: MiddleGrove
tornadoes.notes:
A brief EF-1 tornado touched down in southwestern Monroe County near Route M and Highway 151. The primary damage caused by this tornado was a farm just south of Highway 151. Numerous large tree limbs were broken on the property with one tree limb pointed to the west. One farm building was collapsed on the western side of the barn. The eastern facing part of the building which was attached to the cement slab was still standing, while the western facing part of the building had completely collapsed. Due to this, we estimated slightly below the expected wind speed which also matched the surrounding tree damage.

On the south side of the tornado, a rear inflow jet formed producing multiple straight-line wind damage reports. Damage was primarily across the southwest portion of Monroe County from Highway NN to just north of County Road 95. Damage was primarily to trees which were blown down facing easterly. However, damage did occur to two farms in which partial or near total collapses occurred to farm outbuildings. Winds likely reached up to 95 mph in the southern straight-line area.

The National Weather Service would like to thank Steve Jones at Monroe County Emergency Management for their assistance with this survey.

tornadoes.label: Near Marine, IL
tornadoes.timing_issue: start and end time are identical

tornadoes.name: JacksonTor
tornadoes.label: JacksonTor
tornadoes.notes: Tornado touched down just east of Co Road 300E where multiple trees were snapped about 15 to 20 ft above ground. Tornado moved northeast and caused substantial damage to barns and to at least one home across a three to four mile path then lifted near Co Road 600E to the north of County Road 1000N. The tornado may not have been on the ground continuously for the whole track.

tornadoes.name: Mt Pulaski - Chestnut Tornado
tornadoes.label: Mt Pulaski - Chestnut Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A tornado touched down in south-central Logan County, commencing near the intersection of 1250th Ave and 600th St, where it caused minor tree damage. The tornado tracked east-northeast, impacting the northwest side of Mount Pulaski. Along this path, it crossed 700th St and State Route 121, resulting in further damage to trees, a machine shed, and several small grain silos. Continuing its movement, the tornado crossed State Highway 54, uprooting additional trees and tearing metal paneling from an old barn near the intersection of Highway 54 and 2000th Ave. The path continued just south of Chestnut, snapping small tree limbs, before crossing the Logan-De Witt county line with minor tree damage. The tornado ultimately lifted approximately two miles south of Kenney.

tornadoes.name: Rowell Tornado
tornadoes.label: Rowell Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado initially caused damage near the intersection of Rowell Rd and Bantam Rd, evidenced by extensive tree damage, including large trees snapped halfway up the trunk and a few healthy trees uprooted. Traveling east-northeast along Rowell Rd, the storm continued to cause tree damage. It then crossed Rowell Rd near Bearsdale Rd, snapping a wooden power pole. Further damage was observed near the interchange of Rowell Rd and Highway 51, where a single-residence home and a barn sustained minor roof damage. The tornado then turned northeast, causing minor roof damage to a home and additional minor tree damage along Ospur Rd before finally lifting just prior to reaching Weldon Springs Rd.

tornadoes.name: Weldon - De Land Tornado
tornadoes.label: Weldon - De Land Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado developed 8 miles west of Weldon, snapping several electric poles and damaging trees. It continued tracking through the town of Weldon, causing more tree damage, removing roofing material from a single family residence, and peeling back the roof on the Deland-Weldon High School. The tornado crossed State Highway 10, striking a few farm outbuildings and damaging more trees before dissipating about 1 mile north of De Land.

tornadoes.name: Harp Township Tornado
tornadoes.label: Harp Township Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Small machine shed collapsed with its debris strewn toward the ENE near the intersection of Birkbeck Rd and Northfork Rd.
tornadoes.timing_issue: start and end time are identical

tornadoes.name: Galesville - Mahomet Tornado
tornadoes.label: Galesville - Mahomet Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado spun up west of Galesville, damaging trees and causing roof and structural damage to farm outbuildings. It continued tracking northeast into the northern side of Mahomet, causing extensive tree damage. The tornado dissipated a couple of miles northeast of Lake of the Woods near the intersection of County Road 700 and 2400N.

tornadoes.name: Rose Bud Tornado
tornadoes.label: Rose Bud Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A weak tornado formed in a field on the west side of Carter Lane in Rose Bud.Several snapped trees were visible in the tree-line in the distance. The tornado then crossed Carter Lane into a field and across several more tree-lines. Multiple breaks in tree lines were observed before the widest point of damage occurred. Multiple trees were uprooted or snapped in a field along an approximately 100 yard stretch. The tornado then began to weaken as it pushed further southeast approaching County Line Road. As it crossed County Line Road it broke large branches off a few trees before lifting further into the woods in White County. This tornado was rated and EF-1 with 100mph winds with a peak width of approximately 100 yards.

tornadoes.name: Junction Ferry
tornadoes.label: Junction Ferry
tornadoes.notes: A combination of radar and Sentinel-2 satellite data concluded an EF0 tornado occurred about 1.5 miles east of Junction Ferry. Satellite data depicted intermittent patches of tree damage in a confined path from County Road P-235 to just east of State Highway 106. Most of the path width ranged from 75 to 125 yards, but at its widest point, the tornado's damage path was measured to be 150 yards in width. The damage path length was 3.54 miles.

tornadoes.name: MorganTor1
tornadoes.label: MorganTor1
tornadoes.notes: Some scattered reports of tree limbs being snapped from the early stages of this storm, along with hail, but once the storm approached the southern portion of Mooresville it strengthened and started snapping large trees, with a mix of hardwood and softwoods being found from the storm survey conducted by NWS Indianapolis personnel. This began roughly within the neighborhood off of Carol Lane and East Wilson Drive, crossing over Rooker Road. Then the tornado continued east towards the Pennington Road and E Neitzel Road location. This tornado began to drift northeast along Neitzel Road in Morgan County before dissipating before Turner road.

tornadoes.name: MorganTor2
tornadoes.label: MorganTor2
tornadoes.notes: The second touchdown began after the initial circulation began to cycle with damage beginning about a half mile south of E Spring Lake Road. The tornado then crossed over N Kitchen Road also within Morgan County. This second touchdown demonstrated a more notable surface impact with ground splatter being found on several homes and barns along E Spring Lake Road and several large healthy hardwood and softwood trees snapped or uprooted. This path continued to the east and slightly northeast crossing over Forest Grove Road and ending off of Ruth Lane off of E Spring Lake Road in Morgan County.

tornadoes.name: Stone County Tornado
tornadoes.label: Stone County Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Storm survey revealed a tornado developed south of Mt. View just east of AR State Hwy 9 west of Stewart Road northwest of the community of Hanover. The tornado continued generally east-southeast crossing Hanover and Luber Roads. The tornado then moved a more easterly direction toward the intersection of Misenheimer and Waco Roads, dropping off the plateau crossing AR State Hwy 5 west of Arbana. The tornado then crossed Iron Mountain Road, eventually lifting near the intersection of Stone County Road 273 and Bob Davis Mountain Road southwest of the Pleasant Grove community. Damage to barns and outbuildings was noted, along with many trees blown down. This tornado was rated EF1, with maximum estimated winds of 110 mph and width of approximately 400 yds.

tornadoes.name: Ashbyburg-Jewel City, KY
tornadoes.label: Ashbyburg-Jewel City, KY
tornadoes.notes:
Trees were snapped and rooted and numerous large limbs were downed. Two electrical transmission line cross members were broken.

A swath of straight line winds accompanied the tornadic circulation across far eastern Webster County, far northern Hopkins County, and across southern McLean County and the community of Livermore with tree damage.

tornadoes.name: Livermore, KY
tornadoes.label: Livermore, KY
tornadoes.notes: Extensive tree damage along the path of the tornado, including snapped tree trunks and uprooted trees. Two homes suffered significant damage when trees fell onto them. Other homes suffered shingle and fascia damage. A few power poles were damaged. A barn lost part of its roof.

tornadoes.name: East Tuckerman Tornado
tornadoes.label: East Tuckerman Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Storm survey revealed a brief weak tornado occurred mainly over open fields west of the intersection of AR State Hwy 37 and I-57/US-67, with some power poles bent just west of the interstate. No evidence was observed of damage crossing I-57/US-67 nearby. This tornado was rated EF0, with maximum estimated winds of 80 mph, and approximately 50 yds wide.

tornadoes.label: Near Livermore, KY
tornadoes.notes: A tornado briefly touched down and affected all trees in sparsely populated locations of western Ohio County. The tornado touched down just south of Locks Road and did tree damage along a nearly 2 mile track through the Rough River Valley.

tornadoes.name: Dyersburg Tornado
tornadoes.label: Dyersburg Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A weak, short-lived EF0 tornado touched down on the southeast side of Dyersburg shortly after midnight Tuesday, April 28. The most significant damage occurred at a warehouse on E Court St, where ten skylights were blown out, and a large metal panel was pulled from the side of the building. The tornado continued southeastward almost parallel to E Court Street, causing tree damage on both sides of the road. Minor roof damage was noted at a house on Auburn Ave. The tornado lifted just before reaching U.S. Highway 412.

tornadoes.label: Near Hartford, KY
tornadoes.notes: The EF-1 tornado touched down briefly near the Rough River. It intensified as it crossed Highway 69, doing significant tree damage and some minor structural damage to homes along Highway 69. The tornado continued to the southeast where it ripped much of the roof of a home along Mill Run Lane, before lifting just before the Hartford, KY Airport.

tornadoes.label: Near Upton, KY
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado touched down near Raider Hollow Road. It continued on the ground for roughly one mile, doing mostly tree damage along its one mile path.

tornadoes.name: Coleman-Butterfield Crossing
tornadoes.label: Coleman-Butterfield Crossing
tornadoes.notes: A tornado began near Oklahoma State Highway 48 north of Coleman where a barn lost part of its metal roof and trees were snapped. Additional tree and outbuilding damage occurred eastward along West Butterfield Crossing. The tornado snapped a few trees as it crossed South Park Lane, south of West Boggy Depot Road. The tornado then began to weaken and move to the northeast, lifting near the intersection of West Boggy Depot Road and South Park Lane.

tornadoes.name: North Caney-Allison Road
tornadoes.label: North Caney-Allison Road
tornadoes.notes:
A tornado began near South Bluebird Lane, where a few homes sustained minor roof damage and a large tank was knocked over and rolled. The tornado snapped several trees as it crossed South Park Lane, just north of the West Voca Road intersection. The tornado then paralleled West Voca Road where tree and minor roof damage was noted eastward towards U.S. Highway 69. The tornado then crossed U.S. Highway 69 and Old U.S. Highway 69 just north of Caney, where trees were snapped and uprooted. The tornado continued to the southeast, damaging trees and outbuildings along east Allison Road. The most significant damage occurred near the intersection of Allison Road and Forest Hill Road, where a mobile home was destroyed and other homes received varying degrees of roof damage. The tornado also bent several large metal high-tension power poles east of this intersection along Allison Road. Further to the east, a house along South Sawmill Road lost a significant portion of its roof. Another concentrated area of damage was noted near the East Cottonwood Road and South Iron Stob Road intersection, where several homes, barns and at least one camper were significantly damaged. Two additional residences along East Cottonwood Road experienced light damage as the tornado began to dissipate, just west of Oklahoma State Highway 109A.

In addition, very strong straight-line winds just south of the tornado path caused significant damage in and near Caney. In addition to widespread damage to trees, roofs and outbuildings, an anchored 20-ft storage unit was completely destroyed on the southwest side of town. Maximum wind speeds associated with this damage are estimated to be as high as 100-105 mph, equivalent to portions of the tornado track.

tornadoes.name: White Church
tornadoes.label: White Church
tornadoes.notes: A combination of ground surveys, radar data, and Sentinel-2 satellite data concluded an EF0 tornado briefly occurred approximately 2 miles south of White Church. A short 0.6-mile confined path of trees were damaged just east of State Route 17.

tornadoes.label: Near Paradise, TX
tornadoes.notes: A tornado formed near the intersection of Spring Valley Road and Wise County Road 3355. This tornado initially moved south, producing scattered tree, shingle and outbuilding roof damage consistent with high end EF-0 winds. The tornado crossed FM 2123, just east of its intersection with Wise County Road 3355 in the Cottondale community, and dissipated shortly thereafter.

tornadoes.label: Near Rattan, OK
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed west of the 4240 Road, near Pinekke Road. It moved east-southeast snapping large tree limbs and uprooting small trees. The tornado crossed Highway 93 on the northern banks of Lake Hugo, where some trees were uprooted and large tree limbs were snapped. Numerous trees were uprooted and a few were snapped south of Apple, and a home was damaged. It continued to move east-southeast across the E2000 Road, and then crossed Highway 147 before dissipating over rugged terrain.

tornadoes.name: Mineral Wells Tornado
tornadoes.label: Mineral Wells Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
The tornado touched down north of Mineral Wells near Sundown Road and FM 1821, producing minor tree and fence damage. The tornado then continued southeast crossing Ellis White Road before moving into the Country Club Estates neighborhood. Multiple trees were uprooted, multiple carports collapsed, and multiple homes were damaged in this neighborhood. The most notable was a home that had its entire roof and truss structure removed and displaced approximately 200 feet, consistent with 120 mph winds.

The tornado continued southeast damaging homes and businesses southeast of Country Club Parkway producing damage consistent with 100 to 130 mph winds. A commercial building with a personal weather station measured 100 mph winds before the sensor failed. The tornado then intensified as it moved through the Fort Wolters Historical Park and Holiday Hills Estates. Multiple homes in Holiday Hills Estates had significant roof and window damage, producing damage consistent with 130 mph winds.

Significant damage was observed to numerous World II Era warehouse structures in the Fort Wolters Historical area. Several warehouses fully collapsed, while others only partially collapsed. All of the warehouses were built similarly with wood frames and large open spaces. The roofs were initially built similar to a residential home with plywood decking and asphalt shingles and covered with either tar and single-ply roofing membrane or sheet metal. Two warehouses also contained a brick parapet wall within the structure. One of these walls remained standing despite the entire structure around it being blown off the foundation while the other wall collapsed with the structure. Due to these factors and others surrounding the construction and structural integrity of the warehouses, it is most likely that the damage to the warehouses is consistent with 120 to 145 mph winds.

The tornado continued southeast, producing tree damage along US-180 from Washington Road to High Point Road. It then moved south of US-180 and lifted in an inaccessible wooded area near the Dry Creek.

tornadoes.name: Pollard, AR
tornadoes.label: Pollard, AR
tornadoes.notes: A brief EF0 tornado touched down near the intersection of CR 339 and CR 321 northwest of Pollard. When the tornado touched down, a large tree was uprooted, damaging an awning on a residential porch. The tornado quickly began to weaken after its initial touchdown, but not before ripping some metal roofing off a barn and blowing a few shingles off the roof of Trailer's Chapel General Baptist Church along CR 321. The tornado also caused minor tree damage along CR 328, lifting after crossing Highway 139. This survey was assisted by law enforcement camera footage.

tornadoes.name: Cresson Tornado
tornadoes.label: Cresson Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado was captured on video on the east side of Cresson. A drone flyover of the area allowed us to determine a path based on damage to crops and vegetation in areas the survey team could not access.

tornadoes.label: Near Cleburne, TX
tornadoes.notes: A tornado formed in Byron Stewart Park, west of Cleburne, crossed onto Lake Pat Cleburne, and exited the lake on the southeast side. Tree damage was observed in the park and video evidence shows the tornado over the lake. On the southeast side of the lake along Lakeshore Dr, a small porch was damaged and overhead doors were damaged in an RV storage garage. This tornado was rated EF-0 with maximum winds of 80 mph.

tornadoes.name: Rio Vista Tornado
tornadoes.label: Rio Vista Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A second tornado from the same storm impacted a small area east of Rio Vista. Mostly scattered tree damage and damage to lightweight metal objects was observed along the path of the tornado. The tornado started near Hill Ct northeast of Rio Vista. One manufactured home off CR 1205 lost most of its roof covering, and the roof of a nearby home on CR 1107 was also partially removed. The tornado continued southeast crossing FM 916 and dissipating near CR 1204 and 1104. This tornado was rated a low-end EF-1 with winds of 90 mph.

tornadoes.name: Keevil Tornado
tornadoes.label: Keevil Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed near the community of Keevil near the intersection of AR Hwy 17 and Hildson Lane near the Union Pacific Rail Road tracks. Debris evidence began with large limbs down in the tree-line, and then the tornado tracked generally east towards US HWY 49 when several power poles were snapped, and a house and out-building were damaged. The tornado then crossed Stoops Road where it completely destroyed an vacant 1930s farm house resting on cinder blocks. Several large oak trees around the house were all snapped in half. Along Stoops Rd, 24 power poles were snapped in half as the tornado crossed the road. The tornado then crossed another tree-line damaging a few more trees before dissipating in the fields near Mopac Road. This tornado produced maximum estimated wind speeds of 120 mph, consistent with an EF-2 rating.

tornadoes.name: Ashley Co Tornado
tornadoes.label: Ashley Co Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A very brief tornado occurred along County Road 498 in Ashley County. This tornado uprooted trees and caused wooden power poles to lean. The tornado crossed County Road 498 and dissipated in the field just after uprooting more trees. The tornado is rated EF-0 with winds of 85 MPH.

tornadoes.name: HardinLaRue
tornadoes.label: HardinLaRue
tornadoes.notes: The National Weather Service investigated an area where radar briefly showed a tornado debris signature as the outflow from two different storms merged along the Hardin and LaRue County line. This track moves along a lot of open field, but the TDS apparently started in a forested area just south of Union Church Rd and east of Mack Thomas Rd in far eastern Hardin County. This EF0 tornado likely skipped several times along its 2.2 mile track. Damage indicators were hard to come by, but a playground at Union Christian Church was damaged. No damage was found along Kerrick Lane where the track of the rotation passed, but then some tree damage was noted on Dan Dunn Rd and then ended on Spencer School Rd. Thanks to LaRue County Emergency Management for escorted the survey team through the region.

tornadoes.name: Washington County
tornadoes.label: Washington County
tornadoes.notes: A very brief tornado occurred south of MS 454 along Deerfield Road. A few trees were uprooted along the road and trees were topped in a field. This tornado is rated EF-0 with 85 MPH winds.

tornadoes.label: Near Hico, WV
tornadoes.notes:
An EF1 tornado began between US 19 and Whispering Pines Lane in the Pine Grove community of Fayette County. The tornado skipped along in an east-southeasterly direction with the damage path ending near the intersection of Mountain Vista Dr and US 60 in the Lookout community.

Tree damage was extensive along Edmond Rd and between Lansing Edmond Rd and US 60 with the trunks of some healthy mature hardwood trees snapped in both locations and many trees uprooted. Only some minor roof damage occurred to a couple structures.

Thanks to Fayette Co Office of Emergency Management, Fayette Co 911 and the Fayette County Sheriff's Office for assistance with the damage survey.

tornadoes.name: S Jasper Tornado
tornadoes.label: S Jasper Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This weak brief tornado touched down near the intersection of CR 8 and CR 31. Multiple large branches were broken off with an uprooted tree along CR 31.

tornadoes.label: Near Bloomington, TX
tornadoes.notes: Evidence of a high-end EF-1 (110mph) tornado was found in south- central Victoria County. Drone footage showed a scour track that began over farmland between Crouch Rd and HWY-185, and ended near Crouch Rd east of York Rd along with a track of debris. In between, several manufactured homes on Jared Rd, Lexie Ln, and York Rd suffered significant roof damage, broken windows, and scattered debris correlated to circulation of a tornado. One manufactured home was completely destroyed along Jared Rd. The tornado track was found to be around 1.1 miles long and a width of around 400 yards, spanning from 2:02-2:06pm CDT.

tornadoes.name: Deer Park Tornado
tornadoes.label: Deer Park Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado downed multiple trees along a path in a wooded area west of LA Hwy 15 just north of the Deer Park community. The tornado was observed from LA 15 by a storm chaser.

tornadoes.name: Smithburg-Dillon, MS Tornado
tornadoes.label: Smithburg-Dillon, MS Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A NWS ground survey confirmed an EF-1 tornado with maximum sustained winds of 100 mph tracked across portions of southeast Pike and southwest Walthall counties. This tornado began near Smithburg, MS at the intersection of Mount Herman Road and Silver Drive where it uprooted a tree and snapped branches. Additional EF-0 tree damage was identified on Blanchard and Smithburg roads. The tornado peaked in intensity as an EF-1 as it approached and crossed over Harold Alford and Magnolia roads uprooting and snapping several trees as well as taking down wooden transmission lines. The tornado then weakened causing EF-0 damage to trees and removed metal panels from an industrial chicken coop as it approached Brockdale Rd and then crossed the Bogue Chitto River. The end point of this tornado is estimated to be after it crossed MS Hwy 27 where it caused additional tree damage in a confluent pattern.

tornadoes.name: Garden City Lincoln Monticello
tornadoes.label: Garden City Lincoln Monticello
tornadoes.notes:
Over the course of two hours and nine minutes, a strong, long track tornado trekked 81.9 miles across South Mississippi. It began in southwestern Adams County, then moved across northern Wilkinson, southeastern Adams, southern Franklin, and central Lincoln counties, before lifting on the south side of Monticello in Lawrence County. The tornado intensity peaked at a high-end EF3 with an estimated maximum wind of 160 MPH just east of Garden City in southwestern Franklin County. The maximum path width was 1.5 miles in east central Lincoln County.

The tornado began in the St. Catherine Creek National Wildlife Refuge in southwestern Adams County, then tracked near the Homochitto River across northern Wilkinson County and far southeastern Adams County before moving across southern Franklin County, central Lincoln County, and into Lawrence County, lifting on the south side of Monticello. Communities along and near the path of the tornado included Possum Corner, Garden City, West Lincoln, Bogue Chitto, Enterprise, East Lincoln, and Harmony. The first instance of EF3 damage was an area of nearly complete devastation to mixed forest east of the Garden City community. A second area of EF3 damage was identified in western Lincoln County between W Lincoln Drive and Rowan Lane, where another intense area of tree damage occurred. A third corridor of EF3 damage occurred just east of I-55 between Brookhaven and Bogue Chitto. In this area, tree damage was extensive with some debarking, a home was heavily damaged with exterior walls collapsed, and a mobile home park was devastated with debris and vehicles rowed along a center vortex path. Additional heavy tree damage occurred along the entire path. There were also multiple instances of EF2 structural damage in Wilkinson, Franklin, Lincoln, and Lawrence counties.

tornadoes.name: Coal Town - Purvis Tornado
tornadoes.label: Coal Town - Purvis Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began near or just west of the intersections of Tatum Salt Dome Road and R Thompson Road where it produced damage to trees crossing Tatum Salt Dome Road with a narrow swath of damage produced just north of R Thompson Rd. The tornado moved eastward through the Half Moon Creek lower wooded areas before crossing Beach Road, retaining a consolidated core that could be observed transecting the roadway twice as the tornado track roughly paralleled the roadway. The tornado produced mostly vegetative damage until it approached western Purvis in the Boggy Hollow areas where outbuildings were damaged or destroyed and trees were blown onto homes. A mobile home was blown off of its blocks just north of Purvis-to-Columbia Road, which the tornado approximately moved along as it traveled east-northeast. The tornado intensified to its maximum intensity, producing damage that suggests maximum winds were at least 135 mph as several residences had roofs removed as well as some exterior walls blown inward near Coal Town Road and Highway 589. Significant damage was also observed along Central Industrial Row where several metal building system (MBS) warehouse and commercial buildings had walls and internal structures including pillars/columns and roofing purlins destroyed. Numerous other facilities suffered substantial loss of roofing materials including the Lamar County Multi-Purpose Center. The tornado continued eastward downing numerous trees and causing widespread damage to roofs and outbuildings before dissipating just east of US Highway 11. The tornado at maximum width was estimated at 600 yards, had a track length of 13.4 miles, and had a maximum estimated intensity of 135 mph, EF-2.

tornadoes.name: Beaumont
tornadoes.label: Beaumont
tornadoes.notes:
Preliminary ground survey confirms EF1 damage beginning along US Highway 98 between New Augusta and Beaumont, with multiple areas of softwood and hardwood trees snapped or uprooted. Two concentrated areas of tree damage were noted along US Highway 98, suggesting multiple subvortices within a broader circulation. The maximum intensity occurred around US Highway 98 with winds around 100 mph. The tornado continued generally eastward, crossing Highway 198 and tracking along or near V L Toussaint Blvd before weakening over the north side of Beaumont. Farther southwest, sporadic tree damage was also observed along Highway 29 south of New Augusta. Satellite data will be examined over the coming weeks to determine the starting point for the tornado, as radar suggests that it likely formed over a wooded area southwest of New Augusta. Further track adjustments are likely once satellite data is available.

After review of available Sentinel 2 satellite imagery the tornado track had major changes to its beginning and end points, width, and intensity. The tornado was found to have began much further west to the west of Highway 29 and just north of Red Hill Road. The tornado traversed forest uprooting and snapping trees along its path, reaching a peak intensity north of Red Hill Road where a large section of forest sustained significant damage. Here wind speeds were likely in the 100 to 110mph range. The tornado evolved into a multi-vortex evident by several notable corridors of tree damage along the main tornado track. The tornado continued east of Highway 29 gradually shrinking in size and weakening. During this period it dropped southeast a bit along FS Road 312 A. The tornado began to re-intensify as forest damage became more noticeable until reaching Highway 98 where ground survey crew assessed damage. Satellite imagery supported the tornado being multi-vortex as several focused corridors of damage became evident as it crossed Highway 98, consistent with ground survey assessments. Afte the ground survey end point, the tornado did continue into the forest causing forest damage across Horseshoe Bend Lake. It then reached the Leaf River where the last evidence of forest damage associated with the tornado was visible on Sentinel 2 satellite imagery. This is the estimated end point for the tornado. The tornado width was also updated to be approximately 700 yards wide. Additional adjustments are possible later as high-resolution satellite imagery becomes available over the next month.

tornadoes.name: Jonathan
tornadoes.label: Jonathan
tornadoes.notes: After review of available medium to high resolution satellite imagery, it was determined an EF1 tornado occurred near Jonathan. This tornado began southwest of Highway 63 where it began causing intermittent tree damage across portions of the forest. After crossing Highway 63, it moved into some open fields where it continued to cause tree damage in a focused corridor. The tornado strengthened on approach to Jonathan Road where a more persistent corridor of tree damage was able to be observed. The tornado continued northeast across Jonathan Road, reaching its peak intensity around 90mph just northwest of Albert Smith Road where a corridor of more substantial treefall was evident on satellite imagery. The damage path becomes intermittent after this point, with the last visible tree damage east of the Albert Smith Road and Old Avera Road intersection. This is also where the radar tornado debris signature dissipates, and no further damage is evident further east via satellite imagery. Adjustments to the tornado are possible later as high-resolution satellite imagery becomes available over the next month.

tornadoes.name: Prentiss Tornado
tornadoes.label: Prentiss Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began on the south side of Prentiss near MS Hwy 13, tracking across Old Highway 13, Tom Bullock Rd, and MS Hwy 42. A storm chaser observed turbulent debris and power flashes. As it approached the Lake Jeff Davis area, it began to occlude tracking along Ed Parkman Rd before lifting. Along this path, several small trees and various tree limbs were downed.

tornadoes.name: Wilson Rd Tornado
tornadoes.label: Wilson Rd Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began near Oilwell Rd and tracked across Wilson Rd near Burkhalter Rd, lifting shortly thereafter. Along the path, several large hardwoods were uprooted and part of the roof was blown off of a shed.

tornadoes.name: Enon-Darbun, MS Tornado
tornadoes.label: Enon-Darbun, MS Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A NWS ground survey confirmed an EF-1 tornado with maximum sustained winds of 95 mph tracked across portions of northern Walthall County, near Enon, MS. This tornado began near L. L. Coon Rd where high resolution satellite imagery showed areas of damaged/displaced trees on a confined path that tracked southeast toward MS Hwy 44. The tornado strengthened to EF-1 strength as it moved into Willie Cothern Rd where it uprooted trees, lifted metal roofing off a porch, and snapped a swath of tree trunks on private property. The tornado turned more eastward as it crossed MS Hwy 583 where it damaged shingles on a church and uprooted and snapped a few trees. Minor tree damage continued eastward across New Home Church Road with plenty of tree debris across the road. The tornado then restrengthened some over inaccessible forested areas south of New Home Church Rd where patches of heavier tree damage/displacement was identified on high resolution satellite imagery. This tree damage gradually became more minor again near Hope Rd and Dee Toney Rd. Numerous small trees were leaning in a confluent pattern with large branches down near MS Hwy 27. Minor tree damage continued with uproots and large branches predominantly occurring along the damage path on Jordan, Sauls, and Dan Holmes roads. This tornado continued east-southeast into Marion County, within the NWS Jackson area of responsibility, where additional EF-0 and EF-1 tree damage was identified by ground survey. It's estimated that the tornado finally lifted near Circle Bar Road after being on the ground for approximately 16.5 miles and 24 minutes.

tornadoes.name: Darbun Tornado
tornadoes.label: Darbun Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado moved into Marion County from northeastern Walthall County near the Darbun community, crossing Reid Rd, Bracey Rd, and Rowley Rd before lifting near Circle Bar Road. Along the path, multiple trees and tree limbs were downed.

tornadoes.name: Grand Bay
tornadoes.label: Grand Bay
tornadoes.notes:
Preliminary ground survey confirms low end EF1 damage northeast of Grand Bay, Alabama. Maximum intensity of 88 mph was found on Jim McNeil Loop Road where several large tree limbs were down over a compact area. The tornado tracked southeast and produced sporadic damage on Dedicated Road where a horse trailer was flipped and more trees were damaged. After passing over Old Pascagoula Road, additional tree damage with downed limbs and snapped trees were found on Wells Road West. Satellite data will be examined in the coming weeks to confirm the starting point of the tornado, which is likely further to the northwest in wooded areas over Jackson Creek east of Grand Bay Wilmer Road.

After review of available Sentinel 2 satellite imagery, the beginning and end points of the tornado have been adjusted to reflect a narrow corridor of persistent tree damage along the tornado track. The start point is brought back to just south of Davis Lane along Jackson Creek where minor tree damage becomes evident. The end point was adjusted southeast across Interstate 10 where tree damage became apparent again in the vicinity of Boe Road and Henley Road, in line with the location that the radar TDS began to dissipate. No additional damage is visible southeast of this location. Further refinements of the track are possible later as higher resolution imagery becomes available.

tornadoes.name: Theodore Industrial Park
tornadoes.label: Theodore Industrial Park
tornadoes.notes: Available Sentinel 2 satellite imagery and available radar data with a tornado debris signature revealed a weak EF0 tornado occurred near Theodore Industrial Park. Minor tree damage was evident, beginning along the tree line north of Degussa Road. This is where the first signs of a radar tornado debris signature appear. The tornado crossed Rangeline Road, producing another small corridor of tree damage west of Dauphin Island Parkway along Cedar Wood Drive North. The damage path comes to an end at Dauphin Island Parkway and serves as the end point for this tornado.

tornadoes.name: Delco_EF1
tornadoes.label: Delco_EF1
tornadoes.notes: Damage began near 356 Delco School Road, where several trees were snapped and power lines were downed. A short distance away at McPherson's Acme General Store (1355 Old Stage Road), a metal awning was torn from the structure and destroyed, damaging a nearby 500-gallon propane tank and causing a fuel leak. The tornado continued east-northeast approximately 1.3 miles with only intermittent damage before intensifying near the 1225 block of Fertilizer Road. There, three structures sustained significant roof damage, including two single-family residences, and a large oak tree was uprooted. The tornado then rapidly dissipated with no further damage noted.

tornadoes.name: Paulina, LA Tornado
tornadoes.label: Paulina, LA Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A brief, weak EF-0 tornado touched down in the community of Paulina, LA causing minor uplift of shingles on two homes. The tornado tracked north-northeast from Lena Street to Angelle Street at around 8 miles per hour before it was estimated to have lifted. This damage was collocated with a tight tornado vortex signature visible on TMSY doppler radar. No additional damage was identified via reports or aerial imagery. Time estimated by radar.
