tornadoes.name: Hudson Tornado
tornadoes.label: Hudson Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A storm exhibiting supercell characteristics for multiple hours while offshore moved ashore with a tornado estimated to have touched down around 1814 UTC (2:14 PM EDT) west of U.S. Hwy 19 near Hudson in Pasco County, while continuing to exhibit a distinct rotational signature via KTBW WSR-88D and TTPA TDWR. Damage was initially observed along Saltwater Blvd, where a tree branch was snapped and fell onto a power line. Additional damage points were noted to manufactured homes further east along Saltwater Blvd -- one having its rear screened porch lifted from its base attachment and partially shifted, along with metal roofing peeled and tossed across the street, and another suffering partial roof loss with metal roofing above its garage lifted and peeled off. Additional damage was noted north of Saltwater Blvd, with a family residence along Neptune Drive having approximately five to ten feet of fascia peeled off the side of the home near the roof. Neighboring manufactured homes located approximately a quarter-mile to the east along Puffin Lane experienced rear porch roof and lanai damage, with one home losing part of its aluminum roof as it was peeled from the back of the home and lofted over the home and into a vehicle parked in its front yard, and also onto the street in front of the home. The neighboring home just to its east had its rear lanai peeled from the home and tossed around it onto a metal fence across the street from the home. Along the adjacent Osprey Lane to the north, a large pine tree had its top snapped off, and a small wooden outdoor shed was collapsed, while on adjacent Heron and Curlew Lanes to the north, homes suffered partial carport aluminum panel loss and partial aluminum roofing material loss, respectively. The final damage point noted west of U.S. Hwy 19 consisted of small to medium sized branches snapped and broken from trees near the intersection of Gull Lane and Delmar Drive. The tornado then crossed U.S. Hwy 19 with the radar signature becoming increasingly disorganized shortly thereafter, and it is estimated that the tornado dissipated sometime around 1819 UTC (2:19 PM EDT) between Whitby Road and Lakeshore Blvd after tracking for just over one mile.

tornadoes.name: Shady Hills Tornado
tornadoes.label: Shady Hills Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The development of a second circulation became apparent west of Shady Hills approximately 20 minutes after the circulation associated with the Hudson tornado weakened, and it is estimated that a tornado touched down near Gladwin Avenue to the west of East Road at approximately 1843 UTC (2:43 PM EDT). Damage from this tornado consisted largely of snapped tree limbs and branches as it slowly tracked south and southeast across largely rural areas along Fulton and Eden Avenue, although a large tree was uprooted and downed onto a mobile home along Eden Avenue near the intersection of East Road. The tornado then turned east and east-southeast as it appeared to exhibit a bit of a binary interaction with the remnant circulation that produced the Hudson tornado that was located to its east, before radar indicated it likely dissipated around 1848 UTC (2:48 PM EDT) between East Road and Alliance Lane, less than mile from where it is estimated to have touched down.

tornadoes.name: Shullsburg
tornadoes.label: Shullsburg
tornadoes.notes: Tornado appeared to start along/west of County Road I and Penny Benton Rd. Along PB Rd, it hit 6 trees, 1 uprooted, 1 snapped at the trunk but was rotted, and 4 others had limbs topped. As it tracked east, it hit some metal farm buildings along Mullen Rd and south of Copeland Rd. Corn stubble from the field to the west was noted deposited along the farm driveway with sheet metal from the barns lofted up the hill and into the forest to the east.

tornadoes.name: Linn County MO Tornado 1
tornadoes.label: Linn County MO Tornado 1
tornadoes.notes: A severe thunderstorm over northwestern Linn County Missouri developed an EF-0 Tornado at 6:22 PM Saturday, May 16, 2026. This tornado developed between Arbor Dr. and Beacon Rd. on Highway 139, resulting in EF-0 damage to an outbuilding, before crossing a wooded area as it moved east-northeast toward Clark Dr. The tornado produced additional EF-0 damage to a single family home before removing a substantial area of metal roof covering over a barn. Debris was spread east, northeast, and south of this structure across an open field. Damage to trees east of the farm was noted.

tornadoes.name: Linn County MO Tornado 2
tornadoes.label: Linn County MO Tornado 2
tornadoes.notes: The same severe supercell thunderstorm that resulted in the first Linn County tornado, resulted in a second north and east of Shafter, MO. This tornado began at 6:28 PM CDT near the intersection of Daisy and Clark Rd. It continued southeast resulting in EF-1 damage to several farm outbuildings, including a wellbuilt barn. It picked up two empty grain bins and distributed them east-northeast across open pasture. Damage was noted in the tree-lines beyond the property to the southeast. The track was picked back up along highway DD, where wideswaths of EF-1 and EF-0 tree damage were noted along both sides of the highway. The path ends about a half mile before the intersection with Highway Y around 6:32 PM CDT.

tornadoes.name: Chula, MO
tornadoes.label: Chula, MO
tornadoes.notes: A shortlived tornado developed within a severe supercell thunderstorm at 6:43 PM CDT approximately 2 miles east of Chula, MO in Livingston county. The Tornado damaged trees south of Highway K before crossing the highway, damaging a wood framed metal building. The tornado removed the west facing roof sheeting, depositing debris to the west and southwest. The tornado ended in the open field to the east of this building northwest of the Highway K and KK intersection.

tornadoes.name: Fort Myers Landspout Tornado 1
tornadoes.label: Fort Myers Landspout Tornado 1
tornadoes.notes: A landspout tornado was observed at 3:17 PM EDT near the intersection U.S. Hwy 41/S Cleveland Ave and Gorham Ave, where a citizen submitted video of a rotating cloud base and funnel near the Wawa and Culvers, and later confirmed that they witnessed a ground circulation with surface and lofted dust and small debris. No significant damage was reported, and no other reports, pictures or videos have been received indicating that the track extended beyond that location.

tornadoes.name: Fort Myers Landspout Tornado 2
tornadoes.label: Fort Myers Landspout Tornado 2
tornadoes.notes: A landspout tornado likely associated with the circulation responsible for a previous landspout is estimated to have formed around 3:25 PM EDT approximately 1.75 miles to the northwest of the previous landspout, where damage was first noted along Reynard Ave in the Tanglewood area where a large tree had numerous medium to large branches snapped. Branches and limbs were snapped at multiple locations across Cumberland and Woodwind Courts, and a home near Tanglewood Pkwy had a large tree uprooted in its yard. Additional footage was submitted from the Tanglewood vicinity depicting lawn furniture and yard decor scattered about, along with fencing and roof damage, and a video taken by a resident along Westminster Dr at 3:28 PM EDT showed airborne debris along with indications of the ground circulation as the landspout neared the McGregor Gardens area and Argyle Dr and McGregor Blvd. The circulation continued northwest across the Georgetown area just south of Colonial Blvd and began crossing the Caloosahatchee River just to the west-southwest of McGregor Colonial Memorial Park, and to the south of the Midpoint Bridge around 3:30 PM EDT. Videos taken by the public showed surface spray associated with the circulation as it approached and crossed the Midpoint Bridge west of McGregor Colonial Memorial Park and continued northwest toward the central section of the river north of the bridge, where it is estimated to have dissipated sometime around 3:31 PM EDT before reaching the western shore of the river.

tornadoes.name: Cape Coral Landspout Tornado
tornadoes.label: Cape Coral Landspout Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A landspout tornado formed over Cape Coral just north of the Sovereign Canal around 3:35 PM EDT in association with a separate segment of the cluster of thunderstorms, with evidence of the circulation visible in video taken by residents along SW 4th Ave and SW 5th Ave. Footage from SW 4th Ave showed a pickup truck in the driveway of a home being displaced a number of feet as the circulation passed by the location, and footage from the SW 5th Ave location showed the funnel of the landspout and the surface circulation behind a home over the Niagara Canal. Additional footage of the circulation was taken approximately one-quarter mile to the northwest near the Seabell Canal, where footage from a home on the southern edge of the canal along SW 26th Ter showed the circulation blowing lawn chairs around and lofting additional unidentified debris, while also knocking over and blowing around vinyl fencing in the backyard of a home on the opposite/northern side of the canal along SW 26th St. A few additional reports and photos from the vicinity also indicated fence and some roof damage as the circulation neared the intersection of Skyline Blvd and Veterans Pkwy before before it is estimated to have dissipated around 3:38 PM EDT, as no other reports, pictures or videos have been confirmed to indicate that the track extended further.

tornadoes.name: Archer Tornado
tornadoes.label: Archer Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Brief tornado in this location per damage survey, RaXPol radar data, and chaser video. Damage was limited to a couple overturned pivots and an empty grain bin and broken tree branches at a farmstead.

tornadoes.name: Hebron South Side Tornado
tornadoes.label: Hebron South Side Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Most of the damage was broken tree limbs. The golf cart shed at the Hebron golf course lost its roof.

tornadoes.label: Near Ida Grove, IA
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado moved across a home along German Ave between Hillside Way and Highway 175. Damage was done to multiple trees at the property.

tornadoes.label: Near Winnebago, NE
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado touched down west of Highway 77 and tracked northeast damaging trees and the roofs of homes. The tornado impacted locations near baseball fields on the south side of Highway 75. Damage to bleachers, signage, and the dugout occurred, and across the highway there was damage to grain bins and a large tree landed on a home. The tornado continued northeast and did minor damage to a large water tank and additional tree damage along D Avenue.

tornadoes.label: Near Sergeant Bluff, IA
tornadoes.notes: A tornado touched down south of the Sergeant Bluff Rest Area and moved northeast through open fields before downing several large tree limbs along 220th St. The tornado lifted shortly thereafter.

tornadoes.label: Near Bronson, IA
tornadoes.notes: A tornado touched down near the intersection of Glen Ellen Rd and County Home Rd and moved northeast to near 180th St and Charles Ave before lifting in the adjacent field to the east. Several outbuildings and trees were damaged along the path with the most severe damage to an attached garage of a single family home.

tornadoes.label: Near Beacon View, NE
tornadoes.notes: A tornado developed in an open field, snapping and throwing several large branches in a field. It then progressed east northeast to the Sandy Pointe lake area where it threw a dock approximately 100 yards, removed shingles from one house, and removed much of a roof from another house, throwing it approximately 80 yards away into the lake. Video suggests that the tornado ended to the northeast, with no damage to any vegetation along the Platte River.

tornadoes.label: Near Plattsmouth, NE
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado formed on the southwest side of Plattsmouth east of Highway 75. The tornado moved northeast and snapped several pine trees on the top of a small incline that had a house and several grain bins. One empty grain bin was destroyed. The tornado continued northeast, causing minor tree damage and light damage to some mobile homes,

tornadoes.name: Plover
tornadoes.label: Plover
tornadoes.notes: Damage in Plover. Tornado reported in the area

tornadoes.label: Near Ruthven, IA
tornadoes.notes: Path noted in Copernicus Sentinel satellite imagery. Damage reported from Grand View Park is in line with path.
tornadoes.timing_issue: duration over 3 hours

tornadoes.name: Graettinger
tornadoes.label: Graettinger
tornadoes.notes: Drone footage and photos shows narrow damage track across the eastern side of Graettinger.

tornadoes.name: Moorland
tornadoes.label: Moorland
tornadoes.notes: Estimated tornado path via video, radar, damage, and tower camera.

tornadoes.name: Gruver
tornadoes.label: Gruver
tornadoes.notes: Virtual survey with information from emergency management. 8 power poles broke and splintered. Video confirmed. 82 mph wind gusts recorded at Estherville Airport.

tornadoes.name: Plymouth
tornadoes.label: Plymouth
tornadoes.notes: Damage to trees and outbuildings.

tornadoes.name: Paxton
tornadoes.label: Paxton
tornadoes.notes: A short-lived EF-0 tornado caused damage to a farmstead and power poles along N 1500E Road just north of E 100N Road near Paxton.

tornadoes.name: Elk Creek Area
tornadoes.label: Elk Creek Area
tornadoes.notes: A tornado developed in open fields near the intersection of 625 Avenue and 725 Road, and moved quickly east. The tornado damaged many trees, flipped pivots, and destroyed at least two large farm sheds. The damage along the track was somewhat sporadic at times, and this concentrated area of tornado damage was embedded within a much broader area of 60 to 80 mph winds in the downdraft regions of the parent thunderstorm. The peak width of the tornado was determined where it traveled through a long line of trees and gave evidence to the most intense focused zone of winds being approximately 200 yards wide.
tornadoes.timing_issue: duration over 3 hours

tornadoes.name: Highway 136 West of Auburn
tornadoes.label: Highway 136 West of Auburn
tornadoes.notes: A tornado developed just south of Highway 136 and west of 636 Avenue, and moved east northeast to the area near Highway 136 and just east of 637 Avenue. This tornado caused sporadic tree damage and uprooting, and impacted two farms. At one farm, a large trailer was rolled approximately 50 yards and debris distributed downstream across a field. Several trees were snapped or uprooted and landed on a home. Another farm had a large shed destroyed with the debris field extending more than a half mile downstream. This tornado was embedded in a broad area of straight line downburst winds estimated at up to 95 mph, especially near and just south of the tornado track.

tornadoes.name: Highway 75 North of Auburn
tornadoes.label: Highway 75 North of Auburn
tornadoes.notes: Video from broadcast media showed a small, rain-wrapped tornado moving generally eastward just south of Road 733A and Highway 75. Damage consisted of a small cluster of large downed tree branches, with estimated maximum winds of 80 mph.

tornadoes.label: Near Sabetha, KS
tornadoes.notes: Old barn lost 30-40% of roof and wall, small barn completely destroyed with debris carried about 1/4 mile ENE.

tornadoes.name: 8 SW Salem
tornadoes.label: 8 SW Salem
tornadoes.notes: At approximately 4:55 PM, a tornado developed near the Nebraska/Kansas border just west of 639 Boulevard, damaging some trees. It continued northeast, crossing 639 Boulevard and producing significant damage to the roof of a large metal outbuilding. The tornado then crossed US Highway 75 just northwest of the intersection with 641 Avenue, causing further tree damage and impacting a second metal outbuilding in the area. Additional tree damage occurred near Rock Creek and 642 Avenue, where the tornado came to an end.

tornadoes.name: 1 NE Salem
tornadoes.label: 1 NE Salem
tornadoes.notes: A tornado developed at approximately 5:07 PM near the intersection of 646 Avenue and 708 Road, about 1 mile northeast of Salem. Intermittent damage to trees and farm outbuildings was noted between 646 and 647 Avenues. The tornado continued northeast, damaging more trees and breaking power poles along 650 Avenue. Additional damage to trees and farm outbuildings was noted near the intersection of 651 Avenue and 710 Road. The tornado then crossed US Highway 73 and lifted the roof off another farm outbuilding east of 652 Avenue before dissipating shortly thereafter.

tornadoes.label: Near Beattie, KS
tornadoes.notes: Tornado snapped large tree limbs and a few tree trunks. Grain bins were also destroyed.

tornadoes.label: Near Benton, IA
tornadoes.notes: Damage along path consistent of weak tornado. SRV Rotational couplet evident at this time. Photo evidence of tornado provided by Ringgold County Emergency Management.

tornadoes.label: Near Holton, KS
tornadoes.notes: Outbuilding and barn destroyed. Several large branches broken along the path. Windows blown out of south facing porch.

tornadoes.label: Near Allen, KS
tornadoes.notes: QLCS tornado resulted in damage to several power poles and large tree limbs. One two-story home had uplift on roof material.

tornadoes.name: Fillmore, MO Tornado
tornadoes.label: Fillmore, MO Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A NWS Damage Survey team confirmed an EF-0 tornado occurred Monday evening, 5/18/2026 in and near the city of Fillmore, MO. The tornado started at 8:11 PM CDT, southwest of the city of Fillmore. The tornado caused EF-0 tree damage southwest of Fillmore, and then caused EF-0 damage to several residences and outbuildings within the city of Fillmore. The tornado continued to the northeast of Fillmore, causing more EF-0 tree damage and eventually lifting at 8:16 PM CDT 4 miles east northeast of Fillmore, near the intersection of County Road 40 and County Road 55.

tornadoes.name: Ray County 01
tornadoes.label: Ray County 01
tornadoes.notes: NWS Damage Survey team confirmed a tornado occured Monday evening, 5/18/2026, beginning at 9:47 PM CDT in southwestern Ray County Missouri. This tornado caused primarily tree damage along its path, but did impact two properties, one north of Fishing River, shortly after the tornado developed. EF1 Damage to two power poles, one out building was noted, along with the roll over of an empty livestock trailer. The tornado resulted in widespread EF1 tree damage near Reynolds Road and W 108th Street. The tornado continued east-northeast, crossing highway 10 south of Elkhorn before causing tree damage north of Swanwick before crossing highway 13. The tornado ended near the intersection of Frazier Road and Millville Road at 10:06 PM CDT.

tornadoes.name: Midway Road Tornado
tornadoes.label: Midway Road Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This weak tornado tracked north northeastward roughly along Midway Road from north of Oakley Palestine Road to Thigpen Road, then lifted near Seven Springs Road. Along the path, several large tree limbs were downed. A tornadic debris signature was observed on radar.

tornadoes.name: Isney
tornadoes.label: Isney
tornadoes.notes: Available Sentinel 2 satellite imagery revealed a weak EF0 tornado occurred in the Isney area. The tornado began south of Wildflower Road, tracking northeast across Poultry Road, causing a roughly 180-yard-wide corridor of tree damage. This tornado also crossed the path of another tornado that occurred near this location back on March 11th of this year along Poultry Road. The tornado lifted just prior to reaching Highway 84. Additional adjustments to this tornado are possible as higher resolution imagery becomes available. Review of additional high resolution satellite imagery revealed the tornado crossed Highway 84 affecting a property to the north of the road damaging a few trees.

tornadoes.name: Smyer
tornadoes.label: Smyer
tornadoes.notes: Available Sentinel 2 satellite imagery revealed an EF1 tornado occurred in the Smyer area off of Highway 69. The tornado remained solely within forest staying just east of Highway 69. It tracked northeast for approximately 3 miles causing a 100-yard-wide corridor of tree damage. Additional adjustments to this tornado are possible as higher resolution imagery becomes available.

tornadoes.name: Sparks Road Tornado
tornadoes.label: Sparks Road Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A tornado developed along Sparks Road, east of Demopolis, near the Marengo County/Hale County line, where several hardwood trees were snapped and uprooted, and a residence had siding damage either from wind or fallen trees. The tornado then moved northeast and impacted homes just off Highway 80 near Yellow Creek Road. Shingles and siding were removed from a couple of homes, a shed was destroyed, and general yard items were strewn. Perhaps the most eye-catching item was the displacement and flipping of a box truck and a pontoon boat. The tornado then crossed Highway 80 with minimal signs of damage and came to an end just past the Hale County line, along Mount Olive Road, where tree branches were broken.

tornadoes.name: Exmoor Tornado
tornadoes.label: Exmoor Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado occurred in the Exmoor community along County Road 6, between County Road 7 and Lewis Road. The tornado began along the back tree line of a property then moved northeast where it shifted a camper northward a few feet off of its cinder block supports. A manufactured home suffered damage to its porch and awning. Some trees were snapped and uprooted as the tornado crossed County Road 6 before dissipating as it downed trees across the road.

tornadoes.name: Campbell
tornadoes.label: Campbell
tornadoes.notes: Available Sentinel 2 satellite imagery revealed that an EF1 tornado tracked across forested parts of Clarke County in the Campbell area just west of Highway 69. The tornado remained solely within the forest, causing an approximately 250 yard wide corridor of tree damage. The tornado lifted just prior to reaching Wood Bluff Road. Additional adjustments to this tornado are possible as higher resolution imagery becomes available.

tornadoes.name: Bama Rock Garden Road Tornado
tornadoes.label: Bama Rock Garden Road Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down just north of Interstate 20/59 nearly 2 miles east of exit 89 in a largely open field with a few trees here and there, one of which was uprooted.  Numerous video recordings on social media showed a lowering cloudbase and nebulous funnel cloud crossing the interstate, with what looked like a very narrow drill bit tornado finally touching down.  From there, the tornado moved north, crossing Union Road, where minor damage occurred to a double wide manufactured home and the first hint of a debris signature appeared.  The tornado then traversed inaccessible forests and fields and intensified before reaching K and R Road, where several hardwood and softwood trees were snapped or uprooted.  Only minor damage occurred to any homes on the street.  The tornado then turned more northeasterly, crossed Bama Rock Garden Road—where a carport was tossed and a home sustained other minor damage—and crossed Charles Brook Rd, snapping and uprooting several trees. The tornado dissipated over inaccessible forest somewhere beyond Charles Brook Rd.

tornadoes.name: Baileyton Tornado
tornadoes.label: Baileyton Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down at approximately 12:57 PM CDT just north of U.S. Highway 278 and west of Holly Pond near the intersection of County Roads 1650 and 1682. There, it quickly assumed EF1 status, uprooting a hardwood tree, and causing door damage to small farm outbuildings nearby. The tornado tracked generally northeastward, uprooting and snapping large hardwood trees along County Rd 1683. Farther northeast, near the intersection of County Roads 1709, 1710, and 1711, multiple hardwood trees were snapped and uprooted, and in a small neighborhood there, a house experienced roof damage. The tornado continued to track generally northeastward across a mix of open farmland and woodland, with snapped and uprooted hardwood trees again observed along County Rd 1716. To the northeast in the Brooklyn community, the tornado uprooted and snapped hardwood trees along County Rd 1684, and minor roof damage occurred to a single family dwelling. There were also two cattle deaths due to tree falls off of County Rd 1684. The tornado crossed northward on the east side of Brooklyn, and headed farther northeast to east side of Baileyton, where it occasionally snapped and uprooted hardwood trees along the way. Just to the northeast of Baileyton along County Rd 1762, the tornado caused tree damage, with one large tree falling on and damaging a truck. Roof damage also occurred to a nearby house. Farther northeast along County Rd 1763, the tornado uprooted hardwood and softwood trees, pushed a mobile home off its foundation, and caused significant roof damage to the dwelling. The tornado began curving slightly westward as it neared the intersections of Highway 67 and 69, causing sporadic tree damage along the way and also along Apple Grove Rd. The tornado then tracked north-northwestward, ending on County Rd 1589 just west of AL Highway 67 at approximately 1:14 PM CDT.

tornadoes.name: New Tazewell Tornado
tornadoes.label: New Tazewell Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A tornado touched down in New Tazewell on Friday evening. The tornado first touched down along Coffee Road where several hardwood trees were damaged and one home had minor siding damage. The tornado intensified as it approached downtown. Here several building sustained significant damage with several having roof damage. Duncan lumber had multiple building damaged with one sustained major roof uplift and subsequent wall collapse. Other businesses in this area also sustained minor damage. Here the tornado was at it widest point of approximately 75 yards. Several power poled were snapped in this area as well. The tornado then wound down quickly with only very minor roof damage noted along Highway 33 and 5th avenue. Although notable debris was found further downstream of this location no additional damage was identified.

tornadoes.name: Morgantown Tornado
tornadoes.label: Morgantown Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service conducted a storm survey and determined that an EF0 85 mph tornado occurred in southwest Morgantown the evening of Friday, May 22, 2026.

Tree damage was first observed at a farm at the end of Viles Cemetery Road, where several treetops were damaged and pointing in different directions ranging from the southwest to southeast consistent with a convergent pattern from the small tornado. The damage continued to the east toward Viles Cemetery where some large branches were on the ground. Nearby Viles Cemetery Road, a field of tall grasses were bent and laying south in the direction of the tornado inflow.

The tornado continued across Gardner Lane where Final Finish Repair Shop sustained extensive roof damage. The roof was peeled back to the northwest direction, while a lot of insulation was carried eastward into nearby trees and power lines. Right to the east of Final Finish Repair Shop, the tornado lifted with no additional ground damage. However, insulation from Final Finish Repair Shop was lofted into nearby fields, across the Natcher Parkway (I-165) and in nearby trees at the Butler County High School Football Stadium. In total the short lived tornado was 0.32 miles long, although insulation from the Final Finish Repair Shop was observed at least another third of a mile from the end of the tornado as it was carried by the thunderstorm.

The National Weather Service would like to thank Butler County Emergency Management for the assistance with the storm survey. The National Weather Service would also like to thank the many individuals who sent helpful pictures and video footage of the tornado.

tornadoes.name: Villages of Bayport Tor
tornadoes.label: Villages of Bayport Tor
tornadoes.notes: On Sunday, May 24th, 2026 a developing thunderstorm produced a waterspout that moved onshore in the Villages of Bayport Community. Damage to a single pool cage was noted, and some images show small debris being lofted into the air. Residents in the neighborhood reported and shared images of a few additional structures that sustained minor damage. Additionally, a large tree was also blown over in the community one street over from where the main damage was noted. No additional damage or reports could be located.

tornadoes.label: Near Miramar Beach, FL
tornadoes.notes: A tornado moved ashore from the Choctawhatchee Bay into the small village of Villa Tasso. The tornado snapped and uprooted many hardwood trees, primarily on Yacht Club Drive, Robert Avenue, Magnolia Street and Virginia Court. Structural damage was largely due to fallen trees. However, one home on Hal Street suffered damage to about 40% of its roof. The tornado caused two trees to fall on a car at the intersection of Defuniak Street and CR 20 before lifting. Damage along most of the path was consistent with EF-1 damage with maximum winds estimated at 105 mph.

tornadoes.label: Near Webb, AL
tornadoes.notes: The tornado initially touched down just north of U.S. 84 near Cowarts in Houston County, damaging trees and outbuildings. A pool screen was damaged at a home along Omussee Road, with additional tree and minor damage to homes. The tornado damaged the WDHN television station as it crossed Highway 52, breaking windows and damaging the roof. The tornado continued north-northeast downing trees and causing minor structural damage before moving into Henry County at County Road 22 and Buckhead Drive. The most severe damage was along County Road 15 where two homes were heavily damage. One home was destroyed. This home separated from the concrete foundation, slid, and then collapsed. Assessment is ongoing regarding the rating at this location. All other damage is consistent with an EF1 tornado with maximum winds of approximately 105 mph.

tornadoes.name: Parrish Tornado
tornadoes.label: Parrish Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A tornado briefly touched down just west of U.S. Hwy 301, where the resident of a home along Loch Ness Gln witnessed damage to the backyard fence. The resident reported that the tornado lifted shortly thereafter, while another area resident witnessed debris being lofted in an open field just to the north prior to the tornado lifting. No additional damage or reports were received.

tornadoes.name: North Quemado
tornadoes.label: North Quemado
tornadoes.notes: Several storm chasers reported funnel cloud moved across highway 277 and briefly had fully condensed east of the highway for a short time (1 to 3 minutes). small broken tree branches were noted.

tornadoes.label: Near Antlers, OK
tornadoes.notes: Approximate path of weak tornado based on damage reports from the public.

tornadoes.label: Near Hammond, NY
tornadoes.notes: Video demonstrated a brief tornado developed over a corn field and toppled an apple tree, and then lifted a well cover into a window. Considering lack of additional damage, the tornado likely lifted in the vicinity of a nearby barn as it moved south-southeastwards.

tornadoes.label: Near Bridgewater, SD
tornadoes.notes: A tornado was noted from a storm chaser livestream in an open field south of 263rd St, moving slowly to the northeast. At times, the tornado exhibited smaller brief vortices. The tornado passed over a farmstead along 263rd St, west of 438th Ave, damaging an old barn before lifting.

tornadoes.name: wall_lake
tornadoes.label: wall_lake
tornadoes.notes: A tornado touched down in an open field southwest of the intersection of 266th St and 459th Ave. The tornado moved to the northeast and across a farmstead where it damaged two barns, downed several large tree limbs, and a fence. The tornado moved northeast across 266th St before lifting in an open field to the north.

tornadoes.name: viborg
tornadoes.label: viborg
tornadoes.notes: The tornado was first visible from a storm chaser livestream in an open field west of 466th Ave and north of 291st St. The tornado moved southeast toward a farmstead at the intersection of 466th Ave and 291st St, where minor tree damage was reported. The primary circulation then broadened and at times exhibited smaller brief vortices. Additional minor tree damage occurred before the tornado lifted in the vicinity of 291st St and 467th Ave.

tornadoes.label: Near Centerville, SD
tornadoes.notes: A very brief tornado rotating around a much larger mesocyclone moved southeast to northwest across Mount Hope Dairy, destroying one barn and damaging another before quickly lifting. Debris from the barns was scattered north of 290th St in a southwest to northeast orientation.

tornadoes.name: S of Tomah, WI
tornadoes.label: S of Tomah, WI
tornadoes.notes: This very short-lived tornado damaged some stands of trees. A TDS was observed via radar during this time.

tornadoes.label: Near Deemston, PA
tornadoes.notes: On June 6th, a brief EF-1 tornado occurred just southwest of Beallsville, originating from a meso-vortex within a broad line of storms that impacted the region. Initial damage, consisting of several large snapped branches and uprooted trees, was observed along Kefover Road. A farm on Glendon Lane became a primary area of focus after a barn was partially destroyed, with debris scattered northeastward across a field and onto a neighboring property; the fact that this debris was lofted to the left of the storm's general path served as an indicator of rotation. This location also saw a line of trees uprooted at a valley base and several pines snapped mid-trunk, though the residence sustained only minor porch damage. As the storm moved eastward up the hillside, it left sporadic tree damage in its wake before causing further concentrated destruction along Martindale Road, where numerous trees were snapped or uprooted at a farm and adjacent site.

tornadoes.name: Ellsworth Tornado
tornadoes.label: Ellsworth Tornado
tornadoes.notes: On the afternoon of June 6, 2026, an EF1 tornado, generated within a squall line, tracked just over 7 miles eastward across Washington County, PA. The tornado first formed near Cokeburg, snapping large pine trees between Route 917 and Washington Street. After a brief lift, it reformed two miles east near Ellsworth, along Beallsville Road and Cherry Street. This segment recorded the highest intensity, with maximum wind gusts of 110 mph. Damage included the snapping of approximately 50 hardwood trees and partial roof damage to one home on Cherry Street from a falling tree. The tornado continued its path, primarily snapping or uprooting hardwood trees as it crossed Deems Park Road, Woodland Road, Locust Road, Scenic Drive, California Drive, and Deer Run Lane, before finally dissipating at Cross Ridge Road.

tornadoes.label: Near Centerville, PA
tornadoes.notes: After analyzing both Sentinel satellite data and drone footage, we are adjusting the beginning and ending of this tornado track. The Satellite data clearly shows a swath of damage to trees just along and south of Bailey Road, just east of the intersection with Ridgewood Dr. This path continues and crosses Fishport Rd, where two other notable patches of trees were downed. The concentration of damage would indicate 95-100mph wind given the amount of tree coverage lost. As the tornado crossed Ridge Rd, Dague Rd, and Nobles Rd, the damage becomes more sporadic in nature. However, drone footage in this region shows the tops of several softwood trees snapped off, particularly near Dague Rd. Concentrated was again noted along Conti Rd and throughout the National Pike Steam Gas and Horse Association grounds as noted in the original survey. Here, nearly 200 trees were down around the National Pike Steam Show property. Trees were both snapped and uprooted. Additional damage was noted in the drone footage to the south and west, continuing toward Rye's Bar and Restaurant. After this point, the tornado most likely lifted as damage was more widespread in nature, and more indicative of straight-line wind.

tornadoes.name: Linn Tornado
tornadoes.label: Linn Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A strong line of storms crossed over the Monongahela River at around 2:49pm on June 6th. An embedded meso-vortex developed in the line with tightening rotation around 2:50pm, when the tornado is estimated to have touched down in Linn near Railroad Avenue. Time was estimated from radar. The strongest winds accelerated on the southern end of the vortex as it moved downhill into Redstone Creek Valley. Winds on the southern end of the vortex and northern end of the rear flank downdraft were the strongest, estimated at 100mph with a large amount of small hardwood trees down. The strongest winds were along Braznell Concrete Road, just northeast of its intersection with Taylor Flats Road. Some shingle damage was noted on a home before it ended. The vortex collapsed, along with a weakening of the rear flank downdraft push around 2:51pm after crossing Braznell Concrete Road one more time.

tornadoes.name: Virgin Run Tornado
tornadoes.label: Virgin Run Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A strong line of storms entered northern Fayette County, crossing Route 51 at around 2:56pm on June 6th. At the same time, it was evident that an embedded meso-vortex developed based on radar; this rotation extended to the surface resulting in an estimated tornado touchdown near Reservoir Road just east-southeast of Star Junction at 2:57pm. Time was estimated from radar. Damage continued, coincident with the vortex, and just south of the vortex for around 5.1 miles. Damage was sporadic at times, the tornado may have lifted and re-formed multiple times. Most damage was hardwood trees uprooted along Maplewood Road, Virgin Run Road, and Dickerson Run Road. The strongest damage was estimated at 90mph along Maplewood Road, just west of its intersection with Virgin Run Road where multiple hardwood trees were down with shingle damage to a home at around 2:58pm. The tornado continued, crossing the ridgetop just west of Dickerson Run road where drone footage shows a narrow swath of convergent tree damage, before the vortex continued across multiple fields, ending near Cemetery Road just north of Vanderbilt at 3:02pm.

tornadoes.name: Jacobs Creek Tornado
tornadoes.label: Jacobs Creek Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A brief EF1 tornado struck the northern border of Fayette County, Pennsylvania, on the afternoon of June 6, 2026, originating within a squall line. The tornado was active for four to five minutes, starting its track between Banning and Layton in Fayette County. Following a path that included Banning Road, Cross Road, and Boy Scout Road, the tornado’s wind gusts, which peaked between 95 and 110 mph, snapped and uprooted numerous large hardwood trees. The damage extended to remote locations, as aerial video provided by the South Huntington Township volunteer fire department later confirmed. The tornado dissipated in southern Westmoreland County where Meadow Run Road and Epsey Road meet.

tornadoes.label: Near Huntington, AR
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed along Hoff Road, west of Highway 71 and north of School House Road. It moved north-northwest crossing Hoff Cutoff and Nickletown Road, and then dissipated south of Palestine Road. The tornado uprooted trees, damaged a couple outbuildings, and snapped numerous large tree limbs.

tornadoes.label: Near Greenwood, AR
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed along Watson Road, west of Highway 71 and north of Young Ridge Road. It moved northwest across Vineyard Creek Road, Hendrix Road, and Nickletown Road, before dissipating just south of Highway 10. The tornado uprooted trees, damaged an outbuilding, and snapped numerous large tree limbs.

tornadoes.label: Near Barling, AR
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed in a large corn field north of Gun Club Road and east of Highway 59. It moved north-northwest across Hollis Lake Road where a few trees were uprooted and numerous large tree limbs were snapped. It then moved across an oxbow lake, crossed Hale Farm Road, and dissipated.

tornadoes.name: Battlefield
tornadoes.label: Battlefield
tornadoes.notes: Tree debris from a EF0 tornado was visible along Farm Road 131 southeast of Battlefield, MO. Eyewitness account depicted the tornado as it crossed Plainview Road at James Road. Additionally, Sentinel-2 satellite data analysis revealed some tree damage just outside of the Rivercut Golf Course. Max winds were estimated at 70 mph with a width of 50 yards.

tornadoes.name: Spokane-Highlandville
tornadoes.label: Spokane-Highlandville
tornadoes.notes: An NWS survey team confirmed a short, narrow path of tree damage consistent with an EF0 tornado between Spokane and Highlandville in Christian County. Additionally, Sentinel-2 satellite data analysis revealed tree damage at the start of the track near Camp Creek, southwest of Stoneshire Drive.

tornadoes.name: Sparta
tornadoes.label: Sparta
tornadoes.notes: An NWS survey team concluded that a tornado developed just east of Sparta and moved to the northeast. A wide tract of uprooted trees and large tree limbs fell in a cyclonic pattern spanning the path, where a tornado debris signature was observed on radar. A mobile home and a single-family home were found to be damaged.

tornadoes.name: Rogersville
tornadoes.label: Rogersville
tornadoes.notes: Sentinel-2 satellite data analysis in conjunction with radar analysis revealed a brief EF0 tornado with estimated max winds of 70 mph occurred within a forested area southeast of Rogersville. An intermittent 50-yard wide and half-mile long path of tree damage was noted on satellite in the vicinity of a TDS on radar. It is noted that radar showed debris beginning to be lofted southwest of this track's start point, but no damage indicators via ground or satellite surveys were found.

tornadoes.name: NW Douglas Co
tornadoes.label: NW Douglas Co
tornadoes.notes: A combination of NWS ground surveys and Sentinel-2 satellite analysis concluded that an EF1 tornado began within a forested area in far western Douglas County and tracked 8.9 miles, passing by Arden, and ending southeast of Tigris. Along the track, the tornado produced an intermittent path of extensive tree damage and caused roof damage to a couple outbuildings and pushed a manufactured home several feet. The tornado peaked with estimated winds of 100 mph and was 400 yards at its widest point.

tornadoes.name: Bowbells
tornadoes.label: Bowbells
tornadoes.notes: Reports and videos of a brief, dusty tornado southeast of Bowbells. Tornado fully formed around 8:50 PM and soon after knocked over a grain bin and sheared off the top half of pine trees. The tornado then tracked to the northeast for a couple of miles before dissipating before reaching the river.

tornadoes.label: Near Carlton, KS
tornadoes.notes: Large mesocyclone slowly moved southeastward across western Dickinson County. Widespread wind damage was noted well outside of the tornadic region due to the strong low-level mesocyclone. Tree branches broken and corn flattened in a convergent pattern on the periphery of the overall circulation, with several enhanced areas of damage within the tornadic centerline. Tornado path was likely internment due to transient nature of individual tornadic vortices.

tornadoes.label: Near Tecumseh, KS
tornadoes.notes: Short-lived QLCS tornado resulted in damage to two residential properties along Paulen Road.

tornadoes.label: Near Lawrence, KS
tornadoes.notes: Intermittent track, mainly topping trees

tornadoes.name: 20260609-Eaton
tornadoes.label: 20260609-Eaton
tornadoes.notes: The tornado began southwest of the intersection of Saint Joe Highway and Oneida Road and damaged mostly trees along its path. Near the Oneida Township Hall, a storage outbuilding was completely destroyed. Some minor additional property damage was noted along the path, mainly due to fallen trees. The tornado lifted in a field just east of St Johns Chase Road and south of W Eaton Highway.

tornadoes.name: Lomira
tornadoes.label: Lomira
tornadoes.notes: Damage in a short path to the northeast across Lomira include several homes/mobile homes with roof damage, trees uprooted and limbs snapped.

tornadoes.name: Kaneville Township
tornadoes.label: Kaneville Township
tornadoes.notes: This brief tornado caused damage at Kuipers Family Farm where a large portion of the south-facing roof of a barn was peeled up with debris blown northeast. Several small trees were also snapped on the property. Additional damage occurred at the Acquaviva Winery where a portion of the roof of a large pole barn was peeled off.

tornadoes.name: Eden
tornadoes.label: Eden
tornadoes.notes: Damage to numerous trees, a few uprooted. Barn damaged with roof decking blown across the intersection of County Road V and F.

tornadoes.name: Ravanna
tornadoes.label: Ravanna
tornadoes.notes: A rapidly developing supercell thunderstorm produced a tornado north of Ravanna, MO, on the afternoon of 10 June. The storm caused extensive damage to a garage and barn near the intersection of Route M and Route W east of Mercer. The tornado crossed Bobcat Street to the northeast. Owing to inaccessibility to property to the northeast, relied on spotter reports to confirm that the track continued northeastward to Route M east of Route W southwest of Cleopatra, where extensive tree damage was observed. No damage indicators were found closer to the town of Cleopatra.

tornadoes.name: Princeton
tornadoes.label: Princeton
tornadoes.notes: A second supercell in Mercer County produced a brief EF-0 tornado near U.S. Highway 65 north of Princeton on 10 June, continuing to the northeast across Finch Avenue before lifting near Muddy Creek. The tornado produced tree damage and bent over power poles on Finch Avenue.
tornadoes.timing_issue: duration over 3 hours

tornadoes.name: Alta Vista Tor
tornadoes.label: Alta Vista Tor
tornadoes.notes: A supercell thunderstorm produced its first tornado north of Weatherby in Dekalb County along NE Irwin Road. It traveled to the east-northeast and crossed into Daviess County north of Alta Vista. The tornado traveled generally along Route KK before dissipating a couple of miles west of Interstate 35. The tornado primarily produced minor to moderate tree damage on its path, consistent with spotter reports.

tornadoes.name: Alsip
tornadoes.label: Alsip
tornadoes.notes: A brief EF-0 tornado with estimated peak winds of 80 mph impacted areas roughly between W 120th Pl and W 121st St in Alsip. Most of the damage caused by the tornado consisted of uprooted or snapped trees, along with some downed power poles and lines.

tornadoes.name: Putnam County EF2
tornadoes.label: Putnam County EF2
tornadoes.notes: On Wednesday afternoon, June 10th, 2026, a severe thunderstorm resulted in an EF2 tornado developing south of Lucerne, Missouri, in southwest Putnam County. This tornado began at 3:57 PM CDT, causing minor damage to a home on 212th Street, destroying two empty grain bins, and damaging four outbuildings. Corrugated steel damage was deposited north and northeast across an open farm field toward County Road 455. Tree damage was found toward Terre Haute, MO, before the tornado intensified to EF2, causing significant damage and destruction to an expansive pole barn and two of three large grain bins near the intersection of County Road 469 and 470. The tornado continued northeast toward the intersection of 190th Street and County Road 391, here damage to an older outbuilding was surveyed. The tornado continued east along 190th Street resulting in EF1 damage to an outbuilding and trees before turning slightly southeast and strengthening back to EF2 near State Highway EE and 190th Street. Here the tornado destroyed a mobile home, with estimated max wind speeds of 125 mph. The tornado continued east causing damage to trees north of 190th Street before ending south of US Highway 136 as it crossed East Locust Creek. Special thanks to Missouri SEMA, Putnam County EM, and Putnam County commissioners office for assistance with the survey.

tornadoes.name: Lake Viking Tor
tornadoes.label: Lake Viking Tor
tornadoes.notes: The second tornado of the Dekalb/Daviess County supercell began north of Lake Viking just east of Interstate 35. It damaged trees and a manufactured home along Lilac Avenue. The tornado traveled to the east-northeast and crossed Route DD. It continued across the Grand River and caused tree damage on the south side of Jameson before dissipating. This tornado was timed to spotter reports in the area, since two supercells essentially traveled the same path.

tornadoes.name: Jameson
tornadoes.label: Jameson
tornadoes.notes: The third tornado, an EF-1, from the Dekalb/Daviess County supercell began just southeast of Jameson near Highway 13, destroying a pole barn along 235th Street. The tornado tracked northeast and caused extensive damage to several trees on a property near 250th and Route P. The path continued to the east-northeast, causing tree damage before ending just before the Grundy County line between Jameson and Trenton. The timing of this tornado was tied to spotter reports, as a second supercell traversed the same area about 30 minutes later. However, spotter reports clearly tied this to the leading supercell.

tornadoes.name: Putnam County EF0
tornadoes.label: Putnam County EF0
tornadoes.notes: The thunderstorm that developed the Lucerne - Terra Haute EF2 tornado southwest of Unionville continued northeast across Putnam County. Minor, sporadic tree damage was noted along the track of the mesocyclone into northeast Putnam County. The only damage of note was to a single family residence and one outbuilding. Minor tree damage was noted as well. The convergent damage noted was consistent with that of a brief EF0 tornado that likely developed around 4:49 PM CDT and ended at 4:51 PM CDT. Wood frame and corrugated steel construction of the home was noted, with numerous complete roof panels missing.

tornadoes.name: Laredo
tornadoes.label: Laredo
tornadoes.notes: A brief EF-0 tornado occurred near the intersection of Route E and 8th Street north of Laredo, causing some minor tree damage.

tornadoes.name: Galt
tornadoes.label: Galt
tornadoes.notes: A brief, likely rain-wrapped, EF-0 tornado occurred on the west side of Galt, damaging trees and a few grain bins in a mostly west-to-east path.

tornadoes.name: Adair County
tornadoes.label: Adair County
tornadoes.notes: Wednesday night, June 10th, 2026, an EF0 tornado developed at 6:36 PM CDT. west of US Highway 63 near Sugar Creek Conservation Area. This tornado continued east-northeast across open country, with minor damage noted to a solar panel array and trees before crossing US 63 and across open country north of Millard, MO, and south of Hwy 6. Storm chasers reported visuals of the tornado and were observed via livestreams by NWS meteorologists. Damage survey confirmed an EF-0 tornado.

tornadoes.label: Near Enterprise, KS
tornadoes.notes: Track based on input from chasers who witnessed the short track tornado in this area.

tornadoes.label: Near Navarre, KS
tornadoes.notes: Video and photos of a small tornado were provided and minor damage was noted on a storm survey in the vicinity of where the photo and video were taken.

tornadoes.name: Lincolns New Salem Tornado
tornadoes.label: Lincolns New Salem Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado spun up 3 miles northeast of Tallula, damaging a grain bin and several trees at a farmstead on Reimer Ave. It continued tracking east-northeast, damaging several trees and removing shingles from a home on State Park Rd and Lincoln New Salem Park. It crossed IL Route 97, damaging more trees in a neighborhood just south of the Athens Blacktop Rd. It then lifted 1 mile southwest of Tice before ending just before 11 pm CDT.

tornadoes.name: Athens Tornado
tornadoes.label: Athens Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado touched down along Kent St. west of Athens, and tracked southeast to Fitschen Rd. on the south edge of Athens. A number of trees were snapped along the path.

tornadoes.name: Springfield Tornado
tornadoes.label: Springfield Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado began about 3 mile west of the Springfield Capital Airport where it lofted 6,000-lb aircraft hangars and rolled an enclosed trailer. Some of the most significant damage was at the Animal Protective League animal shelter on Taintor Road. The tornado continued east-southeast, producing tree and building damage around Camp Butler and through Mechanicsburg, damaging several farm outbuildings and trees along its path. It ended about 5 miles east of Mechanicsburg just north of the Sangamon River.

tornadoes.name: Mount Pulaski-Forsyth Tornado
tornadoes.label: Mount Pulaski-Forsyth Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down about 3 miles northwest of Mount Pulaski where it did some minor tree damage. The tornado intensified as it progressed east along 900 St, where it did extensive tree damage for about a half mile, damaging numerous trees. The tornado angled southeast and crossed Hwy 54 producing more tree damage. The tornado produced mainly tree damage for the remainder of its time on the ground, dissipating about 3 miles north of Forsyth.

tornadoes.name: Argenta Tornado
tornadoes.label: Argenta Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down about 2 miles west-northwest of Argenta where it damaged an outbuilding and some trees. It progressed east through Argenta where it snapped off several trees. The tornado produced mainly tree damage as it moved east along Newburg Rd before dissipating 3 miles south of Cisco.

tornadoes.name: Bement Tornado
tornadoes.label: Bement Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down about 5 miles southwest of Bement, near the intersection of County Rd 600 and N 500 East Rd where it damaged two large trees. The tornado progressed through open fields just south of State Hwy 105, where a drone captured the rotational marks in the corn fields. The tornado removed the roof of a grain storage building and snapped two power poles where Hwy 105 turns north toward Bement. A camper was flipped over and destroyed along N 1000 East Rd, then the tornado moved northeast and cause damage to a grain bin, a couple of outbuildings and several trees along E 900 North Rd before it dissipated before reaching the county line.

tornadoes.name: 1 NNE Weeping Water Tornado
tornadoes.label: 1 NNE Weeping Water Tornado
tornadoes.notes: At approximately 5:10 AM, a tornado developed just northeast of Weeping Water near Brittini Drive and moved southeast. The tornado produced sporadic tree damage before causing the complete collapse of the walls of a farm building near Weeping Water Road and 124th Street. Based on this damage, peak winds were estimated around 100 mph. Additional tree damage was also noted on the property. The tornado dissipated before reaching Weeping Water Creek at approximately 5:14 AM.

tornadoes.name: South Cedar Creek Tornado
tornadoes.label: South Cedar Creek Tornado
tornadoes.notes: At approximately 5:15 AM, a brief tornado developed east of Weeping Water, just north of South Cedar Creek. The tornado produced sporadic tree damage, with estimated wind speeds of 65 to 74 mph. The tornado dissipated near South Cedar Creek at approximately 5:16 AM.

tornadoes.name: 2 NNW Union Tornado
tornadoes.label: 2 NNW Union Tornado
tornadoes.notes: At approximately 5:21 AM, a brief tornado developed northeast of Nehawka, Nebraska, near 12th Street and Beccard Drive, and moved southeast. The tornado caused fairly extensive tree damage at a residence, including several large broken branches. Based on this damage, peak winds were estimated around 90 mph. The tornado continued southeast, producing additional sporadic tree damage with estimated winds of 65 to 74 mph, before dissipating near 6th Avenue and Hoback Road at approximately 5:24 AM.

tornadoes.name: 4 W Thurman Tornado
tornadoes.label: 4 W Thurman Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado developed just east of the Missouri River at approximately 5:29 AM. The tornado produced minor tree damage as it tracked east towards Interstate 29. As the tornado reached Interstate 29, the tornado intensified. EF1 damage was produced at a residence located along Western Ave with most of the roof lifted off this residence. The tornado then crossed Interstate 29 and produced tree damage along the interstate before dissipating at approximately 5:31 AM.

tornadoes.name: 5 NW Tabor Tornado
tornadoes.label: 5 NW Tabor Tornado
tornadoes.notes: At approximately 5:33 AM, a brief tornado developed north of Tabor, Iowa, and moved east. The tornado produced sporadic tree damage near 235th Street and Pathfield Road, with estimated winds around 65 mph. Shortly after this damage occurred, KOAX radar displayed a tornadic debris signature associated with the tornado. The tornado was estimated to have a maximum width of 20 yards. The tornado dissipated at approximately 5:35 AM.

tornadoes.name: 4 ESE Coburg to 3 NNW Hepburn
tornadoes.label: 4 ESE Coburg to 3 NNW Hepburn
tornadoes.notes: At approximately 5:58 AM, a tornado developed just east of Coburg, Iowa, near 105th Street and K Avenue, and moved east-southeast. The tornado produced sporadic tree damage with an estimated wind speeds of 70 mph. The tornado would then track east, parallel to 110th St. Along the path, trees and farm outbuildings received damage. Max wind speeds were estimated at low-end EF1 intensity of 90 mph. The tornado would dissipate at approximately 6:08 AM near 110th St and R Ave. The estimated max width was approximately 100 yards.

tornadoes.label: Near Villisca, IA
tornadoes.notes: At approximately 6:08 AM, a tornado developed east of Stanton, Iowa, near 230th Street and Q Avenue, and moved northeast. The tornado produced tree damage on the west side of Viking Lake, including large broken limbs and uprooted trees, with estimated winds of 70 to 85 mph. The tornado then crossed to the east side of Viking Lake, where it uprooted two trees, brought down numerous large limbs, caused minor siding and roof damage to a home near 230th Street and Raspberry Drive, and snapped approximately 10 pine tree trunks near S Avenue and Aldersgate Drive. Based on this damage, winds were estimated at 90 mph. The tornado then continued northeast, collapsing the walls of an outbuilding, snapping a tree trunk, and bringing down power lines near U.S. Highway 24 and T Avenue. Based on this damage, peak winds were estimated around 105 mph. The tornado then lofted grain bins from over a mile away into the interchange of Highway 71 and Highway 34. The tornado dissipated at approximately 6:16 AM.

tornadoes.name: South of Villisca Tornado
tornadoes.label: South of Villisca Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado developed south of Villisca at approximately 6:11 AM. The tornado would track along 110th St between V Ave and Willow Ave before dissipating near the county line at 6:13 AM. Along the tornado's path, trees were damaged, a farm outbuilding lost part of the roof and wall, and a carport was destroyed. The tornado had estimated wind speeds of 90 mph earning a rating of EF1. The maximum estimated width of the tornado was approximately 50 yards.

tornadoes.name: Washburn Tornado
tornadoes.label: Washburn Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado developed just east of the Illinois River, mainly damaging trees as it tracked northeast over northwest Woodford county. The tornado strengthened in the Columbia road area, where several houses lost roofs and extensive tree damage was observed. The tornado reached peak intensity (EF3) northwest of Washburn in rural areas of southern Marshall County. Here, a log house had all walls collapsed and a nearby house lost its roof and second floor. Severe tree damage was seen here, where some trees had only trunks and large branches remaining. Extensive crop damage was also noted, with corn leaves ripped off and plants uprooted. Tornado width was measured at 930 yards at this point with estimated peak winds of 155 mph. The tornado continued east, gradually weakening while damaging trees, outbuildings, and damaging roofs of a few more houses. It dissipated in a farm field northeast of Washburn.

tornadoes.name: Ipava Tornado
tornadoes.label: Ipava Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Drone photographs taken by a trained spotter show a tornado path began in a field approximately two miles southwest of Ipava, just north of the east-west oriented portion of north County Highway 12. Drone footage of the tornado showed it continued northeast, impacting a solar farm and tossing a few solar panels. It produced some crop damage in the fields and continued towards Ipava, crossing Bernadotte Street just south of west Main Street. Video shows a very weak tornado continued across Ipava, and there was no damage evident in the footage. The tornado dissipated on the northeast side of Ipava, near the intersection of Kinsey and Mechanic Street, prior to reaching the open field.

tornadoes.name: Osage Township
tornadoes.label: Osage Township
tornadoes.notes:
This tornado track has been updated based on high-resolution satellite imagery and storm chaser video.

This tornado started in the vicinity of N 8th Road near Sandy Creek. Distinct swirl marks are evident as the tornado tracked northeast before tracking almost due east and crossing E 9th Road roughly one third of a mile south of IL-17. The tornado then continued on a northeasterly path, impacting a residence on IL-17 where it caused some roof damage, snapped a large hardwood tree about one-third of the way from the top, and downed a wooden electrical pole. The tornado then continued along IL-17, destroying multiple machine sheds in the 900 block, with debris strewn northeastward toward E 10th Rd. Storm chaser video shows at least three fast-moving subvortices as the tornado continued northeast and crossed E 10th Rd. Here, high-resolution Sentinel satellite imagery reveals significant cycloidal markings, widening to approximately 500 yards as the tornado tracked across multiple fields before appearing to weaken rapidly and lift near N 10th Rd just west of the Livingston County line.

tornadoes.name: Long Point - Streator
tornadoes.label: Long Point - Streator
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began in a field southwest of E 2600 N Road and N 190 East Road. It tracked into Long Point, where some tree damage was noted before continuing northeast with sporadic damage near Ancona and Reading Township. The tornado intensified as it crossed east of N 500 East Road, where it blew a grain bin off its foundation and dragged it along the ground for approximately 700 yards. The tornado reached its peak intensity on the southeast side of Streator near the Livingston-La Salle county line. Here, several houses along Sunbury Drive were heavily damaged. At one residence, only the inner-most walls were left standing, with debris tossed southward, upstream against the tornado path. Damage in this area was consistent with EF-3 winds around 145 mph. The tornado continued northeast before turning nearly due north, causing damage consistent with EF-2 caliber winds to several residences along E 19th Road. The tornado appears to have lifted northeast of Streator near N 1475th Road.

tornadoes.name: Rowe - Dwight
tornadoes.label: Rowe - Dwight
tornadoes.notes: The tornado appeared to start near IL Route 23 just north of Rowe before tracking northeastward across portions of central Livingston County. The tornado may not have been fully condensed to the ground or consisted of intermittent touchdowns along the first half of its path, where damage was primarily confined to trees. Based on storm chaser videos, the tornado appeared to rapidly strengthen and widen northeast of Odell while crossing IL Route 47 and approaching the unincorporated community of Blair, where several homesteads sustained roof and siding damage and several barns were destroyed. Storm chaser video depicted subvortices within the tornado as it crossed several open fields in the general area. The tornado then appeared to lift just north of IL Route 17. The tornado was likely stronger than the official rating of EF-1, though a lack of impacted damage indicators precludes a higher rating.

tornadoes.name: Morton Tornado
tornadoes.label: Morton Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado touched down about 1.5 miles south of Groveland, and moved northeast along the southern edge of Morton. A number of tree trunks were snapped, a few of which fell onto cars. It left town near the intersection of Jefferson St. and Tennessee Ave. and entered the Mayfair subdivision, causing extensive tree limb damage and damage to some shingles. It crossed I-74 about 1.5 miles east of the Washington Rd. overpass. Along Harding Rd., it impacted a couple of farmsteads, damaging an outbuilding at one of them. The tornado crossed into Woodford County about 1 mile north of Deer Creek, before lifting near county road 1200E.

tornadoes.name: Kenosha
tornadoes.label: Kenosha
tornadoes.notes: Brief tornado began on the south side of 18th street west of 72nd Ave. Two barn outbuilding structures were heavily damaged with metal roofing lofted and deposited several hundred yards downwind. Several trees were damaged, uprooted, or received large limbs damage. Tree limbs with damage toward the end of the track along 72nd Ave were blown and deposited across the street.

tornadoes.name: Harpster - Elliott
tornadoes.label: Harpster - Elliott
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began approximately 3 miles southeast of Saybrook in McLean County, where it downed a few tree branches and peeled back the metal roof of an outbuilding. The tornado crossed into Ford County shortly thereafter, where it initially damaged trees, power lines, and an outbuilding in the unincorporated community of Harpster. The tornado then impacted a campground along E 200N Road 2 miles south of Gibson City, where it rolled over and damaged several campers. Trees and farm outbuildings were also damaged at a farmstead one mile east of the campground. The tornado then tracked east-northeastward for a few more miles, primarily producing tree damage before dissipating approximately one mile south-southwest of Elliott.

tornadoes.name: St. John - Schererville
tornadoes.label: St. John - Schererville
tornadoes.notes: This tornado formed roughly at the intersection of 98th Avenue and Sheffield Avenue and then proceeded to track northeastward through St. John. Most of the damage along the tornado's roughly 5.5 mile track was confined to trees, but some roof damage was also noted, and one house also had its garage door and side wall blown out. The tornado dissipated just east of Rohrman Park shortly after crossing into Schererville.

tornadoes.name: Champaign-Urbana Tornado
tornadoes.label: Champaign-Urbana Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado touched down along N Duncan Rd near I-74 and Hwy 150 where it damaged solar panels, fencing and a few trees. It progressed across I-74 where it damaged the roof of a business and toppled a small metal tower along N Mattis Ave. The tornado progressed east and produced tree damage as well as additional roof damage to a warehouse. The tornado produced additional tree damage and an outbuilding damage as it progressed along W Oaks Rd N. The tornado crossed Hwy 45 just northeast of Frasca Field and then largely tracked east. Structural damage was mainly some roof damage close to Hwy 45, with a number of trees snapped further east.

tornadoes.name: Paxton/Loda
tornadoes.label: Paxton/Loda
tornadoes.notes: This tornado tracked east-northeastward between Paxton and Loda, destroying a couple of outbuildings, peeling shingles off of a house, blowing a couple of semi-trailers over on Interstate 57, and damaging a few trees along its slightly under 7-mile-long track.

tornadoes.name: Merrillville - Hobart
tornadoes.label: Merrillville - Hobart
tornadoes.notes: This tornado appeared to touch down just west of Hendricks Street and moved eastward through central Merrillville. Numerous homes sustained significant damage along W 64rd Ave, 61st Pl, 61st Ave, and Grand Pl, including removal of walls and roofing structures. Extensive tree damage was noted in this region, as well. The tornado continued eastward along and just north of W 61st Avenue and moved over Andrean High School, causing significant roofing damage. Thereafter, the tornado crossed Interstate 65 and then moved over S Liverpool Road, causing continued damage to trees. The tornado then tracked into the southwestern side of Hobart before lifting just southwest of W 3rd Street.

tornadoes.name: Ludlow Tornado
tornadoes.label: Ludlow Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado touched down about a third of a mile south of the Champaign and Ford County line, along County Road 2000. It peeled part of the roof off an outbuilding, and damaged some solar panels. It crossed the border about a quarter mile west of Ford County Road 2800E, causing significant damage at a farmstead. Here, the main residence lost part of its roof, an outbuilding was nearly destroyed, and a number of trees were snapped. It lifted a short time later, after crossing 2280E.

tornadoes.name: Cedar Lake
tornadoes.label: Cedar Lake
tornadoes.notes: Video footage captured this tornado forming along W 151st Avenue west of Parrish Avenue. It tracked northeast into the adjacent Lynnsway subdivision on the southwest side of Cedar Lake, where it caused minor roofing and siding damage to multiple houses and lofted trash cans and outdoor furniture into the air. The tornado then tracked east-northeastward for a few miles through the south side of Cedar Lake, primarily producing tree damage before dissipating near the Pheasant Valley Country Club.

tornadoes.name: Schneider - Hebron
tornadoes.label: Schneider - Hebron
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began near Colfax Street northeast of Schneider and caused mainly tree damage along its northeastward track, consistent with EF-0 winds near 85 mph. The tornado appears to have crossed I-65 north of E 205th Avenue. It continued into Porter County before lifting just south of Hebron.

tornadoes.name: Kickapoo Park Tornado
tornadoes.label: Kickapoo Park Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado largely paralleled I-74 to the north. Some outbuildings were significantly damaged near the start of the track, but the greatest damage was in Kickapoo State Recreation Area. Here, an estimated 250 trees were snapped or damaged by winds up to 110 mph. The tornado lifted along Hungry Hollow Rd., just before moving into Danville. Damage in Danville itself was determined to be from straight-line winds of 80 to 100 mph.

tornadoes.name: Hoopeston-Cheneyville Tornado
tornadoes.label: Hoopeston-Cheneyville Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down about a half mile south of Highway 9 east of county road 1300E, overturning an irrigation pivot. It crossed Highway 1 on the south edge of town and damaged the roof of a tractor dealership. It skirted the south edge of Hoopeston, causing damage to trees and shingles. It strengthened by the time it reached the intersection of Highway 9 and 1700E, snapping tree trunks and damaging the roof of a house. Down the road, an outbuilding was flattened, and several additional trees were snapped. It entered Cheneyville and snapped additional tree trunks; significant damage to buildings at the intersection of Highway 9 and 1900E was likely due to rear-flank downdraft winds up to 100 mph. The tornado appears to have lifted before reaching the Indiana border.

tornadoes.name: Watseka
tornadoes.label: Watseka
tornadoes.notes: This tornado tracked across the south side of Watseka before ending near the intersection of US Route 24 and IL State Route 1. Damage along the tornado's path was largely confined to trees.

tornadoes.name: Kouts
tornadoes.label: Kouts
tornadoes.notes:
A long-track tornado initially touched down near the intersection of Grand Boulevard and Clay Street just east of Interstate 65 in rural Lake County and continued northeastward into southern Porter County just north of the Kankakee River. Damage near the beginning of the path consisted of downed and uprooted trees. The tornado appeared to increase in size and intensity after crossing US Highway 231, damaging the walls and roofing of several homes near W 1000 S just north of Breyfogel Ditch.

As the tornado continued northeastward, it further strengthened and widened. The tornado reached its peak intensity of EF-3 from just north of Kouts to just west of the Porter and LaPorte county line. In this area, several homes were destroyed, and two separate sets of high tension power trusses were sheared apart and collapsed. There was significant scouring of the ground and damage to crops in this region, as well. The tornado began to weaken as it crossed into LaPorte County, where drone footage continued to show swirl marks in fields as it tracked northeast and eventually turned toward the north-northeast. The tornado then dissipated after damaging trees and residences along S 1050 W Road.

tornadoes.name: Prairie Green Township
tornadoes.label: Prairie Green Township
tornadoes.notes: This tornado destroyed an outbuilding at a farmstead about 2.5 miles northeast of Wellington. It also downed a few power poles and left a clear, narrow damage path through crops in a field to the east of N 2700 East Road and north of E 500 North Road before dissipating shortly thereafter.

tornadoes.name: Bartlett
tornadoes.label: Bartlett
tornadoes.notes: Eyewitness reports and radar data indicate that a tornado began in Pratt's Wayne Woods before quickly intensifying and tracking east-northeastward into Bartlett. The tornado produced a concentrated area of EF-1 damage at a shopping center at the intersection of Sutton Road and Stearns Road, where roofing material was peeled off of buildings, brick columns and metal fencing were blown out at a garden center, and all of the gas pumps at a gas station were blown over. The tornado continued to produce extensive tree damage at Beaver Pond Park and in the subdivisions to the east of the shopping center before dissipating east of Bartlett Road.

tornadoes.name: Boswell - Atkinson
tornadoes.label: Boswell - Atkinson
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began approximately one and half miles southwest of Boswell, initially damaging an outbuilding and peeling a few roof shingles off of a house at a farmstead on S 400 W Road. The tornado tracked east-northeastward and blew down a barn and power lines along S 200 W Road before curving off more towards the northeast. It then blew a press box off of the bleachers at Daugherty Speedway and into a nearby power pole and field before reaching peak intensity as it tracked into the unincorporated community of Chase. There, a grain elevator and multiple associated grain bins were destroyed, and a couple of tree trunks were snapped. The tornado then continued to the east-northeast, snapping multiple rows of power poles from Meridian Road to S 200 E Road and downing another set of power poles in the unincorporated community of Atkinson. As the tornado reached E 200 S and S 600 E roads, it downed more power poles; downed a few trees; damaged the roof, chimney, and gutter of a house; and blew a chicken coop into a field, killing 30 chickens. The tornado likely dissipated shortly after crossing S 600 E Road.

tornadoes.name: Ade - Mount Ayr
tornadoes.label: Ade - Mount Ayr
tornadoes.notes: This tornado formed near the intersection of S 500 W and W 1075 S roads in Washington Township. It tracked northeastward through rural portions of central Newton County for several miles before ending near Curtis Creek Country Club in Newton Township in western Jasper County, west of Rensselaer. Along its over 15-mile-long path, the tornado damaged or destroyed multiple farm outbuildings, downed several trees and tree limbs, downed a few power poles, and destroyed a grain bin.

tornadoes.name: Morocco
tornadoes.label: Morocco
tornadoes.notes: This tornado touched down near S 600 W Road just north of the intersection of W 550 S Road before tracking northeast across mainly open farmland in western Newton County. The tornado damaged a farm outbuilding along with several trees near S 550 W Road consistent with 85 mph winds and an EF-0 rating. From there, the tornado continued northeast through the town of Morocco, where a corridor of tree damage occurred, including near the town park. Additional tree damage across the broader Morocco area was consistent with straight-line winds in excess of 60 mph. After exiting Morocco, the tornado crossed US-41 before turning to the north-northeast across open farmland, where damage was confined to mainly trees and irrigation pivots. The tornado ended just east of the intersection of E 300 N Road and N 300 E Road. No injuries or fatalities were reported with this tornado.

tornadoes.name: Northern Warren
tornadoes.label: Northern Warren
tornadoes.notes: A fast-moving QLCS brought sporadic tree and farm structure damage to portions of northern Warren county. Damage began near West County Road 850N with an uprooted tree with additional minor damage to a barn after the tornado crossed US 41. The most significant damage was noted near the intersection of Rainsville Road and State Road 26 where multiple trees were downed and corn fields showed clear convergence. The tornado tracked mostly through open fields with additional tree damage noted on North 200E and North 300E before dissipating just south of the Benton county line.

tornadoes.name: Naperville - Lisle
tornadoes.label: Naperville - Lisle
tornadoes.notes: An EF-0 tornado with peak winds of around 80 mph, a path length of around 1.3 miles, and a maximum width of around 150 yards began near the intersection of Gartner Road and Olesen Drive and continued northeast through the Huntington Hills and Olesen Estates neighborhoods of Naperville. Damage through both neighborhoods was in a very narrow path of around 50 to 75 yards and consisted of snapped and uprooted trees. The tornado appeared to broaden in width while crossing Naper Boulevard and passing over Huntington Apartments, where a roughly 150-yard-wide swath of extensive tree damage was noted. The tornado appeared to lift just west of Benedictine Parkway.

tornadoes.name: Hickory Hills - Garfield Ridge
tornadoes.label: Hickory Hills - Garfield Ridge
tornadoes.notes: An EF-2 tornado with peak winds of around 120 mph, a path length of around 8.4 miles, and a maximum width of 350 yards began in the Spears-Pioneer Woods Forest Preserve north of 95th St. and continued northeast into northern Hickory Hills, where tree damage and some light pole damage occurred. The tornado strengthened in intensity to EF-2 level on the southeast side of Justice, where two apartments had roofs fully removed near 83rd St. and Roberts Rd. The tornado maintained EF-2 strength into Bridgeview, where additional roof damage was noted near 79th St. and Oketo Ave. The tornado then weakened as it moved into the Clearing and Garfield Ridge community areas of Chicago west of Midway Airport, where tree, shingle, roof, and siding damage occurred. The tornado lifted north of Midway Airport around 52nd St. and Leamington Ave. after producing additional tree damage.

tornadoes.name: Barry1
tornadoes.label: Barry1
tornadoes.notes: updated track based on new information

tornadoes.name: Delphi
tornadoes.label: Delphi
