tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado touched down near the Tippecanoe River causing tree and home damage to several properties along Tippecanoe Ranch Road and Horshoe Bend Road, crossing the Tippecanoe River 2 to 3 times. Two roofs showed significant damage. The tornado then made an easterly turn, impacting two homes along US 421 before impacting a hog farm near County Road 500N causing roof damage. Signs of ground circulation was noted in the fields near the farm. The tornado then dissipated in an open filed southwest of 550N.

tornadoes.name: NorthernCarroll
tornadoes.label: NorthernCarroll
tornadoes.notes: Drone footage revealed clear convergence within a grove of trees south of a home south of West County Road 122 North. The tree damage began and ended within a grove of trees with little to no damage to nearby properties.

tornadoes.name: Georgetown
tornadoes.label: Georgetown
tornadoes.notes: Drone footage from Cass County Emergency Management shows evidence of a tornado southeast of Lake Cicott. Dozens, if not hundreds, of trees were damaged by the brief tornado along with instances of property damage. The tornado appears to have begun over a wooded area near the termination of S CR 750 W (South of W CR 50 S). Here, a few trees were uprooted followed by an area of trees snapped near the base. Based on a convergent signature, the tornado appears to have curved quickly to the northeast, taking a few roof panels off a nearby outbuilding. Now approaching the bend in the road of W CR 50 S, the tornado appears to have intensified sharply with intense destruction and uprooting of trees, resulting in a clear convergent pattern. Nearby buildings appear to have avoided significant damage. On yet another sharp jaunt to the north, now headed to a farmstead, the tornado continued to destroy trees but also destroyed two barns, removed portions of roof off three other outbuildings, and completely destroyed a grain bin. Debris was gathered at the base of a nearby tree line. Aloft, a few large branches appear to have been snapped. Beyond this, trees are untouched suggesting the tornado lifted.

tornadoes.label: Near Twelve Mile, IN
tornadoes.notes: Drone footage provided by Cass County Emergency Management confirmed an EF-1 tornado occurred within a line of severe thunderstorms across northeast Cass County. The tornado began just south of County Road 325 N between County Road 400 E and 450 E where the roof of a barn was damaged. The tornado then tracked northeast and produced noticeable scouring of crops. The tornado destroyed a 40ft pole barn on County Road 375 N and caused additional damage to the roofs of barns along County Road 500 E. The tornado dissipated by County Road 425 N where some minor tree damage was observed.

tornadoes.name: Plymouth, IN
tornadoes.label: Plymouth, IN
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado spun up south of 8A on King Rd, uprooting or snapping multiple trees and causing damage to a barn. The tornado continued northeast, flipping a center pivot before entering a grove of trees causing several snapped trees. The circulation moved quickly northeast, knocking down a few more trees north of 8A Rd. The tornado quickly lifted on the north side of 8A Rd after doing significant damage to a barn.

tornadoes.name: Argos
tornadoes.label: Argos
tornadoes.notes: A brief EF-0 tornado with maximum winds estimated at 75 mph touched down on the far southwest side of Argos in Marshall County. Damage along the path was largely confined to trees. Special thanks to the Marshall County EMA and Argos FD for assisting with the survey.

tornadoes.label: Near Wabash, IN
tornadoes.notes: A tornado touched down in the vicinity of W 400 S and S 300 W on the southwest edge of Wabash. At this location, a number of wood power poles were snapped at the base. The tornado then raced northeast to Glendale Dr., McKibben St., and Barkley Dr. in Wabash where a number of homes of damaged. Homes lost shingles or even portions of the roof decking. Debris was lofted into nearby tree lines. One dual-axle fifth-wheel camper was tipped over. Insulation and dirt splatter was noted at a few different homes. Beyond Berkley Dr., damage was limited to instances of small limbs down in the neighborhood. Farther northeast, in the vicinity of Lafountaine Ave and W Waterworks Rd., an outbuilding was destroyed when its south-facing door appeared to be blown, in resulting in a collapse of walls and loss of roof panels. The tornado reached its peak intensity as it moved over properties on W Water Works road. Here, two injuries were reported as homes lost windows and roof decking, and a manufactured home was shifted several feet off its foundation. Dirt and insulation splatter was noted in these areas. Beyond S Meridian Rd., damage was once again limited to instances of trees or branches down. Powerlines were down near E Baumbauer Rd, where the tornado appears to have lifted.

tornadoes.name: Bourbon
tornadoes.label: Bourbon
tornadoes.notes: Another tornado, perhaps from the same parent circulation that spawned the Argos tornado, developed on the northeast side of Bourbon in Marshall County. The tornado touched down in a field, with tree damage observed in the distance just east of Beech Road and north of 10B Road. The tornado raced northeastward, striking a property where two old barns collapsed and a third was damaged. Metal roofing material was also blown off, and several trees sustained major damage, consistent with an EF-1 rating. The tornado then crossed the county line into Kosciusko County, where it impacted multiple Amish properties. In this area, a camper was flipped, several softwood trees were snapped, and maximum winds were estimated at 90 to 100 mph.

tornadoes.label: Near Andrews, IN
tornadoes.notes: A tornado developed southwest of Andrews, racing northeast toward Huntington. At least two properties on W Division Rd were impacted, as indicated by a loss of shingles, siding, and roof panels. Numerous trees were damaged as well, including trees snapped. Near the intersection of W 100 N and N 800 W, additional tree damage was observed and an outbuilding lost several roof panels. Along W 200 N, a number of trees were damaged at one property. Across the street, a mobile home lost its roof. The tornado appears to have lifted prior to reaching the Yake Subdivision, just south of the Wabash River. In the subdivision, isolated tree branches were down.

tornadoes.label: Near Mount Etna, IN
tornadoes.notes: A tornado touched down north of Pleasant Plain, at a residence on S 500 W. Here, nearly two dozen trees were damaged, including multiple trees snapped at least halfway up their trunks. Tree damage appeared to continue into a tree line off to the northeast. Throughout its nearly 8-mile long path to the northeast, sporadic instances of tree damage occurred until it approached State Route 5, just northwest of I-69. Here, the tornado caused almost total destruction to a newly built barndominium. Only the eastern wall was left standing with debris lofted at least 100 yards into adjacent fields. Tree damage continued east-northeast of here where at least two tree trunks were snapped. The tornado lifted just east of I-69, along S 200 E. Many thanks to Huntington County Emergency Management who helped document this tornado path.

tornadoes.label: Near Huntington, IN
tornadoes.notes: In an open area north of US 24 and east of State Route 9, an incredibly brief tornado appears to have touched down and impacted a single residence. Here, a two-story home completely lost its roof and debris was deposited into adjacent fields. Hardly any rafters remain and no roof decking is present. Intense dirt and insulation splatter was noted on the east and north side of the home. Additionally, a detached garage to the south-southeast of the home was demolished by the tornado. A property less then 500 yards to the northeast was not impacted, suggesting the tornado quickly lifted beyond 600 N.

tornadoes.name: Shipshewana
tornadoes.label: Shipshewana
tornadoes.notes:
The same storm that produced the EF-2 tornado in Bristol, IN continued eastward into LaGrange County. While radar suggested the correlation coefficient signature persisted between Bristol and this tornado (albeit weaker), damage was very sparse, and there was not enough confidence or evidence to definitively connect the two areas of concern. Due to a 10-mile separation, it was determined to treat these as two separate tornadoes.

The tornado in LaGrange paralleled SR 120, producing an impressive swath of tree damage and causing visible damage to barns and center pivots. Given the time elapsed between the storm and the ground survey, it is likely some homes had already been repaired. The circulation reached a maximum width of 0.75 miles on the north side of Shipshewana, with a maximum intensity estimated to be EF-1 at 100 mph. The tornado occluded on the western side of Twin Lakes before a broader swath of straight-line wind damage took over in the Howe, IN and Sturgis, MI areas.

tornadoes.label: Near Pennville, IN
tornadoes.notes: Drone footage provided by Jay County Emergency Management confirmed a brief EF-0 tornado occurred within a line of severe thunderstorms across northwest Jay County. The tornado began just south of 550 N where a barn had the roof blown off. There was also some roof damage to a nearby house and several trees were snapped off. Debris was lofted well northeast into the nearby fields. Debris was observed all the way to State Road 1 where additional minor tree and roof damage was observed. The tornado dissipated shortly after crossing State Road 1.

tornadoes.name: Johnson/Shelby
tornadoes.label: Johnson/Shelby
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down west of Campbell road and impacted several farm buildings along Campbell road. One of the farm buildings was completely destroyed with debris scattered into an open field to the east. The tornado then mostly traveled over farm fields in eastern Johnson county before impacting two homes along Rocklane Road. Debris from a damaged outbuilding near the first home on Rocklane Road was picked up and thrown about 650 yards to the northeast. The tornado continued into Shelby county where it impacted one home along West 525 North before traveling through open fields and impacting one additional home on 600W. The tornado then tracked mostly through open fields, impacting a home south of Clover Village before it crossed Interstate 74 and passed harmlessly through several additional fields. There was another concentrated area of damage near 75W and 600N where widespread tree damage and minor home damage was noted. It then dissipated in an open field near Hill Branch Creek. The tornado may have lifted briefly along the path.

tornadoes.name: Timberhurst
tornadoes.label: Timberhurst
tornadoes.notes: A tornado embedded within a line of severe thunderstorms developed Thursday night in extreme southeast LaGrange County. Around Taylor Lake and Lake of the Woods, damage to electrical poles, along with impressive tree damage in spots, was determined to be consistent with an EF-1 rating, with maximum winds estimated at 90 mph. The tornado then raced northeastward into Steuben County. As the parent cell merged with another portion of the line, the tornado took a more easterly turn, impacting portions of western and northern Angola. Much of the damage along the path was inflicted on trees, suggesting the tornado may have occasionally lifted off the surface. Special thanks to Steuben County Emergency Management for their assistance with this survey.

tornadoes.name: Farmland
tornadoes.label: Farmland
tornadoes.notes: A weak tornado touched down in a field northwest of a tree line west of County Road 675N. It then crossed another tree line and traveled through a corn field with drone footage revealing a clear circulation and path within the corn. It then impacted a home north of the intersection of County Road 675N and 100N. It pushed and rotated an RV, ripped off an awning and ripped a 500 gallon propane tank off the concrete block. The drone footage then shows the circulation ends east of 675W.

tornadoes.name: Avondale
tornadoes.label: Avondale
tornadoes.notes: During the evening of Saturday June 13, 2026 a line of damaging thunderstorms moved across the Kansas City Metropolitan Area. At 8:33 PM CDT, a tornado formed on the leading edge of the line near Avondale, MO. The tornado produced sporadic tree damage near the Harrah's Casino before moving over the Missouri River. Sporadic tree damage was found near Birmingham, MO before the tornado crossed the Missouri River near MO-291 and produced substantial tree damage in LaBenite Park. The track could not be followed east of the park and no more damage was found further, so the tornado likely ended east of the park around 8:50 PM CDT. Thank you to Sugar Creek PD for their assistance with the damage survey.

tornadoes.name: Liberty
tornadoes.label: Liberty
tornadoes.notes: During the evening of Saturday June 13, 2026 a line of damaging thunderstorms moved across the Kansas City Metropolitan Area. At 8:47 PM CDT, a tornado formed on the leading edge of the line in Liberty, MO. The tornado produced sporadic tree damage as it moved northeast through multiple residential areas and farm fields. The tornado lifted at 8:54 PM CDT approximately 2 miles east of Liberty.

tornadoes.name: Fidelity Tornado
tornadoes.label: Fidelity Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The National Weather Service storm survey determined that an EF-1 tornado with peak winds of 90mph touched down 1 mile east southeast of Fidelity. The tornado lifted and rolled a secured carport before moving to the east northeast. Multiple trees were were uprooted or snapped off between 4 and 6 feet up along an intermittent path to a home along County Road 120. There were multiple 2 to 3 foot in diameter trees downed in a convergent pattern, with a home suffering significant roof and structural damage from the fallen tree. In addition, a truck was crushed under the a tree before the tornado lifted just east of the home in an open field.

tornadoes.name: Purdy
tornadoes.label: Purdy
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado touched down along Highway 97 to the south of Capps Creek. The intermittent tornado path tracked to the east-northeast before lifting just west of Highway 37, between Monett and Purdy. Several uprooted trees and large branches snapped along the path. Walls collapsed on two farm outbuildings, with sheet metal tossed over 300 yards.

tornadoes.name: Butterfield
tornadoes.label: Butterfield
tornadoes.notes: A tornado began near Farm Road 1078, just to the northwest of Butterfield. NWS ground surveys concluded that the tornado path tracked to the east across Highway 37. A couple of old wooden power poles snapped or were brought down along Highway 37. Several uprooted trees and large branches snapped along the path. Sentinel-2 satellite data analysis revealed that the tornado continued to the northeast, crossing State Highway U, producing an intermittent path of tree damage about 6.6 miles long. Satellite data revealed the tornado was 350 yards at its widest point with estimated max winds of 85 mph.

tornadoes.name: Conneautville Tornado
tornadoes.label: Conneautville Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
A National Weather Service Cleveland storm survey determined that a brief EF-0 tornado touched down on the west side of Conneautville, Pennsylvania, at about 4:10 PM EDT on Sunday, June 14, 2026.

The tornado left a path of damage, uprooting several trees and snapping large limbs along Mulberry Lane and Mulberry Street. The circulation then moved east across Mulberry Street, causing additional tree damage before dissipating shortly thereafter. Additionally, several trees were uprooted and snapped along State Highway 198.

Based on the observed damage, the tornado's maximum winds were estimated at 85 mph, yielding an EF-0 rating. The tornado was 100 yards wide. It was brief and produced a relatively short damage path before evolving into straight-line thunderstorm winds.

Although the tornadic circulation ended, strong straight-line winds persisted south of the tornado path. These winds caused additional damage, including several trees downed across the railroad tracks near Main Street and Smith Avenue. Maximum straight-line wind speeds reached 80 mph.
tornadoes.timing_issue: start and end time are identical

tornadoes.name: Crawford County Stoltz Tornado
tornadoes.label: Crawford County Stoltz Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
A National Weather Service Cleveland storm survey determined that a brief EF-1 tornado touched down in central Crawford County at approximately 4:28 PM EDT, south of Dibble Hill Road and east of Theuret Hill Road, and tracked southeast.

The tornado snapped several large tree limbs near the point of touchdown before crossing Stoltz Road, where several large trees were uprooted and fell onto a detached garage. A power pole snapped and fell toward the northwest even as the tornado moved southeast. Leaves and hay debris were scattered and pasted across the east side of a barn and nearby structures, indicating rotational winds. Additional trees were snapped and uprooted south of the property and within a tree line to the east.

Based on the damage, maximum winds were estimated at 90 mph, yielding an EF-1 rating. The tornado had an estimated maximum width of 75 yards.

The National Weather Service Cleveland thanks the Crawford County EMA for its assistance during the storm survey.

tornadoes.name: Leimbach Road Tornado
tornadoes.label: Leimbach Road Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
A National Weather Service Cleveland storm survey determined that a brief tornado touched down in central Crawford County near Leimbach Road at approximately 4:29 PM EDT. The tornado touched down west of Leimbach Road and north of Double Hill Road, then moved generally east-southeast.

Damage consisted primarily of snapped and uprooted trees. Several trees were snapped near the point of touchdown, and a falling tree clipped and damaged a well-constructed detached garage. As the tornado crossed Leimbach Road, several large hardwood trees were uprooted. The fallen trees were oriented toward the northeast, consistent with the localized tornadic wind field despite the tornado's overall east-southeast movement.

Based on the observed damage, maximum wind speeds were estimated at 93 mph, yielding an EF-1 tornado rating. The tornado had an estimated maximum width of 50 yards and produced a short, intermittent damage path before dissipating.

tornadoes.name: Anita Tornado
tornadoes.label: Anita Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
With the guidance of Jefferson County EMA, a survey team from NWS Pittsburgh evaluated damage from Sunday's storms in Jefferson County, PA. The team has confirmed that the damage observed was the result of a tornado.

Damage was first seen in a wooded area bounded by Nickles Road and London Road, mainly in the form of sporadic snapped limbs.

As the storm emerged from the wooded area, it snapped softwood trees at a farmstead near Burns and Anita Oliveburg Road.

The tornado weakened briefly as it progressed eastward, with intermittent damage to limbs along Anita Oliveburg Road and Blocks Rd, including one on a shed.

After crossing to Knox Dale Road, the tornadic circulation strengthened and grew in size, and damage became considerably more consistent and notable. Beginning here and continuing northeast toward Route 310, large swaths of healthy and sturdy hardwood and softwood trees were snapped and uprooted, most notably near Team Road and along an adjacent hillside. On this hillside was the most significant damage, where almost no tree was left intact. Despite the increase in intensity, damage to adjacent structures appeared limited, suggesting the gradient in wind speed across the tornadic circulation was sharp.

**NEW** Based on drone video and photography, wind speed along the segment of the path from Knox Dale Road along Team Road was estimated to be up to 115 mph. This tornado has been upgraded to EF2 strength.***

After descending the hill along Route 310 toward Shane Dr, the circulation weakened only slightly, and damage continued, consisting of snapped and uprooted trees. Also in this area, a home lost its carport and suffered light damage to siding and roof material. Here wind was most consistent with 90-100 mph speed.

***NEW***Damage to a barn and trees along Graffius Ave Ext was brought to the survey team's attention on Tuesday, enabling the survey team to extend the prior path over the hillside adjacent to Shane Dr.***

The most significant observed damage is consistent with EF2 wind speed (max wind 115 mph).

No tornadic damage was reported elsewhere across Jefferson County. Additional extensive searches for damage were conducted in the Ringgold area, and near Corsica, to no avail.

As of this update, the tornado's path is updated to 3.8 miles long, with a maximum width of 300 yd.

NWS Pittsburgh is grateful for the assistance of Jefferson County EMA, local township fire department personnel, and the public for their damage reports and aerial imagery that facilitated the completion of this survey.

tornadoes.name: Cochranton Tornado
tornadoes.label: Cochranton Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
A National Weather Service Cleveland storm survey determined that an EF-1 tornado touched down at approximately 4:51 PM EDT on Sunday, June 14, 2026, along Lippert Road, just east of the intersection with Mallory Road in Crawford County.

The tornado tracked east along Lippert Road, causing significant damage to one residence, including roof damage, the loss of an attached porch, damage to four vehicles, displacement of an RV approximately 50 feet, and damage to a garage roof. An additional six homes sustained minor damage, including damage to roofs, siding, and windows.

As the tornado continued east, numerous trees were blown down, blocking driveways and roadways. Several large limbs snapped and fell onto a barn and a nearby home. The tornado gradually weakened and dissipated northwest of the intersection of Lippert Road and Vincent Road.

Based on the observed damage, maximum winds were estimated at 90 mph, resulting in an EF-1 rating. The tornado had an estimated maximum width of 50 yards.

The National Weather Service Cleveland appreciates the assistance provided for this storm survey and thanks Crawford County EMA for their support in documenting the damage.

tornadoes.label: Near Salem Heights, OH
tornadoes.notes:
Tornado damage was first noted near the intersection of Cider Mill Road and Georgetown Road, with some trees snapped and uprooted. As the tornado travelled southeast, it ripped off a metal roof of a business on State Route 9 and lofted pieces of the metal sheet 800ft into neighboring properties and into the trees. Several trees in this location were also snapped half way up the base or uprooted. Additional damage was noted, again to trees along Steward Rd and Hunt Road. Here, trees were uprooted and snapped, bringing down a power pole. A house also had some shingles removed and three large pines uprooted. A definitive path continued to the south and east with additional damage noted along Depot Road, State Route 45, Salem Grange Road, Lisbon Road and just south of State route 558. All of this damage was to trees. The tornado then lifted just west of State Route 11, near Lower Elkton Road, where damage became much more sporadic and more indicative of straight-line winds.

The National Weather Service would like to thank Columbiana County Emergency Management for assistance on this survey.

tornadoes.label: Near Titusville, PA
tornadoes.notes:
UPDATE: tornado track has been extended, and peak speed has been raised to 95 mph based on several damage points noted in high-resolution satellite imagery.

Updated Narrative:

Damage began just west of Stone Spring House Road in a wooded area, where large tree branches were broken. It crossed to an area south of Breedtown Road, with a continuing swath of fallen trees.

A delayed report of a home with roof damage south of the Titusville Airport runway was conveyed to NWS Pittsburgh by local Fire Department personnel. This location is coincident with radar indication of very strong, compact rotation off of the Pleasantville radar, suggesting the tornadic circulation was ongoing.

Additional damage near Dempseytown Greshem Rd, Fairview Rd and Barker Rd also was brought to the attention of NWS Pittsburgh, also near the continuing radar-indicated compact vortex. A notable swath of tree damage has since was noted in high-resolution satellite data in the wooded area north of Fairview Road, continuing across Myers Ln and almost to Cherrytree Rd, suggesting the tornado was ongoing here with vigorous intensity.

One last pocket of damage was noted near Fairview Road/Route 8, coincident with the weakening tornado. Based on the high-resolution satellite data and radar data from the nearby Climavision radar, the tornado has been upgraded to EF1 intensity, and the track has been extended beyond its original endpoint.

The tornado appears to have weakened rapidly thereafter as the vortex became disorganized amid a surge in outflow.

A broad (almost 3.0 miles in width) swath of damage to trees from Wilson Mills to Bradleytown/Plum Corner to Sunville to Wallaceville appears to be caused by a strong surge of wind on the southern flank of a mesovortex that crossed this region at the same time that the tornado to the north was beginning to form. High-resolution satellite data has a stronger signal of more intense damage near Rice Road/Wallaceville Road.

NWS Pittsburgh appreciates the large number of photos and reports provided by residents in the affected areas that have enabled us to identify damage swaths in northern Venango County more completely.

tornadoes.label: Near Negley, OH
tornadoes.notes: Cell that produced the tornado northwestward over Salem continued to track southeastward toward Negley OH with a much weaker presentation on radar then it had prior. Just before the storm reached the border, another tightening of the couplet was noted coincident with a swath of damage along and south of Darlington/Cannelton Road, with several trees downed along the Youngstown & Southern Railroad tracks and on a property just across the PA line into Beaver County. At this location, an awning of a garage was ripped off and flipped over the garage from south to north as trees were snapped and uprooted through the property. This would be where the tornado would be it's strongest before beginning to weaken as it moved to the south and west. Some tree damage was noted just south of Cannelton Road before Watts Mills Road but no additional damage was noted east of there. Pending additional aerial surveys, the track could be extended but the radar not long after this location a storm developing ahead of this one most likely interacted with a disturbed tornadogenesis.

tornadoes.name: Moraine1
tornadoes.label: Moraine1
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service in Pittsburgh concluded an EF1 tornado formed just north of Moraine State Park on Sunday June 14th.

The tornado started near Patterson Road, west of West Park Road, then moved east-southeast, snapping large branches and a few trees near the trunk along Cornelius Road. The largest amount of tree damage was observed on West Park Road where an old barn roof was lifted off and numerous large trees lost larger branches.

Toward the end of its track, the tornado curved northeastward near Mount Union and Reichert Roads before weakening.

tornadoes.label: Near West Mayfield, PA
tornadoes.notes: Concentrated damage was first noted by Darlington Road and Clayton Road, which is coincident with a tightening couplet on the radar. Damage in this location was mainly to trees, with large branches snapped and one tree uprooted. Damage then continued along Clayton road and in the neighborhood just south of Clayton Road. Some siding was ripped off of a home on George St and trees were snapped off at varying levels in a southeastward direction. A garage was smashed after a portion of a pine tree was sheared off at its top. Tree damage was noted until around 27th street, when the tornado appears to have lifted and the radar signature weakens.

tornadoes.label: Near West Liberty, PA
tornadoes.notes:
A second track is evident from a recently reported damage swath across northern Butler County beginning in the wooded area west of Alexander Road and ending in an area near Berkley Rd and Prospect Rd.

Along this swath, the most intense damage was observed near the start of the track along Alexander Rd., where a large number of trees were uprooted or had trunks snapped. The scope of trees impacted and degree of damage here is consistent with wind speed of 100 mph.

The circulation began to weaken with eastward movement, and curved northward toward the end of its cycle.

A third mesovortex circulation appears to have formed in its stead, beginning a third tornado track in an area bounded by Burton Dr, Berkley Rd and West Liberty Rd.

NWS Pittsburgh appreciates the photo and video imagery provided by a local resident that enabled us to be able to identify this swath with greater completeness.

tornadoes.label: Near Unionville, PA
tornadoes.notes:
A third tornado along this mesovortex family began in a wooded area bounded by Burton Rd, West Liberty Rd, and Barkley Rd, tracking east-southeast across Muddy Creek Dr and SR8 before dissipating along Euclid Rd.

This storm largely snapped large branches from hardwood trees. No structural damage was observed.

Imagery from drones and ground observations during and just after the storm confirm damage east of SR8 likely was the result of the dissipating tornado.

Damage along this swath was consistent with wind speed up to 85 mph, leading to this tornado's EF0 rating.

NWS Pittsburgh appreciates the photo and video imagery provided to us that have enabled us to establish this track more completely.

tornadoes.label: Near Coudersport, PA
tornadoes.timing_issue: start and end time are identical

tornadoes.label: Near Kirkwood, PA
tornadoes.notes: A storm survey team from The National Weather Service office in State College confirmed an EF-1 tornado near Kirkwood in Lancaster County. Maximum winds of 90-100 mph snapped several tree trunks and large limbs. The damage began on Wesley Rd between Puseyville Rd and Noble Rd in Little Britain Township at approximately 9:32 PM EDT on Sunday, Jun 14. Over the next 5 minutes, the tornado continued into Colerain Township, producing sporadic damage including damage to trees on Noble Rd near White Rock Rd and damage to power poles on Kirkwood Pike near Morrison Mill Rd.

tornadoes.name: Belle Union
tornadoes.label: Belle Union
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down east of US 231 with the first area of damage occurring along County Road 250 East with significant damage to a mobile home. The tornado then moved along 600S with damage noted to two groves of trees between 425E and 550E. The tornado also impacted two homes and destroyed one barn in that area. The tornado then moved mostly through farm fields in eastern Putnam county with the tornado likely skipping at times before it ended just on the Morgan county side.

tornadoes.name: Linby Tornado
tornadoes.label: Linby Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A brief EF1 tornado, with peak winds of 90 mph, developed just south of Pekin, IA, impacting areas from Pekin Community Schools east-southeast towards Linby, IA. At Pekin Schools, softwood trees were snapped above the base in a narrow area just north of the football field. There were also portions of a metal roof peeled off of an outbuilding. The tornado blew down a chain link fence near the softball diamond, then damaged one of the softball dugouts and depositing the debris along the trees southeast of the softball diamond. The tornado then moved east-southeast towards Linby, where several broken tree branches and sheared trees were reported, along with a hardwood tree being uprooted.

tornadoes.name: Monmouth Tornado
tornadoes.label: Monmouth Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A short-lived EF-1 tornado developed in Monmouth Illinois and tracked southeast through town for 1.3 miles, with estimated maximum winds of 100 mph. Along the tornado path, structural damage was observed in the heart of Monmouth, with a few buildings seeing roofing damage, many windows blown out, and part of their brick walls damaged. Some houses also saw loss of shingles. Otherwise, a lot of damage was observed to trees along a clear convergent path, with numerous snapped, uprooted, and a lot of trees with downed large branches throughout. Some of these large tree sections were downed on houses as well.

tornadoes.name: Warsaw Tornado
tornadoes.label: Warsaw Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A brief EF1 tornado uniquely tracked across three states. This developed just inside Lee County, Iowa, with peak winds of 105 mph, and tracked southeast through Clark County, Missouri. It then continued across the Mississippi River into Hancock County, Illinois, impacting northern parts of Warsaw. This tornado persisted for about 1.3 miles, doing damage largely to numerous trees, with concentrated snapping including along the banks of the Mississippi River, as shown by drone footage. There also was damage to two gas station canopies along US Highway 61 in Missouri.

tornadoes.label: Near Enterprise, AL
tornadoes.notes: A tornado briefly touched down just west of Coppinville Junior High School. The tornado damaged an awning on the westernmost building of the school and tossed some debris around the lawn. The tornado then crossed a wooded area snapping some branches before lifting northwest of Thornbird Loop. The track was flown by drone and video footage also captured the tornado. Damage was minor, consistent with EF0 strength with maximumwind estimated to be 70 mph.

tornadoes.name: Springfield Tornado
tornadoes.label: Springfield Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado first touched down in southern Menard county and moved southeast into Salisbury. In town it mainly did tree damage, but also damaged a garage and roof of an adjacent home. As it continued southeast into northern Springfield, it continued to do mainly tree damage. As it exited the city on the northeast side, it blew in the garage door of a business. As it moved east-southeast it continued to do only tree damage and actually followed the same path as the June 10th EF1 tornado. The tornado ended about 2 miles west of Mechanicsburg.

tornadoes.name: Elon, IA to Boscobel, WI
tornadoes.label: Elon, IA to Boscobel, WI
tornadoes.notes: This long-track tornado developed about 5 miles east of Waukon, IA and continued tracking ESE, crossing the Mississippi River at Lock and Dam 9. It continued southeast through Crawford County before lifting just before reaching the Wisconsin River. Nearly continuous tree damage occurred along its path, significant in some areas. Other damage included destruction of some farm outbuildings and minor damage to a few residences. Damage along the 33 mile path was mostly EF0 to EF1 in magnitude, with localized pockets of EF2 damage to trees and powerlines.

tornadoes.name: Blue Mound Tornado
tornadoes.label: Blue Mound Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado began in northern Christian County in the Griswold Conservation Area, causing extensive tree damage throughout the property. It crossed the county line into Macon County, damaging more trees and structures in Blue Mound, including the roof of Meridian Elementary School. It also destroyed 2 grain bins south of the school. It tracked east-southeast, taking down electrical transmission lines and numerous large tree branches. It crossed US-51 and tracked east-southeast into Shelby County where it damaged more trees and electrical transmission lines along the Shelby/Macon county line. The tornado lifted 3 miles northeast of Moweaqua along N 1000 East Rd.

tornadoes.name: Bethany Tornado
tornadoes.label: Bethany Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down about 4 miles southwest of Bethany in northeast Christian County where it snapped a softwood tree trunk and removed large branches from hardwood trees. It continued east, crossing the county line into Moultrie County and damaging more trees along its path. It lifted near County Road 300 N, about 2 miles south of Bethany.

tornadoes.name: Grant - Iowa County, WI
tornadoes.label: Grant - Iowa County, WI
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed just to the southeast of Boscobel and exhibited a weak and diffuse path for much of its existence, with an RFD interacting with and disrupting the tornado circulation from eastern Grant County into Iowa County. The majority of the damage caused by this tornado in Grant County was EF0 with pockets of EF1 damage, consisting of significant tree damage and some heavily damaged farm outbuildings. The tornado intensified slightly into Iowa County as the RFD became more of a driver in the damage field.

tornadoes.name: Ridgeway
tornadoes.label: Ridgeway
tornadoes.notes: Tornado appears to have started southwest of Ridgeway, hitting the Town of Ridgeway salt shed near Highway 18/151. It then tracked to the southeast and destroyed a metal shed along County Road H. Otherwise, sporadic tree damage was noted along the end of the path with rear flank downdraft winds occurring to the southwest-south of the of the path. Some tree damage was noted east of the end of the path but appeared to fan out and not be a path near County Rd K and Mounds View Rd.

tornadoes.name: Charleston-Mattoon Tornado
tornadoes.label: Charleston-Mattoon Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado developed 4 miles north of Mattoon and tracked southeast, damaging trees, homes, and electrical transmission lines as it crossed US Highway 45. It intensified as it reached County Rd 700E, uprooting large hardwood trees and lifting the roof off a single family residence. It continued east-southeast from there, crossing Interstate 57 where it flipped a semi, resulting in one injury. It then heavily damaged a few farm outbuildings and trees on the western outskirts of Charleston. It continued eastward through the north side of Charleston, causing damage at the fairgrounds, a few outbuildings, and trees throughout town before lifting 2 miles east of Charleston along Illinois 16.

tornadoes.name: Pawnee Tornado
tornadoes.label: Pawnee Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down about 1.5 miles west of Pawnee Junction near the I-55 exit, then traveled east across I-55 affecting Commanche Village and the town of Pawnee before dissipating 0.75 miles southeast of Pawnee. During its time on the ground it produced mainly EF0 tree damage, along with minor damage to home soffits and roofs. No injuries were reported. during its 5.7 mile path.

tornadoes.name: Belleville
tornadoes.label: Belleville
tornadoes.notes: Tornado began west of a farm in an open field and moved east southeast through the northern portion of Belleville. Numerous trees were snapped and uprooted. Peeled shingles and siding as well as damage to soffit and guttering on several homes. A garage one on home fell in after its roof was lifted. A garage on another home was breached at the garage door and the structure failed, peeling downwind and taking a large portion of the dwelling's roof decking. The tornado continued east southeast over a farm field damaging corn and a long water sprinkler. The end of the path east of County Road D featured additional trees snapped and uprooted before lifting in the Brooklyn Wildlife Area.

tornadoes.name: Argyle
tornadoes.label: Argyle
tornadoes.notes: Video of a brief tornado shared with Lafayette County Emergency Management shows a narrow tornado on the ground near the East Branch of the Pecatonica River south of Argyle. In the video, some tree branches/limbs are hit/downed. Storm survey wasn't able to yield any additional damage points.

tornadoes.name: Effingham Tornado
tornadoes.label: Effingham Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
Originating in Beecher City within Effingham County, the tornado first touched down along E State Highway 33. The storm's initial path spanned approximately one-quarter mile in width, resulting in EF0 and EF1 level damage. This impact was characterized by the snapping and uprooting of large trees, alongside sporadic damage to grain silos and farm out-buildings, with notable effects observed near N 300th St on the outskirts of Beecher City.

Moving eastward through Shumway, the tornado crossed State Highway 32 and proceeded parallel to E 1800th Ave. Although the path width constricted to just over one-tenth of a mile, the storm intensified, producing EF-2 level damage. The increased strength resulted in hardwood and softwood tree trunks being snapped approximately two-thirds of the way up. Additionally, the tornado caused significant structural destruction, including the removal of a roof from a single-family home and the collapse of several farm outbuildings.

Upon reaching the northern outskirts of rural Effingham, the tornado intensified to EF-3 status as it traveled along E 1800th Ave. During this stage, the storm produced peak wind speeds estimated at 145 mph, leading to severe tree damage and the total destruction of one single-family home, which suffered complete exterior wall collapses.

Continuing its path along Effingham's northern perimeter, the EF-3 tornado maintained a width of one-tenth to one-quarter mile. Substantial structural damage occurred at a farmstead on E 1680th Ave, where several large outbuildings were demolished and a single-family home suffered a total roof uplift alongside partial exterior wall failure. Upon entering Effingham city limits and crossing US HWY 45, the storm destroyed a substantial metal building system after an X-brace failed on its eastern side. Nearby properties sustained further structural and severe tree damage, and the force of the winds threw a delivery van approximately 150 yards to the east.

After departing Effingham, the tornado tracked southeastward and broadened to a width of approximately one-third of a mile. As the storm crossed Interstate 70, it inflicted major damage to trees and caused total roof uplift at multiple single-family homes. The tornado then proceeded across the northern and eastern parts of Teutopolis, where it caused extensive structural destruction to a farmstead located near the HWY 40 and N 1950th St intersection. Impacts at this location included the complete destruction of several large barns and outbuildings, as well as the total uplift of a single-residence roof. The tornadic storm maintained its EF-3 intensity as it moved eastward into rural Teutopolis, though its path narrowed to roughly one-tenth of a mile. Near the intersection of N 2100th St and E 1500th Ave, the storm produced peak wind speeds of 140 mph, resulting in the destruction of two single-family homes and significant damage to trees and outbuildings. Multiple non-life-threatening injuries were reported in this area.

As the tornado moved across the Effingham-Jasper county line, it continued on a southeastward trajectory while weakening to EF-2 intensity. With estimated wind speeds of approximately 120 mph, the storm caused moderate damage to outbuildings and trees, along with minor structural impacts to single-family residences.

The tornado continued to the southeast where it caused major roof damage to a two-story house, rolled an SUV, damaged an outbuilding, and snapped several large hardwood trees. Moving southeast toward E 1700th Ave, the storm snapped the top of another large hardwood and stripped shingles from a single-story residence, with further tree damage reported just north of that location. East of N 700th St, more tree damage occurred alongside shingle damage to a mobile home. As the tornado tracked further along E 1700th Ave, it damaged another outbuilding, two grain bins and additional trees before finally lifting approximately 0.25 miles east of N 800th St.

A special thanks is extended to Effingham County EMA for their assistance in supplying geo-referenced data for severely damaged buildings. We also wish to recognize the local agricultural community along E 1800th Ave in rural Effingham; their willingness to provide transportation was essential for navigating a section of the path obstructed by active utility restoration efforts.

tornadoes.name: Cory
tornadoes.label: Cory
tornadoes.notes: The tornado began in Vigo County south of Riley impacting mostly trees along East Dallas Drive before crossing into Clay county and doing the most significant damage of the path along 2 residences on County Road 200S. Both homes had their roofs completely lifted and blown away with a garage also destroyed. Several outbuildings were also destroyed or damaged along with tree damage across the properties. There was additional tree and barn damage further east along 200S with another concentrated area of damage along a home along 425W. This home had a 100 year old brick barn partially destroyed along with tree damage on the property. An abandoned home next door also experienced damage but it was difficult to determine what damage was new. As the tornado continued to the east it mostly impacted a grove of trees with another home impacted on County Road 200S west of 250W. The tornado then lifted just to the west of 250W.

tornadoes.name: Rose Hill SW Tornado
tornadoes.label: Rose Hill SW Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A tornado touched down in an open field and snapped multiple trees along N 1050th St southwest of Rose Hill. The tornado probably dissipated in the trees near Lick Creek after being on the ground for about 2 minutes.

tornadoes.name: OwenMonroeTornado
tornadoes.label: OwenMonroeTornado
tornadoes.notes:
A thunderstorm that had been showing supercell characteristics across portions of west central Indiana moved east over Owen County. Rotation was observed but no reports had occurred across much of western Owen County. Then shortly after 9:40 pm the rotation began to strengthen as it approached US 231. Tornado touched down just east of US 231 where sporadic tree damage was noted with some larger limbs knocked down and a few upper trunks of trees snapped. The tornado crossed the White River and continued to strengthen. Numerous trees were uprooted and/or large trunks of trees snapped along Macville Road in Owen County. Some of the trees fell on a house on Macville Road. All of this damage was consistent with an EF1 tornado.

The tornado continued east into Monroe county with numerous tree damage along County Line Road. Further east along N Texas Ridge Road the roof of a single story was removed and blown out into a field along with two garages that were completely destroyed. The amount of tree damage increased further to the east with damage along Moon Road and Brighton Road. Two houses along Brighton Road had portions of the roof panels removed. A metal garage in the same area had a quarter of the roof pulled back. All of this damage remained consistent with an EF1 tornado. The tornado strengthened further as it approached Bowman Road, where a house with a large attached barn/garage was damaged. The garage was completely destroyed and large portions of the roof were removed on the house. This damage was estimated to be primarily EF2 strength.

Additional damage to houses and outbuildings was found along Mount Pleasant Road with an increasing amount of tree damage. Some of the most widespread and strongest tree damage was found further to the east along Buskirk Road. Large swaths of trees were either snapped or uprooted. In addition, some debarking of trees was noted as well. A mobile home along Buskirk Road was completely destroyed with all debris being blown to the east. This damage is consistent with a higher end EF2 tornado. The tornado continued eastwards over Interstate 69 where continued widespread tree damage was observed. Further analysis using drone footage indicated additional debarking of hardwood trees near and east of I-69, consistent with EF3 damage. Initially, we had to end the survey at the entrance of the Morgan Monroe State Forest at the interaction of Old State Road 37 and Forest Road where the amount of tree damage prevented the survey team from going any further. However, satellite analysis later on was able to find tree damage all the wat to the Monroe County border.

tornadoes.name: Saddlebrook Farms Tornado
tornadoes.label: Saddlebrook Farms Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado produced tree damage and sporadic roofing damage across the far northern portion of the Saddlebrook Farms subdivision near Grayslake.

tornadoes.name: HilltopCamp
tornadoes.label: HilltopCamp
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down near Christianburg Road with extensive tree damage within a large grove of trees. The tornado then moved into Hilltop Camp where it caused additional extensive tree damage along a path with the center line of the tornado tracking just to the southwest of a group of buildings. A steel frame door was sheared off a building and pushed to the northwest with roof damage on the buildings also strewn about in numerous directions. The tornado continued through another tree grove before crossing Hamilton Creek Road and finally impacting a home near the 6700 block of Hamilton Creek Road before dissipating.

tornadoes.name: Aurora IN
tornadoes.label: Aurora IN
tornadoes.notes:
The first damage produced by the tornado occurred on Texas Gas Road, where a large tree was uprooted and other smaller trees were downed. Farther east along Cole Lane, an attached garage was destroyed and a large tree was downed onto a house. In addition, a roof was lifted from another garage and several trees were snapped at their trunks.

The tornado strengthened and proceeded east near East Laughery Creek Road, where it completely destroyed a house and two outbuildings. Debris from these buildings was strewn east along the path of the tornado across a large field. Based on this damage, estimated wind speeds were around 130 MPH in this area, and the damage also resulted in a Tornadic Debris Signature on the Wilmington, Ohio radar at this time. The tornado continued toward Alta Vista Ave, where a large number of hardwood trees were snapped.

The tornado then moved across Laughery Creek, producing significant tree damage along and near Laughery Creek and in wooded areas along Hartford Pike where numerous trees were snapped. Along Holmes Hill Road, more tree damage was observed along with the roof being lifted off an outbuilding.

On Thuermer Hollow Road, more trees were damaged and a roof was lifted off a barn. Along State Road 56, additional roof damage from a barn and damage to large healthy trees was noted. Farther east on the Indiana side of the Ohio River, numerous trees were knocked down at a campground. The tornado weakened as it moved across the Ohio River into Boone County, Kentucky. The last observed damage from this tornado was noted on Belleview Road, where large tree branches were snapped.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Dearborn County, Indiana Emergency Management Agency, the Ohio County, Indiana Emergency Agency and Boone County, Kentucky Emergency Management Agency for their assistance and support with this damage survey.

tornadoes.name: Florence KY
tornadoes.label: Florence KY
tornadoes.notes:
The first evidence of the tornado was found on Landings Way where several trees were snapped at their trunks. Farther east, along Oakbrook Road near Pleasant Valley Road, additional tree damage was found along with minor damage to building fascia. The tornado proceeded east through residential areas of Oakbrook near Sentry Drive and Thunder Ridge Drive where a few larger hardwood trees were snapped and minor roof damage was noted.

The tornado progressed east, uprooting trees and snapping tree trunks along Hopeful Road, Surfwood Drive, and Rosetta Drive. The tornado then crossed Interstates 71/75 where it lifted a portion of the roof of one commercial building and caused additional roof damage to a second building. A large power pole was snapped near the intersection of US-42 and Dream Street and a local business had its sign destroyed. This is where the tornado is estimated to have reached peak intensity, with winds around 100 MPH.

The tornado then continued east into additional residential areas from here. Large tree limbs were downed along Hollywood Drive and there were numerous trees and large branches down along Ann Street, Lee Street, and Julia Avenue. The home near Ann Street had a large tree fall onto it, causing minor roof damage.

The tornado continued southeast, crossing into Kenton County, snapping several trees at residences along Autumn Road. The final known instance of tornadic damage was on Tallwood Circle, where multiple large branches were downed.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Boone County, Kentucky Emergency Management Agency and the Kenton County, Kentucky Emergency Management Agency for their assistance and support with this damage survey.

tornadoes.name: Drewersburg IN
tornadoes.label: Drewersburg IN
tornadoes.notes:
The first evidence of tornado damage occurred along Gobblers Knob Road, where some trees were damaged. Additional damage was found on Seeley Road, where large tree limbs were knocked down. The tornado moved east, producing more tree damage along Johnson Fork Road. The tornado strengthened as it moved into Drewersburg, producing more significant tree damage along Welsh Drive and Drewersburg Road. One single family home along Welsh Road had its roof completely lifted off with collapse of some exterior walls. Winds that produced this damage were estimated to be around 125 mph, which corresponds to an EF-2 rating on the Enhanced Fujita Scale. A roof was also lifted off a home on Drewersburg Road.

The tornado curved southeast as it moved onto State Line Road, blowing some large tree limbs down. The tornado weakened to EF-0 intensity as it moved into Butler County, Ohio. A few large tree limbs were knocked down on Schradin Road, and this is believed to be the end of the tornado.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Franklin County, Indiana Emergency Management Agency and the Butler County, Ohio Emergency Agency for their assistance and support with this damage survey.

tornadoes.name: Montegut, LA Tornado
tornadoes.label: Montegut, LA Tornado
tornadoes.notes: An EF-0 tornado touched down near Bayou la Cache, east of Chauvin, LA in Terrebonne Parish and tracked northeast toward Montegut, LA. High resolution satellite imagery depicted a defined swath of tree damage beginning over inaccessible areas which aligned with a tornado debris signature on Climavision V014. The damage path grew to a maximum width of 200 yards and peaked in intensity over inaccessible forest west of Blue Jay St as it enroached on neighborhoods near Crochetville Rd. The tornado gradually weakened and decreased in size as it moved over southern parts of Montegut, near Crochetville Rd where mainly minor tree damage was noted. It is estimated that this tornado dissipated near Willow Aly and Bayou Terrebonne.

tornadoes.label: Near Lockport, LA
tornadoes.notes: A defined damage path in inaccessible marsh areas due to a short-lived tornado was identified via high resolution satellite imagery. The existence of this tornado was corroborated by a brief tornado debris signature on V014 Climavision radar. Lafourche Parish emergency management relayed that a tree was downed on a private road where this tornado crossed and is the basis for the EF-0 rating of this tornado.

tornadoes.name: Bayou des Allemands, LA
tornadoes.label: Bayou des Allemands, LA
tornadoes.notes: A well-defined damage path of an EF-0 tornado was identified on high-resolution satellite imagery over rural, inaccessible parts of southeast St. Charles Parish. The tornado touched down near Bayou des Allemands and tracked north-northwest over rural, inaccessible marshland. While the majority of damage along this path was marsh vegetation, a narrow swath of trees were evidently damaged/displaced which is the basis for its EF-0 rating. The tornado continued north-northwest with the narrow damage path becoming less defined with time. The tornado dissipated east of Bayou Gauche after being on the ground for over 3 miles.

tornadoes.name: Scott-Jefferson-Trimble
tornadoes.label: Scott-Jefferson-Trimble
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service completed a storm survey and determined that a tornado occurred during the early morning hours on June 18, 2026 in Scott County and Jefferson County Indiana and then crossed the river into Trimble County Kentucky. The tornado was 1000 yards wide and 23.62 miles in length. Maximum winds were EF2 130 mph.

The tornado first touched down on the northeast side of Austin, Indiana near the community park. Several trees were damaged with twisted tops or brought down entirely in the park. Some fencing and bleacher damage was also observed at the ball fields. The tornado continued across rural portions of Scott county just north of state road 256 with tree damage along the way. The most notable damage started occurring in extreme eastern Scott county north of Wooster along Blanton Road. Drone footage had shown a clear path in the woods of extensive tree damage with several house structures also having damage south of Hardy Lake. High end EF1 winds around 110 mph began here.

The tornado continued into western Jefferson County Indiana along Henry road where the tornado gained size and strength. Several farms north of Henry road had barns totally destroyed with extensive tree damage. Some residences also were completely demolished. Max sustained winds of EF2 120 mph occurred north of the Republican, Kent, and Hanover communities to the west of Madison. The tornado dropped over the cliff past state road 56 toward Clifty Creek Generating Station, where the tornado gained strength. The maximum winds for the entire tornado occurred at the power plant at EF2 130 mph. At this location, a steel electrical transmission line was completely toppled and mangled. The power lines dropped into the Ohio River and closed river traffic at Madison Indiana due to this tornado. In Jefferson County, at least one injury was reported and at least 6 cattle were killed from the tornado.

The tornado then crossed the Ohio River into Trimble County, Kentucky near Milton. Several trees and campers along Coopers Bottom Road received extensive damage with maximum winds at EF1 110 mph. The tornado ended just along US Highway 421 near Milton with no additional damage observed to the east of the Highway.

The National Weather Service would like to extend a big thank you to Scott County Emergency Management, Jennings Township Fire Department, Jefferson County Emergency Management, Trimble County Emergency Management, the Indiana Department of Homeland Security, and the many helpers that assisted Emergency Management with damage assessments and mapping provided to the NWS to assist with this survey. Thanks also goes to the many helpful homeowners who gave their tornado accounts and gave access to their damaged properties to allow for a complete documented tornado survey.

tornadoes.name: Jug Lake, LA Tornado
tornadoes.label: Jug Lake, LA Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The damage path of an EF-0 tornado was identified on medium resolution satellite imagery over lower Terrebonne Parish, near Jug Lake. This damage path is closely aligned with a strong tornado vortex signature that was on KHDC radar, but no debris signature was ever evident. Swaths of damage to marsh vegetation were most evident throughout the track. Additional pictures of trees damaged along the path provided by a private landowner were the basis for the EF-0 rating.

tornadoes.name: Carrollton KY
tornadoes.label: Carrollton KY
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service conducted a damage survey and confirmed a tornado in Carroll County, Kentucky and Switzerland County, Indiana during the early morning hours on June 18th, 2026. The tornado was determined to be an EF1 with maximum winds of 100 MPH.

The first sign of tornadic damage was just east of Patton Hollow Rd in Switzerland County, IN, where numerous trees were damaged. The tornado would continue SE, where notable damage occurred at two properties located off of E SR-56. Several large, hardwood trees were uprooted and/or snapped at the base. Additionally, both of these homes observed a substantial loss of roofing materials, as well as damage to their wooden porches.

The tornado would cross the Ohio River, with the next area of damage appearing along US Route 42 along the Ohio River where several wooden electrical power lines were downed and extensive tree damage occurred. Just to the west of Tom Harris Road, a hillside had extensive tree damage as well. The tornado continued across rural areas east of Carrollton where additional damage occurred along State Route 36. Here several power lines were downed, along with extensive tree damage. The tornado continued near the Easterday community near Boone Road and State Route 36. Several tree lines and residences had damage. The tornado then continued along Dividing Ridge Road, crossed Interstate 71, and then slowly became weaker along Ghent Eagle, Briar Fork, and Indian Creek Roads. Beyond Indian Creek Road, no additional damage was observed in Carroll County.

The National Weather Service would like to thank Switzerland County Emergency Management, Carroll County Emergency Management and NWS Louisville forecast office for the escort and assistance into the affected communities to help complete the damage survey.

tornadoes.name: Crozier Drive, Houma, LA
tornadoes.label: Crozier Drive, Houma, LA
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado touched down over inaccessible areas west of Bayou Dularge and tracked northeast toward Crozier Drive. Predominantly minor to moderate patches of tree damage were visible on high resolution satellite imagery along its path which were collocated with a tornado debris signature on Climavision radar V014. Trees were more evidently displaced and damaged as the tornado exited the inaccessible marsh and forested areas and moved over Crozier Drive. A NWS survey team observed two homes on Crozier Drive that had significant roof loss and at least one exterior wall collapsed for both homes. The tornado continued northeast across Bayou Dularge Rd and into more inaccessible marsh and forest vegetation where more minor damage was evident on satellite imagery. The end point of this tornado is estimated and it's possible it extended further northeast though no conclusive evidence of damage was identified.

tornadoes.name: Elm Grove OH
tornadoes.label: Elm Grove OH
tornadoes.notes:
The first evidence of tornadic damage occurred on Union Hill Road in Pike County about six tenths of a mile north of Appalachian Highway where a few hardwood trees were snapped and multiple limbs were broken off trees. The tornado then moved through a heavily forested area towards the intersection of Lansing Road and Chenoweth Fork Road where more tree damage was noted. Tree damage continued in a concentrated path to the east northeast along Chenoweth Fork Road before crossing Appalachian Highway and causing a fair amount of tree damage at a rest station on Meads Road. The damage noted in the first third of the tornado’s path consisted of broken branches, snapped trunks, and uprooting of mature trees. This is consistent with EF0 and EF1 damage.

After the damage occurred at the Meads Road rest station, the tornado continued east through a forest with a large hillside that was not reachable by ground survey. This coincided with the first evidence of a Tornadic Debris Signature on the Wilmington, OH radar. When the tornado came down the ridgeline just west of Elm Grove, the most significant damage indicators were noted. An entire section of hardwood forest, about 200-250 yards wide, was blown down. Drone photography and ground survey confirms all hardwood trees in this location were snapped with none left standing. The estimate for this type of tree damage is around 115 mph, which is consistent with low end EF2 damage.

Some higher-end EF1 damage was observed as the tornado moved northeast off the hillside into Elm Grove where complete collapse of out buildings and barns, 70% removal of a roof off a house, and snapping of large power transmission lines occurred. After Elm Grove, the tornado turned southeast causing additional damage near the intersection of SR 772 and Appalachian Highway. The final evidence of tree damage was located on Sun Fish Creek Road about a half mile south of Tennyson Road.

The National Weather Service would like to thank The Pike County Ohio Emergency Management Agency and the Ohio Emergency Agency for their assistance and support with this damage survey.

tornadoes.name: Evelyn Ave, Houma, LA
tornadoes.label: Evelyn Ave, Houma, LA
tornadoes.notes: A NWS survey team concluded an EF-1 tornado tracked from Evelyn Ave towards Woodhaven Dr and Roberta Grove Blvd. Several businesses in the Lynn Park Shopping Center (at the corner of Prospect Ave and Grand Caillou Rd) sustained damage to almost every window and had partially collapsed interior walls and their roof. HVAC equipment on the roof was thrown northward onto the ground from these businesses. 4 homes had partial to significant roof loss. One home had an exterior wall collapsed. Several carports were significantly damaged.

tornadoes.name: N Williamstown KY
tornadoes.label: N Williamstown KY
tornadoes.notes:
The first evidence of tornadic damage occurred on a property just east of Clarks Creek where several trees were uprooted or snapped. The tornado would continue east towards Baton Rouge Rd, where several more hardwood trees had large branches broken off, with tree debris thrown onto both sides of the road. Additionally, a barn was completely destroyed in the same area. Sporadic tree damage would continue along Baton Rouge Rd, eventually leading to another barn where the walls completely collapsed and the roof blown off. The damage to these outbuildings was consistent with EF1 damage, with maximum winds around 90 mph. Just a bit farther down the road, another outbuilding had its sheet metal roof completely ripped off, with pieces of sheet metal thrown ~50 yards into the nearby field. Some of the siding was also peeled off.

The damage path would continue along portions of Baton Rouge Rd, with extensive tree damage noted leading up to the intersection of I-75. Most of the tree damage was primarily large branches that were broken off, but there was one hardwood tree that was uprooted. Just east of I-75, additional tree damage occurred, including some wooden power poles that were snapped.

The area of most concentrated damage would occur in several neighborhoods just east of US-25. On Ridgelea Dr, there were multiple large, healthy trees that were uprooted and/or snapped at the base. On Humes Ridge Rd, more large trees and wooden power poles were snapped. The most significant damage occurred near the end of the tornadic path on Waterworks Rd, where a standalone, multi-car garage had the majority of its roof ripped off. Multiple sections of the garage observed a significant loss of its cinderblock exterior walls, including some minor damage to the interior walls between car ports. Debris from the garage was spread out into the nearby field. Given the structural integrity of the garage, it’s expected that wind speeds up to 95 mph were observed in this part of the tornado track, which is consistent with EF1 damage. Finally, some minor tree damage was observed in the field just off to the east before the tornado lifted.

The National Weather Service office would like to thank Grant County Emergency Management Agency, State of Kentucky Emergency Management, and the Williamstown Fire Department for their assistance with this damage survey.

tornadoes.name: Bonvillain Canal, LA Tornado
tornadoes.label: Bonvillain Canal, LA Tornado
tornadoes.notes: An EF-0 tornado touched down over inaccessible areas of Terrebonne Parish, southwest of Houma, LA. A weak path of damage to marsh vegetation and trees was observed on high resolution satellite imagery which was collocated with a large, vertically and temporally continuous tornado debris signature on Climavision V014 radar. The tornado apparently lifted prior to crossing Bayou Dularge Rd given that no substantive damage was observed by the ground survey team in the area despite the weakening tornado debris signature still being present on radar.

tornadoes.name: Wise Circle, Houma, LA
tornadoes.label: Wise Circle, Houma, LA
tornadoes.notes: A NWS survey team concluded an EF-0 tornado produced damage to trees, several homes, and several electrical wooden poles in the McCord area of Houma. Time estimated by radar.

tornadoes.name: Afton Street, Houma, LA
tornadoes.label: Afton Street, Houma, LA
tornadoes.notes: A NWS survey team concluded that an EF-1 tornado tracked from the corner of Afton St and Richmond Ave towards Dixie Ave in Houma. A truck was tossed 30 feet and sustained significant damage. Multiple snapped and uprooted trees were observed. Several homes sustained a partial loss of their roofs. One home had a collapsed carport. Time estimated by radar.

tornadoes.name: Megan Dr, Houma, LA Tornado
tornadoes.label: Megan Dr, Houma, LA Tornado
tornadoes.notes: An EF-0 tornado touched down near Megan Drive, off of Coteau Rd, in northeast Terrebonne Parish. This tornado caused predominantly tree damage with some additional visible roof and siding damage to a couple homes. This tornado continued into Lafourche Parish where trees were visibly damage/displaced near Bayou Blue Rd on high resolution satellite imagery. The tornado continued into inaccessible marsh areas northeast of Bayou Blue Rd. A tornado debris signature was evident on Climavision Radar V014 through the duration of this tornado with the TDS dissipating near Hollywood Canal.

tornadoes.name: Maysville KY
tornadoes.label: Maysville KY
tornadoes.notes:
An EF-2 tornado occurred on the southwest side of Maysville during the early morning hours of June 18. The tornado began just west of Martha Comer Drive, snapping several hardwood tree trunks before moving across the southern portion of the Maysville Community College campus. The Kentucky Mesonet site on campus measured a wind gust of 114 mph. The tornado then tracked east and northeast across open field, eventually hitting several businesses along Kentucky Highway 9 (AA Highway), causing roof and structural damage.

As the tornado approached East Maple Leaf Road, it quickly intensified. A couple of residences were severely damaged, including an outbuilding demolished with pieces and contents of the structure thrown between 100-200 feet. This includes a 690 pound four wheeler and a large cinder block. A dual axle trailer jacked up on a block with two zero turn mowers and various other outdoor equipment inside was pushed nearly 100 feet before being stopped by a cement barrier. A house suffered extensive roof damage. A property on the east side of East Maple Leaf Road was also heavily damaged with the debris in a convergent path here as well. This includes the roof and siding of a house, several snapped and uprooted hardwood trees, and a couple of hardwood fences posted well into the ground being pulled toward the circulation. Splatter was observed on the east and south sides of the home, further suggesting a cyclonic rotation. The tornado then took a left turn toward the northeast as it snapped more trees and destroyed another portion of a fence. Additionally, on the southern side of the tornado, a couple of large barns were heavily damaged with both roofs a total loss as outflow winds occurred on the south side of the tornado. As the tornado continued on a northeast track across a field, a metal outbuilding was pulled down a hill as the circulation neared. Additional tree damage was observed east of Hill City Road before the tornado dissipated. Sporadic tree damage was reported farther northeast toward the Ohio River as a result of outflow winds.

The National Weather Service in Wilmington would like to thank Mason County Emergency Management and the state of Kentucky Emergency Management for their assistance in completing this survey.

tornadoes.name: Bayou Guache-Luling, LA
tornadoes.label: Bayou Guache-Luling, LA
tornadoes.notes: NWS ground survey in addition to high resolution satellite analysis confirmed an EF-0 tornado tracked from northeast of Bayou Gauche to west of Luling, LA in St. Charles Parish. The tornado evident damaged a patch of trees on high resolution satellite imagery and additional damage to marsh vegetation was evident with brief, weak tornado debris signatures also present on KHDC during this time. The tornado continued bending northward in direction as it approached the Blouin Canal with a larger, well-defined tornado debris signature becoming more evident on approach. A large tree was visibly damaged/displaced on high res satellite imagery in addition to other minor tree damage noted near Santa Cruz Ct as the tornado began to weaken and lift. The only minor tree damage was noted by the ground surveyor in the location.

tornadoes.name: Bayou Cane, LA Tornado
tornadoes.label: Bayou Cane, LA Tornado
tornadoes.notes: NWS ground survey confirmed an EF-1 tornado impacted areas near Bayou Cane and moved northeast across US Hwy 190 west of Lacombe, LA in St. Tammany Parish. The tornado touched down near the shore of Lake Pontchartrain or came ashore as a tornadic waterspout with evident damage to marsh vegetation and trees per high resolution satellite imagery. The tornado was at peak intensity west of Lemieux Blvd where ground surveyors observed a few snapped trees on Cane Bayou Access Trail. Additional tree damage occurred on private property including several uprooted trees and a few snapped trunks as well as visible damage to a shed. The tornado uprooted and partially snapped trees as it crossed the Tammany Trace Bike Trail. The tornado began to evidently weaken as it approached and crossed US Hwy 190 causing only minor tree damage north of the highway. The tornado is estimated to have lifted near Azalea St and Cane Bayou Ln.

tornadoes.label: Near Destrehan, LA
tornadoes.notes: As the Bayou Gauche-Luling Tornado occluded and weakened, it quickly handed off to another EF-0 tornado that quickly strengthened and caused a defined damaged swath of minor tree damage over largely inaccessible areas northeast of Destrehan, near Interstate 310. The tornado evidently weakened and lifted before reaching Airline Hwy. This damage path aligned closely with a strong tornado vortex signature on TMSY and evident weak debris signature on KHDC.

tornadoes.label: Near Avondale, LA
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado tracked across parts of St. Charles and Jefferson Parishes, affecting the community of Avondale, LA. This tornado began over the Salvador Wildlife Management Area as evidenced by a well-defined 15-20 yard wide path of damage to marsh vegetation oriented southwest to northeast that was collocated with an intensifying area of rotation on both TMSY and KHDC. This damage path gradually broadened and fluctuated in intensity causing minor damage to trees as it traveled over uninhabited and inaccessible marsh areas. The tornado damage path evidently became larger and more noticeable again near Bayou Verret. As the tornado crossed into Jefferson Parish, a clear path of tree damage was evident on high resolution satellite imagery spanning to approximately 300 yards wide with numerous trees damaged or displaced. The damage path within this inaccessible area became weaker and less apparent as the tornado approached US Hwy 90. The tornado was at EF-0 intensity as it crossed US Hwy 90 into Avondale. As it tracked northeast, the tornado caused light home damage and snapped tree branches. The tornado restrengthened to low-end EF-1 intensity at George Street, rolling a single-wide manufactured home into another home which was the cause of the most significant structural damage. The manufactured home was thrown to the northeast with the frame being well bent. 2 people were injured as a result. Additional home damage was also found on Defourneaux Ln as the tornado began to weaken again. It's estimated that the tornado lifted after crossing Restlawn Park Cemetery, near Center Street.

tornadoes.label: Near Metairie, LA
tornadoes.notes: An EF1 tornado touched down on the east bank of the MS River and moved northeast to the University of New Orleans. Damage across the city was mostly tree damage and minor building damage. Additional analysis, points and information will be added later. Additional changes are possible.

tornadoes.name: Eden Isle, LA Tornado
tornadoes.label: Eden Isle, LA Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
A brief EF0 tornado touched down in Eden Isle, LA and moved east. Widespread branches and tree debris was found in Eden Isle along with a few houses with minor damage. One house had a failure at the garage where the wind looks to have been pushed into the garage. The tornado damaged businesses right near I-10 as it crossed over with a few more homes damaged and trees down in Lakeshore Village.

The widespread light damage across Eden Isle did make this a difficult track, especially track width, to find. The additional damage was likely inflow from straight line winds and/or debris that was swirling out of the tornado.

tornadoes.name: Avery Estates, LA Tornado
tornadoes.label: Avery Estates, LA Tornado
tornadoes.notes: NWS ground survey confirmed an EF-1 tornado with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph tracked from Treasure Isle in southeast St. Tammany Parish to rural parts of southwest Hancock County, north of Pearlington. The tornado began near or before moving into Treasure Isle where it flipped a large boat on its side. Additional visible damage to homes and lofting of outdoor fixtures was noted as the tornado moved into Martin Drive. The tornado reached EF-1 intensity near Bluegill Drive where it removed shingles off of homes, snapped a few trees, and collapsed garage door structures and blew out a wall or two as a result in two different homes. A defined damage path was observed on LA Hwy 433 and then crossed into inaccesible marsh areas. A weak tornado debris signature was evident on KHDC and is the basis for connecting this damage to Avery Estates. The tornado continued northeast into Avery Estates where minor metal roof damage and tree damage was noted on Avery Drive and Smokey Hollow Drive. The tornado evidently strengthened and grew in size to around 300 yards in width as it moved just south of the northern part of Avery Drive and into US Hwy 190 where numerous trees were uprooted or snapped. Several outbuildings were damaged and tension cables on a cell tower were snapped. It's possible the tornado slowed in this area as it pivoted and turned more to the east per KHDC radar imagery. Along US Hwy 190 a manufactured home had most of its roof removed and it was shifted significantly off its foundation. The tornado then moved into Pearl River Basin, inaccessible to ground survey. The tornado evidently maintained strength or even strengthened further over this area, evidenced by the deepening of a tornado debris signature lofted over 5000 feet. Tree damage was found by ground survey team on rural roads of southwest Hancock County as the tornado began to weaken and lift back to the northeast. The tornado is estimated to have lifted near or after Point Road prior to reaching MS Hwy 607.

tornadoes.name: Rural NW Harrison, MS Tornado
