tornadoes.label: Rural NW Harrison, MS Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The damage path of a brief EF-0 tornado was identified via high resolution satellite imagery in northwest Harrison County. This tornado caused predominantly damaged to trees over inaccessible areas between West Wortham and McHenry roads. This focused damage path closely aligned with a strong tornado vortex signature that crossed through the area. The tornado apparently lifted as it crossed McHenry Rd as no other damage could be identified as the circulation lifted northward.

tornadoes.name: Dedeaux-Lizana, MS Tornado
tornadoes.label: Dedeaux-Lizana, MS Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A NWS survey team concluded that an EF-1 tornado tracked northeast across Hancock and Harrison counties. Tree damage was widespread along the track including several large trees uprooted and snapped. Minor damage was done to several properties. Additional revisions via high resolution satellite analysis concluded the tornado began west of Standard Dedeaux Rd, north of Rock Hill Dedeaux Rd where it quickly strengthened into an EF-1 tornado and reached its peak width of 275 yards wide. The tornado then evidently weakened and the damage path become more intermittent until it reached the Wolf River where another swath of trees was rated low-end EF-1. The tornado damage path became intermittent once more after crossing the intersection of Cemetery and Steel Bridge Rd. The tornado then evidently reached its third peak as an EF-1 tornado as it crossed Cemetery Rd and MS Hwy 53 where swaths of trees were damaged and uprooted. The tornado then rapidly dissipated as it continued northeast and it's estimated to have lifted prior to reaching Herman Ladner Rd.

tornadoes.name: Whites Crossing
tornadoes.label: Whites Crossing
tornadoes.notes:
The tornado first touched down just northwest of the intersection of King Bee Rd and Ten Mile Church Rd. The tornado uprooted trees at a residence at Spiers Rd and King Bee Rd. The tornado intensified and likely reached its maximum intensity as it moved northeast toward Flint Creek Road. Numerous trees were snapped and uprooted. In addition, the roof was torn off of a residence and a mobile home, and roof damage was observed to several sheds and outside storage buildings. The tornado continued northeast and weakened as it crossed John Willis Rd. The tornado briefly intensified again to EF-1 strength as it crossed Highway 26 where several trees were uprooted and snapped. The tornado weakened and lifted as it crossed Big Four Rd north of Highway 26.

Review of Sentinel 2 and Planet high resolution satellite imagery revealed the tornado path to have started earlier along Ten Mile Church Road where scattered tree damage became apparent in a focused corridor. To the south, scattered trees were damaged in association with the storms RFD. The maximum tornado width has also been adjusted to approximately 375 yards.

tornadoes.name: Whites Crossing 2
tornadoes.label: Whites Crossing 2
tornadoes.notes: After reviewing available Sentinel 2 and Planet high resolution satellite imagery, it was determined a brief EF1 tornado occurred northeast of Whites Crossing, shortly after the first EF1 tornado had dissipated. This is also supported by a brief radar indicated tornado debris signature off of KMOB in this area. This tornado caused substantial tree damage primarily in forest after crossing Melton Hatten Road. The tornado lifted in the forest due north of Miles Cemetery Road.

tornadoes.name: McHenry
tornadoes.label: McHenry
tornadoes.notes: A brief EF1 tornado occurred in the McHenry area, beginning just southwest of Beech Road, tracking northeast across Beech Road and Hall Road. On the tornadoes short track, it caused an approximately 40-yard-wide swath of tree damage visible via both Sentinel 2 satellite imagery and broadcast media supplied damage photos. Most the damage was in the form of tree uproots and snaps, with only minor roofing damage to one of the homes on Hall Road. It is possible the tornado tracked further northeast; however additional clearer high resolution satellite imagery will be needed for any further track adjustments.

tornadoes.name: Leaf
tornadoes.label: Leaf
tornadoes.notes: A brief EF1 tornado occurred across the forest adjacent to Hicks Camp Road and the Leaf River in rural southwestern Greene County. This tornado was identified via a combination of high resolution satellite imagery and the presence of a weak radar tornado debris signature visible off of KMOB radar. The tornado caused a narrow path of tree damage, with several trees taken down along Hicks Camp Road. The tornado likely lifted along the Leaf River where any visible tree damage comes to an end.

tornadoes.name: Avera
tornadoes.label: Avera
tornadoes.notes: Another EF0 tornado was found via NISAR and Planet satellite imagery in rural Greene County southeast of Avera. The tornado occurred almost solely in forest, beginning northeast of Highway 63 near William Roberts Road. This tornado caused minor tree damage along its track, mainly with damage to treetops and the occasional uproot. A weak radar tornado debris signature was also noted off KMOB radar collocated with a strong velocity couplet.

tornadoes.name: Yates Tornado
tornadoes.label: Yates Tornado
tornadoes.notes: An EF1 Tornado hit Rock Stream, NY, crossed Seneca Lake and hit lakeshore residence south of Hector, NY during late morning on June 18, 2026. Though there was pockets of minor tree damage from the storm itself, tornadic damage started around Reading Road at 1045 AM. This tornado strengthened to as much as 90 mph from Old Lake Road to State Route 14, as rotation tightened with the storm quickly moving at 50 mph from higher elevations into the Seneca Lake basin. Numerous trees were uprooted in a convergent chaotic fashion, and around 40 vineyard posts were snapped. Twigs and branches were impaled into the ground as missiles in portions of the vineyard, and shingles were found more than a quarter mile from their source. A garage outbuilding collapsed, with some metal roof peelback and siding damage also noted on the residence with small branches squeezing into gaps. After crossing State Route 14 with a continued corridor of uprooted trees, the tornado crossed Seneca Lake around 1050 AM. Significant damage was observed near the lake at the end of Wickham Rd. A large tree branch was impaled into a house and several trees and numerous large branches were downed.

tornadoes.name: Cortland Tornado Path
tornadoes.label: Cortland Tornado Path
tornadoes.notes: An EF-0 tornado briefly touched down 3.4 miles west of Cortland in Cortland County NY around 11:32 AM, moving east-northeast at 50 mph. Tree damage along the route was the most common type of damage, with a swath of tree damage showing a convergent pattern, which is indication of a brief tornado touching down. Going east along Route 222, and along residential streets south of Route 222, multiple trees fell in the east-northeast direction, with a few falling due north. Where convergent damage was evident was just north of the Cortland County Airport, with a few trees falling in the southwest direction. Among the damage, some of the most extensive was mainly large uprooted trees and large snapped trees. Going further east-northeast, further scattered tree damage was observed, but did not show a convergent pattern. This indicated that the brief tornado dissipated heading into town, and was residual thunderstorm wind damage.

tornadoes.label: Near Lincoln, VT
tornadoes.notes: A briefly strong EF-1 tornado touched down in the woods approaching York Hill Rd. The tornado crossed into the nearby ravine where damage trailed off.

tornadoes.label: Near West Woodstock, VT
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 Tornado wound through the valley along Route 4, where it uprooted and snapped numerous trees. It also warped solar panels, a metal shed, and took off some roofing before traveling up the hill where it lifted. A snapped tree collapsed a wooden structure.

tornadoes.label: Near Ellerslie, GA
tornadoes.notes: An EF1 tornado touched down at 6:37PM Thursday June 18, 2026 along Chatsworth road just south of Hwy 80 in northeastern Muscogee county. The tornado snapped and uprooted numerous trees as well as knocked down powerlines along Chatsworth road. The tornado continued ENE crossing Midland Road and Hwy 80 snapping and uprooting trees. On the north side of hwy 80, the tornado paralleled Fulton road snapping and uprooting trees. There are several homes along that stretch of road which received only minor damage, most of which from trees and tree debris. The tornado continued east crossing Jenkins Road and into a small neighborhood along Bentley Drive. A large tree fell onto a home near the entrance to the neighborhood. The tornado continued east across McKee road and Daniel court before lifting as it moved into a largely wooded area around Kendall Creek

tornadoes.label: Near Ellaville, GA
tornadoes.notes: An EF0 tornado touched down at 7:44pm Thursday June 18, 2026 just east of Hwy 19 near the intersection of county road 271 as a line of storms moved through the region. The tornado snapped and uprooted numerous trees along the county road as it traveled east crossing Heath Road and La Crosse Road. The tornado lifted as it crossed railroad An EF0 tornado touched down at 7:44pm Thursday June 18, 2026 just east of Hwy 19 near the intersection of county road 271 as a line of storms moved through the region. The tornado snapped and uprooted numerous trees along the county road as it traveled east crossing Heath Road and La Crosse Road. The tornado lifted as it crossed railroad tracks just south of county road 271. Radar data from the V010 location in Americus was utilized to both estimate the time as well as confirm the presence of the tornado within the line of storms.

tornadoes.label: Near Bolingbroke, GA
tornadoes.notes: An EF1 tornado touched down at 7:50PM Thursday June 18, 2026 along Hwy 341 in Crawford county just south of the community of Musella. Trees were snapped along Hwy 341 on both sides of the highway. The tornado intensified quickly as it traveled ENE crossing Musella Road and Johnson Road where numerous trees were snapped and uprooted in an around several homes. Shortly after crossing through this region a Tornado Debris Signature appeared on the KJGX radar at approximately 7:52pm. The tornado continued northeast crossing Fairplay Hill Road and Dent Road snapping an uprooted dozens to hundreds of trees in a mainly wooded region. The storm crossed Hopewell road near the intersection of Smith Chapel Road knocking over trees and powerlines before crossing into Monroe county south of Tharpe Road. The storm crossed Montpelier Station road and Montpelier Church road snapping and uprooting trees including onto the back of a church along hwy 74. As the tornado crossed 74 it moved into an area with several homes along Hudson Hill Dr, Shady Dale Dr and Lower Simmons Road. Several homes sustained moderate to severe damage as a result of trees falling onto them. Other homes in the area sustained roof damage from the wind and a couple of cars were crushed by falling trees. The tornado continued NE into a largely wooded area before lifting as it got to Zebulon road where 2 trees were uprooted. Radar data indicates that this tornado was rotating north and eventually absorbed into a larger circulation/mesocyclone that had developed in the line of storms moving through the region.

tornadoes.name: Moffett Road
tornadoes.label: Moffett Road
tornadoes.notes: The tornado began along Howells Ferry rd near Grider rd as a weak EF-0 bringing down a couple branches resulting in minor damage across two properties. The tornado then continued southeast across Carlisle Dr and strengthened as it approached Central Blvd and Mississippi St. south of Howells Ferry Rd. Several large uprooted hardwood trees were noted within this area with more widespread small to large branches snapped throughout several roads within the community. The tornado then continued east towards Moffett Rd as it likely moved along Moffett before resulting in a few sporadic uprooted trees near a water treatment plant on the north side of Moffett Rd. The tornado likely weakened as it destroyed two businesses signs before dissipating near Northview Dr.

tornadoes.label: Near Bolingbroke, GA
tornadoes.notes: An EF0 tornado touched down at 8:14PM Thursday June 18, 2026 near the intersection of Wadley Road and Estes Road to the southwest of the Bolingbroke community. The tornado traveled northeast along Estes Road snapping and uprooting trees particularly as it moved north of Lentz road. The tornado continued NE crossing I475 where a couple trees were downed before reaching Cory Dr and Kopfler road where several trees were snapped and uprooted before dissipating. There were other trees downed sporadically to the northeast of the last plotted location of this tornado, however, both the radar data and the ground survey lacked the clarity to be able to determine if a weak rotation continued or if the damage was due to strong winds associated with the strong mesocyclone moving through the area.

tornadoes.name: Squirrel Bayou
tornadoes.label: Squirrel Bayou
tornadoes.notes: Review of available satellite imagery revealed just enough foliage/tree damage within Squirrel Bayou to assign an EF0 tornado rating to this tornado. Satellite imagery revealed minor damage, and most of the track is estimated for its start and end points based on the presence of a radar tornado debris signature. Further adjustments are possible with this tornado as additional high resolution satellite imagery becomes available in the coming days and weeks.

tornadoes.name: Carpenter
tornadoes.label: Carpenter
tornadoes.notes:
A brief EF-0 tornado touched down just west of Highway 225 between Kilcrease Rd and Green Jordan Rd and lifted just east of Hwy 225. The tornado produced spotty tree damage. A couple of small pine trees were snapped with many other large limbs down. No structural damage was noted to the homes in the area. The damage also lined up in the exact location of the radar identified tornado debris signature.

Review of available satellite imagery revealed substantial changes to the overall track and strength of this tornado. The tornado began just west of State Highway 225 near Soloman Lane, tracking north-northeast across Highway 225 and Green Jordan Road. It was here the tornado caused low end EF1 tree damage. As it continued northward, it once again reached Highway 225 where it dissipated.

tornadoes.name: Spanish Fort
tornadoes.label: Spanish Fort
tornadoes.notes: Available high resolution satellite imagery revealed a short-lived EF1 tornado began along Bay Minette Creek, tracking eastward for just over a half mile. The tornado primarily caused scattered tree damage along its track through Buzbee Road, with the most noteworthy tree damage being west of Buzbee Road after moving onshore. Further review of available imagery revealed the tornado track ended along Edwards Lane where minor tree damage continued in tandem with the velocity couplet and radar tornado debris signature.

tornadoes.name: Carpenter 2
tornadoes.label: Carpenter 2
tornadoes.notes: After review of high resolution satellite imagery and KMOB radar imagery, a new EF0 tornado was found in the Carpenter area. This tornado began along Cliffs Landing Road, tracking east-northeast across D'olive Street before dissipating in the forest. This tornado caused primarily minor tree damage, with a peak width around 100 yards on the south side of D'olive Street adjacent to State Highway 225.

tornadoes.label: Near Gray, GA
tornadoes.notes: An EF0 tornado touched down at 8:25PM Thursday June 18, 2026 in northeastern Monroe County along Tobler Creek near Searcy Drive where several trees were snapped and uprooted. The tornado tracked ENE crossing Hwy 23 where several trees were downed before crossing Rivermist Road and Popes Ferry Lane snapping and uprooting trees before crossing the Ocmulgee River. Monroe county Emergency Management confirms the tornado continued east in a largely wooded area via drone footage of snapped and uprooted trees on the Jones County side of the River. The tornado continued east in Jones County crossing hwy 18 downing a few trees before reaching the Five Points community. Numerous trees were snapped along Five Points Road as the tornado continued north paralleling that road before lifting past the intersection of Five Points road and Hitchiti road.

tornadoes.name: Steelwood
tornadoes.label: Steelwood
tornadoes.notes: After review of available high resolution satellite imagery and KMOB radar data it was determined an EF1 tornado occurred primarily within forested areas northeast of Steelwood Lake. Mostly minor tree damage was observed in a narrow, defined path throughout its track. The tornado lifted along Brady Road as the circulation cycled/weakened and a new tornado began to its northeast.

tornadoes.name: Gateswood
tornadoes.label: Gateswood
tornadoes.notes: After review of high resolution satellite imagery and KMOB radar data a new EF1 tornado was found to have occurred north of Gateswood. This tornado began northeast of Brady Road after the previous tornado dissipated. The tornado caused scattered tree damage all along a persistent path south of Brady Mill Dam Road. This is likely where the tornado reached its peak intensity and width with nearly all widely spaced trees throughout the fields it crossed being taken down in a nearly 400-yard-wide swath. An extensive swath of damaging winds also occurred to the south of the tornado track with around 75 to 85mph RFD winds. The tornado gradually weakened and narrowed after crossing Brady Mill Dam Road and County Road 112, with the damage path becoming intermittent. The radar velocity couplet off KMOB carried all the way through the Escambia/Baldwin County line east of River Road along with the intermittent narrow damage path, supporting continuing the tornado track through this location. After crossing Perdido River, the tornado quickly dissipated.

tornadoes.name: Gateswood 2
tornadoes.label: Gateswood 2
tornadoes.notes: A brief, weak EF0 tornado occurred within a field and adjacent forest between Wiggins Still Road and Mosquito Fork Road. High resolution satellite imagery revealed a narrow, brief path which lined up well with a weak velocity couplet and tornado debris signature identified off KMOB radar data. The tornado caused minor tree damage along its track and was preceded to the northwest by a strong swath of damaging winds estimated in the 70 to 85mph range.

tornadoes.label: Near Gray, GA
tornadoes.notes: An EF1 tornado touched down at 8:37PM Thursday June 18, 2026 in Jones County south of the community of Wayside to the west of Green Settlement Road. The tornado snapped and uprooted trees as it crossed Green Settlement Road before crossing Hwy 11, or Monticello Hwy, where several trees were snapped and uprooted including one onto a home. The tornado continued north of hwy 11 reaching peak intensity in a grove of trees on Wayside Farm where numerous trees were snapped and uprooted. The tornado continued travelling north before lifting in a wooded area south of Otis Redding Drive.
tornadoes.timing_issue: implied speed over 120 mph

tornadoes.label: Near Gray, GA
tornadoes.notes: An EF0 tornado touched down at 8:41PM Thursday June 18, 2026 in Jones County to the west of Hungerford Road in a wooded area where several trees were snapped and uprooted. The tornado traveled north parallel to Hungerford Road crossing Jackson road snapping and uprooting trees along both sides of the road. The tornado lifted after a 1.4 mile path in a wooded area to the west of Hungerford Road.

tornadoes.label: Near Crooked Creek, GA
tornadoes.notes: An EF1 tornado touched down in northeastern Jones county at 8:51PM Thursday June 18, 2026 to the south of Damascus Church road where several trees were snapped and uprooted. The tornado continued northeast crossing Roosevelt Road snapping and uprooting numerous trees which resulted in 1 of 2 areas of EF1 damage within the path. The storm continued travelling ENE along Hwy 129 snapping and uprooting trees before travelling along Mathis road into Baldwin County where it became Lumpkin Road. Trees were snapped and uprooted along both sides of that road before snapping and uprooting numerous trees along Hwy 212 in far northern Baldwin county along Lake Sinclair. The tornado crossed Lake Sinclair and snapped or uprooted numerous trees on the northern bank of the lake in southern Putnam County along Whipporwill Lane and Phillips road. A couple of homes sustained damage from falling trees along the lake. The damage in this location was classified as the 2nd area of EF1 damage from this tornado. The storm continued northeast crossing Napier road and Twin Bridges road downing a few trees before lifting as it reached the lake at the location where Twin bridges road crosses Lake Sinclair.

tornadoes.label: Near Crooked Creek, GA
tornadoes.notes: An EF0 Tornado touched down in southeastern Putnam County at 9:04PM Thursday June 18, 2026 along Twin Bridges Road just east of the community of Nona where several trees were snapped and uprooted. The tornado continued northeast along Twin Bridges Road snapping and uprooting trees including along Welch Trl before reaching the intersection of Hwy 441 and Pea Ridge Rd in the Flat Rock Community. Numerous trees were snapped on the western side of the intersection as well as sporadically on the eastern side. East of Hwy 441, trees were snapped along various locations on Pea Ridge Cir in and around several homes. The tornado continued east and lifted as it approached Pea Ridge Road in a wooded area. There were 2 fatalities and 2 injuries which occurred near the path of this tornado the morning after this tornado passed through the area as a result of a tree falling onto a vehicle. While it is likely but not certain that the tornado weakened the tree which caused the fatalities and injuries, they are not considered a direct result of. Final determination will be that these were indirect injuries and fatalities from the tornado/storm itself.

tornadoes.label: Near White Plains, GA
tornadoes.notes: An EF0 tornado touched down in northern Putnam County along Hwy 16 at 9:19PM Thursday June 18, 2026 where several trees were snapped and uprooted. The tornado travelled north in a largely wooded area before emerging onto Lake Oconee in Greene County before reaching a shoreline which included numerous homes along Quail Hollow, Chieftain Way, Tomahawk Ct, Cherokee trail, and Howard Lewis Road where numerous trees were snapped and uprooted including several onto homes. A boat and boathouse was flipped and partially sunk and several powerlines were downed. It is likely that the damage along this portion of the shoreline was maximized due to the orientation of the lake and the wind direction associated with the parent storm which spawned this tornado. The tornado weakened and lifted as it crossed White Oak Dr.

tornadoes.label: Near Ebro, FL
tornadoes.notes: Brief tornado touched down along Highway 79 near Potter Spring Road. No structural damage was reported, with only small limbs down reported. A TDS signature was reported on radar. Exact start and end locations is estimated based on damage photo and radar signatures.

tornadoes.name: Laporte EF0
tornadoes.label: Laporte EF0
tornadoes.notes: Per video and pictures along with real time reports a weak tornado tracked ESE to the south of HWY 200 for about 7 minutes with intermittent kicking up of dust, leaves, and other small debris. No damage could be seen either in pictures or via high resolution satellite so the track is an estimate based on video evidence of time and location.

tornadoes.name: Arabi, LA
tornadoes.label: Arabi, LA
tornadoes.notes: An EF0 tornado with winds of 85 MPH tracked north to south across Arabi, LA in St. Bernard Parish. This was confirmed via eyewitness videos, along with debris thrown to the SE and convergent debris in that direction. Almost all of the damage was shingles off well built homes, fence damage and large branches down. Three houses had a good part of their roof removed. Two were older houses, one built in the 50s. One house had a car port attached to the roof which is where the failure occurred. The third was abandoned and neighbors confirmed it also had extensive termite damage. That and rot was observed on the roof. Given that well built homes had minor damage and the damage on the three houses were from older roofs, the rating is an 85 MPH EF0.

tornadoes.name: Osseo, WI
tornadoes.label: Osseo, WI
tornadoes.notes: This brief, weak, and narrow tornado began as a highly visible funnel cloud just west of Osseo. It touched down at Merchants Baseball Field off US Highway 10 where it destroyed a storage garage and caused tree damage. The tornado likely lifted temporarily as it tracked southeast and crossed the highway, with the next downstream damage occurring off W 5th St near Spruce Rd. In this area, it damaged a couple sheds, trees, and a power pole before dissipating.

tornadoes.name: SG_HV
tornadoes.label: SG_HV
tornadoes.notes: The brunt of the damage was to a double wide manufactured home that was bolted to a poured basement foundation. Unfortunately there was a fatality at this residence. Most of the debris from the home and outbuildings was scattered to the northeast. The debris could be found six miles to the northeast, but there wasn't additional structural damage in this path.

tornadoes.label: Near Warson Woods, MO
tornadoes.notes: Damage photos provided by broadcast media revealed EF-0 tree damage along Warson Woods drive. This aligns well with radar indicated rotation and a video of a very low, rotating wall cloud.
tornadoes.timing_issue: duration over 3 hours

tornadoes.name: Stewardson Tornado
tornadoes.label: Stewardson Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado in a field in far southern Shelby County and moved northeast. It hit one farmstead and did minor tree damage and peeled parts of the metal off a barn. The tornado continued northeast and dissipated near the intersection of E 100 North Rd and N 2700 East Rd.

tornadoes.name: Louisville Tornado
tornadoes.label: Louisville Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado was observed 2 miles south-southwest of Louisville just south of Grover Creek Ln. The tornado moved northeast entering the south side of town, removing a large portion of the roof of a business storage building and attached residence. The tornado continued through town in a weakened state with minor branch damage occurring. The tornado re-intensified just northeast of town where is snapped off power poles and large trees along Old Bible Grove Rd. The tornado moved northeast and damaged a few more trees, but remained on the ground in the fields before dissipating south of Lorimar Lane.

tornadoes.name: Neoga Tornado
tornadoes.label: Neoga Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down about 1 mile southeast of Neoga, on the east side of I-57. It damaged a few farm outbuildings and trees along its path, which was less than 1 mile long, lifting just north of County Road 1000 N.

tornadoes.label: Near Vernon, IL
tornadoes.notes: A chaser photo taken around 3:50 on hwy 51 shows a tornado directly in front (south) of a tree line along the Fayette/Marion county line. Just to the west of the tornado in that image, an NWS storm survey found minor (EF-0) damage along the county line.

tornadoes.name: Bradbury Tornado
tornadoes.label: Bradbury Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado began about 1 mile southeast of Bradbury near County Road 1350. It tracked northeast, damaging several trees and a couple of farm outbuildings. It turned east-northeastward and tracked just south of Cottonwood, causing more tree damage before lifting northwest of Diona near the county line.

tornadoes.name: Newton South Tornado
tornadoes.label: Newton South Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down about 2 miles south of Newton where it produced EF2 tree damage. It progressed to the northeast and crossed Hwy 130 before dissipating just northeast of the intersection of E 850 Ave and N 1325th St. The tornado cause significant tree damage along Hwy 130 and again along N 1325 St. It also destroyed an outbuilding along N 1100th St and tossed the debris in several directions.

tornadoes.name: Newton East Tornado
tornadoes.label: Newton East Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Radar supports a new tornado developing in the area of N 1400 St near the Embarrass River where it destroyed an outbuilding and caused tree damage. It progressed northeast through wooded areas, causing significant tree damage. Numerous very large trees were snapped off and other tree tops were shredded. Corn in the fields was flattened into the ground, with a suction vortice evident down the central path. The tornado continued across the Embarrass River crossing 900th Ave, causing more tree damage before dissipating near N 1600th St line of woods.

tornadoes.label: Near Farina, IL
tornadoes.notes: NWS storm survey found very clear tornadic damage (EF-1) east of Kinmundy, with supporting video showing a multi-vortex tornado in that location.

tornadoes.name: Annapolis North Tornado
tornadoes.label: Annapolis North Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado began 3 miles southwest of Annapolis and tracked east-northeast toward N825th St. It continued northeast from there, ending about 4 miles east of Annapolis north of E 2000th Ave. Damage along the path was mostly to trees and electrical transmission lines.

tornadoes.name: Annapolis South Tornado
tornadoes.label: Annapolis South Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down about 3 miles SSE of Annapolis and progressed northeast for 2 miles. During its lifespan it produced primarily tree damage, along with some minor roof damage to a garage. The tornado reached peak intensity near E 1700th Ave and N 825th St where large trees were uprooted. The remainder of the damage was minor tree damage.

tornadoes.name: Dix, IL
tornadoes.label: Dix, IL
tornadoes.notes: An EF-3 tornado touched down 2.5 miles south of Dix along Hwy 37. It quickly intensified and lead to complete destruction of several mobile homes leading to 2 fatalities along July Road and Ranch Lane. A few power poles were snapped and a couple sheds were damaged or destroyed. The degree of tree damage along the path was impressive including dozens that were snapped or uprooted. The tornado crossed over into Wayne County Illinois and was on the ground just over 1 mile before lifting 6 miles northwest of Wayne City. Thank you to the Jefferson County EMA for their assistance with the survey.

tornadoes.name: Hymera
tornadoes.label: Hymera
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down west of County Road 300 E before damaging a barn just to the east with part of the roof ripped off. The tornado caused extensive damage to a grove of trees between County Road 300E and 375E with additional damage to 3 structures along 375E. Structural damage was minor with damage to mainly siding or shingles, but many trees were snapped along the path. The tornado then continued southeastward snapping and uprooting more trees. The tornado crossed 475E before dissipating near State Road 48.

tornadoes.name: Birds Tornado
tornadoes.label: Birds Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down about 3 miles west of Birds and travels for 4.3 miles to the east and northeast. It dissipated about 2 miles north of Birds in southern Crawford County. During its time on the ground it produced primarily tree damage. The peak wind speeds occurred after it crossed Hwy 1 and uprooted and snapped numerous trees between Hwy 1 and E 1350th St.

tornadoes.label: Near Vernon, IL
tornadoes.notes: Video from around 1/2 mile south of the Marion/Fayette county line shows a weak tornado to the north of a treeline along the county line. Just to the west of the tornado in that video, NWS storm survey found minor (EF-0) damage slightly north of the county line.

tornadoes.name: Sims, IL
tornadoes.label: Sims, IL
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado touched down 4 miles northeast of Sims near County Road 1100E. It moved and then flipped a shipping container, shifted a shed off its foundation, destroyed a 12x16 storage shed, and heavily damaged a barn. Otherwise numerous trees were uprooted or snapped along it's path. The tornado lifted north of County Road 1125 E about 5 miles northeast of Sims. Thank you to Wayne County EMA for assistance with the survey.

tornadoes.name: Hadley Tornado
tornadoes.label: Hadley Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado developed 3 miles to the southwest of Hadley. It traveled east through farmland, damaging many trees before lifting southeast of Hadley.

tornadoes.name: Patricksburg
tornadoes.label: Patricksburg
tornadoes.notes: Survey damage suggests a tornado began west of North Humpty Dumpty Road south of Patricksburg, IN just before 7:00 PM local time, and continued eastward for 3 minutes before lifting near North Byerly Road. This tornado caused sporadic tree damage mostly consisting of large tree limbs and a few small tree trunks.

tornadoes.name: Bicknell
tornadoes.label: Bicknell
tornadoes.notes: Drone footage shared from Knox County Emergency Manager shows a swath of damage west of Windmill Road in Knox County associated with a Tornado. The footage shows some large limbs knocked down to the west of high-tension power lines. Then to the east some missing or pulled up metal roof panels of an outbuilding are observed in the video. The strongest damage was observed closer to Windmill Road where large limbs of several hardwood trees were destroyed. Then a metal outbuilding had the roof completely removed and lofted. Panels are observed to the north of the building and the debris field to the east of the structure supports tornadic activity. Based on satellite imagery believe the structure was open to the southeast allowing for an easier inflow of wind into the structure which allowed the roof to be lofted. This resulted in a lowering of the wind speed given the damage indicator. A brief TDS is also evident on radar directly over this location. The tornado then lifted as it approached Windmill Road with some large limbs down along the road. No additional damage was evident to the east of the road.

tornadoes.name: Golden Gate, IL
tornadoes.label: Golden Gate, IL
tornadoes.notes: An EF-0 tornado briefly touched down about 5 miles north northeast of Golden Gate along County Road 1250N. Several tree branches were broken and it also flattened some wheat and corn fields. The tornado appeared to lift along County Road 2900E.
tornadoes.timing_issue: end time is before start time

tornadoes.name: Dover Hill
tornadoes.label: Dover Hill
tornadoes.notes: Weak tornado developed along Dover Hill Road to the southwest of Dover Hill. Tornado moved southeastward crossing SR 450 where a metal bard roof was peeled off and lofted 100 ft and convergence was noted in nearby snapped tree damage. Tornado continued southeast through inaccessible hilly terrain and diminished near Hickory Ridge Road to the north of Shoals.

tornadoes.name: Fort Branch, IN
tornadoes.label: Fort Branch, IN
tornadoes.notes: An EF-2 tornado touched down about 2.5 miles north of Cynthiana near Hwy 65. It travelled northeast before eventually crossing Hwy 41, passing by to the northwest of Fort Branch. It lifted just north of County Road 350 S about 5 miles northeast of Fort Branch. There were 9 large wooden transmission poles that were snapped along Hwy 65 near the start of the track. One home suffered significant roof damage along with several others with minor damage. A church experienced complete roof loss. There were also dozens of trees that were uprooted or had trunks snapped. Thank you to Gibson County EMA for their assistance with this survey.

tornadoes.name: Jeffersonville, IL
tornadoes.label: Jeffersonville, IL
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado touched down 2 miles east of Jeffersonville and continued east along County Road 1320N flattening corn on the north side of the road. At one residence there was a carport lifted up over a barn. Another house suffered damage from a tree falling on it. Tree damage primarily consisted of large branches broken but there were a couple uprooted. The tornado lifted 6 miles east of Jeffersonville. Thank you to the Wayne County EMA for assistance with this survey.

tornadoes.name: Taylorsville
tornadoes.label: Taylorsville
tornadoes.notes: Tornado began east of US 31 and continued northeast through a tree line and into a corn field. A convergent wind pattern was noted within the corn field. Damage to trees occurred just northwest of the intersection of W 450 N and N 110 W. Large trees were uprooted and snapped, blown towards the northwest. The tornado ended just after crossing N 110 W.

tornadoes.name: Mackey, IN
tornadoes.label: Mackey, IN
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado touched down 0.5 miles east of Mackey and travelled along County road 700 S. One mobile home suffered partial roof damage along with an outbuilding that collapsed. Some tree damage occurred along with extensive damage to corn in one of the fields. The tornado lifted 2 miles east of Mackey. Thank you to Gibson County EMA for their assistance with this survey.

tornadoes.name: Lynnville, IN #1
tornadoes.label: Lynnville, IN #1
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado touched down 2 miles north of Lynnville, crossed Spurgeon Road, and lifted 2.5 miles northeast of Lynville along Gore Road. Several power poles were leaning and a few trees experienced some broken large branches. Thank you to Warrick County EMA for their assistance with this survey.
tornadoes.timing_issue: end time is before start time

tornadoes.name: Lynnville, IN #2
tornadoes.label: Lynnville, IN #2
tornadoes.notes: A brief EF-0 tornado touched down 3 miles northeast of Lynnville along Clutter Road. The only damage that was observed was some tree damage including a few that were uprooted. Thank you to Warrick County EMA for their assistance with this survey.

tornadoes.name: Selvin, IN
tornadoes.label: Selvin, IN
tornadoes.notes: An EF-0 tornado touched down along Hwy 68 about 4 miles west of Selvin and continued east before lifting about 3 miles west of Selvin. Several trees were uprooted along its path. Thank you to Warrick County EMA for their assistance with this survey.

tornadoes.name: Eminence
tornadoes.label: Eminence
tornadoes.notes: NWS ground survey along with public reports determined that an EF0 tornado with a 200 yard wide path initially touched down in a wooded area at the end of County Road H-522 to the southeast of Eminence. The tornado damaged a barn then both broke and uprooted trees as it crossed Highway H and along Highway NN to the Rocky Falls Shut In area off County Road NN-526.

tornadoes.name: Dale, IN
tornadoes.label: Dale, IN
tornadoes.notes: A brief EF-1 tornado touched down about 1 mile northwest of Dale. Drone footage showed extensive crop damage in a convergent pattern. Several turkey barns suffered roof damage. One home suffered some shingle damage. There was also a few trees uprooted. Thank you to the Spencer County EMA for their assistance and drone footage of this survey.

tornadoes.name: Newburgh, IN
tornadoes.label: Newburgh, IN
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado touched down 3 miles northwest of Newburgh just north of Deaconess Gateway Hospital. It travelled east just north of Hwy 66 before lifting near the intersection of Hwy 261. The roof of a dentist office was blown off and thrown into an assisted living complex causing the front wall of some units to cave in. Many apartment buildings experienced roof and fascia damage along with some siding loss. A few light poles and at least one fast food sign were damaged. Several sections of roofing and HVAC were removed from Ruler Foods Store. Two people experienced injuries when they were hit by flying debris. Thank you to the Vanderburgh and Warrick County EMAs for their assistance and drone footage of this survey.

tornadoes.name: Harrison County, IN
tornadoes.label: Harrison County, IN
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service conducted a storm survey in Harrison County, Indiana and determined a small EF0 tornado occurred west of Central, IN. Maximum winds were 85 mph and a max path width of 100 yards.

While most damage in southern Harrison County was consistent with straight line wind damage, a small area west of the town of Central had indications of rotation. A home and farm north of Hisey Road and along Ripperdan Valley Road SW had extensive barn roof damage, as well as damage to a garage. While the straight line wind damage was consistently going toward the southeast direction, the damages to the barn and garage were going to the west and southwest toward the center of the tornado passage. Some barn material and barn doors were lofted over the barn, the home, and dropped in the front yard. There was also impalement of wood planks in the backyard in the northeast direction. Several rotational directions were noted on the property consistent with a small EF0 tornado that formed along the leading edge of the thunderstorm squall line.

The tornado continued with sporadic damage into a nearby tree line where there was damage leaning toward the southwest on the north side of the track, and tree damage leaning toward the northeast on the south side of the track, evident of being pulled into a circulation center along Hisey Road. Beyond Hisey Road, several trees and barns had damage near and southeast of Central along Watson Road, Old Goshen Road, and Rehobeth Road. All damages beyond Hisey Road west of Central were in the south to southeast direction, consistent with straight line wind damage.

The National Weather Service would like to thank Harrison County Emergency Management for the help with the damage survey, along with the many helpful homeowners who shared pictures, stories, and access to their properties.

tornadoes.name: Grandview, IN
tornadoes.label: Grandview, IN
tornadoes.notes: A brief EF-0 tornado touched down in the town of Grandview travelling east along 8th Street before lifting just west of Hwy 66. At least one home suffered some shingle damage and a few trees were uprooted or had large branches broken. Thank you to Spencer County EMA for their assistance with this survey.

tornadoes.name: Chandler, IN #1
tornadoes.label: Chandler, IN #1
tornadoes.notes: A brief EF-1 tornado touched down approximately 2 miles northwest of Chandler crossing Tow Path Road. An outbuilding experienced partial roof loss. Dozens of trees experienced snapped trunks along with several others that were uprooted. Thank you to Vanderburgh and Warrick County EMAs for their assistance and drone footage for this survey.

tornadoes.name: Chandler, IN #2
tornadoes.label: Chandler, IN #2
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado touched down about 1 mile northwest of Chandler and carved a path along the north fringes of town before lifting about 2 miles northeast of town. Several power poles were broken and dozens of trees experienced snapped trunks. At least one home experienced some shingle damage. There was also widespread corn crop blown down in one field. Thank you to Vanderburgh and Warrick County EMAs for their assistance and drone footage of this survey.

tornadoes.name: 260622 Harrah
tornadoes.label: 260622 Harrah
tornadoes.notes: A QLCS tornado likely began just north of NE 23rd Street and the Kickapoo Turnpike. The tornado moved south and east through Harrah, producing tree and power line and power pole damage. The circulation moved across the county line, before dissipating.

tornadoes.name: 260622 Wetumka
tornadoes.label: 260622 Wetumka
tornadoes.notes: The Wetumka tornado began at 310 AM south of SH9 to the west of Wetumka. The tornado then produced damage to trees and power lines near the intersection of SH9 and SH27, before moving eastward. The most intense damage was consistent with EF1 damage and/or wind speeds, with trees and power pole damage on the east side of town. South of SH9 and along N381 road, there were a few trees uprooted as well.

tornadoes.label: Near Ozark, AR
tornadoes.notes: This tornado developed just south of Highway 64 and west of Woodland W Road. It moved east-northeast, crossing Woodland W Road and Highway 64, where numerous trees were snapped or uprooted, some fell onto homes, power poles were snapped, and outbuildings were destroyed. The tornado then moved east across two neighborhoods just north of Highway 64. Numerous trees were uprooted or snapped in these neighborhoods and some homes were damaged when trees or large limbs fell onto them. The tornado then turned southeast and crossed Highway 64 near the Highway 23 intersection, where large tree limbs were snapped and signs were damaged. It then crossed the Arkansas River and then Highway 23, and dissipated east of Santa Fe Trail and Aux Arcade Park Road, snapping numerous large tree limbs before it ended. The tornado produced a tornadic debris signature from the KSRX WSR-88D radar.

tornadoes.name: Larkin Tornado
tornadoes.label: Larkin Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
The first area of rotation investigated by our survey team today took place near the intersection of Hwy 65 (near Mile Marker 21) and County Road 27.

Drone footage provided additional views of the start and end point of this tornado, courtesy of Jackson County EMA.

The tornado began in a creek on the property at this location, snapping and uprooting numerous hardwood and softwood trees as it approached the house. The house had minor structural damage consisting of missing shingles and damage to a few gutters.

In the front yard of the home, a small chicken coop was destroyed and a hay-barn-like structure covering the tractor was destroyed as well. The tornado continued moving northeast as it approached the ridge to the east, ending in a flat area on the top of the ridge just beyond Hwy 65.

For now, this is the end point of the tornado. Pending further satellite imagery within the next week, the end point may be extended when/if this data becomes available.

tornadoes.name: New Market Tornado
tornadoes.label: New Market Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
The tornado touchdown southwest of the pond located in Sharon Johnson Park snapping the first initial softwood trees and downing large branches on the property. The tornado continued across the pond, spraying leaf debris across a wide area, before crossing the property line behind the RV park on the premises, further snapping additional hard and soft wood trees.

The tornado then crossed Winchester Road and produced additional damage along Frank Hereford Road. Several trees were sporadically snapped and uprooted along this road, on the farms that dotted the landscape between Hurricane Road and Frank Hereford Road. The road network in this area was too rural for additional specific roadways near the damage other than farmland.

Damage was noted on Hurricane Road close to Mountain Fork Road, where a few trees were snapped. In this location, 5 to 6 wooden power poles were snapped. This was not due to the tornado, it was due to the force of the 70 MPH winds from the line of severe storms moving through the area. Specific convergent tornado damage was noted in this area separate from the damage associated with the line of storms, which matches up very well with radar data that survey teams interrogated.

After producing this damage, the tornado climbed up and over Backbone Mountain, before producing the final damage found on the survey today along Upper Hurricane Creek Road. In this location, the tornado was at its widest (approximately 60 yards) and produced additional hard and soft tree damage. Trees were snapped and uprooted in this area, concurrent with the final rating of EF1 tornado with 90 MPH winds.

The Jackson County line is located approximately 1/4 mile to the northeast of this point. For now, the tornado stops at this point, but it is believed that the tornado continued into portions of Jackson County Alabama and Franklin County Tennessee. Pending additional surveys later this week, this will mark the end point of the tornado for now.

tornadoes.name: New Market Satellite Tornado
tornadoes.label: New Market Satellite Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A small satellite tornado developed to the south of the New Market Tornado, with damage first noted along Hurricane Rd. at 4:03 PM. At this point, trunks of large hardwood trees were partially snapped. The satellite tornado then traveled cyclonically within the circulation of the New Market Tornado, crossing the southern end of Backbone Mountain. Shortly before the satellite tornado merged with the New Market Tornado, it produced sporadic hard and soft wood tree damage along Upper Hurricane Road.

tornadoes.name: Scenic Hills Tornado
tornadoes.label: Scenic Hills Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The third area of rotation investigated today produced another tornado track along Scenic Hills Rd. Several trees were either snapped or uprooted and some tin was peeled off a shed. A power pole was also snapped at a residence where additional trees were snapped and uprooted. The tornado continued skipping along the field as it approached the ridgeline to the east, snapping and uprooting numerous hardwood trees. Here, it produced 107 mph winds damage, consistent with an EF1 tornado. No further damage was noted across Hwy 65 on Koger Lane, ending the track at this location.

tornadoes.name: Francisco Tornado
tornadoes.label: Francisco Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The second area of rotation investigated by the survey team found several trees between 8-10 inches in diameter snapped between 6-12 feet up on the trees along Hwy 65 near County Road 233. Several smaller snapped trees and one larger tree were seen at this location. Tree damage here was found to be consistent with an EF0 tornado, producing 85 mph winds.

tornadoes.name: Reubens Run Tornado
tornadoes.label: Reubens Run Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A discrete storm ahead of an incoming line of storms developed over western Marion County at around 5:30pm on the evening of June 22nd. As the storm matured, it developed mid-level rotation and turned right, becoming more favorable for tornado-genesis. The first sign of a touchdown occurred at 6:11pm, with the time estimated from radar. This occurred just south of Reubens Run Road in Marion County. A narrow swath of trees down was found just south of the road, and one tree was reported down on a car along Cowger Lane. The tornado lifted just one minute later at 6:12pm. In the succeeding minutes, the mid-level rotation weakened aloft upon crossing into Preston County and interacting with terrain.

tornadoes.name: Mutual
tornadoes.label: Mutual
tornadoes.notes:
...NWS Damage Survey for 06/22/26 Tornado Event...

.Mutual MD Tornado...

Rating: EF-0 Estimated Peak Wind: 75 mph Path Length /statute/: 1.3 miles Path Width /maximum/: 75 yards Fatalities: 0 Injuries: 0

Start Date: Jun 22 2026 Start Time: 7:02 PM EDT Start Location: 2.7 W Mutual / Calvert County / MD Start Lat/Lon: 38.471 / -76.598

End Date: Jun 22 2026 End Time: 7:04 PM EDT End Location: 1.3 W Mutual / Calvert County / MD End Lat/Lon: 38.470 / -76.574

Survey Summary: A line of severe thunderstorms moved east into southern MD Monday evening June 22, 2026. This line of storms was the cause of a widespread severe weather outbreak across portions of both VA and MD. One of the storms developed rotation as it moved out of St. Marys County and across the Patuxent River into Calvert County.

Once that storm moved into Calvert County, terminal doppler weather radar at Joint Base Andrews (TADW) indicated an intensifying rotation as it neared Battle Creek, moving quickly east at 50 mph. A drone video captured the tornado developing, and tornadic damage was first reported off Honey Cove Court on the west shore of Battle Creek. Several large branches were snapped on several trees, one fell onto a dock. An eyewitness on Shamrock Ct on the east shore of Battle Creek saw the tornado crossing the creek before they took shelter. More tree damage was reported along Shamrock Court, as well as along Crane Road and Shannon Way. An eyewitness off Crane Road passed along a video recording of rotating and lofted leaf debris. After crossing Shannon Way, the tornado lifted, although intermittent minor tree damage continued in St. Leonard due to downburst winds after the rotation weakened.

The National Weather Service Baltimore/Washington Weather Forecast Office thanks the Calvert County Office of Emergency Management for their assistance. Additionally, thanks to the trained spotters, media, and public that sent in videos of the tornado, as well as damage reports.

tornadoes.name: Barbour
tornadoes.label: Barbour
tornadoes.notes:
An EF1 tornado with maximum estimated winds of up to 110 mph began near Richman Rd and traveled east about 1.1 miles lifting just prior to Bud Edge Rd. A barn near the beginning of the tornado track was destroyed with the debris scattered from NW to SE of the original structure. Debris from the barn was found over a third of mile to the NE.

A double-wide also near the beginning of the path had significant siding damage on the south side and some windows broken out on the west side. The rear end of an SUV parked in gravel next to the double-wide was pushed about 2 feet to the NE while a flag pole in the front yard of the double-wide was blown down in a southwesterly direction.

From there, the tornado traveled through mostly open fields but did intersect a couple patches of hardwood trees. As it descended a small hill near the middle of the path, several healthy and mature locust trees were uprooted and some trunks were snapped about 15 feet up and a swirling pattern was noted in the surrounding pasture grass. One tree was observed down near Bud Edge Rd and this is assumed to be the end of the tornado track as no further damage was found.

We would like to thank the Barbour County Office of Emergency Management & 911 and the homeowner for their assistance with this damage survey.

tornadoes.label: Near Medicine Bow, WY
tornadoes.notes: A brief landspout tornado was documented by storm chasers forming over Highway 30, traveling southeastward up a ridge. The tornado remained over open terrain and was too weak to damage powerlines and fences that it went over. Therefore, this tornado will be rated EF0.

tornadoes.name: Plain Dealing LA
tornadoes.label: Plain Dealing LA
tornadoes.notes:
This weak EF-1 tornado spawned during the evening hours of June 23, 2026, from a quasi-linear convective line segment passing through and near the community of Plain Dealing. A vast majority of the damage was to trees with many hardwood and softwood trees being uprooted along the path. Sporadic softwood tree snaps throughout the assessed path of nearly 5 miles long garnered the peak wind speed of 88 mph for the tornado. Many power lines were downed in the path of the tornado, but the survey team surmises that most of this occurrence was due to trees and tree limbs falling on the lines. Fortunately, the survey team has heard of no human casualties in association with this weak tornado. It is also important to note that there were other sporadic instances of tree damage throughout northern Bossier Parish due to the severe line of thunderstorms moving through during the evening, but the assessed tornado damage featured much more concentrated damage along a path.

Many thanks to the Bossier Parish Office of Homeland Security and Emergency Preparedness for assisting the NWS Survey Team in locating the damage near Plain Dealing.

tornadoes.name: Huntley
tornadoes.label: Huntley
tornadoes.notes:
A brief tornado touched down in a field just northwest of Harmony Road and Briar Hill Road. The tornado moved to the southeast, causing damage to the roof of a barn and downing a few branches. A few metal panels from the roof of the barn were scattered approximately 200-300 yards. A video shows this brief tornado with no clear condensation funnel but swirling debris being lofted.

Thanks to McHenry County EMA and McHenry County Sheriff's Office for their assistance with this survey.

tornadoes.name: Beaver Tornadoes - 06/25/26
tornadoes.label: Beaver Tornadoes - 06/25/26
tornadoes.notes: Most of the tornado path was estimated by triangulating the location using chaser video/pictures and utilizing radar data. Toward the end of the life cycle after becoming rain wrapped and weakening, the tornado did encounter some damage indicators. Damage included large tree limbs which were snapped and one uprooted tree all of which were around an old dilapidated homestead. Adjacent power lines were not damaged and this also provided clues to the intensity toward the end of the life-cycle. Imagery and video suggests the tornado was potentially stronger earlier in the track while in open grasslands. Maximum width was also estimated using photos and video.

tornadoes.name: Los Lunas
tornadoes.label: Los Lunas
tornadoes.notes: Land spout tornado began in an open field southwest of the I25 and Hwy 6 intersection, crossed I25 just south of the intersection moving ENE, then turning more to the NE crossing Hwy 6 east of I25 through multiple businesses. Damage to medal awnings and covered parking caused a debris field damaging multiple vehicles in parking lots. Batting cage netting was lifted into tall light poles for the baseball field SE of Los Lunas High School. There were multiple videos on social media confirming the land spout. NWS employee video showed evidence of where it began. No other damage was found beyond the baseball fields signaling the end point. Damage width based on debris field from emergency management, media and public accounts. Emergency management reported 911 calls around 345PM MT reporting the incident.

tornadoes.name: Sue-Lin Tornado
tornadoes.label: Sue-Lin Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
A storm developed over Muskingum County around 4:30pm on June 25th, 2026. This storm intensified into a supercell in Cambridge, Ohio, before taking a sharp right turn and heading into northern Noble County around 5:30pm. It was at this point that the storm developed low level rotation, which was capable of touching down in Sue-Lin Acres, just north of Senecaville Lake at 5:49pm. Sue-Lin Acres saw the most damage from this tornado, with one softwood tree down, and multiple large branches which fell on top of a camper and a home in the neighborhood. No injures or property damage was noted with these branches down. From there, it moved over the lake, knocking large branches down on the other side, just off of State Route 147. Additional damage, including large branches down and a hardwood tree down were noted along Oak Hill Road, with one tree down across the roadway. From there, only sporadic leaf litter and small branches down were noted along Palestine Ridge Road, Batesville Road, and Burr Road before a final intensification along Maple Drive and Clear Valley Road with one final hardwood tree down with severe large branches off trees. The maximum estimated wind speed with this EF-0 was 75mph at the beginning and end of the track.

Special thanks to Noble County Emergency Management and the Noble County Sheriff's Office for their assistance with this survey. This will go down as Noble County's first tornado since an F2 that occurred on June 27th, 1998. This is the 5th tornado on record for Noble County.

tornadoes.name: 5 West Allison - June 25, 2026
tornadoes.label: 5 West Allison - June 25, 2026
tornadoes.notes: A damage path was discovered across northern wheeler county associated with a supercell circulation suggesting a weak tornado. In addition, a storm chaser documented a periodic funnel clouds with the storm and although it didn't fully condense to the ground, there was periodic dust picked up below at the surface. Isolated damage indicators provided challenges for the survey, however a relatively narrow path of damage mainly consisting of snapped large tree limbs did exits west to southwest of Alison. There was one small out building destroyed as well, but the EF1 tornado rating was based on snapped power poles early in the track. Otherwise, most of the path was EF0 damage.

tornadoes.name: Mount Zion
tornadoes.label: Mount Zion
tornadoes.notes: A National Weather Service ground survey determined that an EF-1 tornado with estimated peak winds of 95 mph occurred a mile southwest of Mount Zion in Douglas County, lasting approximately 2 minutes and traveling a half mile. The tornado produced a 75 yard wide path of tree damage consisting of snapped trunks, uprooted trees, and large branches thrown around. Track extensions are still possible with additional satellite data analysis.

tornadoes.name: Mountain Dale
tornadoes.label: Mountain Dale
tornadoes.notes: A National Weather Service ground survey determined that an EF-0 tornado with estimated peak winds of 80 mph occurred 2 miles north of Mountain Dale, or 4 miles north of Seymour. Both video of the tornado and the ground survey revealed an intermittent 75 yard wide path of mostly tree damage, lasting for 6 minutes and traveling one and a half miles. The most substantial damage was a tin roof blown off a barn. Track extensions are still possible with satellite data analysis.

tornadoes.name: Clark County, IN
tornadoes.label: Clark County, IN
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado touched down in a neighborhood in Memphis, IN. The tornado started along Village Lane. It continued northeast, with the most significant damage to a couple of homes along Nature View and Harmony Woods Roads, where some roofing material was lost. The tornado quickly lifted as it approached Highway 31.
tornadoes.timing_issue: start and end time are identical

tornadoes.name: Stoy Tornado
tornadoes.label: Stoy Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Spotters provided video of a tornado touching down in the vicinity of Stoy IL near the intersection of IL 33 and North 600th Street. They provided images of some minor tree damage. The tree limbs were several inches in diameter.

tornadoes.name: Poseyville, IN
tornadoes.label: Poseyville, IN
tornadoes.notes: An EF-0 tornado touched down about 3 miles east of New Harmony along Old Evansville Road. Damage along it's path consisted of numerous large limbs and a few broken branches of trees. The tornado appeared to lift along Goodman Road about 4 miles southwest of Poseyville. Thank you to Posey County EMA for their assistance with this survey.

tornadoes.name: Lynnville, IN
tornadoes.label: Lynnville, IN
tornadoes.notes: A brief EF-0 tornado touched down in far northern Warrick County about 3 miles north of Lynnville. The initial touch down was just east of Petersburg Road. It moved northeast and knocked a semi-trailer off its blocks, while picking up and moving a grain cart. Several tree branches were broken off as it moved into far southwest Pike County, where it then lifted.

tornadoes.name: Brookport, IL
tornadoes.label: Brookport, IL
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado touched down 1 mile northwest of Brookport along Strawberry Road. It snapped several tree trunks along with producing some damage to the front awning of one house. It continued east crossing Hwy 45 and snapping one more tree along Pell Road before lifting.

tornadoes.name: Belfield Tornado
tornadoes.label: Belfield Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Storm chaser report and video of tornado north of Belfield. Billings County Emergency Manager relayed damage from this tornado. Property owner reported multiple large spruce trees knocked over and uprooted laying in different directions. Also noted apple and olive tree damage. There was some minor roof damage and broken windows to the house and detached garage.

tornadoes.name: Hawley EF0
tornadoes.label: Hawley EF0
tornadoes.notes: Via multiple storm chaser videos and pictures along with radar the tornado was assessed to have tracked for four minutes mainly across farm fields while also striking and inflicting minor tree damage to at least one shelter belt. Further refinements to both the length, placement, and rating of the tornado may occur if additional supporting information becomes available.

tornadoes.label: Near Hoskins, NE
tornadoes.notes: Overhead imagery provided by local emergency management assisted in identifying a short tornado track on the north edge of a larger intense downburst. The evidence of rotation in the damage begins in a corn field near 845 Rd, impacting a farm where it destroyed a barn, damaged several trees and a grain bin, and removed shingles from the roof of a home. The tornado continued across a pasture before damaging several trees along 564 road. The tornado damage evidence appears to end just east of 564 Rd while the broad downburst continues to cause straight-line wind damage for several miles to the east northeast.

tornadoes.label: Near Iron Junction, MN
tornadoes.notes: Final revision of track after reviewing drone imagery of damage path.

tornadoes.label: Near Rock, MI
tornadoes.notes: Path estimated using drone footage provided by Alger County Sherriff Department and ground survey.
tornadoes.timing_issue: duration over 3 hours

tornadoes.name: Iliff TOR
tornadoes.label: Iliff TOR
tornadoes.notes: Quick moving tornado, embedded within a larger area of stronger straightline winds, moved through Iliff, CO right around 830 PM MDT on June 30, 2026. One vacant single wide home was heavily damaged by the swirling winds before lifting to the northeast of town.

tornadoes.name: S of Stacyville, IA
tornadoes.label: S of Stacyville, IA
tornadoes.notes: This very brief tornado damaged a grove of trees. Recorded by multiple storm chasers.

tornadoes.label: Near Oto, IA
tornadoes.notes: A tornado touched down between Hwy 31 and Lee Ave southwest of Oto and moved north across a cemetery, resulting in minor tree damage and the toppling of several old headstones. The tornado continued north and lifted briefly as it crossed Deer Run Trail. The tornado touched down again to the north, damaging trees at a farmstead along Lenox Ave and then damaging an outbuilding near the intersection of 270th St and Lenox Ave. The tornado lifted shortly thereafter north of this intersection.

tornadoes.name: White Creek, WI
tornadoes.label: White Creek, WI
tornadoes.notes: This brief tornado damaged trees and several mobile homes.

tornadoes.label: Near Huron, SD
tornadoes.notes: An intermittent ground circulation was observed by the public south of U.S. Highway 14 from approximately one-half mile west of Dakota Ave N to near Custer Ave NE. This tornado damaged an outbuilding and produced minor tree damage.

tornadoes.name: Hubbell Tornado
tornadoes.label: Hubbell Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Combination of reports, local storm survey by EM and radar information.

tornadoes.name: Lamb's Gap Tornado
tornadoes.label: Lamb's Gap Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado path started just north of Evergreen Dr, and traveled SSW breaking off numerous trees. The most concentrated damage was along Lamb's Gap Rd near the edge of the State Game Lands. The damage seemed to end less than 50 yards to the SW of Lamb's Gap Rd. The tornado was on the ground for approximately 4 minutes. Maximum wind speed was 100 MPH.

tornadoes.name: Lake Bronson
tornadoes.label: Lake Bronson
tornadoes.notes: Video shows a brief spin up tipping what appeared to be a horse trailed as a truck pulled into a cenex at 2:45pm on July 6th. Separete video shows a funnel at the same time.
tornadoes.timing_issue: start and end time are identical

tornadoes.name: Floyd Lake
tornadoes.label: Floyd Lake
tornadoes.notes:
1 injury can be directly attributed to the tornado as a homeowner was injured in their home when their roof was removed by the tornado. The second injury was after the tornado during the cleanup stage and could due to shock or trauma according to the county emergency manager. The details and circumstances of the third injury are unknown as the individual was not transported by EMS.

The tornado appears to have begun about northwest of Wheeler Lake, tracking over the lake where it caused roof damage to a few homes and snapped the trunks of a few large oak and poplar trees on the west side of the lake. The tornado continued east where it appears to have widened to around a half mile in width along the western shore of (Big) Floyd Lake. This is where the highest rated survey damage occurred with a few anchored and modestly built garages were collapsed. A few other more questionably built garages and outbuildings were swept clean in the Oakland Beach neighborhood along with widespread roofing and tree damage. It was in this same area that a 6 by 12 foot horse trailer was lofted and carried about 1/8sm from its stables. The tornado then continued across the lake onto the eastern shore inflicting more roof and tree damage. The last visible surveyed damage was near the corner of Co HWY 25 and Anchor Rd about 3 miles east of the southern end of (Big) Floyd Lake. Based on Satellite the tornado appears to have tracked another 3 miles ESE from where it crossed Co HWY 25.

tornadoes.name: Norcross
tornadoes.label: Norcross
tornadoes.timing_issue: implied speed over 120 mph

tornadoes.name: Butler
tornadoes.label: Butler
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service surveyed damage along with Butler County Emergency Management along Brownsville Rd. A tornado hit a home in the 7700 block of Brownsville Rd, lifting up both the front porch and the carport roof that were attached to the house. The pillars under the front porch shifted slightly, but the pillars under the carport fell over, allowing the roof to land on two cars parked there. The tornado then skipped over mostly open fields before hitting a couple of trees, knocking down branches, and then a barn in the 9600 block. The sides of this barn were well anchored to the ground, but the roof was able to peel off. Portions of this roof were strewn east southeast up to 0.4 miles downstream. The tornado then turned southeastward where it heavily damaged a barn and snapped a large cedar tree at the intersection of Jetson Rd and Brownsville Rd. No other damage was noted downstream of this location.

The National Weather Service would like to thank Butler County Emergency Management for collecting pictures and damage points and escorting us to several residences along the path.

tornadoes.name: Rolla Tornado
tornadoes.label: Rolla Tornado
tornadoes.notes: An EF0 tornado with peak winds of 80 to 85 mph began along Homelife Plaza in Rolla and travelled south before lifting near Soest Road. Tree and building debris was laying in convergent patterns. Additional limbs were downed south of Soest Road, however it could not be determined as tornadic from that point on due to the lack of convergent damage. The tornado was on the ground for a total of 0.7 miles with a width of 200 yards and caused damage to trees and the roofs of several businesses.

tornadoes.name: CasarTornado
tornadoes.label: CasarTornado
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado touched down near Casar, North Carolina. The first evidence of damage was observed along Parker Road near Jesse Mountain Road, where several large pine trees were uprooted or snapped near the tops of their trunks. The most concentrated damage occurred as the tornado tracked eastward across Dirty Ankle Road and Ankle Road. Numerous trees were uprooted or snapped, and several homes sustained primarily minor damage. An attached porch was displaced several feet from a manufactured home. Trees fell in a convergent pattern, supporting the determination that the damage was tornadic. A camper was overturned, and one person who was inside at the time sustained minor injuries. The tornado continued eastward into far northwestern Lincoln County, producing sporadic tree damage near North Carolina Highway 10 before dissipating near the Lincoln County and Catawba County line. The estimated peak wind speed was 90 mph.

tornadoes.name: Uvalde Estates
tornadoes.label: Uvalde Estates
tornadoes.timing_issue: start and end time are identical

tornadoes.name: Shield Ranch Tornado
tornadoes.label: Shield Ranch Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Comparison of high resolution satellite imagery taken on June 27 and July 27 indicates a narrow swath of vegetation damage near and along Shields Ranch/Phillips Rd and Ranch Creek southeast of Camp Wood. The damage swath was consistent and aligned with a weak tornadic debris signature observed on the morning of July 16 from the KDFX WSR-88D. Intermittent tree damage may have occurred farther to the northwest past the northwestern terminus of the defined satellite-observed data swath. This satellite analysis was corroborated with a report of damaged, broken, and mangled live oak canopy along the path reported by the Shield Ranch.

tornadoes.name: SW Maddock
tornadoes.label: SW Maddock
tornadoes.notes: A tornado touched down approximately 4 to 5 miles southwest of Maddock and tracked southeast where it hit a shelterbelt and barns doing EF-0 damage. The track is based on Sentinel satellite analysis showing scarring associated with the tornado tracking to the southeast towards where the damage to the trees and barns were filmed. Width is approximated from scarring visible on Sentinel satellite with the maximum width occurring to the southwest of Legreid Lake early on in the lifecycle.

tornadoes.label: Near Summerville, PA
tornadoes.notes:
NWS Pittsburgh has confirmed a EF1 tornado occurred near Limestone as a storm crossed northern Clarion County on July 18, 2026.

Along Route 66, there was a large, uprooted tree that fell on a house. This was in addition to small trees on the property with snapped branches and uprooted smaller trees. Along Trail 682, there was a group of trees snapped mid-trunk. In this area there was also another large tree uprooted. Damage here was consistent with wind gusts around 90 mph, on the low end of EF1 range.

The storm then continued east-southeast where more damage was noted along Olean Trail. Here, a tree had snapped branches and another tree on a hill top was snapped mid-trunk. No other damage was noted further east.

NWS Pittsburgh appreciates the photo and video imagery provided by Clarion County EMA and Jefferson County EMA.

tornadoes.name: Burnside Township Tornado
tornadoes.label: Burnside Township Tornado
tornadoes.notes: At approximately 4:33 PM EDT on July 18, 2026, a supercell thunderstorm produced a tornado in northern Centre County just east of Eddy Ridge Road near State Line Road. The tornado produced multiple areas of concentrated tree damage over the next 2 minutes as it travelled southeastward for just over a mile in a heavily wooded area. Approximately 200 trees were downed or snapped. We would like to thank the PA Bureau of Forestry for their help with this survey.

tornadoes.label: Near Punxsutawney, PA
tornadoes.notes:
NWS has confirmed a second tornado of EF0 intensity occurred from the same storm as it crossed near Punxsutawney on July 18, 2026.

The storm moved into areas just north of Punxsutawney and caused damage to a BMX track. The track was just off to the east of Scotland Ave. Here, there were numerous instances of uprooted small trees. The damage to the trees were indicative of wind gusts up to 80 mph. The tornado curved northeasterly along Graffius Ave, consistent with a rapid occlusion of the circulation at the end of its brief existence.

NWS Pittsburgh appreciates the photo and video imagery provided by Jefferson County EMA and Punxsutawney Fire Department.

tornadoes.label: Near Latrobe, PA
tornadoes.notes:
A brief tornado occurred on July 18, 2026 to the north of Latrobe. An aerial damage survey suggests the tornado began near Red Cut Lodge Rd, and progressed southeast, crossing Route 981 before dissipating.

An earlier tornado LSR was issued confirming this tornado. No damage to crops or trees was evident along Stewart Rd where the LSR was issued.

Damage with the tornado was consistent with wind gusts up to 75 mph, which leads to this tornado being rated EF0. The path length, width and magnitude are all subject to change pending additional information received.

tornadoes.label: Near Derry, PA
tornadoes.notes:
NWS Pittsburgh has confirmed a brief tornado southeast of Derry, PA from a storm on July 18, 2026.

Sporadic damage primarily to trees was noted along a path beginning near Carey Ln and continuing southeast across Matson Rd through heavily wooded areas. A review of aerial photography has helped identify impacted areas inaccessible by foot.

At its peak, damage appears consistent with wind of up to 70 mph.

Beyond this point, no damage was evident. However, the path, magnitude and width of the tornado is subject to change pending additional reported damage coming to light.

tornadoes.name: Jenner Township Tornado
tornadoes.label: Jenner Township Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A supercell moving across Westmoreland County began showing increasing rotation as the cell moved into northern Somerset County during the early evening hours of Saturday, July 18, 2026. A tornado associated with this supercell formed northwest of Conemaugh Township Reservoir. The damage at tornado onset was mainly in the form of multiple trees being uprooted in a convergent pattern before the tornado strengthened and produced a widespread swath where all trees in the area just west of the reservoir were completely snapped. This entire swath of hardwood trees comprised of mostly healthy hardwood trees with virtually no trees remaining standing in a quarter mile swath. Tree damage continued onto the south end of the reservoir, with multiple snapped and uprooted trees being knocked into the south end of the reservoir before shifting to a more southeasterly path following Ferndale Road for a brief period of time. Concentrated convergent tree damage continued to be observed on Ferndale Drive leading up to the reservoir before the damage became more sporadic and less convergent north of Ferndale Road near Bens Creek. NWS State College would like to thank the Conemaugh Township Municipal Authority for drone imagery of this damage near the reservoir and Somerset County Emergency Management Agency on their collaboration on this damage survey.

tornadoes.label: Near Deposit, NY
tornadoes.notes:
A tornado touched down along Farnham road approximately 3 miles south-southwest of Sanford at 6:12 PM on July 18th. It caused sporadic EF-0 damage along Farnham road, mainly consisting of trees snapped or uprooted. There was minor damage to an old barn along the road and a gazebo was lifted into a pond. The tornado strengthened to EF-1 intensity (maximum winds of 95 mph) as it approached NY State Route 41, snapping and uprooting numerous trees, and power lines.

The tornado crossed Oquaga Creek and caused more EF-1 level damage on Farnham Road and Old Plank Road. The damage mainly consisted of numerous downed trees, including a tree that fell onto a car. A home was damaged when the metal skirting was blown out from underneath it on Farnham Road. The tornado continued tracking southeast over a hill and paralleled Old Plank Road and Old Route 17 where it caused lighter sporadic tree damage at an EF-0 level. The weak tornado continued south and east, crossing State Route 17 just west of exit 83. It continued south and east, likely causing sporadic damage as it crossed over the inaccessible Whittacker Swamp State Forest. There was visible damage of numerous trees down and snapped along the hillside just west of River Road and State Highway 17. The weak tornado continued on, to the south and east causing light damage as it moved through the town of Hale Eddy, NY.
