Additional tree damage was noted across the Delaware River along Penn York Road.

The tornado crossed NY Route 17 again and moved across the town of Hancock, causing significant tree damage at the Hancock Golf Course. The tornado then crossed county highway 268 and the East Branch of the Delaware River. It restrengthened to EF-1 and caused significant tree damage mainly along the south bank of the river, along with some damage to out buildings and porches of residences. The tornado lifted just southeast of Peas Eddy Road as it moved up the hill.

The same storm later resulted in a strong microburst about a mile and a half northwest of Rock Valley. This microburst resulted in extensive tree damage, including numerous snapped and uprooted trees with a path length of 0.7 miles and path width of 0.3 miles. The maximum winds were estimated to be 105 mph.

We would like to thank Delaware County Emergency Services and the Town of Hancock Fire, as well as local residents for their assistance with this survey.

tornadoes.label: Near Houtzdale, PA
tornadoes.notes:
Tree damage began near the northwest terminus of Gum Street and continued east-southeast toward Morann Avenue (PA-153). Several pine trees were snapped off halfway up between Gum Street and Hemlock Street along with minor damage to a few structures. Upon crossing Morann Avenue, the tornado moved across N Railroad street and continued to produce extensive damage to trees and power lines. A single wide mobile home and adjacent vehicle were shifted slightly northeast as winds surged around the south side of the circulation. Farther northeast toward the intersection of N Railroad St and Hale Rd, a chimney was ripped off the side of a house and a couple trees fell northwest/upwind. Seeing trees fall opposite the direction of the tornado's motion provided the confidence to lean toward the upper end of damage indicators, making this a high-end EF-1 at 110mph.

Remarkably, there was only very minor damage to many of the structures in the path of this tornado, but extensive snapping of trees. In particular, the forested area southeast of N Railroad Street and southwest of Hale Rd suffered extensive tree fall. Dozens to perhaps hundreds of trees were knocked over and/or snapped off. The camp owner at the top of the hill at the southeast edge of the forested area remarked that he could not previously see the mountain to his northwest. His previously "shaded" camp now had a much improved view, he said. Again, little to no damage occurred to any of the structures (campers and a cabin) at the camp, but extensive tree damage occurred. The tornado then briefly lifted/stopped producing damage to the southeast of a hilltop as it crossed an open field. Damage resumed as the tornado moved back into a forested area along Hale Rd toward Sonia Ln. Extensive tree and powerline damage was observed along that stretch with a convergent pattern of tree fall. The damage became much more sporadic as the circulation crossed Moshannon Creek, marking the end of the tornado path.

NWS State College would like to send a sincere thanks to Clearfield County Department of Emergency Services and the Houtzdale Fire Company for their assistance with today's survey. Additional surveys may be conducted in the coming days for this severe weather event and additional Public Information Statements will be sent as needed.

tornadoes.label: Near Olivia, PA
tornadoes.notes:
A line of thunderstorms with an embedded supercell moved through northeast Blair County the evening of Saturday July 18th. The same storm that produced a tornado about 7 miles to the northwest near Houtzdale produced another tornado along Vanscoyoc Hollow Rd in Camp Anderson. The tornado began just north of Decker Hollow Rd and continued southeastward across Vanscoyoc Run Stream and Camp Anderson Lake before lifting just past the southeast-most campsite. A few trees on the north side of the track fell to the southeast, while several trees on the south side of the track fell northeast or east-northeast, indicating convergence associated with a tornado.

Additional sporadic tree damage was observed farther southeast along Vanscoyoc Hollow Rd, but it was spread out enough to preclude extension of this tornado path.

We would like to thank the owners of Camp Anderson along with Blair County Emergency Management Agency for their assistance with this survey.

tornadoes.label: Near Chapin, IA
tornadoes.notes: Intermittent tornado path that produced damage to roof of home along with convergent signature in the corn field.

tornadoes.label: Near Aplington, IA
tornadoes.notes: This tornado track was identified using satellite imagery and drone overflights.

tornadoes.label: Near Carney, MI
tornadoes.notes: Drone footage and on ground surveys indicate swath of damage to mostly large white pines of approximately 1 to 3 feet in diameter. Damage path is cyclonic in nature, with varying damage path directions along within the northern half of the polygon.

tornadoes.name: S of Kellogg, MN
tornadoes.label: S of Kellogg, MN
tornadoes.notes: This very narrow tornado damaged one farmstead. The track was too narrow to discern in satellite imagery and is derived from the radar rotational signature and TDS.

tornadoes.name: E of Whitehall, WI
tornadoes.label: E of Whitehall, WI
tornadoes.notes: Public report of a brief tornado that was corroborated with a radar TDS. No damage reported or observed via satellite. Since it occurred over trees, it is rated EF0 vs. EFU.

tornadoes.name: Stratford_Tornado
tornadoes.label: Stratford_Tornado
tornadoes.notes: At approximately 7:15 PM CDT a small tornado touched down at the Wisconsin Farm Technology Days. The tornado produced minor damage to one tent and a few portable restrooms. There were subsequently several reports of tornadoes in the Stratford area from this tall, skinny thunderstorm. Location and path determined from photos, video, and radar time-matching.

tornadoes.name: SW of Black River Falls, WI
tornadoes.label: SW of Black River Falls, WI
tornadoes.notes: This tornado was observed via webcam images and produced an impressive TDS, but no damage was found via a partner survey or in Sentinel satellite imagery. Given that it went over trees, it is rated EF0 vs. EFU.

tornadoes.name: Zoar_Tornado
tornadoes.label: Zoar_Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Storm chaser report of a tornado in the Zoar area from a tall, skinny thunderstorm. The tornado crossed highway 47 between Neopit and Zoar, producing some tree damage. Location and path determined from photos, video, and radar time-matching. Winds estimated to be around 70 mph.

tornadoes.name: SE Ritchie Co
tornadoes.label: SE Ritchie Co
tornadoes.notes:
The tornado began just east of Rt 16 and then tracked east-southeast, crossing Leatherbark Rd and then up the adjacent hillside snapping large mature hardwood trees at the center of a nearly half mile wide path. A house near the edge of the track had some shingle damage to the roof. The tornado continued east-southeast from there ending just prior to Rock Lick Rd.

Thanks to the landowner for access and assistance with this survey.

tornadoes.name: Greene11
tornadoes.label: Greene11

tornadoes.label: Near Waymart, PA
tornadoes.notes:
A brief small spin up tornado occurred on the western edge of Wayne County in the South Canaan vicinity.

A heavy shower starting exhibiting loose rotation while crossing the Archbald Mountain ridge. As the shower dropped in elevation, rotation quickly tightened to spin up a short-lived tornado. It took out well-established apple trees in an orchard, while causing siding and soffit damage to a couple houses as well as destroying a hunter shed. The tornado lost some intensity while tracking over and then past Lake Quinn, before falling apart shortly after Easton Turnpike.

tornadoes.label: Near Greene, NY
tornadoes.notes: A second confirmed EF1 tornado occurred within a Quasi-Linear Convective System (QLCS) at 145 PM EDT on Tuesday July 21. Though this line caused scattered damage in general, a tornadic convergent pattern was evident starting near the Shafer Wylie Horton Road intersection. It nearly paralleled Wylie Horton Road for a few miles, and then caused its heaviest damage to a farm just west of Bowbell Road. A haybarn lost its roof and most of its walls, with material strewn across the street and wrapped around a telephone pole. A roof section was lofted at least 100 yards. Roof material from other outbuildings, and the top of a silo, were removed. A section of cinder block wall collapsed from tornadic inflow. The tornado also uprooted a large section of trees just east of Bowbell Road, while departing to mainly south of Wylie Horton Road. The tornado weakened before crossing Highway 235, with the path becoming discontinuous. The tornado ended around 152 PM EDT.

tornadoes.label: Near Stanhope, NJ
tornadoes.timing_issue: duration over 3 hours

tornadoes.name: Zane2
tornadoes.label: Zane2
tornadoes.notes:
A weak EF0 tornado commenced just north of Fultonham near Workman road. Video evidence of a funnel cloud was captured just prior to this touchdown near the Muskingum - Licking county line. The twister then had intermittent touchdowns as it moved east southeast through the southern part of the county. Most of the damage was single trees down and large branches. The amount of damaged trees that were visible during the survey was less than 50 for the duration of the track. This number could increase pending additional reports over the coming days. The storm traveled east downing a few trees in Avondale on the west side of state route 93. When it arrived near Baughman run and Butterbean ridge area large limbs and a few hardwood trees were observed to be down. The last observed damage point was along Buttermilk Road east of Gaysport where large limbs were down along Buttermilk road. No structural damage nor injuries were observed or reported.

The National Weather Service would like to thank Muskingum county Emergency Management Agency for all their assistance.

These are the 32nd and 33rd tornadoes on record for Muskingum county since 1880. The last tornado to affect Muskingum county was June 6th 2024. With these tornadoes, this brings our office count for the year up to 27 tornadoes. The average number per year is eight. For a state breakdown this is what we have:

Ohio: 5 West Virginia: 2 Pennsylvania: 21

tornadoes.name: Amelia OH
tornadoes.label: Amelia OH
tornadoes.notes:
The first evidence of tornadic damage was observed at the Pierce Reserve & Trails on Pond Run Road, where numerous large tree limbs were knocked down. The tornado strengthened as it moved southeast onto Mott Road, where roof damage was observed at a two story home along with numerous trees being snapped in an adjacent wooded area. Winds in this area were likely near 90 mph, which corresponds to EF-1 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale. Tree damage was common and in a very convergent path along Fagins Run Road and Wilson Dunham Hill Road. While damage became more sporadic farther southeast, additional tree damage within the convergent tornadic path was reported at a residence on OH-132 and Wildfire Way. Large tree limbs were also knocked down along New Richmond Nicholsville Road, and this is where this tornado appears to have ended.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Clermont County Ohio Emergency Management Agency and Pierce Township Fire Department for their assistance with this storm damage survey.

tornadoes.name: Lees Creek OH
tornadoes.label: Lees Creek OH
tornadoes.notes:
The first evidence of tornadic damage was observed at a single family residence off of Henry Rd, where a hardwood tree was snapped and fell onto the roof of the home. Additionally, the field adjacent to the home had some flattened corn stalks, with minor tree damage also observed across the street. More flattened corn stalk was found in a field near the intersection of Henry Rd and State Highway 729.

The most significant damage came along Larrick Rd, with several properties observing tree damage. One property in particular had six trees that were either uprooted or snapped at the base. Wind speeds in this area were likely near 75 MPH, which corresponds to EF-0 strength on the Enhanced Fujita Scale.

The last observed damage came on Larrick Rd where a tree was uprooted and additional corn stalk was partially flattened. No other visible evidence was observed to the south and east of this property.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Clinton County Emergency Management Agency for their assistance with this storm damage survey.

tornadoes.name: Zane1
tornadoes.label: Zane1
tornadoes.notes:
Damage from this tornado commenced off of Darlington road with large branches down and a few uprooted trees. Given limited road access there were just spotty reports as the storm traveled east through Moxahala Ridge. The most significant damage of the storm occurred on Old River road where an estimated 100-200 down hardwood trees were snapped, uprooted, or large limbs knocked over. The peak tornado intensity was located here and just across the Muskingum river on the property of Shelly and Sands where part of an outbuilding roof was lifted. The storm lifted as it skirted through Duncan Falls, OH causing large limbs to come down. Tree damage was reported on both sides of the river south of Durant road of State Route 60 before entering Duncan Falls.

The National Weather Service would like to thank Muskingum county Emergency Management Agency for all their assistance. We would also like to thank a media station out of Columbus Ohio for providing drone footage.

These are the 32nd and 33rd tornadoes on record for Muskingum county since 1880. The last tornado to affect Muskingum county was June 6th 2024. With these tornadoes, this brings our office count for the year up to 27 tornadoes. The average number per year is eight. For a state breakdown this is what we have:

Ohio: 5 West Virginia: 2 Pennsylvania: 21

tornadoes.name: NE of Owenton KY
tornadoes.label: NE of Owenton KY
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service has confirmed an EF1 tornado in Carroll, Gallatin, Owen, and Grant counties in Kentucky. This tornado occurred during the afternoon of July 21, 2026.

The first evidence of the tornado was along Kentucky State Route 47 near and northwest of Interstate 71 in Carroll County, where some large branches and a couple trees were downed. Much more significant damage occurred between the Gallatin County Airport and Eagle Creek, including State Route 467. Significant tree damage was noted here, including a majority of the trees along the Eagle Creek bottomland with their trunks snapped. This is believed to be one of the locations where the tornado was near peak intensity, with maximum winds of around 110 MPH. Drone footage provided by the Gallatin County Sheriff's Office confirmed the scope of the tree damage at this location. Additional stands of snapped trees were observed near New Liberty Sparta Road.

As the tornado moved into Owen County, a property on State Route 35 near US Route 127 sustained significant damage to numerous outbuildings. On Stewart Ridge Road, one residence was destroyed, with wood posts on a concrete slab snapped off. An injury occurred at this location when a large RV was rolled by the tornado. An old tobacco barn near this location was destroyed, and several snapped trees were also observed in the vicinity.

On Golden Circle Road and Jonesville Road, numerous trees were downed, and roof damage was observed on several outbuildings. One home on Jonesville Road had its roof lifted. Another outbuilding was destroyed at a property on Agee Road, with significant damage to trees along the hillside near this location. Drone footage provided by Owen County Search and Rescue provided significant help for determining the location of damage in this area.

The tornado weakened somewhat as it approached State Route 22, with just a few trees damaged. However, a more concentrated area of downed trees was noted near the bridge on Cross Roads Drive and Lusby Mill Road, as the tornado crossed from Owen County into Grant County. One house near this bridge had significant roof damage. The last observed damage was at a property north of Keefer Road. At this property, three outbuildings were mostly or completely destroyed, and the house lost a significant portion of its roof. The brick garage of the house was shifted very slightly on its slab foundation, with cracks in some of the bricks noted. Debris from this location was carried into the tree line to the east. This location is also a place where the tornado was near peak intensity, with maximum winds of around 110 MPH. The tornado weakened as it moved east, with occasional additional damage noted north of Keefer Road, on US Route 27, and on Fork Lick Road.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the emergency management agencies in Carroll, Gallatin, Owen, and Grant counties, along with Kentucky Emergency Management Area 6, for their assistance in this damage survey.

tornadoes.name: Feesburg OH
tornadoes.label: Feesburg OH
tornadoes.notes:
A tornado occurred just east of Feesburg during the mid afternoon of July 21. Damage was first observed along State Route 505 where multiple pieces of a roof were blown off of an outbuilding along with a tree being downed across the road. The tornado then continued moving to the southeast along Day Road where numerous trees were snapped and downed along a convergent path. Additional tree damage occurred along Eden Road up to Daugherty Marks Road before the tornado dissipated.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Brown County Emergency Management Agency for their assistance with this storm damage survey.

tornadoes.name: Hardin County
tornadoes.label: Hardin County
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado occurred along Railroad Trestle Road that caused tree damage, including snapping large tree trunks and branches. Fortunately, no structures were damaged from this tornado. The tornado lifted after 1 minute on the ground, with very little damage seen at the triangular intersection of Louisville Nashville Turnpike and Railroad Trestle Road.
tornadoes.timing_issue: start and end time are identical

tornadoes.name: Tornado 1
tornadoes.label: Tornado 1
tornadoes.notes:
THE NATIONAL WEATHER SERVICE IN COORDINATION WITH LOCAL AND STATE PUBLIC SAFETY OFFICIALS CONFIRMED A SHORT LIVED AND INTERMITTENT EF0 TORNADO THAT DEVELOPED IN PURCHASE, WESTCHESTER COUNTY, NY AND TRAVELED EAST NORTHEAST TOWARD RYE BROOK, NY. THIS CONFIRMATION WAS STRENGTHENED BY RADAR EVIDENCE OF A ROTATING THUNDERSTORM WITH NON- METEORLOGICAL DEBRIS (LIKELY LEAVES AND SMALL BRANCHES) LOFTED SEVERAL THOUSAND FEET ABOVE THE GROUND.

THE TORNADO LIKELY BEGAN ON MANHATTANVILLE COLLEGE CAMPUS WHERE IT UPROOTED SEVERAL TREES IN ADDITION TO SNAPPING LARGE BRANCHES. THE TORNADO LIKELY LIFTED BEFORE TOUCHING DOWN TO THE SOUTHEAST AND SHEARING OFF THE TOPS OF TREES AND UPROOTING A FEW TREES ON LINCOLN AVENUE NEAR LODEN LANE. THE TORNADO LIKELY LIFTED ONCE AGAIN, BEFORE MAKING FINAL TOUCHDOWN TO THE EAST NORTHEAST NEAR LAWRIDGE DRIVE AND DOWNING A FEW TREES AND WIRES. THE TORNADO LIKELY LIFTED ONE LAST TIME AND DISSIPATED BEFORE THE STORM MADE ITS WAY OVER THE NY/CT STATE LINE, WITH A SPOTTER REPORTING TREE BRANCH AND LEAF DEBRIS LITTERING DOWN ON THE HUTCHINSON PARKWAY SHORTLY BEFORE 420PM.

THE NATIONAL WEATHER SERVICE WOULD LIKE TO THANK WESTCHESTER COUNTY EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, HARRISON NY POLICE DEPARTMENT, CONNECTICUT DIVISION OF EMERGENCY MANAGAEMENT AND HOMELAND SECURITY, BROADCAST MEDIA, AND SPOTTERS WHO SHARED VIDEO AND PHOTOGRAPHIC EVIDENCE, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC WHO SHARED REPORTS THROUGH SOCIAL MEDIA, IN ASSISTING THE SURVEY AND FORMULATING THIS PRELIMINARY DAMAGE REPORT.

tornadoes.name: Washington to Pleasants #1
tornadoes.label: Washington to Pleasants #1
tornadoes.notes:
The tornado began between Glendale Rd and Hartline Rd in the Caywood community, then tracked southeast through the Hills community, knocking over a silo and damaging several homes. The most intense damage and EF2 rating occurred along State Route 26 near the intersection with Township Road 635, where a roughly 600 yard long by 400 yard wide patch of pine trees was completely mowed down with every trunk snapped several feet above the ground. The tornado weakened while still causing sporadic tree damage as it continued to the southeast, crossing the Ohio River on the west side at Newell Run and entering West Virginia at Belmont damaging and rolling several camper trailers at Riverview Estates. The tornado then continued southeast up a ridge then skipped through the Green Run neighborhood before dissipating.

Thanks to the Washington County, OH Sheriff's Office and Emergency Management Agency, who provided excellent video of the track taken by their drone. Also, thanks to Tyler County, WV Search and Rescue for also providing drone imagery and an aerial survey of the track in West Virginia.

tornadoes.name: Washington to Pleasants #2
tornadoes.label: Washington to Pleasants #2
tornadoes.notes:
The tornado began between Newells Run Rd and Kerr Run Rd, where numerous trees were uprooted and snapped before tracking southeast through Newport, where some minor damage occurred to homes and some sporadic tree damage was noted. The tornado then strengthened as it crossed the Ohio River and entered the West Virginia side at the Saint Marys Bridge. A large sign was left barely hanging off the side of the bridge structure and a large patch of trees around the bridge showed significant damage. From there, the tornado tracked southeast up the hillside reaching peak intensity and a high end EF2 rating near the intersection of Greens Run Rd and Rt 16 where several homes suffered significant damage, a roughly 600 yard wide by 300 yard long patch of hardwood trees was leveled, and a large communications tower was buckled over. The tornado path then became intermittent as it skipped basically along Rt 16 to the Cloverdale community, then ended near the Ritchie County line east of Rock Run Rd.

Thanks to the Washington County, OH Sheriff's Office and Emergency Management Agency, who provided excellent video of the track taken by their drone. Also, thanks to Tyler County, WV Search and Rescue for also providing drone imagery and an aerial survey of the track in West Virginia.

tornadoes.name: Washington to Doddridge
tornadoes.label: Washington to Doddridge
tornadoes.notes:
The tornado began in the Wayne National Forest near Archers Fork Rd, then tracked southeast through the Leith Community, crossing the Ohio River and entering West Virginia near Raven Rock. The tornado then took a non-continuous path in a southeasterly direction through northern Pleasants County, southern Tyler County, northern Ritchie County, before lifting finally near Arnolds Creek Rd in Doddridge County.

It is interesting to note that the tornado track became increasingly wide, expanding to three-quarters of a mile wide at the Pleasants/Tyler line, along Rt 74 near Mountain, WV, and along Long Run Rd in Doddridge County, but only EF0 to EF1 tree damage was found in these areas. However, most of the track was over a very rural area with wide spans of forest between the available road network so it is likely that higher end damage was missed by the ground survey.

Thanks to Tyler County, WV Search and Rescue for providing an aerial survey of parts of the track.

tornadoes.name: Bourbon County Tornado
tornadoes.label: Bourbon County Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
A personal video was received that showed damage just to the west/southwest of property along Oldson Road in far southeast Bourbon County. The video clearly depicts lofted debris, with a small circulation moving across the field. A field survey was unable to reach the suspected minor tree damage.

A big thanks to NWS Jackson, KYEM, and Bourbon County Emergency Management who helped up with this survey and tracking this video down.

tornadoes.name: Grayson-Hart County Tornado
tornadoes.label: Grayson-Hart County Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
An NWS Storm Survey concluded than a long track, EF-2 tornado touched down in far eastern Grayson County, right along Nolin River Lake in the Wax, KY area. The worst of the accessible damage was noted here towards the beginning of the track, where winds of 115 mph did significant damage to some homes and outbuildings along Nolin River Lake. One injury was reported in this area where a man sustained a head injury from the tornado.

The tornado maintained high-end EF-1 strength throughout much of the rest of its path through Hart County. This high end EF-1 damage was most widespread and pronounced from the town of Rowletts and southeast along Red Buck Estes Road. Most trees and structures had some sort of damage in these areas and this is likely where the tornado was at its peak width. The tornado continued southeast along Lonoke Road into the small town of Uno, KY, where it finally lifted before crossing into Metcalfe County, KY. In total, the path was over 20 miles long and this tornado was on the ground continuously for 41 minutes!

NWS Louisville would like to express gratitude to Kentucky Emergency Management, Grayson County Emergency Management, and Hart County Emergency management for their timely reports of the damage and their help with the survey process.

tornadoes.name: Casey/Lincoln County
tornadoes.label: Casey/Lincoln County
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service confirmed a brief EF-1 tornado touchdown in northeast Casey County and northwest Lincoln County, Kentucky. A briefly tornadic storm first produced a tornado in far northeastern Casey County along Kentucky Highway 78 just north of the intersection with Kentucky Highway 906 around 5:37 PM EDT. Several large tree trunks were snapped near the intersection of a home on a hillside next to an open field. Estimated wind speeds from the tree damage were observed at 95 mph which is EF-1 damage.

The tornado continued moving NE parallel to Kentucky Highway 78 and damaged a barn just downstream of the hillside home that was also in the middle of an open field. The north-facing roof slope had large sections of roofing ripped off, with estimated tornado wind speeds around 95 mph as well. Then, the tornado continued moving NE snapping large trunks and tree limbs on the southern facing side of a small forest next to the open field. The tornado here slightly increased in strength, with estimated winds here near 100 mph, or high-end EF-1 damage.

Beyond the barn, the tornado continued its track NE through the open field with scattered tree cover. It began weakening as it moved towards Black Pike in far western Lincoln County west of Hustonville. At 5:39 PM EDT, power poles were snapped along with additional large tree limbs snapped with estimated winds of 85 mph, or a high end EF-0. Shortly after, the tornado lifted and no other tornadic damage was observed.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Casey Emergency Management teams for assistance with this damage survey.

tornadoes.name: Barbour County
tornadoes.label: Barbour County
tornadoes.notes:
An EF0 tornado with maximum estimated winds of up to 85 mph began around 5:38 PM just south of Taylors Drain Road along a railroad track. It then traveled southeast along the railroad track before lifting at approximately 5:39 PM. The length of the track is estimated at 0.35 miles, but could be longer given limited road access in the area. Multiple hardwood trees were either uprooted or snapped along the track of the tornado. Some of the hardwood trees that were uprooted were in excess of 18 inches in diameter.

Barbour County now has a total of 5 tornadoes dating back to the late 1800s. The last tornado that occurred in Barbour County was an EF-1 on June 22, 2026 that touched down just northeast of Moatsville, or approximately 6 miles east-northeast of the track of this tornado.

We would like to thank the Barbour County Office of Emergency Management with this damage survey.

tornadoes.name: Knob Lick Tornado
tornadoes.label: Knob Lick Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
An EF-1 tornado occurred in northwestern Metcalfe County, near Knob Lick, during the late afternoon hours on July 21, 2026. The tornado first touched down just north of Glenn Finn Road at 5:19 PM CDT and continued south-southeast. The tornado produced EF-0 damage initially between Glenn Finn Road and Ratliff Mitchell Road. The tornado then strengthened as it crossed Ratliff Mitchell Road and produced winds over 100 mph and caused EF-1 damage, especially to a large barn near a residence on Pleasant Valley Church Road. Debris was lofted to the SSE across an empty field, and metal roof panels were found wrapped around trees nearly 1000 feet away along McCandless Coomer Road.

The tornado continued southeastward nearly parallel to Pleasant Valley Church Road, eventually crossing it, and creating additional EF-1 tree damage. The tornado then lifted just north of Knob Lick at approximately 5:25 PM CDT, near the intersection of Pleasant Valley Church Road and Sulphur Well Knob Lick Road.

tornadoes.name: High View WV
tornadoes.label: High View WV
tornadoes.notes:
A tornado descended on the 5100 block of Back Creek Road. Here there was roof and siding damage to the house and outbuildings. On this farm property and to the east through unpopulated forest, thousands of trees were downed (80 to 90 percent at one point just east of property), many of which were hardwoods 1-2 feet thick snapped at the trunk.

Once the tornado crossed the ridge into Virginia, notable tree damage occurred across the northernmost part of Wilde Acres, VA. Damage was first visible on Otter Trail and extended southeast with damage visible on each street until stopping near Fawn Drive. While tree damage was visible throughout this path, the greatest concentration of damage was on Cardinal Drive. Trees were observed uprooted, snapped, or sheared off at the top. Considerable leaf and small branch debris was observed throughout the entire path.

The National Weather Service thanks both Hampshire County WV Office of Emergency Management and Frederick County VA Emergency Management Division for their assistance with this survey.

tornadoes.label: Near Hydetown, PA
tornadoes.notes:
A storm persisted over Crawford County around 6:00pm. This storm intensified into a supercell over the county, before heading into northern Venango County around 6:34pm. With ample low-level rotation as evidenced by local radar, the cell proceeded to touch down at 6:37pm in Diamond, PA. The most evidence of tornadic activity was noted by a hardwood tree down in a tree-line north of town with some tree tops snapped by wind. This was the tied for the strongest damage indicator, with 80mph wind estimated. Some medium sized branches were snapped off trees in Diamond-proper, but most damage observed was from a prior storm which moved through on June 14th, 2026. The damage direction from this tornado was observed from northeast-to-southwest, while the June damage direction was east-to-west. Additional tree damage was observed on the east side of PA-428 before the tornado moved into a wooded area. A large tree was down in a similar direction on Goodwin Road, which signaled the final damage on the tornado track, with estimated wind speeds also at 80mph. This will go down as a 80mph EF-0, that lasted 2 minutes and traveled about one mile.

Venango County now has a total of 10 tornadoes dating back to 1950. The last tornado that occurred in Venango County Pennsylvania was on June 14, 2026. This was an EF-0 tornado that touched down east of Diamond.

tornadoes.name: Edmonton Tornado
tornadoes.label: Edmonton Tornado
tornadoes.notes: An EF-0 tornado touched down along Joe Stephens Road. It did some concentrated tree damage in this area. The tornado traveled south/southeast towards Greensburg Road, where it removed part of a roof on the southward face of a mobile home, along with tree damage. The tornado continued southward across the Cumberland Parkway. The most widespread damage was along Columbia Road, where large limbs were toppled on to some homes and some large trees were uprooted. The tornado continued its narrow path through a residence along Breeding Road, where it likely lifted just south of Breeding Road.

tornadoes.name: Youngstown Tornado
tornadoes.label: Youngstown Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
A National Weather Service Storm Survey team has determined that an EF-0 tornado with maximum estimated winds of 85 mph occurred in Trumbull and Mahoning Counties on July 21, 2026. The tornado extended for over 6 miles with a maximum path width of about 100 yards.

The tornado formed in the southeast portion of Liberty Township in Trumbull County, Ohio at the northwest corner of Hubbard Road (US Route 62) and Logan Gate Road, where a couple tree branches were snapped. The tornado continued southeast along Applegate Road, crossing into Hubbard, causing more tree damage and some minor roof damage to a residence, exhibiting 85 mph winds. Dozens of trees were damaged further southeast in a heavily wooded area, as the tornado crossed into Mahoning County and into the Youngstown city limits. The tornado entered the McGuffey Heights neighborhood with tree damage observed in the vicinity of Jacobs Road and Orrin Avenue and extending southeast onto Gerwig Avenue. The tornado reached the vicinity of Coitsville-Hubbard Road (Ohio State Route 616) and McGuffey Road causing more minor tree damage and flipping a wagon that was attached to a heavier trailer. The tornado reached the vicinity of North Hubbard Road and Johnson Road, prompting more minor tree damage. The tornado intensified once again to 85 mph along Wilson Lane with a concentrated area of large snapped tree branches that caused minor damage to a residence. The tornado then uprooted several trees along Oak Street before continuing southeast to the Ohio/Pennsylvania state line, north of US Route 422.

From here, this tornado continued southeast into Lawrence County, Pennsylvania. Please see the Public Information Statement from the National Weather Service office in Pittsburgh for details for that portion of the tornado.

In summary, for Ohio, this EF-0 tornado had estimated maximum wind gusts of 85 mph in southwest Hubbard and southeastern Coitsville Township and was on the ground for about 16 minutes, extending for over 6 miles with a maximum path width of about 100 yards.

The National Weather Service would like to thank Trumbull County and Mahoning County Emergency Management Agencies with their assistance in the storm survey.

tornadoes.name: Randolph County
tornadoes.label: Randolph County
tornadoes.notes:
An EF1 tornado with maximum estimated winds of up to 95 mph began around 6:55 PM just west of Whitmer Road midway up Rich Mountain, or approximately 2 miles northwest of the town of Whitmer. It then traveled east-southeast down the steep terrain of the mountain, uprooting or snapping numerous trees along its path, with most of the damage in the hollow down the side of the mountain. Some of the hardwood trees that were uprooted were in excess of 18 to 24 inches in diameter. The tornado continued to the valley at the bottom of Rich Mountain, with the last observed damage just east of Dry Fork Road. The tornado lifted at approximately 6:57 PM and was on the ground for 0.90 miles.

Randolph County now has 6 documented tornadoes. The last time a tornado occurred in the county was 7/9/1980. Two tornadoes occurred that day, one was rated an F2, while the other an F1.

tornadoes.name: Seneca Rocks WV Tornado
tornadoes.label: Seneca Rocks WV Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A tornado briefly touched down near Seneca Rocks just after 7 PM. Damage was limited almost entirely to trees. About 30 to 50 percent of trees were damaged on property in the 400 block of Thunder Road, with trees mostly uprooted in a convergent pattern. The tornado tracked east-northeast. None of the farm buildings sustained significant damage, nor did the house on the property. The tornado crossed the road and tracked up a hillside across the street with continued tree damage before dissipating after about two minutes.

tornadoes.name: Kiser Gap WV
tornadoes.label: Kiser Gap WV
tornadoes.notes:
Scattered to numerous large trees uprooted and snapped along the path that started along Kiser Gap Road a half mile north of the intersection with US Route 33. The tornado tracked east- northeast. Where it crossed the 1600 block of Troublesome Valley Road it snapped a tree down over the road on a vehicle. The driver was extracted uninjured.

Substantial tree damage continued over the 1000 to 2300 blocks of Corner Road, and 6500 to 7000 blocks of Sweedlin Valley Road and the 300 block of Redbud Hill Lane. The tornado then tracked through an unpopulated, wooded area across the ridge/state line. It reached the 24300 block of Gochenour Lane 3 miles southwest of Criders. The damage continued up Gobble Mountain before lifting.

In summary, thousands of trees were downed along this rural 10.5 mile path. In peak intensity areas, most of the trees in the path were uprooted or snapped. Structural damage was mainly from tree falls, although there was some wind damage to siding and outbuildings noted.

The National Weather Service thanks the Pendleton County Office of Emergency Management for their invaluable assistance to this survey.

tornadoes.name: Timberville
tornadoes.label: Timberville
tornadoes.notes:
A tornado touched down on a farm in the 19300 block of Mechanicsville Road. Numerous trees on this property had their tops snapped off, with farm equipment (trailers and carts) tossed about. In the woods surrounding the property, a path of trees were snapped and uprooted in a convergent pattern. About 50 to 60 percent of the trees in the path were blown over. The tornado tracked through unpopulated woods and fields for about a mile before reaching another farm in the 19600 block of Cold Spring Road. Here, additional trees were uprooted or snapped at the top.

The tornado continued east and crossed the 800 and 900 blocks of Ridge Road where approximately 50 trees were downed, one on a chicken coop structure. Further tree damage occurred along the 1900 and 2000 blocks of New Market Depot Road where several trees were uprooted and snapped, with numerous large branches snapped down. The final noted damage was to the 500 block of Hayneswood Lane where one large tree was uprooted and several large branches were snapped.

The NWS thanks local broadcast media for their assistance in collecting damage reports.

tornadoes.name: Glen Ellyn
tornadoes.label: Glen Ellyn
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado began near the intersection of Stacy Court and Railroad Street in unincorporated North Glen Ellyn. A narrow corridor of primarily tree damage continued south-southeast across portions of Glen Ellyn. This damage included large branches that fell onto power lines and damaged some homes and a vehicle. Damage in this area was consistent with peak winds near 75 mph. The tornado continued southward, producing additional sporadic tree damage until it dissipated northwest of Glenbard West High School near the intersection of Hawthorne Boulevard and Park Boulevard.

tornadoes.name: Wheaton
tornadoes.label: Wheaton
tornadoes.notes:
This brief tornado began in the vicinity of E. Liberty Drive and S. Washington Street south of Wheaton College. A concentrated corridor of damage was noted, particularly in the vicinity of E. Indiana Street and Campbell Avenue and along Pershing Avenue where the tops of several softwood trees were snapped and numerous limbs were downed. Damage in this area was consistent with peak winds near 75 to 80 mph. The tornado continued southward, producing sporadic tree damage until it dissipated in the vicinity of Alchester Drive.

Additional damage was noted in the area which was likely associated with a swath of damaging straight-line winds that moved through a few minutes after this tornado occurred.

tornadoes.name: Appleton-Menasha, WI
tornadoes.label: Appleton-Menasha, WI
tornadoes.notes:
NWS Damage Survey team confirmed a tornado touched down around 11:56 AM CDT in Appleton in urban southern Outagamie County and moved south through northeast Winnebago County, causing damage consistent with an EF3 rating to portions of Menasha, before it dissipated over Lake Winnebago around 12:22 PM CDT.

The tornado developed just north of Wisconsin Avenue in Appleton, partially tearing the roof off houses and several businesses on Wisconsin Avenue consistent with EF0 damage and winds of 85 mph. The tornado strengthened south of Wisconsin Avenue to EF1 by collapsing exterior walls to a warehouse building east of North Perkins Street with winds of 110 mph. The tornado continued producing EF1 damage to warehouses, retail buildings and strip malls as it continued south to College Avenue. The tornado strengthened to EF2 south of College Avenue near South Perkins Street by buckling the roof purlins to a metal building structure with winds of 118 mph. The tornado continued to produce EF1 damage through the rest of southern Outagamie County, by snapping and uprooting trees as well as damage to residential buildings, reaching the county line around 12:00 PM CDT as it crossed the Fox River while widening to around 1000 yards.

The tornado entered northeastern Winnebago County around 12:00 CDT, producing EF1 damage by snapping and uprooting trees and damaging residential buildings just south of the Fox River. The tornado continued to widen and eventually strengthened again to EF2 damage just south of Palisades Drive by uplifting significant portions of the roof deck and collapsing garage doors to residences with winds of 120 mph. The tornado continued to strengthen and widen, reaching a width of 1400 yards and producing EF3 damage to a well-built low-rise brick building just north of Highway 10 in Menasha. At this location, significant damage occurred to the exterior walls and some interior walls with winds of 140 mph.

The tornado path then narrowed south of Highway 10 in Menasha to just below 1000 yards, producing pockets of EF2 damage along and just south of Midway Road by collapsing an entire roof with winds of 125 mph. EF2 damage was also observed east of highway 10 near Airport Road with the collapse of the exterior walls of a small professional building and winds of 135 mph. The tornado continued south and damaged the bleachers at Calder Stadium east of Racine Road, consistent with EF2 damage and winds of 120 mph.

The tornado widened again as it tracked south, reaching its maximum width of 1500 yards between 5th and 6th street in Menasha between Little Lake Butte des Morts and northern Lake Winnebago. The tornado again reached EF3 intensity just south of this area, between Plank Road and 3rd Street. In this area a car was flipped over, there was a collapse of exterior walls of a small retail building, and a house was destroyed with winds of 140 mph.

The tornado continued south, crossing the Menasha Channel and producing EF2 damage to eastern Doty Island east of Smith Park with large sections of roof structures removed to residential structures along with snapped trees and exterior walls collapsed on one residence with winds of 130 mph. The tornado then tracked over Lake Winnebago passing east of Neenah Point. Although the tornado at this point mainly stayed over the water, it did clip Davis Point, producing EF0 damage by uprooting trees with winds of 85 mph. The tornado continued south and eventually dissipated over Lake Winnebago somewhere east of Perkins Point.

tornadoes.name: Downers Grove
tornadoes.label: Downers Grove
tornadoes.notes: This tornado touched down near the intersection of Maple Avenue and Brookbank Road before continuing southeastward through neighborhoods on the south side of Downers Grove. Damage along the path of the tornado consisted of snapped and uprooted trees and downed tree branches. The tornado appeared to lift over McCollum Park. This tornado was within a broader region of straight-line winds and was identified by a corridor of locally more intense wind damage with tree branches torn from the tops of trees as well as a subtle radar debris signature visible on KLOT radar imagery.

tornadoes.name: Romeoville
tornadoes.label: Romeoville
tornadoes.notes: Based on a storm survey and radar data from TMDW, a brief EF-0 tornado touched down near or just northeast of the intersection of Illinois Route 53 and Material Road across from Romeoville High School. The tornado then traveled southward along Route 53 and passed directly over the campus of Lewis University. Damage on the campus consisted of numerous downed and snapped tree limbs, damage to a dugout and fencing material at a baseball field, and damage to an HVAC system on the roof of a university building. The tornado appeared to lift near Renwick Road.

tornadoes.name: Orland Park
tornadoes.label: Orland Park
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down near W 131st Street near Tampier Slough and moved southeastward across western Orland Park. Numerous trees were downed along the path of the tornado before it lifted in a neighborhood west of Orland Square Mall.

tornadoes.name: Country Club Hills - Glenwood
tornadoes.label: Country Club Hills - Glenwood
tornadoes.notes: This tornado appeared to start just east of Interstate 57 and moved eastward, crossing Interstate 80 on the northwest side of Country Club Hills. The tornado then progressed east-northeastward through Hazel Crest, downing trees and tree limbs and removing roofing material off of multiple apartment buildings along 171st Street. After crossing Interstate 80 again at the junction with Interstate 294, the tornado made an unusual counter-clockwise loop as it tracked into the east side of Markham and then the southwest side of Harvey, causing primarily tree and cosmetic structure damage. After reaching its northernmost point between W 154th Street and W 155th Street, the tornado looped back southward, rapidly accelerating as it re-entered Markham and Hazel Crest. The tornado reached its peak intensity here, removing the roof of an industrial building on W 167th Street and causing exterior wall and roof damage to an apartment complex on 171st Street. After crossing Interstate 80 for a third time, the tornado continued southeastward through the north and east sides of Homewood. There, four double-stacked intermodal containers weighing approximately 75 tons each were tipped over in a rail yard, and numerous additional trees were damaged. The tornado caused more tree damage on the northwest side of Glenwood before dissipating near the Glenwood Academy. There were 12 injuries reported associated with the tornado.

tornadoes.name: Lynwood - Munster
tornadoes.label: Lynwood - Munster
tornadoes.notes: The tornado touched down just east of State Route 394 and progressed northeastward into the community of Lansing. Damage along the path was most severe in a neighborhood near Heritage Middle School where several homes sustained damage to exterior walls and roofs. The tornado continued northeastward, causing primarily tree damage and cosmetic damage to structures while moving into Indiana before lifting on the far west side of Munster. Two minor injuries were reported in Lansing as a result of this tornado.

tornadoes.name: Sweester_Marion, IN
tornadoes.label: Sweester_Marion, IN
tornadoes.notes: Ground and drone surveys found a swath of sporadic wind damage from Sweetser to Marion and near Gas City Indiana. Within this swath, evidence of a weak, disorganized circulation touching down was noted in some locations. The tornadic damage began in a cornfield near W 200 N and N 500 W on the north side of Sweetser, IN. The tornado crossed over the cornfield and impacted a neighborhood on the northeast side of Sweetser. Several large tree branches were downed and a few tree trunks snapped on Allen Drive, Mary Lou Road, and Laura Lane. The tornado continued southeast, affecting residences on W Magers Road where significant tree damage occurred including a large tree falling on the roof of a house. Another residence experienced large tree branches downed along with damage to fencing. The tornado crossed N 400 and caused damage to an apartment complex including large tree branches downed and some roof damage to a few of the apartment buildings. The tornado then affected open fields before crossing State Road 18 causing damage to a trucking company facility on the south side of State Road 18. Much of the roofing material was removed, but the plywood boards remained intact. Some of the debris from the damage to this facility was tossed to the north side of State Road 18 including a steel reel. The tornado then continued southeast across open fields between County Roads 325W and 200W before causing extensive tree damage to residences from W 9th Street to W 16th Street between Buffalo Avenue and Norton Avenue. Survey results indicate a transition occurred from tornado damage to straight line wind damage on the south side of Marion to the southeast of State Road 9 and towards Gas City. Maximum winds are estimated around 75 mph.

tornadoes.name: Hoopeston Tornado
tornadoes.label: Hoopeston Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Video evidence of a touchdown of a tornado just outside of Hoopeston. Minor damage occurred to two light poles. The tornado traveled to the south for a mile before dissipating behind a bank building.

tornadoes.name: Camp Creek Tornado
tornadoes.label: Camp Creek Tornado
tornadoes.notes: On the afternoon of July 28th, a southeast moving supercell thunderstorm spawned a short-lived tornado in the Camp Creek area. The tornado was first identified via the Tornado Debris Signature algorithm on radar. Due to the very rural nature of the area where the tornado occurred, detailed analysis was impossible. However, with the use of drone imagery and satellite date the office was able to determine that a defined path of tree damage occurred from just south of Camp Joshua Lane across Norton Spring and into the higher terrain of Green Mountain. Based on satellite imagery, the path width was estimated to be a maximum of around 300 yards with a maximum intensity around 95 mph.

tornadoes.name: MarshallTor
tornadoes.label: MarshallTor
tornadoes.notes:
An EF-0 tornado, with peak estimated winds of 80 mph, touched down in the Allegheny area of Madison County. Initial tree damage, consisting of broken large branches and a few uprooted or partially snapped trees, was first observed along Rock Branch Road. The tornado tracked southeastward across Highway 212, producing the most concentrated area of damage along the southward-facing slope of Shelton Laurel Creek, where numerous trees were snapped and uprooted. The track continued southeastward to Cutshall Town Road, where several pine trees were snapped. Additional broken branches and possibly a few uprooted trees were noted in a distant wooded area looking back toward the creek. All observed tree damage was consistent with EF-0 intensity.

Although the damage was relatively minor and sporadic, it correlates well with radar data showing a tornadic circulation moving through the area. Due to the rugged, mountainous terrain, earlier portions of the potential track were inaccessible by ground survey teams. The National Weather Service will continue to evaluate the exact start point in the coming weeks if high-resolution satellite imagery becomes available.

tornadoes.name: Riviera Beach Tornado
tornadoes.label: Riviera Beach Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
What likely began as a waterspout moving toward the south- southwest over the tidal Patapsco River moved onshore along Cox Creek in the Riviera Beach area of northeastern Anne Arundel County. A grill was flipped and numerous trees were snapped near the top, falling in a convergent manner near the intersection of Waterview Drive and Riverside Drive.

The tornado continued toward the south, where a street sign was bent and large sections of siding were removed from a house near the intersection of Waterview Drive and Hilltop Road; numerous trees were downed in a convergent manner on this block, as well. Large tree limbs and tree tops were snapped near the intersection of West End Drive and Park Place, with additional large limbs twisted off and tops of trees sheared off near the intersection of West End Drive and Fieldstone Place.

The tornado then crossed Stoney Creek near the bridge on MD-173 Fort Smallwood Road, before felling additional trees and a power pole prior to dissipating in the Sunset Beach area.

The National Weather Service thanks trained spotters, media, and local emergency officials for their assistance in this survey.

tornadoes.label: Near Cape St. Claire, MD
tornadoes.notes:
A tornado descended around Patapsco Road where a few trees were uprooted and snapped. As the tornado tracked through New York Avenue and Magothy Road, the intensity of the wind increased with numerous trees uprooted along with a power pole and several tree trunks snapped. A boat was also lofted into the air, over a pier, and onto a jet ski. Damage was laying in different directions, indicative of rotation. A large tree also fell onto a house. Another home off Magothy Road had roof singles ripped off, along with a loss of some siding. The tornado tracked over Grays Creek and more trees were uprooted along Dobbins Lane. Numerous trees were uprooted along Edgewater Road with damage facing different directions. A few tree trunks were snapped as well. A security camera near Edgewater Road recorded the swirling winds passing through.

Based on data from the FAA BWI Terminal Doppler Weather Radar, the tornado continued across the Magothy River, moving onshore in Cape St. Claire just east of Persimmon Point. Damage consisting of snapped and uprooted trees was observed along River Bay Road and in the vicinity of Broadview Drive and Saint Catherine Drive. Here, an eyewitness observed dust and debris that had been lofted into the air. The tornado lifted near this area, prior to the mouth of the Little Magothy River, as radar data showed it being undercut by outflow associated with the storm that had previously spawned Tornado 3 listed below. No additional damage has been reported to the east of this point.

tornadoes.name: Arnold Cape Saint Claire
tornadoes.label: Arnold Cape Saint Claire
tornadoes.notes:
Survey Summary: A tornado touched down in a wooded area north of Shore Acres Road in the 900 block, with trees snapped at the top. The tornado tracked east crossing Lake Drive in Cape Saint Claire. Significant tree damage was observed in a convergent direction. Many healthy hardwood trees up to a few feet in diameter were toppled. On Lake Drive, and a garage door of a house was completely blown in, with some insulation removed.

The National Weather Service thanks the Anna Arundel County MD Office of Emergency Management for their assistance with this survey.

tornadoes.name: 20260728_graham
tornadoes.label: 20260728_graham
tornadoes.notes: A brief, weak tornado developed near Lake Santeetlah in Graham County. The first damage was observed from a distance on a ridge near Funnel Top Mountain where several trees were down. The tornado traveled SSW and crossed Highway 143, downing trees along the road. Additional trees were downed along a trail just east of Snowbird Mountain Lodge. The path was sporadic with just some limbs down as the tornado traveled WSW, with additional trees downed along Old Santeetlah Road and W Buffalo Rd.

tornadoes.label: Near Tate, GA
tornadoes.notes:
A brief tornado occurred across very complex terrain of eastern Towns County (far northeast Georgia) during the evening of July 28th. The tornado was embedded within a severe line of storms (quasi-linear convective complex / QLCS). This line produced additional tornadoes as it moved south over north Georgia.

Ground and aerial (drone) surveying revealed the tornado damage came from mainly trees snapped or uprooted, initially seen along Hwy 76, near Adkins Lane. Multiple trees were down heading up the ridge from Hwy 76 and additional damage was seen from Hwy 76 looking west toward the Towns and Rabun county line.

A big thanks to NWS Greenville-Spartanburg for leading this ground survey.

tornadoes.label: Near Talking Rock, GA
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado occurred in north Pickens County, GA in the late evening hours of July 28, 2026, first producing damage at 10:29 PM EDT. Damage was first observed to the south of the Pickens/Gordon County line, where a few trees were uprooted near a home on Phil Dundee Way. The tornado continued southeast, where it uprooted trees along the northern portion of Outback Rd. To this point, the uprooted trees combined with minimal damage near the ground indicated that the rotation remained mainly elevated, only sporadically touching the surface. As it continued along its southeast path, the tornado brought trees down across E Price Creek Rd and additionally uprooted or snapped trees on Outback Ridge Trail. The most substantial damage occurred near a home at the intersection of Outback Ridge Trail and E Price Creek Rd, where several trees were uprooted and another was snapped. A barrier comprised of 6x6” boards was also pulled from the ground by one tree being uprooted. The elevation of the terrain decreased to the south of this location, though there were signs of disturbance in the trees along the downward slope. The next indicator of damage was observed along Jack Pinyon Rd where a tree was snapped. Additional damage occurred near the intersection of E Price Creek Rd and Mountain Crest Dr where smaller trees and limbs were downed on both sides of the road. After taking a more southerly turn, the tornado last produced damage on Old Burnt Mountain Rd where a partially dead tree was brought down across the road. The tornado appears to have dissipated by 10:33 PM EDT.

tornadoes.label: Near Chamois, MO
tornadoes.notes: Video from local resident shows tornado moving through a wooded area just west of Highway 89. The tornado impacted the resident's farm, causing minor damage to the house and partial roof loss to an outbuilding. Minor tree damage was also noted in the vicinity. Path is based on video footage and details provided by resident.

tornadoes.label: Near Terre du Lac, MO
tornadoes.notes: An EF1 tornado formed along Stoney Point Rd and briefly tracked southeastward, producing sporadic tree damage and minor structural damage before dissipating over Lac Capri.

tornadoes.label: Near Folly Beach, SC
tornadoes.notes: Waterspout formed offshore and moved onshore. Waterspout was videoed by several onlookers. Tents were thrown up in the air.

tornadoes.label: Near Indianapolis, IN
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado quickly developed and touched down at approximately 5:20 PM EDT near the corner of Madison Avenue and Southern Avenue. A large was tree uprooted with a few large branches and smaller tree limbs scattered around the area. Additional minor siding damage was done to a nearby home. The tornado moved north along Madison Avenue causing additional damage to trees and minor siding damage to another home. A truck trailer was pushed towards the north denting a parked truck. The tornado uprooted or snapped a few trees near Christel House South Academy before quickly dissipating at approximately 5:22 PM EDT.

tornadoes.name: St. Leon IN
tornadoes.label: St. Leon IN
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service has updated EF0 tornado during the early evening of August 1, 2026 in Dearborn and Franklin counties in Indiana. A concentrated area of damage in southeast Franklin County was updated to 90 MPH or EF1 damage.

Damage was first observed just east of Lawrenceville, Indiana along Batta Road, near the Batta and Legion Road intersection. Some roof damage to farm buildings was observed, as well as a large farm wagon overturned. The tornado appeared to cross over farm fields where crops were flattened. The tornado then crossed Legion Road where there were several large trees that were damaged or snapped. Peak wind in this area was estimated to be near 70 MPH.

The tornado continued north-northeast and continued to produce tree damage as well as garage door damage along Trackville Road just north of Old Hickory Road. Peak wind in this area was estimated to be between 70 and 75 MPH.

The tornado continued into southeast Franklin County, where it strengthened slightly to produce roof damage to a single family home as well as roof and wall damage to barns. Peak wind in this area was estimated to be between 75 and 80 MPH.

The tornado continued north-northeast to properties just northwest of the intersection of Saint Peters and Stone Roads. There was additional roof damage to a single family home, as well as the destruction of 3 barns, as well as some snapped pine trees and hardwood tree damage. It was in this area where the peak wind was updated to near 90 MPH or EF1 damage.

The tornado continued to move north-northeast along a narrow path through southeast Franklin County, producing additional barn and tree damage along Wewe Hill Road which was consistent with wind damage between 70 and 75 MPH.

The tornado is believed to have dissipated just north of where Wewe Hill Road becomes West to East, about 2 miles southwest of Cedar Grove.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the emergency management agencies in Dearborn and Franklin Counties for their assistance in this damage survey.

tornadoes.name: Bledsoe/Cumberland EF0 Tornado
tornadoes.label: Bledsoe/Cumberland EF0 Tornado
tornadoes.notes: At approximately 6:21 PM, a tornado touched down near Grapevine Road in Bledsoe County and moved northeast into Cumberland County. The tornado uprooted trees, removed shingles, and damaged multiple outdoor buildings and a barn. It continued to track to the northeast crossing a wooded area before lifting near Jerry Edmonds Road.

tornadoes.name: Bledsoe Tornado
tornadoes.label: Bledsoe Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The start of the weak tornado occurred in Bledsoe County near Grapevine Road about one quarter of mile south of Cumberland County at approximately 621 PM EDT. Several trees were uprooted. No structures were affected in Bledsoe County. This track represents the start and end of the tornado in Bledsoe County. The tornado then continued into Cumberland County before dissipating 4 miles NW of Melvine. The total path length of the tornado was 1.77 miles.

tornadoes.name: Fentress County EF0
tornadoes.label: Fentress County EF0
tornadoes.notes: At approximately 6:22 PM, a tornado touched down near Heiness Road in Fentress County. The tornado snapped treetops and uprooted a few trees. It continued to track to the northeast before lifting near Baseline Road.

tornadoes.name: NW of Eaton OH
tornadoes.label: NW of Eaton OH
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service has confirmed an EF1 tornado northwest of Eaton in Preble County, Ohio.

This tornado primarily impacted areas near Surface Road. The first known damage occurred on the 1600-1700 block of Surface Road. There was some minor roof damage to well-built homes. One barn was destroyed, with cinder block wall collapse, and some sheet metal roofing material thrown into the field to the east.

Damage was then observed on the 1300-1400 block of Surface Road, where significant roof damage was noted at two homes, with sections of roofing material entirely removed. This damage supports wind speed estimates of 100 MPH. Other homes in the area had some minor roof damage. Tree damage was also extensive in the back yards of these homes, with several large healthy trees snapped.

Drone images provided by the Preble County Emergency Management Agency also depicted significant corn field damage in the vicinity of Surface Road. This damage also extended well to the east of Surface Road. Some of this corn field damage is from the tornado, but there is also a large expanse of flattened corn to the north of the path of the tornado, especially northeast of the bend on Surface Road. Much of the northern extent of the corn damage is oriented from northeast to southwest, suggesting a wide swath of strong inflow in the opposite direction of the tornado's motion. No damage of any kind was observed closer to State Route 726.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Preble County Emergency Management Agency for their coordination and assistance.

tornadoes.name: Franklin OH
tornadoes.label: Franklin OH
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service has confirmed an EF0 tornado in Franklin in Warren County, Ohio.

Southwest of Franklin, several large tree limbs were downed along Hamilton-Middletown Road and State Route 73. As the tornado moved northeast, more tree damage was noted on Dayton-Oxford Road, and a segment of a corn field near Water Source Drive was flattened. Just northeast of Water Source Drive, one large metal building at an industrial facility had a large portion of a northwest-facing wall removed, along with a portion of the roof. Damage at this location supported wind speed estimates of 80 MPH, the highest wind speeds from this tornado.

Several tree limbs were downed in a neighborhood near Forest Ave, Chestnut Street, and Park Ave. One house on Park Ave had some siding damage.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Warren County Emergency Management Agency for their coordination.

tornadoes.name: New Lebanon OH
tornadoes.label: New Lebanon OH
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service has confirmed an EF0 tornado east of New Lebanon in Montgomery County, Ohio.

The tornado first developed near Stacey Road, moving to the north. Corn field damage was evident in satellite imagery, beginning just south of Stacey Road. Additional corn field damage, with some tree damage, was observed near Germantown Liberty Road, south of Forney Road. The tornado then moved due north, on a track that closely approximated Snyder Road until reaching US Route 35. Along this stretch of Snyder Road, there was extensive tree damage, including a few large trees uprooted or broken near the base. One barn on the east side of Snyder Road lost a portion of its roof.

North of US Route 35, some shingle damage occurred at a business, with a few garage doors damaged at a storage facility. Some additional tree damage was noted to the north of these businesses. Satellite imagery depicted additional corn field damage as the tornado progressed to the north, dissipating just east of Snyder Road near Old Dayton Road.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Montgomery County Emergency Management Agency for their coordination.

tornadoes.label: Near Hazleton, IA
tornadoes.notes: A well documented, large spatially, HP supercell, low-level mesocyclone produced an EF2 tornado along its 5 mile path. Most of the damage was EF1 damage to structures and trees. It is likely that this tornado had numerous short-lived vortices on the ground leading to the damage observed. Towards the end of it's path. The tornado snapped a wooden H frame power pole at its base, and also pulled four other H frames from the ground. The damage to the powerpoles suggests winds at least up to 120 MPH.

tornadoes.label: Near Prairieburg, IA
tornadoes.notes: A short lived EF1 tornado with max winds to 100 MPH hit a farmstead causing damage to an outbuilding. A piece of the roof of that building was shot through the wall of the house. The homestead then experienced 2 to 3 minutes of 80 to 90 MPH straight-line winds.

tornadoes.label: Near Richland, IA
tornadoes.notes: An EF1 tornado with max wind speeds of 95 MPH entered the west end of Rubio and tracked across the entire town ending east of town at the end of it's 1.4 mile long path. One house had damage to shingles and a carport was completely destroyed. Gravel caused damage to the north side of the house while the carport and a basketball hoop was thrown to the west. Some trees were snapped as well in town. Numerous branches were down throughout town. To the east damage to crops were noted.

tornadoes.name: Washout
tornadoes.label: Washout
tornadoes.notes: A waterspout developed from a shower just offshore of Folly Beach, SC near the Washout area around 1235 PM. The waterspout moved slowly west-northwest before coming onshore as a tornado around 1236 PM, near the Fort and East Ashley Avenue intersection at the Washout. The tornado moved across the beach, throwing a few tents/umbrellas, chairs, surfboards and beach coverings into the air before dissipating just beyond East Ashley Avenue approximately 30 seconds after reaching land. Damage was minimal, with only minor impacts seen on video at the beach given a lack of vegetation and structures in the vicinity. Despite the tornado moving directly over a group of people, no injuries have been reported. Based on public video footage and the lack of damage indicators, the tornado is rated EF0 with maximum winds estimated to be near 55 mph.

tornadoes.name: Amboy
tornadoes.label: Amboy
tornadoes.notes: A tornado began just east of Amboy near Shaws. This tornado tracked northeast and then turned slightly northwest as it crossed U.S. Highway 30 before dissipating south of Pipeline Road. The tornado caused damage to trees, power lines, outbuildings, and crops along its nearly 7-mile long track.

tornadoes.name: Streator
tornadoes.label: Streator
tornadoes.notes: A tornado began southeast of the intersection of N 17th Road and Illinois State Route 23. It initially tracked towards the northeast before making a counterclockwise loop and eventually dissipating near E 18th Road and N 16th Road. It caused damage to multiple outbuildings, a few houses, trees, crops, and utility poles along its nearly 5-mile-long track.

tornadoes.name: Kernan
tornadoes.label: Kernan
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began near the intersection of N 16th Road and E 21st Road northeast of Streator. It made a nearly complete 5.1-mile-long counterclockwise loop, causing damage to trees and crops and peeling shingles off of a house before dissipating a little less than half a mile north of its start point.

tornadoes.name: Ransom
tornadoes.label: Ransom
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began southwest of the intersection of N 17th Road and E 23rd Road northwest of Ransom. It initially tracked northeastward, then westward towards E 22nd Road, before looping back towards its start point. The tornado appeared to increase in size as it tracked eastward along N 17th Road, but remained at EF-0 intensity here with damage being confined to trees and crops. The tornado then jogged northeastward, downing power poles and damaging outbuildings along E 24th Road before reaching EF-1 intensity as it destroyed an outbuilding along N 18th Road between E 24th Road and E 25th Road. Outbuildings and trees were damaged at a farmstead along N 19th Road as the tornado began to turn east, and additional damage to crops and power poles occurred just east of this farmstead as well. The tornado then derailed several empty autorack rail cars east of E 26th Road before curving back towards the northwest, then southwest and dissipating north of the intersection of N 19th Road and E 26th Road.

tornadoes.name: Baltimore
tornadoes.label: Baltimore
tornadoes.notes:
Survey Summary:

On Tuesday, August 11, 2026, the National Weather Service Baltimore/Washington Weather Forecast Office sent a team to the City of Baltimore and Baltimore County to survey storm damage from thunderstorms that occurred on August 10, 2026. Additionally, several videos from trusted sources were received and analyzed, along with weather radar and eyewitness reports.

Video taken from the Johns Hopkins Bayview Medical Center shows a brief circulation, likely a waterspout, over the Patapsco River moving towards the Seagirt Marine Terminal, Port of Baltimore. As the waterspout moved onshore, it became tornadic, and continued east-northeast toward Broening Highway where a large hardwood tree was uprooted and another hardwood tree was snapped. The tornado crossed Colgate Creek and a power pole was snapped along Ralls Avenue just east of Colgate Creek. The tornado continued to track east-northeast and a vehicle was displaced around Sollers Point Road in Dundalk. A tree was also uprooted in this area and an awning was ripped off an apartment as well. The tornado dissipated around this area. The FAA Terminal Doppler Weather Radar for Thurgood Marshall BWI Airport (TBWI) showed a tornadic signature along this path, corroborating the damage observations.

Based on radar observations from nearby TBWI and damage on the ground, it was determined that an EF-0 tornado, with a maximum velocity of 65 MPH, path width of 90 yards, and a path length of 2.0 miles occurred Monday afternoon in the City of Baltimore and Baltimore County.

The National Weather Service thanks trained spotters, media, and local emergency officials for their assistance in this survey.

tornadoes.name: SouthernJay
tornadoes.label: SouthernJay
tornadoes.notes: Jay County Emergency Management found a narrow damage path through a mature soybean crop as they were traveling on S 350 E in extreme southern Jay County. This crop damage seemed to be going from NW to SE. An original short EF-U tornado was designated as there was originally no evidence of this tornado hitting one of the designated damage indicators. Due to improving weather, emergency management was able to get their drone up and found clear evidence that the tornado began farther to the northwest in another field of crops. It traversed southeast, coming very close to a property which is located along the county boundary. It is in this area that the tornado was likely the widest and most intense based on crop damage. It then crossed S 300 E and continued southeast. It appears to have struck a small cluster of trees where it broke several large limbs, earning the designation of an EF-0. It quickly terminated after that before reaching the county boundary road. Special thanks to Jay County's Office of Emergency Management for the assistance in documenting this storm.

tornadoes.name: West of Greeley Tornado
tornadoes.label: West of Greeley Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A high-end EF1 with peak gusts of 110 MPH caused significant damage to two farmsteads at the beginning of its 2.4 mile long path. Here two farm outbuildings were destroyed along with numerous snapped trees. A power pole was also snapped at this location. The tornado was roughly 150 yards wide at this location. As the tornado moved east, it began to become smaller causing mostly tree damage.

tornadoes.name: Southeast of Greeley Tornado
tornadoes.label: Southeast of Greeley Tornado
tornadoes.notes: An EF1 tornado, with max wind speeds of 90 MPH caused damage to trees and crops across it's 1.5 mile long path. A hoop outbuilding was flung into the southside of a farm house causing damage to windows and exteriors walls of the house. At this homestead, all trees were snapped to the north. Just north of this location crops and other branches were downed to the south. The tornado was around 100 yard wide at this location. As the tornado tracked east, damage to crops were noted.

tornadoes.name: 4N of Earlville Tornado
tornadoes.label: 4N of Earlville Tornado
tornadoes.notes: An EF1 tornado with max wind speeds of 95 MPH caused damage to trees, a house and a couple of farm outbuildings. A tree fell on a house heavily damaging a garage. A large tree branch was embedded in the metal roof of the house and into a bedroom. As the tornado tracked to the east, it mainly caused damage to trees along it's 2.6 mile long path. Towards the middle of it's path, a farm outbuilding's west wall was pushed in, causing part of the roof to be removed.

tornadoes.name: N of Springfield OH
tornadoes.label: N of Springfield OH
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service in Wilmington Ohio has confirmed an EF0 tornado north of Springfield in Clark County, Ohio.

This tornado was first observed at a large manufacturing and trucking facility on Urbana Road. Video evidence shows a tornado moving through a parking lot, and a semi trailer was flipped.

As this tornado moved east-southeast, additional tree damage was observed on Willow Road, and in several locations north and south of Moorefield Road. Several snapped trees were observed just east of Mechanicsburg Road, which is the last known damage from this tornado. The magnitude of the tree damage supports an estimated maximum wind speed of 80 MPH.

Sporadic tree and barn damage was observed elsewhere in this area, including on E County Line Road and N Plateau Drive. Damage at these locations was determined to be from straight-line winds of up to 70 MPH.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Clark County Emergency Management Agency for their assistance and coordination.

tornadoes.label: Near DeWitt, IA
tornadoes.notes: An EF0 tornado, with max wind speeds of 85 MPH, caused damage to trees and houses across its half-mile path. The tornado first caused some minor shingle damage to a home before crossing 14th Avenue. Then, damage to a few more houses was seen, including portions of a roof peeled off one house and damaged awning to another. As the tornado crossed 1st Street, it also damaged the tops of some trees and blew the branches southeastward.

tornadoes.name: SE of Urbana OH
tornadoes.label: SE of Urbana OH
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service in Wilmington Ohio has confirmed an EF-1 tornado southeast of Urbana in Champaign County Ohio.

Tornado damage was first noticed along a residence on Pisgah Road. The home had a portion of the roof lifted off along with siding damage. It was noticed that mud and debris were splattered on multiple sides of the house. A nearby barn was also destroyed. The tornado continued southeast, producing damage at a residence on Hurst Road, where a large section of the roof was removed. Winds producing the damage to this home were estimated to be up to 110 mph. Tree damage was also observed on the property.

The last known tornadic damage occurred just southeast, in the area of Catawba Station. On OH-54, or Virts Road, large tree branches were knocked down.

Other storm damage in Champaign County, including the Urbana area, was determined to be a result of straight-line winds.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Champaign County Emergency Management Agency for their assistance with this storm damage survey.

tornadoes.name: E of Springfield OH
tornadoes.label: E of Springfield OH
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service in Wilmington Ohio has confirmed an EF1 tornado east of Springfield in Clark County, Ohio.

This tornado began in the area near Ogden Road, Old Columbus Road, Ventura Ave, and Heatherwood Ave. Tree damage occurred, with a few trees downed on top of houses. Tree damage was also observed on California Ave and Adlyn Road.

South of London Plattsburg Road, between Fletcher Pike and Newlove Road, two barns were heavily damaged, with sheet metal blown downstream into adjacent fields. Corn field damage was also noted at this location.

At a property on Stewart Road, east of Urbana Lisbon Road, a home had its garage removed, with some siding and roof damage to the house. A barn was also heavily damaged at the same property. The tornado is believed to have been at its maximum intensity, about 100 MPH, at this location.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Clark County Emergency Management Agency for their assistance and coordination.

tornadoes.name: S of Catawba OH
tornadoes.label: S of Catawba OH
tornadoes.notes:
