The National Weather Service in Wilmington Ohio has confirmed an EF-2 tornado south of Catawba in Clark County Ohio.

The first evidence of damage from this tornado occurred on Vernon Asbury Road, where some trees were downed. As the tornado moved east, passing just south of Catawba, it rapidly strengthened. Additional tree damage was observed in a field west of OH-54. In addition to some tree damage, two outbuildings were destroyed on OH-54. To the south of this damage, the most significant damage occurred at a residence which had its roof completely lifted off and an attached garage was destroyed. Winds at this residence are estimated to be around 115 mph, which corresponds to EF-2 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale. Additional tree damage was observed along McConkey Road and Broadgauge Road, and the tornado is believed to have dissipated shortly after.

Tree damage was also observed in the village of Catawba, just north of the track of the tornado. The damage within the village was determined to be a result of straight-line winds.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Clark County Emergency Management Agency for their assistance with this storm damage survey.

tornadoes.name: Choctaw Lake OH
tornadoes.label: Choctaw Lake OH
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service in Wilmington, Ohio has confirmed an EF-1 tornado on the northeast side of Choctaw Lake in Madison County, Ohio from the storms on August 11, 2026.

The first evidence of tornadic damage occurred near the intersection of Karok Dr and Seneca Dr as hardwood trees were uprooted and several trees had large branches broken off. Numerous trees were either uprooted or snapped on several properties along W Choctaw Drive. The majority of the damage along this stretch was from downed trees, although minor fascia damage to residential homes were observed.

The most significant damage occurred on the northeastern side of the Lake, where five softwood trees were completely snapped near a docking port. This damage was consistent with peak wind speeds around 90 MPH, which would classify this tornado as EF-1 strength. The final evidence of tornadic damage was an uprooted tree that fell onto a car at a residential property off Itawamba Trail.

Additional tree damage was observed across the Choctaw Lake community south of the tornado track, but this was all believed to be associated with straight-line winds.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Madison County Emergency Management Agency for their assistance in this damage assessment.

tornadoes.name: SE of Plain City OH
tornadoes.label: SE of Plain City OH
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service in Wilmington Ohio has confirmed an EF0 tornado southeast of Plain City in Madison County, Ohio.

This brief tornado began near Plain City Georgesville Road Northeast, causing damage to trees and crops. Drone footage revealed damage to trees along Big Darby Creek as the tornado continued moving southeast. Damage then occurred to outbuildings along Amity Pike. Drone and satellite images captured additional signs of convergence in nearby fields north of Amity Pike. Based on the lack of additional crop damage south of Amity Pike, the tornado dissipated quickly. Any damage in the nearby surrounding areas was likely caused by straight line winds.

The National Weather Service would like the thank Madison County Emergency Management Agency for their assistance with this survey and damage assessment.

tornadoes.name: S Columbus OH
tornadoes.label: S Columbus OH
tornadoes.notes:
An EF-1 intensity tornado occurred in south Columbus just after 10 a.m. EDT on August 11. The tornado began on South 8th Street between East Morrill Avenue and East Hinman Avenue, breaking and uprooting several trees. Siding and roof damage occurred to several residences farther east toward Parsons Avenue, while a business lost a substantial amount of its roof on the east side of Parsons Avenue. Tree and mostly light structural damage continued to the east between East Hinman Avenue and Woodrow Avenue as the tornado moved east of Barack Park and damaged numerous trees and homes along and east of South Champion Avenue to Lockbourne Road. Reeb Avenue was particularly hard hit by the tornado's damaging winds before it crossed Lockbourne Road and damaged more trees in conjunction with multiple businesses. Additional trees and homes were impacted west of Fairwood Avenue, including the roof of one home caving in due to fallen trees and significant damage to a metal roof of a business. The tornado lifted just west of Fairwood Avenue.

Several additional locations received damage from a larger line of thunderstorms that moved through Franklin County during the late morning of August 11, but the locations in south Columbus referenced above were consistent with damage along a convergent path suggesting that a tornado had occurred.

The National Weather Service would like to thank Franklin County Emergency Management for their assistance in conducting this storm damage survey.

tornadoes.name: E of Upper Arlington OH
tornadoes.label: E of Upper Arlington OH
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service in Wilmington Ohio has confirmed an EF0 east of Upper Arlington in Franklin County in Ohio.

This tornado likely began near Kenny Road, crossing the Olentangy Freeway (OH-315) on the east side of Upper Arlington. Video footage captured the tornado moving east on the south side of Ackerman road, causing tree and minor building damage. Tree damage exhibiting convergent wind patterns was observed along Ackerman road near Fred Taylor Drive. After crossing the Olentangy River, additional tree damage was observed on North High Street and a few businesses sustained damage involving minor roof damage and broken windows. The tornado then followed Glen Echo Creek eastward, causing damage to trees along the creek and Olentangy Street. Several homes were damaged by the trees. Moving in a more northeast direction, additional tree damage was observed along US-23 and surrounding neighborhoods. As the tornado approached I-71, minor roof damage was observed to a building along Silver Drive. Video from an ODOT traffic camera then observed the tornado crossing I-71 at the Weber Road exit, flipping a single vehicle. Tree damage and minor home damage was then found on Beulah Road and East Weber Road. The tornado likely dissipated near this location, with additional straight line winds observed to the east.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Franklin County Ohio Emergency Management Agency, the Ohio State University Emergency Management Agency, the State Climate Office of Ohio, and the Ohio Department of Transportation for their assistance with this survey and damage assessment.

tornadoes.name: Olde Towne East OH
tornadoes.label: Olde Towne East OH
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service is Wilmington Ohio has confirmed an EF1 tornado in Olde Towne East, east of Downtown Columbus, in Franklin County Ohio.

Minor tree damage and building damage occurred on Oak Street near South 18th Street. Additional damage was observed between Fair Avenue and Oak Street as the tornado moved east. The most intense damage occurred between South Ohio Avenue and South Champion Avenue where multiple structures were damaged. One brick apartment building lost the roof and wall structure of the top floor on the west side.

As the tornado continued east along Fair Avenue, light damage to structures continued, but most of the damage involved trees. The tornado then caused widespread tree damage along Franklin Park South before gradually weakening before South Nelson Road. Additional sporadic damage to the east was likely caused by straight line wind damage.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Franklin County Ohio Emergency Management Agency for their assistance with the survey and damage assessment.

tornadoes.name: Oswego
tornadoes.label: Oswego
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began near Bristol Ridge Road northwest of US Route 34 and then crossed the Fox River. It continued in a generally southeasterly direction, causing intermittent tree damage as it crossed through several subdivisions in the vicinity of Grove Road. The tornado appears to have lifted near Douglas Road just south of Collins Road.

tornadoes.name: Norman Township
tornadoes.label: Norman Township
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began northwest of the intersection of Dupont Road and Verona Road in Norman Township. It initially produced a narrow path of convergent damage through a corn field before impacting a property along Dupont Road, where it removed a large portion of a barn's roof, pushed a grain bin off of its foundation, and downed multiple trees. The tornado damaged several more trees near the intersection of Dupont Road and Gorham Road before dissipating.

tornadoes.name: Morris
tornadoes.label: Morris
tornadoes.notes: This tornado appeared to begin near the intersection of State Route 47 and Granville Road, initially damaging crops in the fields to the southeast of this intersection. Eyewitnesses reported seeing this tornado track across I-80 before it impacted a trailer retailer along US Route 6, where numerous trailers were tossed or rolled and sections of roofing material were peeled off of the retailer's main office building. A semi truck was also blown into a ditch along Route 6, and power lines were downed at this location as well. Farther to the southeast, damage to several trees was noted near the Grundy County Rod and Gun Club, where the tornado appeared to dissipate.

tornadoes.name: Wilmington
tornadoes.label: Wilmington
tornadoes.notes: This tornado started near W Baltimore Street and N 1st Street, where it removed part of the roof of an automotive repair shop and tossed it into the side of an adjacent strip mall. Damage in this area was consistent with peak winds near 90 mph. The tornado then crossed the Kankakee River and subsequently tracked across the Oakwood Cemetery, where it caused substantial tree damage, again consistent with winds near 90 mph. The tornado then tracked east along Ridge Street before lifting near the Forked Creek Preserve.

tornadoes.name: Mokena - Tinley Park
tornadoes.label: Mokena - Tinley Park
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began near the intersection of W. Maple Road and Blodgett Road and then crossed I-80 near mile marker 141. The tornado continued in a southeasterly direction, causing mainly minor tree damage as it roughly paralleled W Regan Road and 195th Street. The tornado reached its peak intensity in a subdivision near St. Mary's Catholic Church, where several residences sustained shingle and soffit damage and large hardwood trees were snapped, consistent with peak winds of 85 to 95 mph. The tornado then continued east roughly along 195th Street before lifting just north of the Hilda Walker Intermediate School.

tornadoes.name: Orland Park - Hammond
tornadoes.label: Orland Park - Hammond
tornadoes.notes: The tornado began just east of the Will-Cook county line in the Brook Hill Subdivision and moved rapidly east and southeastward across southern portions of Orland Park and Tinley Park, resulting in considerable damage to trees and power lines. Some structural damage to several buildings was noted along 183rd St. in Tinley Park. The tornado then crossed Interstates 80 and 57 before moving across Country Club Hills, Flossmoor, and Glenwood, where the most substantial tree damage was noted with numerous large trees snapped or uprooted along the path. Some trees fell onto buildings and cars, causing significant damage. The tornado crossed the Calumet Expressway and moved east-northeastward across Lansing, where it continued to produce considerable tree damage. The tornado crossed the state line just north of Ridge Rd. and continued to produce considerable tree damage into Munster before turning north into Hammond and dissipating shortly after crossing I-80 just east of Calumet Ave.

tornadoes.name: Monee - Crown Point
tornadoes.label: Monee - Crown Point
tornadoes.notes: The tornado began near S. La Grange Road/US Highway 45 three quarters of a mile south of W Dralle Road. It initially progressed in a generally easterly direction, causing sporadic tree damage as it roughly paralleled W. Monee Manhattan Road. Damage in this area was consistent with EF-0 winds of 60 to 80 mph. The tornado then crossed Interstate 57 and damaged exterior doors and roofs at several industrial buildings on the north side of Monee before moving across University Park and into Crete with continued tree damage. The severity of tree damage increased as the tornado progressed into northwestern Indiana. The tornado reached its peak intensity in St. John in a localized area in a subdivision off of Blaine Street on the eastern edge of St. John. Here, a single residence at the corner of Dewey Place and 96th Place lost of most of its roof and south and western walls, consistent with peak winds around 115 mph. Tornado damage became increasingly interspersed with straight-line thunderstorm wind damage as the tornado entered Crown Point near Clark Road, and likely dissipated in this area.

tornadoes.name: Glenwood - Lansing
tornadoes.label: Glenwood - Lansing
tornadoes.notes: This tornado began west of Halsted Street between 183rd and 187th streets and tracked eastward, crossing Halsted and causing structural damage to a strip mall and several buildings in an apartment complex. The tornado then impacted a neighborhood east of the strip mall, causing substantial tree damage as well as some roof damage to a handful of homes. The tornado uprooted and snapped numerous trees across a cemetery off of Glenwood Thornton Road before continuing eastward, then northeastward through the Thornton-Lansing Road Nature Preserve. The tornado dissipated just east of the Calumet Expressway south of Thornton Lansing Road.

tornadoes.name: Shandon OH
tornadoes.label: Shandon OH
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service in Wilmington, Ohio has confirmed an EF1 tornado in southwest Butler County, Ohio into Hamilton County, Ohio.

Although sporadic tree damage was observed at points around the center of the tornadic circulation, the tornado first caused damage in the vicinity of Dunwoody Road where powerpoles were damaged. The tornado then tracked further to the southeast, resulting in additional spotty damage before more significant damage was observed in the vicinity of Chapel Road. Numerous large trees were snapped or uprooted along Chapel Road near the intersection with Jenkins Road, with some damage to structures due to fallen trees. It is within this area that the most significant damage was confirmed, consistent with winds of 90 MPH and an EF1 tornado.

Further to the southeast toward Alert New London Road near Shandon, additional tree and minor outbuilding damage was confirmed before the tornado tracked across the county line into Hamilton County.

Sporadic tree damage occurred within a largely-inaccessible area of the Fernald Preserve, with spotty isolated damage further to the southeast. It is possible the tornado briefly lifted in the vicinity of Willey Road toward New Haven Road before more significant tree damage was observed on either side of the Great Miami River into the area of the Oak Glen Preserve.

Although sporadic tree damage was reported southeast of the Oak Glen Preserve, the nature of the damage, in conjunction with radar data, suggest the tornado had dissipated . Additional tree damage toward Dent is believed to be caused by straight-line winds.

The National Weather Service would like to thank Butler County Emergency Management Agency and Hamilton County Emergency Management and Homeland Security Agency for their assistance with this damage assessment and survey.

tornadoes.name: Owensville OH
tornadoes.label: Owensville OH
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service in Wilmington Ohio has confirmed an EF0 tornado near Owensville in Clermont County, Ohio.

Although sporadic tree and other wind damage was observed across wide swaths of the surveyed area, the most concentrated area of damage began near US Rte 50 where a very large tree was downed onto a portion of a home near the intersection with Benton Road. This is approximately where the tornado likely first caused damage, with damage in these areas consistent with an EF0 tornado with winds of 80-85 MPH. Additional significant tree damage was observed farther to the south on the west side of Parkside Drive, where several patches of snapped trees were observed.

It is possible the tornado briefly lifted farther to the south toward State Rte 132 as there was no discernible damage on either the north or south side of the road. However, farther to the south toward Bauer Road, additional tree damage was observed on each side of the road and along a portion of Peace Haven Lane.

The tornado may have again briefly lifted toward Herold Road as no discernible damage was observed within the narrow rotation swath within this corridor. This being said, it is believed the tornado was again causing significant tree damage toward the south side of State Route 276 where numerous snapped and uprooted trees were observed on either side of Half Acre Road. The tree damage in this vicinity was concentrated and significant, suggesting 80-85 MPH winds once again.

Additional tree and minor structural damage was observed on the southern and western fringe of the center of the narrow tornado track, including along Old State Route 32, and this damage was consistent with straight-line winds. No discernible significant tree or structural damage was observed south of Old State Route 32 and Half Acre Road, so it is believed the tornado had lifted as the storm progressed west and southwest of Williamsburg.

The National Weather Service would like to thank Clermont County Emergency Management for their assistance with this survey and damage assessment.

tornadoes.name: Monterey OH
tornadoes.label: Monterey OH
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service in Wilmington Ohio has confirmed an EF0 tornado near Monterey in Clermont County, Ohio.

Although sporadic tree and other wind damage was observed along large swaths of the surveyed area, it is believed the tornado first caused damage near the intersection of Monterey Road and Hutchinson Road. Several uprooted and snapped trees were observed along Monterey Road progressing southeast toward US Rte 50. Some minor roof shingle damage was also observed on a residence within this corridor.

Farther to the south, it is believed the tornado tracked across US Rte 50 where additional snapped trees were observed near the intersection of US Rte 50 and Monterey Maple Grove Road.

To the southeast, a roof was also completely removed from a large barn just south of Caudil East Road near the intersection of Clemons Road. Additional large tree damage was observed in this area as well.

Some tree damage was observed near the intersection of Jackson Pike and State Route 133. Farther to the southeast, dozens of trees were uprooted or snapped along a portion of McKeever Pike near Schoolhouse Road.

It is believed the tornado weakened and lifted farther to the southeast as the storm transitioned to producing large swaths of straight-line wind damage near the Clermont and Brown county line east of Williamsburg.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Clermont County Emergency Management Agency for their assistance with this survey and damage assessment.

tornadoes.name: Hume KY
tornadoes.label: Hume KY
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service has confirmed an EF0 tornado near Hume in Boone County, Kentucky.

The first evidence of damage was on Webb Road, where a tree was downed on a trailer. Additionally, a residence and barn near the western edge of Webb Road both sustained some roof damage. Satellite imagery depicted tree damage along a path moving south-southeast from this location, with the most significant tree damage observed south of Mountain Ballpark. The narrow swath of tree damage extended about a mile south-southeast of US Route 42, where the tornado likely dissipated.

Additional damage was observed in far southern Boone County on Brown Road, and in far western Gallatin County. Damage in these locations was determined to have been from straight-line winds of up to 70 MPH.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Boone County Emergency Management Agency, Gallatin County Emergency Management, and Kenton County Emergency Management Agency for their coordination and support.

tornadoes.name: NW of Buford OH
tornadoes.label: NW of Buford OH
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service in Wilmington Ohio has confirmed an EF0 tornado northwest of Buford in Brown and Highland counties in Ohio.

This tornado began in Brown County near US Route 68 south of Gauche Road, where most of a roof was removed from a barn. A swath of damage in an adjacent field was observed on satellite imagery as the tornado continued to the southeast. Tree damage was then observed on Huber Road, and in the area of Thery Road and Upper Five Mile Road, where some tree damage was observed. As the tornado moved southeast, a barn was significantly damaged on Dietrick Road, along with some additional tree damage. The tornado then entered Highland County, producing tree damage in various places along Beltz Road. A house on the east side of Beltz Road had some shingles removed. Near the end of the tornado's path, a stand of trees was snapped on Beltz Road just north of Waits Road.

Scattered straight-line wind damage, generally damage to trees, was also observed around the edges of the track of the tornado.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Brown County and Highland County Emergency Management Agencies for their assistance and coordination.

tornadoes.name: White Heath Tornado
tornadoes.label: White Heath Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A tornado touched down northwest of Lodge, causing damage to power poles along route 10. It caused tree damage and crop damage as it moved southeast and flipped a box truck on I-72 in white heath. As it continued southeast, it damaged two large outbuildings and one garage. it continued southeast, resulting in more corn damage and tree damage in Sadorus . It ended in Pesotum with tree damage. Revised track based on Sentinal satellite data.

tornadoes.name: SW of Winchester OH
tornadoes.label: SW of Winchester OH
tornadoes.notes:
An EF-1 intensity tornado occurred south of State Route 32 from far eastern Brown County into far western Adams County during the late afternoon hours of August 11, 2026.

Damage was first observed along U.S. Highway 62 south of Macon, where numerous trees were uprooted and the roof of an outbuilding was lifted off and destroyed. The tornado tracked southeast, snapping and uprooting several trees and collapsing an entire outbuilding on Tibbe Road. Tree and outbuilding damage continued to be observed farther southeast along John Woods Road and Greathouse Road. As the tornado moved into western Adams County, additional tree and roof damage occurred along Tamme Road in a concentrated convergent path. This extended southeast to along Eckmansville Road and Kirkpatrick Road where concentrated tree damage was found, in addition to a large portion of a barn's roof being carried southeast for 200 yards into a crop field which exhibited a clear convergent path. The tornado dissipated prior to reaching Cherry Fork.

The National Weather Service would like to thank Brown County and Adams County Emergency Management for their assistance with completing this storm damage survey.

tornadoes.label: Near Bruceville, IN
tornadoes.notes: The tornado began in a tree grove northwest of Maria Creek with multiple videos of the tornado looking from US 41 to the northwest. The tornado impacted several groves of trees along Maria Creek and through Morgan and Hollingsworth Road before impacting an outbuilding along East Hollingsworth Road and dissipating in a field to the southeast.

tornadoes.name: Winslow, IN
tornadoes.label: Winslow, IN
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado with peak winds of 110 mph struck Winslow, Indiana, on the afternoon of August 12, 2026. The tornado began in a neighborhood just west of the intersection of Highway 61 and Brenton Street. Moving southeast, the tornado severely damaged a few manufactured homes and outbuildings, uprooted or snapped dozens of trees, and damaged the roofs, gutters, and fascia of several homes in Winslow. At least one family was displaced when a large tree fell into their home, causing it to become inhabitable. The tornado lifted near Beardsley Street on the southeast side of Winslow. The tornado occurred from 4:09 to 4:10 PM EDT and had a peak width of 250 yards.

tornadoes.name: SW Humphrey
tornadoes.label: SW Humphrey
tornadoes.notes: A tornado developed in an open field between 400 Ave and 385 Ave southwest of Cornlea, NE and moved east-northeast. The tornado moved across 370 Ave where it overturned an irrigation system, took down several powerpoles, snapped several softwood trees, and took the roof off of a shed. The tornado continued to the northeast producing sporadic tree and corn damage and flipping over another center pivot. The tornado lifted to the southwest off Humphrey, NE before reaching Highway 81.

tornadoes.name: SE Humphrey
tornadoes.label: SE Humphrey
tornadoes.notes: A tornado touched down east of Highway 81 to the southeast of Humphrey, NE near 250 Ave and flattened corn in a field and took down some small branches. The tornado continued east-northest for just over 3 miles before lifting near 445 St and 205 Ave where tree damage was noted. Evidence of the track was visible in the cornfields.

tornadoes.name: Leigh
tornadoes.label: Leigh
tornadoes.notes: A tornado touched down west of a cemetery near 130 Ave southwest of Leigh, NE. The tornado did significant tree damage to the cemetery, snapping 10-12 trees and damaging the metal sign. The tornado continued east and demolished a large machine shed and did significant tree damage to a property just north of 460 St between 115 and 110 Ave. The tornado then turned to the northeast and clipped the southeast side of Leigh producing more tree damage before lifting near Road V and Road 3.

tornadoes.name: Leigh 2
tornadoes.label: Leigh 2
tornadoes.notes: A short-track tornado touched down on the west side of the Club 91 Golf Course and moved northeast across Road V where concentrated tree damage occurred. The tornado continued across the pond on the north side of the baseball field producing more tree damage before lifting after crossing West Fork Maple Creek.

tornadoes.name: NW of St Paris OH
tornadoes.label: NW of St Paris OH
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service in Wilmington Ohio has confirmed an EF0 tornado northwest of St. Paris in Champaign County, Ohio.

This short-lived tornado produced minor tree damage at a property on Mahan Road, just east of Elm Tree road. At another property on Mahan Road, some roof damage occurred to an outbuilding.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Champaign County Emergency Management Agency for their coordination.

tornadoes.name: N of St Paris OH
tornadoes.label: N of St Paris OH
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service in Wilmington Ohio has confirmed an EF0 tornado north of St. Paris in Champaign County, Ohio.

This tornado was confirmed based on video evidence, a storm damage survey, and satellite imagery of crop damage. The tornado began just northeast of the intersection of State Route 235 and Apple Road. The tornado then moved east-northeast across open fields, crossing Mount Pleasant Cemetery Road.

Most of the damage from the tornado occurred near the intersection of Ward Road and Kiser Lake Road. Several trees were downed at this intersection, as well as slightly to the east on Ward Road. A home on Ward Road had some of its siding removed. The tornado continued tracking east-northeast, crossing Ford Road and Cemetery Road before dissipating.

The National Weather Service would like to thank the Champaign County Emergency Management Agency for their coordination.

tornadoes.name: Hookstown
tornadoes.label: Hookstown
tornadoes.notes:
After additional surveys on Wednesday, the initial tornado track along Upper Service Rd has been extended to the west.

Damage began in a wooded area off of Route 168 to the south of US30. Here several large limbs were snapped off, and a few smaller trunks were snapped also at 30-40 ft above ground. At this location, damage was concentrated in a narrow path, with some degree of convergent and cyclonic flow evident in the fall pattern. The damage was consistent with wind of 70-75 mph, marked by sporadic, concentrated snapping within a broader area of relatively unscathed trees.

The circulation appears to have weakened briefly as it progressed eastward across Route 168 and Silver Slipper Rd (where a few snapped limbs were noted).

A surge in the outflow appears to have diverted the circulation toward the southeast briefly, before it began to intensify again near US30 and Lincoln Ct. Along Lincoln Ct, several trees suffered limb damage consistent with wind of 70 mph.

The circulation tracked into the woods north of Bocktown Rd, where it joins with the prior-identified track off Upper Service Rd, where radar and damage both indicate that the circulation tightened and intensified.

...Prior survey summary below... Tree damage was observed from Upper Service Road, with fresh, large limbs snapped and a couple snapped trunks that showed some sign of rot.

The circulation crossed Upper Service Road near the Greene/Raccoon Township line, where considerable fresh tree damage was noted in the woods to the north of the road. Here, additional rotted trunks were snapped, as well as a large number of snapped limbs and possibly an uprooted tree or two (it was difficult to tell from the available ground access point).

Radar data from KPBZ radar suggest a possible tornado debris signature in this area, coincident with the damage swath.

Because of the damage swath's inaccessibility, start and end points of the tornado's path are only estimates, pending additional information from aerial survey or satellite imagery.

tornadoes.name: Lowes, KY
tornadoes.label: Lowes, KY
tornadoes.notes: An EF-1 tornado touched down 3 miles east-southeast of Cunningham near the intersection of County Roads 1011 and 1012. Numerous trees were snapped or uprooted. The tornado moved southeast crossing State Route 849 near the Graves-Carlisle County line. Additional convergent damage in the tree debris was discovered along Morrill Road. This is where we determined the tornado to have lifted as it was hard to find convergent damage east of here. An intense macroburst started right on the heels of the tornado with a large swath of 80 to 105 mph winds occurring across a large area of northeastern Carlisle and northern Graves counties producing significant damage.

tornadoes.name: Viola, KY
tornadoes.label: Viola, KY
tornadoes.notes: Evidence of a tornado exists at the intersection of KY 408 and US 45 near the community of Viola. A large industrial metal building system had garage and roof panels removed with missiling of insulation onto north and east facing surfaces. A gas station/restaurant across the street had its canopy blown over and adjacent outbuildings were knocked over/damaged. It is possible this was part of a continuous path from the initial tornado near Lowe's however radar evidence suggests this was a separate process and the evidence linking the two would have been covered by the intense macroburst winds that occurred across the remainder of the northern portion of Graves County.

tornadoes.label: Near Dover, DE
tornadoes.notes: On August 20, 2026, a tornado formed over the open fields west of Wyoming Mill Rd near Riverside Rd, scarring the crops before moving the tree line east of Wyoming Mill Rd, snapping several branches and tree tops. The tornado then made direct contact with the Dover Little League baseball fields at Schutte Park, causing extensive damage across two of their baseball diamonds. At least seven large wooden field lighting fixtures were snapped at either the base or halfway up, falling onto the fencing surrounding the fields. Additional fencing was also ripped from their posts and believed to have been caused directly from the tornadic winds rather than impacted from another object. One large scoreboard secured by a brick foundation fell over and a second one supported by metal posts was bent and likely crushed by an unknown projectile. Part of a tree was observed in the middle of one of the fields with no clear origin. The tornado then hit the City of Dover VanSant Generating Station, shifting one trailer off its foundation and causing minor roof damage to a metal building structure in addition to visibly denting the metal siding with unknown projectiles. The tornado then carved a path through another tree line before impacting the Kraft-Heinz plant where some of the most significant damage occurred. Two sections of concrete block walls collapsed, a few trailers were sent tumbling, and a small section of the metal roof came off. The collapse of the concrete block walls confirmed max wind gusts of a high-end EF-1. The tornado then moved ENE, missing the the Eden Hill Medical Center. Continuing its path, the tornado zig-zagged through the main downtown area of Dover where it was weaker at this point, downing a few trees and snapping branches along W North Street before turning towards Dover City Hall and turning again towards Memorial Park. The tornado then began moving NNE along Park Dr and Kings Hwy downing large trees and branches. As it approached the intersection of Kings Hwy and N Dupont Hwy, the tornado intensified again and reached its maximum width of 100 yards. The tornado reached a second peak intensity here as it peeled half of the roof off the Super Lodge, damaging the roof to the Days Inn next door, and downing two large business signs. This significant roof damage provided secondary confirmation of max wind gusts of a high-end EF-1. The tornado quickly dissipated afterwards.

tornadoes.label: Near Mountville, PA
tornadoes.notes:
A tornado began northwest of Habecker Church Rd and carved out a narrow convergent swath of damage in a several cornfields as it moves south-southeast. The tornado began to occlude as it crossed Habecker Church Rd, after which the path widened and became a bit less defined.

Interestingly there may have been a second even more narrow vortex that developed east (to the left from a storm-relative standpoint) of the main circulation and joined up with the main circulation near Habecker Church Rd.

The tornado likely lifted as it cycled and eventually produced more damage to the northeast as it crossed a residential area in Centerville.

tornadoes.name: Briar Creek
tornadoes.label: Briar Creek
tornadoes.notes: Review of available Sentinel 2, Planet, and NISAR satellite imagery along with public/media provided video helped to determine the track, intensity, and width of the tornado that occurred in the Mobile River Delta. It was determined an EF0 with peak winds of 70mph and width around 150 yards occurred in the river delta just west of Briar Creek and south of the Mobile River causing minor tree damage along its track. The tornado crossed the far northern portion of the Mobile-Tensaw Cut-off Channel generally moving east-northeast before turning towards the northeast after crossing Briar Creek. It continued northeast across Big Lizard Creek near the railroad crossing adjacent to the Tensaw River, lifting at the river. Radar and satellite imagery support this being the end point of the tornado.

tornadoes.label: Near Downingtown, PA
tornadoes.timing_issue: duration over 3 hours

tornadoes.label: Near Barclay, MD
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado touched town in Barclay, snapping and uprooting several softwood and hardwood trees in a wooded area next to a residence located near the intersection of Dell Foxx Rd and Barclay Rd. The tornado then moved east across a bean field and onto a residential property on Benton Corner Rd, where more softwood and hardwood trees, including a robust cedar tree, were snapped at the trunk.

tornadoes.label: Near Marydel, MD
tornadoes.notes: A tornado occurred in Marydel beginning along the east side of Grygo Rd, about a quarter mile south of the intersection of Mahan Corner Rd, taking down several tree limbs near a residence. It then crossed Grygo Rd and uprooted two very large oak trees that fell on the corner of a home. Additional hardwood trees were uprooted along the property as the tornado headed ENE into a heavily wooded area. Drone footage showed the tornado continued to cut a path through the treeline, snapping large branches and uprooting a variety of trees down a narrow path. While drone footage was unable to confirm the full length of destruction in the wooded area, just on the other side of the wooded area, a residence along Parkers Chapel Rd experienced the total loss of an old barn and shed in addition to several downed trees and branches.

tornadoes.label: Near Wyoming, DE
tornadoes.notes: A brief tornado occurred just east of the community of Hazlettville, primarily impacting a farm and adjacent fields along Bryants Corner Road. The tornado began in a field just east of a residential area, evidenced by somewhat discontinuous swirl marks through a corn field. The tornado moved east-northeastward toward a group of chicken houses and an open air barn. In this area, the tornado removed nearly half of the barn’s metal roof panels, which was the most significant damage the tornado caused with estimated winds up to 80 mph. The tornado also caused some minor damage to the chicken houses’ metal roofs and a row of solar panels affixed to the ground nearby. The tornado continued northeast across another pair of corn fields, just south of a residence, then ended just before reaching Bryants Corner Road.
tornadoes.timing_issue: duration over 3 hours

tornadoes.label: Near Maxwell Colony, SD
tornadoes.notes: Brief touchdown resulting in minor damage to farmstead, including an overturned camper and the loss of roof panels on out buildings.
tornadoes.timing_issue: end time is before start time

tornadoes.name: Henkel
tornadoes.label: Henkel
tornadoes.notes: Based on drone footage provided by the Lee County Sheriff's office, the tornado began in an open field east of the intersection of Henkel Road and US Highway 52 and caused damage to crops. The tornado continued generally southward and damaged several roofs of buildings near the intersection of Cedar Grove Road and US Highway 52 before causing additional crop damage behind a farmstead. The tornado appeared to lift in an open field to the north of Pike Creek west of US Highway 52. The tornado was captured by video and photo by several storm chasers in the area. Thank you to both the Lee County Emergency Management Agency and Lee County Sheriff's Office for their help in completing the survey for this tornado.

tornadoes.name: Depue-Hennepin
tornadoes.label: Depue-Hennepin
tornadoes.notes: An EF0 tornado, with peak winds of 80 MPH, developed along the southern banks of the Illinois River and moved towards the south-southeast. The tornado knocked over a power pole and crossed through a rock quarry, where it tipped over a portion of an industrial conveyor system. The tornado gradually weakened as it passed south of the quarry, producing sporadic tree damage along an intermittent path before completely dissipating near Highway 71.

tornadoes.name: Madera EF-1 Aug 22, 2026
tornadoes.label: Madera EF-1 Aug 22, 2026
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service has confirmed tornado damage in southeast Clearfield County.

At approximately 7:55 PM EDT on Saturday, August 22, 2026, a line of thunderstorms merged with a supercell thunderstorm and produced a tornado in the town of Madera. The tornadic damage began on Belsena Road near Elm Street, where a large tree was blown across the road. Multiple trees were uprooted or snapped and a roof was torn off of a residence on Spruce Street. Trees were also snapped and uprooted on the east side of Madera on Alexander Road and Heritage Lane. The tornado was on the ground for approximately 2 minutes and traveled approximately 1 mile before dissipating. Straight line winds continued to produce sporadic damage to the northeast of Madera.

We want to thank the Clearfield County Emergency Management Agency and Madera Township fire officials for their help with this survey.

tornadoes.name: EF0_PortStLucie_FL_082326
tornadoes.label: EF0_PortStLucie_FL_082326
tornadoes.notes:
A tornado touchdown in Port St. Lucie on Sunday, August 23, 2026, was confirmed through photographic and video evidence, storm spotter reports, and a National Weather Service storm survey. The tornado developed near the North Fork of the St. Lucie River around 6:10 PM EDT and tracked generally west-southwest across portions of Port St. Lucie before lifting near the Florida Turnpike around 6:25 PM EDT.

The tornado initially touched down east of the Tarpon Bay Yacht Club near SE Pruitt Road and SE Morningside Boulevard before moving west toward the condominium complex, where minor structural damage occurred primarily to roofs and awnings. It then moved over the St. Lucie River as a waterspout, where videos from the public showed it meandering for several minutes. The circulation eventually resumed a southwestward motion, crossing a narrow barrier island where several trees were damaged before moving back over the river.

At approximately 6:20 PM EDT, the waterspout moved ashore near the Bay St. Lucie community, where a couple of homes sustained roof damage in the form of displaced or missing tiles, several large tree branches were downed, and a boat on a lift was toppled into the water. The tornado likely reached its maximum intensity and width in this area, with peak winds estimated at 65 to 75 mph and a maximum path width of approximately 200 yards. The tornado continued into the wooded preserve behind the homes of Bay St. Lucie, where vegetative damage was noted, mainly in the form of downed trees, though the damage was discontinuous in nature.

The tornado continued west toward the Southbend section of Port St. Lucie, where homes in and around Jessica Clinton Park sustained minor damage to fences, awnings, and pool enclosures. Several large tree branches were broken, with isolated roof damage also noted. Damage in this area was consistent with peak winds of 60 to 70 mph. The tornado likely lifted near or over the Florida Turnpike at approximately 6:25 PM EDT.

There are no known injuries or fatalities associated with the tornado. The National Weather Service in Melbourne would like to thank the City of Port St. Lucie, St. Lucie County Emergency Management, local residents, and the media for their assistance in providing information about this event.

tornadoes.label: Near Atlantic, NC
tornadoes.notes:
Along Highway 12/Cedar Island Road, just east of the Thorofare Bridge, two cedar trees were snapped up from the base of the trunk. The trees were on the smaller side and an average between the expected values for large branches broken but below trunks snapped were used to account for this. With extensive marshland in this area, the wind estimate was quite difficult with no other trees or buildings to determine a threshold of damage. Powerlines along this road are metal and have a high wind threshold. They did not exhibit any damage. Eyewitnesses reported a waterspout cross Highway 12 (Cedar Island Road) at the same time the radar showed an intense area of rotation just above the surface. A path width could not be determined due to the extensive marshland and lack of other areas of damage. Confidence is high in the determination of a tornado based on the combination of strong radar evidence and eyewitness accounts that match the exact location damage was found. Wind estimate confidence is a bit lower than usual given the lack of any trees or buildings in that area to make a more conclusive determination of wind speed. An estimation of top wind speeds between 75 and 85 MPH is reasonable given the exhibited damage.

It should be noted that pictures of a funnel cloud and potential tornado were circulated on social media about the same time the tornado above occurred. These pictures however are likely from a separate funnel cloud or tornado. The location of where the pictures were taken was in Bettie, NC, along highway 70. This was 16 miles to the southwest of the storm survey location above. In addition the tornado surveyed was likely rain wrapped and would not be visible from that distance. We have not received any damage reports associated with this possible second funnel cloud or tornado, despite reaching out to Open Ground Farms. If additional information comes into the office, a second survey or additional information will be sent out.
tornadoes.timing_issue: start and end time are identical

tornadoes.name: RugglesRd_EF0_20260827
tornadoes.label: RugglesRd_EF0_20260827
tornadoes.notes: A brief EF-0 uprooted several softwood trees in the vicinity of Ruggles Road and Preserve Way.

tornadoes.name: FerrisLakeForest_EF1_20260827
tornadoes.label: FerrisLakeForest_EF1_20260827
tornadoes.notes: Drone imagery shared with the NWS indicates a brief tornado occurred along the western edge of straight line wind damage southwest of DeBraine Lake in Hamilton County.

tornadoes.name: Wilton_EF1_20260827
tornadoes.label: Wilton_EF1_20260827
tornadoes.notes: A tornado touched down west of the Northway in the vicinity of Sheffield Road and Greylock and Glenburnie Drives. The tornado crossed the Northway and snapped trees before dissipating along Edie Road southwest of the Wilton Wildlife Preserve.

tornadoes.name: Gaines Township Tornado
tornadoes.label: Gaines Township Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
On September 1, 2026 at approximately 5:33 PM EDT, an EF-1 tornado impacted areas of eastern Potter County and western Tioga County in the vicinity of Gaines Township. Maximum wind speeds were estimated at 110 mph with a maximum path width of 150 yards.

Damage associated with the tornado began north of Galeton near Phoenix Run in Pike Township, where multiple hardwood trees were snapped along with numerous large branches on both sides of Phoenix Road. There was more extensive damage just east of Phoenix Road, where a larger swath of EF-1 damage was observed with some uprooted trees alongside snapped trees and large branches. Damage continued southeastward on Phoenix Road in Potter County with more sporadic damage including broken large branches and snapped trees. There was an area where the tornado potentially lifted as it approached US Route 6 with damage being largely sporadic and not as concentrated as it crossed the roadway.

Once crossing US Route 6, more widespread damage was observed across Hanky Panky Road in Gaines Township, Tioga County. Numerous uprooted and snapped trees were observed across approximately a 150 yard segment with eyewitnesses mentioning that there were trees across the roadway in a convergent pattern. This damage continued towards the intersections of Dingman Road and Bloody Run Road, where concentrated areas of snapped and uprooted trees continued to be observed. There was another eyewitness that noted multiple trees uprooted at their residence on Dingman Road with what appeared to be a convergent pattern. As the storm continued into Marshlands, multiple large branches as well as uprooted and snapped trees were in a convergent pattern, with surrounding vegetation also outlining a convergent pattern. The tornado likely continued to parallel Elk Run Road just south of the roadway before dissipating on the north side of the intersection with Straight Run Road.

We would like to thank Gaines Township Emergency Management, Tioga County Emergency Management, multiple first responders, and the multiple eyewitnesses from Gaines Township for their assistance with this damage survey.

tornadoes.name: Derry Township Tornado
tornadoes.label: Derry Township Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
During the evening of September 1st, 2026, a supercell thunderstorm moved southeastward through Montour County, resulting in a brief EF-1 tornado which impacted southern portions of the county in Derry Township. We also found damage due to a downburst which occurred on the right side of the tornado, associated with the forward flank downdraft of this supercell. Maximum wind speeds from this tornado were estimated to be 100 mph, and the tornado had a maximum path width of 250 yards. Tornadic damage was first noted in the woods between Steffens Rd and Indian Run Rd, with a start time of 5:40 PM local time. The tornadic damage was primarily on Stable Ln and the hairpin turn on Indian Run Rd. In this location, two large trees snapped and fell on the shed of a residence, with a trail of snapped and uprooted trees into the woods beyond the property. The tornado continued eastward before diminishing near Fossil Hill Rd at 5:41 PM local time. Surrounding this track, numerous trees were snapped and uprooted from straight-line winds, making a broadly divergent pattern particularly to the north of the tornado path.

We would like to thank Montour County Emergency Management, local homeowners, and other members of the local community for their assistance in this damage survey.

tornadoes.name: Salisbury Township Tornado
tornadoes.label: Salisbury Township Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
At 7:44 p.m. local time on September 1, 2026 an EF-1 tornado, with maximum wind speeds of 90 mph, touched down in Salisbury Township northwest of the Mount Vernon Road and Old Philadelphia Pike intersection with a width of 100 yards. It traveled south as it ripped off the roof of a barn and threw sections through the Old Road Mennonite Church graveyard before crossing Old Philadelphia Pike and paralleling Mount Vernon Road. It ripped a roof off another barn and snapped many larger limbs from a tree in the neighboring pasture. Continuing south it took some sections of roof and loose items from three farm outbuildings and ejected them throughout the fields. As it continued along Mount Vernon Road, a clump of trees was hit where many trees were uprooted and large branches snapped. Farther south, a barn sustained some minor roof damage before a one room school house was impacted with its whole roof torn off. At the intersection of Buena Vista Road and Mount Vernon Road, another tree was uprooted and a telephone pole was bent. It continued south to the east of Mount Vernon Road where it crossed Pequea Creek, snapping many large branches and uprooting a few more trees. Past the creek, another clump of trees saw large branches snapped before the tornado dissipated in a field.

We would like to thank Lancaster County Emergency Management and Salisbury Township officials for their assistance in this damage survey.

tornadoes.name: 9/2 Olcott
tornadoes.label: 9/2 Olcott
tornadoes.notes: None.

tornadoes.name: 9/2 East Shelby
tornadoes.label: 9/2 East Shelby
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service in Buffalo completed a damage survey across Orleans County today in response to reports of concentrated areas of damage near Shelby from a line of severe thunderstorms yesterday, September 2nd.

A severe supercell thunderstorm moved into western Orleans county shortly after 6:30 pm passing just south of Medina. As it moved over East Shelby the low level circulation tightened and a tornado touched down in a field east of Bigford Road and south of Martin Road. Several trees were toppled on the edges of this field before the tornado crossed over East Shelby Road causing significant tree damage across several residences on the east side of the road, along with minor structural damage to a home. The tornado then continued eastward through a forested area with numerous trees uprooted and few snapped. The tornado then lifted over an open field west of Townline Road.

The National Weather Service extends its thanks to Orleans County Emergency Services for their assistance with today's survey.

tornadoes.label: Near Marysville, MI
tornadoes.notes: A brief weak tornado tracked across portions of Marysville, Michigan in St. Clair County. Tree damage was sporadic along a narrow path between Gratiot Boulevard and Highway 29. Tree damage was mostly confined to large tree limbs, but a few trees were sheared off towards the top and a few uprooted trees were also documented.

tornadoes.name: 20260902_Alexander
tornadoes.label: 20260902_Alexander
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service in Buffalo investigated storm-related damage from a bowing line of thunderstorms that ended up producing an EF-1 tornado during the evening of September 2nd with estimated peak winds of 110 mph that affected the area east of Alexander, NY near Route 20.

Initial damage from the tornado was noted in a corn field north of Route 20 both north and south of Browns Mill Road. Downed corn crops displayed a convergent pattern with an initial path width paced at 70 yards. Nearby, additional tree damage was observed with multiple tree branches broken and one large tree trunk snapped. The damage path continued southeast toward W Bethany Road where broken tree branches and additional convergent signatures within a corn field were observed both east and west of the roadway immediately north of Route 20. In the distance, uprooted and leaning trees with branches broken were observed along the same path south of Route 20.

Farther to the southeast, the survey team found similar tree damage along Silver Road and Mill Road. A higher density of downed and snapped trees were observed near a residence along Mill Road. This included a dense cluster of large locust tree trunks snapped with a convergent pattern that led to the high-end EF-1 rating for this tornado. Sporadic tree damage continued near Linden and along Skates Hill Road just north of the Genesee-Wyoming County Line.

tornadoes.name: Webster & Ontario
tornadoes.label: Webster & Ontario
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service in Buffalo completed a damage survey across eastern Monroe County and western Wayne County today in response to reports of concentrated areas of damage near Webster and Ontario from a line of severe thunderstorms on Wednesday, September 2nd.

Embedded low level rotation within a squall line moved through Webster shortly before 7:30 pm, and a tornado touched down in the vicinity of Salt Road just north of Route 104 as evidenced by several snapped softwood trees. The tornado then crossed Route 104 as it headed southeastward, with another area of concentrated damage noted near the intersection of Basket Road and Ridge Road. Here several hardwood trees were snapped or uprooted, and a fewl power poles were knocked down. The tornado then continued to the southeast through open fields until encountering a small subdivision just west of County Line Road. Here the most significant damage occurred with roof uplift, considerable shingle loss, and siding damage on a few homes on Halesworth Lane and Bannerwood Drive. Numerous trees in the subdivision were also snapped or uprooted. Additional tree damage was seen along Foxworth Drive, and then the tornado travelled through a large forested area with no road access. Finally, the tornado emerged along North Lincoln Road just north of Whitney Drive, and produced extensive tree damage at a large property where numerous mature trees were uprooted or snapped, before lifting just east of this area.

tornadoes.name: Letchworth
tornadoes.label: Letchworth
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service in Buffalo completed a damage survey across southwest Livingston County today in response to reports of concentrated areas of damage near Portageville and the southern end of Letchworth State Park from thunderstorms on the evening of September 2nd. A line of severe thunderstorms moved through the area during the evening hours, producing areas of thunderstorm wind damage. Several small, brief areas of rotation developed along the line and produced this brief squall line tornado around 8 PM EDT.

The first instance of damage was on the eastern side of the gorge in Letchworth State Park along the East Parade Grounds Rd in the Town of Portage. There was significant tree damage in this area, with dozens of large hardwoods snapped and uprooted. A cluster of a half dozen large and very tall locust trees were snapped off at the trunk, with several falling on a large park pavilion. The structure sustained significant damage from the falling trees. Farther southeast along East Parade Grounds Rd, several dozen hardwood and softwood trees were uprooted or snapped, with tree damage in this area showing a convergent path. The final damage location was along River Rd just northeast of Route 436, with another cluster of a dozen hardwood trees uprooted or snapped at the trunk. Tree damage in this area showed a clearly convergent and rotational damage path. The path of damage ended in a forested area just north of Route 436.

This tornado was in close proximity to another tornado just over the Genesee River in Wyoming County. Radar data and the damage paths suggest these were two separate, distinct tornado damage paths with a different path orientation.

The National Weather Service extends its thanks to Livingston County Emergency Management for providing the location of the most significant damage, and for providing an escort through the heavily damaged east side of Letchworth State Park.

tornadoes.name: Portageville
tornadoes.label: Portageville
tornadoes.notes:
The National Weather Service in Buffalo completed a damage survey across southeast Wyoming County today in response to reports of concentrated areas of damage near Portageville and the southern end of Letchworth State Park from thunderstorms on the evening of September 2nd. A line of severe thunderstorms moved through the area during the evening hours, producing areas of thunderstorm wind damage. Several small, brief areas of rotation developed along the line and produced this brief squall line tornado around 8 PM EDT.

The first instance of damage was noted along Griffith Rd just east of Halvorsen Rd in the Town of Genesee Falls, about one mile west of Portageville. Sporadic tree damage was noted in this area. Sporadic tree damage was also noted along the eastern end of East Koy Rd, which was likely a mix of thunderstorm wind damage and tornado damage. Tree damage became more significant at the eastern end of Griffith Rd near the intersection with Route 19A, where dozens of healthy hardwood and softwood trees were uprooted or snapped off at the trunk. The tree damage in this area showed a distinct convergent pattern. Significant tree damage extended east across Route 19A into Letchworth State Park near the Portageville entrance, with numerous large trees uprooted or snapped off at the trunk on the slope between Park Rd and the Genesee River. The damage then rapidly diminished along the Genesee River, at which point the brief tornado dissipated just north of the Hamlet of Portageville.

This tornado was in close proximity to another tornado just over the Genesee River in Livingston County. Radar data and the damage paths suggest these were two separate, distinct tornado damage paths with a different path orientation.

The National Weather Service extends its thanks to Wyoming County Emergency Management for providing the location of the most significant damage.

tornadoes.label: Near Waterloo, NY
tornadoes.notes:
A line of severe thunderstorms moved into Seneca County well after sunset Wednesday evening September 2, 2026 and produced both intense winds and a pair of embedded tornadoes.

The severe line of storms pushed out into a bow echo of damaging winds, with a bookend vortex on the north side of the bow signature. An initial tornado formed in the center of the broader rotation of the bookend vortex, a few miles west-northwest of Waterloo. A chaotic pattern of oppositionally-facing downed trees and branches became more evident by the time the tornado crossed Hecker Road, reaching EF1 strength up to 95 mph while proceeding across Maple Grove Cemetery and tracking into the village. Despite the track center itself remaining north of US20, including skimming the Seneca County Office Building; inflow winds towards the tornado and then intense downdraft winds behind it caused significant tree damage throughout Waterloo including even south of the Seneca River. As these winds raced ahead to the south, the tornado remained on the north side of US20 while striking a commercial frame tent near the Seneca Falls border, with 750 pound concrete weights that were thrown and 6 inch thick poles that were bent and scattered. The tornado then occluded and weakened while peeling east-northeast into the north side of Seneca Falls before ending. Meanwhile, an even stronger tornado spun up about 5 miles south of the first one, which tracked across most of the width of Seneca County.

The National Weather Service thanks Seneca County Emergency Management for their invaluable assistance, including providing drone images, and interacting with impacted residents during the survey. Much gratitude is also extended to residents providing their accounts and allowing access to damaged areas.

tornadoes.label: Near Romulus, NY
tornadoes.notes:
A line of severe thunderstorms moved into Seneca County well after sunset Wednesday evening September 2, 2026 and produced both intense winds and a pair of embedded tornadoes.

In the very highly sheared and unstable environment, a second circulation quickly picked up roughly 5 miles south of the first one, and rapidly intensified into an even stronger tornado with nearly immediate destruction to a garage and sheds of a residence on Post Road. Radar itself soon confirmed debris lofting as high as 11,000 feet as the tornado strengthened to EF2 with winds up to 115 mph, tracking east across much of the County. Despite occurring after nightfall, the nearly constant lightning revealed the funnel to many eyewitnesses as it approached. Several barns and outbuildings were severely damaged, leveled, or even lofted with damage strewn many hundreds of yards. Peak intensity occurred at a farm property along Watts Road, with a heifer barn destroyed while sending missiles of debris impaling into a house and smashing windows. A large swirling path could be found imprinted in cornfields both west and east of that property. The tornado nearly paralleled Leader road while heavily damaging additional farms and snapping numerous power poles. The tornado was finally overtaken by the severe winds immediately behind it, weakening as it crossed Seybolt Road before ending. Severe damaging thunderstorm winds then continued across Seneca Lake including the Union Springs area of Cayuga County.

The National Weather Service thanks Seneca County Emergency Management for their invaluable assistance, including interacting with impacted residents during the survey. Much gratitude is also extended to residents providing their accounts and allowing access to damaged areas, especially Amish and Mennonite community members heavily impacted by the EF2 tornado. Appreciation also goes out to Cayuga County Emergency Services for additional insights about scattered wind damage in the Union Springs area.

tornadoes.label: Near Hamtramck, MI
tornadoes.notes: None.

tornadoes.label: Near Lincoln Park, MI
tornadoes.notes: A very brief, weak tornado touched down along Fort St near Memorial Park before tracking into the park and lifting near the Senior Center. Within this narrow path, the majority of trees had large limbs snapped with a handful entirely uprooted. Electrical transmission lines along Fort St were bent with wire damage.

tornadoes.name: Sneads Ferry Tornado 1
tornadoes.label: Sneads Ferry Tornado 1
tornadoes.notes: Based on eyewitness videos, a tornado likely touched down in the marshland are north of Old Folkstone Road. The tornado then moved southeast along the edge of a subdivision where tree and roof damage were noted. Most wooden fences along the path of the tornado were damaged or blown down. The tornado then moved through an apartment complex where the worst damage was noted. Here, portions of roof decking of one of the units were uplifted in the opposite direction of the path of the tornado. Multiple trees were snapped in this area. The tornado then glanced an RV park, damaging trees and a couple of RVs. It appears the tornado then crossed Old Folkstone Road near a Food Lion where eyewitnesses observed the tornado. Based on eyewitness videos, it appears the tornado lifted right around NC 210. In this area, minor damage occurred at the Sneads Ferry Library, and a car was damaged after it was partially uplifted and dropped back down.

tornadoes.name: Sneads Ferry 2
tornadoes.label: Sneads Ferry 2
tornadoes.notes: A tornado initially touched down at a marine commercial building near NC 210 in Sneads Ferry as evidenced by security camera footage. The tornado caused minor damage to the roof of the commercial building and flipped a boat on its side. Based on radar, the tornado likely skipped along a path just west of NC 210. The tornado then crossed back across NC 210 near the Mill Creek neighborhood. Minor tree damage was noted in, and near, the Mill Creek neighborhood. The tornado then strengthened as it moved southeast across NC 210. After crossing NC 210, the tornado hit a residence causing notable damage to the roof decking and front outer wall of the residence. Roof debris was lofted and thrown up to 100 yards downwind into a row of trees at the back of the residence. The tornado then began to lift as it moved through a commercial property where minor tree damage was noted. Debris from the home was lofted over the commercial property and found on the south side of the property. Radar showed a max rotational velocity of 23-25 knots, as well as a debris signature.

tornadoes.name: Hammond, LA Tornado
tornadoes.label: Hammond, LA Tornado
tornadoes.notes: An NWS ground survey confirmed an EF-0 tornado touched down in a parking lot south of West Thomas Street (US 190) west of downtown Hammond, LA in Tangipahoa Parish. This tornado tracked south-southwest causing minor tree damage and collapse of an exterior wall of a small professional building near Robinhood Drive. The damage path remained sparse with only minor threshold of visible damage and tree damage noted as the tornado continued southward across Interstate 55. Some additional EF-0 damage was identified near Stein Rd and Saint Rd before the tornado evidently lifted prior to Old Baton Rouge Hwy. Evidence of this tornado was also supported by eyewitness video and a brief tornado debris signature on KHDC radar imagery. Additional revisions to this track will be possible with the supplementation of additional reports or satellite data in the coming weeks.

tornadoes.name: Boyd County Tornado
tornadoes.label: Boyd County Tornado
tornadoes.notes: Tornado started just north of 903rd Road, then traveling southeast before ending just east of 502nd Avenue. Very little damage was observed, and video evidence suggests intermittent vortices in the beginning stages of the tornado. Tree limb damage was observed near where the tornado ended as it crossed 502nd Avenue. Start and end time were based on video evidence.

tornadoes.name: Lafayette Township Tornado
tornadoes.label: Lafayette Township Tornado
tornadoes.notes:
At 7:19 p.m. local time September 9, 2026 an EF-1 tornado with maximum wind speeds of 105mph touched down between Bradford Airport and Bingham Road with a maximum width of about 200 yards. It traveled east/northeast and damaged some trees around and west of Bingham Road. The tornado continued through the area of woods east of Bingham Road before doing its most intense damage along and north of Sprester Road. It uprooted and snapped many trees before flipping a trailer on its side. The tornado turned northeast and continued damaging trees into the woods before dissipating as it approached the Buffalo & Pittsburgh Railroad line around 7:22 p.m. local time.

We would like to thank McKean County Emergency Management and members of the community who provided firsthand accounts, footage, and pictures of damage.

tornadoes.name: Gurn
tornadoes.label: Gurn
tornadoes.notes: A linear convective storm complex moved into Muskingum and Guernsey Counties at 9:00pm on the night of September 9th, 2026. A portion of this line bowed, and on the northern fringe of this segment, a embedded mesocyclone developed overhead with broad rotation which extended to the surface. A tornado touchdown was estimated from radar to be 9:34pm, immediately knocking down a tree and impacting a couple residences at the intersection of Mayfield Lane and US-22. This was where winds were the strongest, up to 85mph. The most destruction was observed near a small business, where wind entered the building through the roof and blew out a backdoor, as well as knocking an old steeple off of the roof. This wind also may have briefly lifted a trailer and displaced it roughly 10 ft away. Some of the debris from the blow-out impacted a neighboring property's fence and front yard. The adjacent property also observed damage to siding and gutters. A small sign was knocked down across US-22 where the tornado is estimated to have weakened as it moved into a swampy area along Crooked Creek. Minor tree damage was observed along I-70. A couple trees were down along Savage Road before the circulation is expected to have lifted at 9:37pm. Minor tree damage was observed downstream, but damage was more consistent with straight line winds as the bowing convective segment continued it's track into Byesville.

tornadoes.label: Near Avoca, NE
tornadoes.notes: An EF-0 tornado touched down in an agricultural field just south of County Road B, between 32nd and 34th Roads, flattening a path through corn. The tornado tracked east, tipping over a large metal storage tank between 34th and 36th Roads. It continued east, breaking large branches off of trees near 38th and County Road B before lifting.

tornadoes.name: Francis Peak Tornado
tornadoes.label: Francis Peak Tornado
tornadoes.notes: This tornado is estimated to have touched down at 1:44PM MT along Bair Canyon near 6000ft in Davis county. It trekked up the canyon producing primarily EF-1 damage to multiple softwood pines and hardwood aspen groves. A few instances of EF-2 tree damage were noted along the southern side of Bair Canyon via Sentinel satellite imagery and other photos from hikers. Numerous pines were felled, as well as pines that were completely defoliated and had the top of the tree completely sheared off. As the tornado summited Francis Peak into Morgan county around 9500ft, it would go on to snap numerous pines along the higher elevations. The tornado would then take a more northeastern turn as it reached the Middle Smith Lake area on its descent down the east facing side of Francis Peak. This is precisely where some of the heaviest damage occurred to numerous pine trees, where they were either sheared off completely at the top of the tree or snapped at the base. This damage would be consistent with EF-2 across many areas near Middle Smith Lake. As the tornado continued to descend the terrain toward Dalton Creek, it began to widen further to 1.1mi in width (1900yds), setting a state record for tornado width. EF-1 damage was consistent within the Dalton Creek areas with numerous pine trees snapped at the base and aspen groves flattened. The tornado would begin to weaken and begin narrowing shortly after reaching its maximum width, though continued to produce widespread damage to aspen groves and other pine trees within Right Hand Fork Dalton Creek before dissipating just to the west of the confluence of Middle Fork Peterson Creek and Left Hand Fork Peterson Creek around 6200ft at approximately 2PM MT. The maximum width of this tornado was 1900 yards with a path length of 5.93 miles and was on the ground for 16 minutes. In total, this tornado managed to gain 3500ft of elevation on its ascent and descend 3200ft to its final point, resulting in a total elevation change of 6700ft. Additionally, many of the pine trees that were snapped have an age estimated to be around 100-200 years old. Special thanks to the Davis county emergency managers for the assistance with the damage survey, and another special thanks to our local spotters for reporting the damage.

tornadoes.name: MONROE-SEP30-TOR1
tornadoes.label: MONROE-SEP30-TOR1
tornadoes.notes: A narrow waterspout moved ashore in the southern portion of the Silver Shores Community in Key Largo in the leading edge of of a squall line crossing the Upper Florida Keys from oceanside. The waterspout's onshore component destroyed a large porch on an elevated waterfront residence, depositing a large section of single-panel porch roofing 500 feet to the west-southwest in into a tree, about 30 to 40 feet above ground level. There were no other damages observed in the vicinity nor inland of the landfall point of the waterspout, and the track termination is estimated one block inland on level of the deposition of the roof panel.

tornadoes.name: Isaias-Eastpoint Tornado
tornadoes.label: Isaias-Eastpoint Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A tornado associated with the outer bands of Hurricane Isaias moved onshore near the intersection of US 98 and State Road 65 east of Eastpoint in Franklin County. The tornado was captured on video, provided by a local media outlet. The tornado moved inland approximately one mile, causing minor damage to several homes along State Road 65 and Michael Way before dissipating in a forested area.

tornadoes.name: Clito Rd Tornado
tornadoes.label: Clito Rd Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A long track supercell produced an initial weak tornado near the intersection of Clito Road and Rough Rider Road in eastern Bulloch County. The National Weather Service received a witness report of a tornado on the ground and, upon conducting a ground and drone survey, found that large trees were uprooted in a convergent pattern, large branches were snapped, and a crop pivot was damaged along the path where the tornado briefly touched down in the area.

tornadoes.name: Captolo Tornado
tornadoes.label: Captolo Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A weak tornado briefly touched down near Wind Mill Road, southeast of Captolo, GA, before moving north-northeast and dissipating just north of Limesink Road. Its track was periodically visible across open grass fields. Tornado damage was minor and limited to the breakage of large branches from both hardwood and softwood trees. The tin roof was pealed back on a standalone garage.

tornadoes.name: Eastern Screven County Tornado
tornadoes.label: Eastern Screven County Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A rapidly intensifying tornado touched down just south of Highway 21 near Ogeechee Creek before dissipating just north of Old Poor Robin Road in far eastern Screven County, GA. The tornado produced significant tree damage along its path with numerous large hardwood and softwood trees being either snapped off or completely uprooted. One mobile home suffered major damage as a large hardwood tree fell on it. Several cars were also crushed from trees falling on them. Tree damage was observed on parts of Old Poor Robin Road, Poor Robin Road, Wiseman Road and Highway 21.

tornadoes.name: Waynesboro Tornado
tornadoes.label: Waynesboro Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A tornado touched down in the swampland south of Highway 80 near rocky Creek. It moved northeast across Highway 80 and Abrams Rd, turning north and crossing Forest Hill Rd before lifting. Significant damage occurred at a residential farmstead on Hwy 80, including roof damage, multiple large trees uprooted, toppled portions of a center-pivot irrigation system, and multiple 18-wheeler trailers toppled over. The rest of the damage was mainly trees and limbs.

tornadoes.name: Western Allendale Co Tornado
tornadoes.label: Western Allendale Co Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado crossed Highway 301 west of Gravel Hill Road, causing some of the most significant damage. In total, four homes were impacted: one sustained destruction of aluminum roofing material and a front porch; another had complete roof and outer wall failure on a rear addition; and the other two sustained minor roofing damage. An outbuilding and two carports were also destroyed. The tornado then continued north through a heavily wooded area, but additional tree damage occurred just west of Moultry Loop and on Revolutionary Trail.

tornadoes.name: Northern Allendale Tornado
tornadoes.label: Northern Allendale Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A tornado touched down in the wooded area between Miller Creek Road and Yackin Road, rapidly moving north across Camp Jackson Road. It dissipated just east of the Camp Jackson facility, short of the Barnwell County line. Impact was primarily limited to forested areas, with high winds snapping and uprooting clusters of hardwood and softwood trees.

tornadoes.name: Kline Tornado
tornadoes.label: Kline Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A National Weather Service storm survey determined that an EF-1 tornado with maximum wind speeds of 95 mph occurred just west of Kline. The tornado developed south of Boiling Springs Rd, east of Shepherd Rd., moved to the north across a large heavily wooded field, before dissipating near Poplar Road. The tornado snapped numerous hardwood trees. This tornado was likely associated with a supercell that spawned multiple tornadoes.

tornadoes.name: Barnwell Tornado
tornadoes.label: Barnwell Tornado
tornadoes.notes: A National Weather Service storm survey determined that an EF-2 tornado with maximum wind speeds of 115 mph occurred in Barnwell. The tornado developed along Hwy 278 south of Mount Olive Cir, then continued north into the City of Barnwell, before turning northwest through Long Branch and just north of downtown Williston. The tornado produced sporadic tree damage along its path, with the most intense damage occurring in a wooded area along a field south of Freedom Road where numerous large hardwood trees were snapped and uprooted. There is also evidence that a few wooden power poles were snapped. The tornado lifted on the north side of Williston near Wilton Drive. This tornado was likely associated with a supercell that spawned multiple tornadoes.

tornadoes.name: Wagener Tornado
tornadoes.label: Wagener Tornado
tornadoes.notes: On Saturday, October 10th, an EF1 tornado touched down just southeast of Bethcar Church Rd. It quickly strengthened and moved northwestward, causing mostly tree damage along its path. The most significant damage was noted beginning alone Coleman Bridge Rd and continuing along Quail Run Rd where numerous trees were uprooted or snapped. The tornado continued causing damage as it moved northwestward, crossing Kennedy Dr and Camp Rawls Rd with sporadic tree damage noted. The tornado likely lifted in a swampy area north of Eagerton Rd where the final snapped/uprooted trees were noted.

tornadoes.label: Near Pomaria, SC
tornadoes.notes: None.

tornadoes.label: Near Candor, NC
tornadoes.notes: A brief, but strong, short-track tornado occurred on the northeast side of Candor in between Brutonville Road and I-73. Drone images and video provided by Eagle Springs Fire Chief assisted in determining the start point between Cherry Circle and Hurricane Drive where a significant number of uprooted and snapped trees occurred.
