The tornado quickly continued to track roughly northeast where significant damage occurred to a community center which had 3 of its exterior walls collapsed and several more softwood trees were snapped; consistent with high-end EF-1 to low-end EF-2 damage. The tornado continued across a small pond and snapped about 10 hardwood/softwood trees and removed a large portion of roof covering from a residence near Etta Drive. From this point, the tornado quickly lifted, not before snapping small branches, before reaching I-73 with no visible damage from drone footage to the northeast.

tornadoes.label: Near Fayetteville, NC
tornadoes.notes:
A long-track storm produced mostly EF-0 to EF-1 damage, including a short, quarter-mile stretch of EF-2 damage with maximum wind speeds estimated at 115 mph. The tornado touched down near the intersection of Skibo and Morganton roads, knocking down several trees and removing a couple of HVAC units from the Burlington Shoes store within a strip mall. The tornado then likely lifted briefly before touching down again and intensifying near the Walmart along Skibo Road, where it removed nearly 10 HVAC units from the roof, causing minor damage as they tumbled across it. The tornado continued between two hotels, where it bent and collapsed poles, damaged roofs, and rolled a car or two. As the tornado continued through the Sam’s Club parking lot, roughly a dozen cars were toppled or lifted, and one minor injury was reported. The tornado likely continued on a discontinuous path as it entered the residential areas to the northeast of the shopping center. The most significant tree damage occurred near Swainey Avenue and Stansfield Drive, where perhaps two dozen trees were snapped and lying in a convergent pattern in a confined area; minor structural damage occurred as well. The tornado crossed Kornbow Lake before snapping perhaps another two dozen trees between Alpine Street and Hogan Street. Sporadic tornado damage continued along a northeast path until Sandstone Drive where minor tree damage was found by local Emergency Management and has been identified as the new endpoint of the tornado track. Minor tree limb damage was also found around Ramsey St and Andrews Drive, but damage type is inconclusive to suggest the tornado was still on the ground at this point and has been classified as thunderstorm wind damage.

We would like to extend our gratitude to the Emergency Management Team from the City of Fayetteville and Cumberland County for their assistance with the storm survey.

tornadoes.label: Near Moncure, NC
tornadoes.notes: None.

tornadoes.name: Clarendon Tornado
tornadoes.label: Clarendon Tornado
tornadoes.notes: The tornado occurred at a property along Roseland Rd east of Joe Brown Hwy South. Several open farm buildings were destroyed due to roof uplift and subsequent wall failure. Debris was scattered along a narrow path. An empty grain bin was also lifted off its foundation and shifted. Sheet metal roofing was scattered along the path including high into tree canopies and into an adjacent field beyond the grove of trees.

tornadoes.label: Near Linden, NC
tornadoes.notes:
A short-lived tornado with maximum wind speeds of 105 mph initially developed along Ramsey Street near Linden, NC, and continued to track northeast. The most significant damage occurred as the tornado crossed through a residential area between Glenmont Creek Place, Hungry Creek Drive, and Rainy Beck Way. Several homes had minor roof and fence damage; however, a select few along Hungry Creek Drive sustained high-end EF-1 damage, where 50% of the windows were blown out, fence posts set in poured concrete were pulled from the ground, and wind-blown timber punctured exterior walls. The tornado continued tracking northeast into an open area, where drone photos provided by the Harnett County Deputy Fire Marshal revealed a noticeable path through a dormant cornfield and a section of downed or snapped softwood trees in a field north of Horseshoe Bend Road. The tornado then knocked down several more trees in the backyard of a residence along Comanche Drive, pulled an anchored carport out of the ground, and flung it 30 to 50 yards. Finally, the tornado crossed a small pond and knocked down a few more small softwood trees before lifting as it traversed a former airstrip.

We would like to extend our gratitude to Harnett County Emergency Management and the Deputy Fire Marshal for their assistance with the storm survey and for providing drone photos and reconnaissance.

tornadoes.name: Oct 2026 East Arcadia Tornado
tornadoes.label: Oct 2026 East Arcadia Tornado
tornadoes.notes: East Arcadia Tornado confirmed with a combination of damage and video provided by a resident north of East Arcadia. The tornado was broad and evidence suggested that it made intermittent contact with the ground, remaining mostly elevated along the path.

tornadoes.label: Near Rolesville, NC

tornadoes.label: Near Archer Lodge, NC
tornadoes.notes: The tornado occurred along a 3.2 mile-long discontinuous path, as it momentarily touched down and lifted several times before finally dissipating at the end of the indicated path. Damage consisted mainly of snapped and uprooted trees, large tree branches broken off, minor shingle and roof damage to several homes or structures, many fences blown over, and several power poles that were snapped and downed. There was also damage to patio furniture and signage at a service station at the intersection of Hwy 36 and Hwy 70 in Clayton. The max wind speed was 85 mph which is an EF-0 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale (EF Scale).

tornadoes.name: SF Tor
tornadoes.label: SF Tor
tornadoes.notes: A tornado developed in the Via Caballero neighborhood in the south central portion of Santa Fe just north of I-25. The tornado traveled northward for approximately 1.5 miles, terminating near the College of Santa Fe. Much of the damage was along Rancho Siringo and Camino Chueco Roads. Damage included broken power poles, uprooted or damaged trees, damage to roofs. Ten homes sustained damaged with one home having the majority of the roof removed and a collapsed wall. This tornado has been given a rating of EF-1 with peak winds of 110 mph.
